Dein litteræ à Senatu regio ad Prætores, Magistratusq; per Provinciam datæ, quibus statuebat; Ne qui clam conventus populi concionesve essent, intraque præturas aut oppida ulli advenæ præterquam probatæ in Ecclesiam fidei reciperentur. Sanxit insuper, ut ex optimis quibusque Magistratus populi Frisici crearentur, arcerenturque communione munerum dignitatumq;, novarum religionum suspecti, tum fædiore vitâ, temulentiâ & adulterijs cooperti. Franequeranos etiam, velut majore rerum licentiâ præ cæteris usfos, idem Senatus commonuit, ut frequentes sacris intersint, remque divinam more majorum agant, abstineantque privatis consultationibus Philippo regi, & simul paci publicæ adversis. Litteræ 111. Eid Novemb. Leovardiæ exaratæ. Unde Ordinum Delegati (in quorum numero Renicum Burmania Jure-Consultum, Ruardum Rcorda, Valerium Camminga, Haringum Glinzium, & Heffelum Ayfma fuisse comperio) velut diuturnioris moræ pertæsi, quod reparandi juris promissa tardius procederent, Commissarios, ut vocant, dari sibi à Senatu regio petiere, qui de læso imminutoque gentis jure cognoscerent, actaq; & postulata toties in spem redituræ libertatis repetita eludi vanis responsionibus deprehenderent. Quare Senatus Regius Carolum Nitzenium Equestris ordinis virum, & Senatus Præsidem, Petrum Dekama, Equitem & Senatorem, Alexium Gelium Senatorem & regij Fisci advocatum, delegavit; cognitisq; quæ Ordinum Delegati prolaturi forent, totum ad Senatum relationes institui jussit. Qui ut commodis Philippi prospiceret, gratiamq; novi deminantis cum odio provincialium demereretur, naves quoq; omnes ex Hispania, Gallia, Anglia, tum è freto Danico, ac emporiis orientalibus in sinum Scolbalgicum provectas, sponte an de consilio Margaretæ Gubernatricis, gravari nautico ære fecit, quo vasorum indicandis syrtibus mari innatantium impendia commercijs negotiantium sedimerentur. Quod cum ægerrimè provinciales haberet, & imprimis Collumanos Doccumanosque, quorum onerariæ naves illo potissimum sinu recipiuntur, Delegati Ordinum, qui indicti oneris novitate offendebantur, recitari Doccomij & per maritima, regij Senatus Edictum vetuere, populoque commercijs florenti, jus antiquum, immunitatemq; asseruere.
units.tr: Mary the Governess confirmed this by a rescript on the 6th of the Ides of January, adding a solemn assurance that the landowners' rights would remain whole and inviolate. It was a remedy that harmed those landowners but served to relieve the common food supply at that time. For Margaret's plan and edict aimed to stop the forestalling of grain and to have all the corn distributed for the general use of the people, so as to meet the present scarcity of that year. The summer had been soaked with heavy rain, and the chilled air had brought rot to the crops, then a plague among the livestock and a pestilence, and the waters standing on the plains, which the fields themselves held wet by their own nature, drained away more slowly. I find in the Annals of Kempo Martena that, while the remnants of the Burgundian and Gelderland factions were still raging through the province, the Frisian Estates, offended by the domination of Georg Schenck and his followers, begged Margaret, the Emperor's aunt and then governess of the provinces, for a remedy like the suppression or the scarcity of grain, and their complaint gave cause for the same edict, often published by Emperor Charles. The same edict was confirmed the following year at the eager urging of the townsmen, and a penalty fixed by law was imposed on violators of the edict by the magistrates throughout Friesland. Hobbius Baerdius, Cornelius Fonckius, Tarquinius Vallesius, Jacobus Jacobaeus, G. Wallema, Theodorus Theodoretus, Focco Andreae, Johannes Julius Beima and Bonno Petraeus subscribed this on the 3rd of the Ides of March. They also renewed the law on weights and measures, passed in the age of the Saxons, and decreed that the principle and form of the Saxon law be observed in the towns. Then came letters from the royal Senate to the governors and magistrates throughout the province, which ordered that no private gatherings or assemblies of the people be held, and that within the governorships or towns no stranger be received into the Church unless he was of approved faith. It further decreed that the magistracies of the Frisian people be filled from the best men of each place, and that those suspected of new religions, and those steeped in a more shameful life, drunkenness and adultery, be excluded from the sharing of offices and dignities. The same Senate also warned the people of Franeker, as those who had enjoyed greater licence than the rest, that they should attend the sacred services frequently, carry out the worship of God in the manner of their ancestors, and abstain from private consultations hostile to King Philip and to public peace. The letters were written at Leeuwarden on the 3rd of the Ides of November. Thereupon the delegates of the Estates (among whom I find Renicus Burmania, a jurist, Ruardus Rcorda, Valerius Camminga, Haringus Glinzius and Heffelus Ayfma) grew weary of the long delay, since the promises to restore their rights were moving too slowly, and asked the royal Senate to appoint commissioners, as they are called, who would examine the injury and diminution of the nation's rights, and who would find that their petitions and demands, so often repeated in hope of the return of liberty, were being mocked with empty replies. Therefore the royal Senate appointed Charles Nitzenius, a man of the equestrian order and president of the Senate, Peter Dekama, a knight and senator, and Alexius Gelius, senator and advocate of the royal treasury, and ordered that once they had learned what the delegates of the Estates were going to put forward, the whole matter be reported to the Senate. In order to look after the advantages of Philip and to win the favour of the new ruler, who was hated by the provincials, the Senate also, whether of its own accord or by the advice of Margaret the Governess, ordered that all ships which had put in from Spain, France and England, and from the Danish strait and the eastern markets, into the Zuiderzee bay, be charged a nautical tax, so that the expense of marking the sandbanks for ships navigating the sea might be met by the merchants' trade. Since this was most distasteful to the provincials, and especially to the people of Kollum and Dokkum, whose merchant ships are chiefly received into that bay, the delegates of the Estates, offended by the novelty of the imposed burden, forbade the royal Senate's edict to be read out at Dokkum and along the coast, and asserted the ancient right and immunity of a people whose trade was flourishing.

units.la: Adeò diffidentiæ vitium, quod postremis etiam Caroli annis se aperuerat, debile rebus se ultrò dissolventibus vinculum, Philippi maximè principatu increvit, pertinacibus populi in libertatem studijs Principi suspectis, & Arembergij Senatusque Regij imperio Provinciæ gravi. Itaq; is jam ante caverat: Ne quis Leovardiæ præterquam officialis regius, aut publicus justitiæ administer, cum telo incederet, ipsove noctis obscuro, sub pœnâ legis de VI PVBLICA latæ, perpetrandis obtegendisque flagitijs uteretur. Post, stabiliendis Romanæ sedis Pontificumque sanctionibus statuta per Provinciam publicavit. Iis præcepit. Ut festis diebus, & divino cultui dictis, quæcunque etiam operæ, commerciaque cessarent, ipsisq; quadragesimæ, aut alijs diebus, quibus Ecclesia jejunium ordinasset, esu carnium Frisij abstinerent. Statuit quoque ne, dum res divina publicè fieret, cauponaria, & commessationes haberentur, pecuniariâ multa, post arbitrariâ & gravi pœnâ transgressoribus irrogatâ. Hoc tantum indultum fuit, ut pro operarum, valetudinisve ratione Decanus, Commissarius, Presbyter, Medicusve disponeret, istiq; rei, ne quæ fraus statuto fieret, testimonium scriberetur. Tum diuturna asperrimaq; hyems omnium, qui tum per Frisiam degebant, memoriam superans Frisiæ incubuit. Quippe non Lavicæ tantum, Amasiqueflumina, sed Austrinum etiam mare, quod latissimis aquis, & qua Flevo proximius est, vehementi æstu concitatur, commeandi potestatem heminibus, curribus, juncntisque fecit, remque oculis expositam, & majoribus infrequentem naturæ quodam miraculo insignivit. Annotatum reperio eadem flumina atque æstuaria, quæ Frisijs prætexuntur, vernum ultra Æquinoctium glaciem aluisse, agrosq; non ante Iunium mensem revirescentes adulti veris amænitatem brumali inclementiâ commutasse. Itaque pecorum fimus, quæ adhuc Majo mense stabulabantur, in ipsis stabulorum fossis adeò per gelu induruerat, ut solis ferramentis comminueretur, agrique antecedentis anni sterilitate infœcundi statò Æquinoctij tempore non pastinarentur. Hyems quoq; ut longa, ita quam maximè aspera accisa pecorum pabula faceret, cultisq; serius arvis metus iterum ab annona, & difficili alimoniâ anxijs sollicitisq; provincialibus haberetur.
units.tr: Thus the vice of mistrust, which had shown itself even in the last years of Charles, a weak bond that was loosening of its own accord, grew especially under Philip's rule, since the stubborn efforts of the people for liberty were suspect to the prince, and the province was burdened by the rule of Aremberg and the Royal Senate. Accordingly, Philip had already provided beforehand that no one at Leeuwarden, except the royal official or a public minister of justice, should go about with a weapon, or use the darkness of night to commit and cover up crimes, under penalty of the law passed concerning PUBLIC VIOLENCE. Afterwards, to confirm the decrees of the Roman See and of the Popes, he published throughout the province the regulations which he ordered the Frisians to observe: on festival days and days set aside for divine worship, all labour and trade were to cease, and on Lent and other days on which the Church had ordained a fast, the Frisians were to abstain from eating meat. He also decreed that, while the divine service was being performed publicly, taverns and drinking parties were not to be held, a fine being imposed on offenders, and afterwards a heavy penalty at the discretion of the judge. This only was allowed: that the dean, commissioner, elder or doctor might make arrangements according to the needs of workers and health, and that a certificate of this be written out, so that no fraud be practised against the decree. Then a long and very harsh winter, surpassing the memory of all who were then living in Friesland, settled upon Friesland. For not only the rivers Lauwers and Ems, but also the southern sea, which is stirred by a violent tide with its broadest waters and nearest to Lake Flevo, allowed men, carriages and draught animals to cross, and by a certain wonder of nature it marked a thing set before the eyes and rarely seen by older men. I find it recorded that the same rivers and estuaries which run past the Frisians kept their ice beyond the equinox in spring, and that fields, which did not turn green before June, were changed by the mildness of spring into the harshness of winter. So the dung of the animals, which were still kept in stalls in the month of May, had hardened in the very ditches of the stalls with frost, so that it could be broken up only with tools, and the fields, barren from the sterility of the previous year, were not dug at the season of the equinox. The winter, being long and also very harsh, reduced the fodder of the livestock, and because the fields were cultivated late, fear of food shortage and of difficult sustenance again troubled the anxious and worried provincials.

units.la: Mox Margareta Gubernatrix datis ad Præsidem Senatumq; regium litteris totius cleri conventum indixit, litterasq; suas prælegente Carolo Nitzenio, in cuius domo congregabatur, recitari hoc modo fecit.
units.tr: Soon afterwards Margaret the Governess, having sent letters to the President and the royal Senate, called an assembly of the whole clergy, and had her letter read out in the following way, by Charles Nitzenius in whose house they were gathering.

units.la: Concilium Tridenti coactum noftis, ac jam Episcopos sacraq; paginae Doctores celebrando isti Christiani orbis conventui isthuc se contulisse. Et quoniam tanta ac tam sancta res sine magnis impensis geri non potest, recte & ex voluntate regis facietis, si, quod ab omni clero per Belgicæ provincias factum est, pecunias quoq; isti negotio colligatis. Neq; spero vos in illo Philippi regis decreto exequendo tardos ac contumaces fore, præsertim cum stabiliendo Ecclesiastico Ordini, & reprimendis erroribus jam ubivis grassantibus, istud Concilium destinetur.
units.tr: You know that the Council has been convened at Trent, and that the bishops and doctors of Sacred Scripture have already gone there to attend this assembly of the Christian world. And since so great and so holy a business cannot be carried on without large expense, you will do rightly and in accordance with the king's wishes if you also collect money for this undertaking, as has been done by all the clergy in the provinces of Belgium. Nor do I hope that you will be slow or stubborn in carrying out the decree of King Philip, especially since this Council is designed for the strengthening of the ecclesiastical order and the suppression of errors which are now spreading everywhere.

units.la: Similes litteræ ad Godefridum Sylvium Horti Mariæ Præsulem datæ, quo eius autoritate, Præsulum per Frisiam animi ex novitate rerum exulcerati, sacrum ad æs corrogandum perducerentur.
units.tr: Similar letters were given to Godefridus Sylvius, bishop of Hortus Mariae, so that by his authority the bishops throughout Friesland, whose minds were inflamed by the novelty of affairs, might be brought to collect the sacred money.

units.la: Neq; enim (scribebat Margareta) huic tributo obloquutum est, etiam ab ijs, qui à Belgicæ olim provinciis secreti, magno corpori ex justis principum imperijs se sociavere.
units.tr: For (Margaret wrote) no one has objected to this tax, not even those who, having once separated from the provinces of Belgium, have joined the great body under the just rule of princes.

units.la: Quo cum Geldros, Ultrajectinos, Transisulanos, & Groningenses innueret, quos aut unius dominatio, aut Sedis reverentia rexerat, Frisiorum quoq; notatam tacitè libertatem obstringi ad conferendum hoc subsidium volebat, ne unius gentis contumaciâ plurium fides laxaretur. Gemma in suâ Cosmocritice notat, præter terræ motum aliaque prodigia, horrendas tempestates, hac æstate exortas, maritimis locis magna damna dedisse, ipsumq; mare etsi minore æstu ardente syrio intumescat, vi ventorum impulsum littoribus infestum fuisse.
units.tr: By this she meant the Gelderlanders, the people of Utrecht, Overijssel and Groningen, who were governed either by the rule of one man or by reverence for the See, and she wished the Frisians too, whose liberty was quietly noted, to be bound to contribute this subsidy, lest by the stubbornness of one people the loyalty of many should be weakened. Gemma, in his Cosmocritice, notes that, besides earthquakes and other portents, dreadful storms arose this summer and did great damage in maritime places, and that the sea itself, though it swelled less than usual when the dog star burned, was driven by the force of the winds and was dangerous to the shores.

units.la: Ita domesticâ ferè fatorum adversitate, foris & per Hispaniam res turbidis consilijs trahebantur. Iam enim Philippus ruptâ cunctatione, regium opinatus præconcepta exequi, eaq; arbitrio regnantis, non ex eventu rerum metiri, quod in Hispaniâ iv. Eid. Maij Anno cIↄ Iↄ lx. de Episcopis perscripserat, consilium vulgabat, multique eâ de re neq; inveri rumores passim per Frisiam ferebantur. Unde subita consternatio, mox tacitus mœror Provinciam frequentavit, secretaque in Philippum murmura, & dissonæ voces præcinentium sinistra audita. Id namque ciendis maximè ingenijs erat, quod novarum rerum instituto inconsultis Ordinibus, quos reprimendis durioribus imperijs majores semper habuissent, sancta, & venerabilis antiquitas convelleretur, imminutoque cœnobiorum jure sacri reditus pijs usibus,
units.tr: Thus, almost by the adverse fortune of the homeland, affairs abroad and in Spain were being dragged along by troubled counsels. For Philip, having broken off his hesitation and supposing that what he had decided beforehand should be carried out, and that such plans should be measured by the will of the ruler rather than by the outcome of events, published the plan which he had written down concerning the bishops in Spain on the 4th of the Ides of May in the year 1560, and many unfounded rumours about the matter were spread everywhere through Friesland. Hence sudden dismay, and then silent sorrow, filled the province, and secret murmurs against Philip and ominous voices of those who sang beforehand were heard. For the thing most calculated to stir up men's minds was this: that by the novel plan, without consulting the Estates, whom they had always thought of more highly for restraining by harsher commands, the sacred and venerable antiquity was being overturned, and, with the right of the monasteries diminished, the sacred revenues were to be given to pious uses,

units.la: Margareta litteras de Concilio Tridentino.
units.tr: Margaret's letters concerning the Council of Trent.

units.la: Temperies. cIↄ. Iↄ. LXIII. bus, & sublevandis egenis tot per sæcula applicati novo Episcoporum luxui, & magnificentiæ destinarentur. Accedebat & illud, quod firmandæ Inquisitioni ordinatio Episcoporum tanquam velum quoddam obtendi diceretur, tabularumque Episcopalium formula ab eâ suspicione non variaret. Ideò scilicet Frisiorum Episcopo erogandarum in novem Canonicos præbendarum (ut loquuntur) potestatem factam, ut in causâ Inquisitionis iStiusmodi assessoribus idem Præsul uteretur, ipsisq; Decreta Sedis, & eum ipsum in conscientias dominatum Inquisitionem de mandato Episcopi exequerentur. Quæ etsi corrigendis paganis (qui ex Africâ opum commerciorumq; cupidine in Hispaniam migraverant) Ferdinando rege excogitata esset, ita intorqueri conscientijs suis aiebant, ut ipsi probrosæ exterminatæq; etiam Germaniâ, ac potiore Italiæ ora servitutis impatientes turbis ac seditionibus sedarent, temeratâque sui in Principem obsequij lege, sibi ipsis exitium, Philippo verò quam ex composito quærebat, opprimendæ multitudinis, & infælicium armorum occasionem accelerarent. Hac de causâ innuebant tributi etiam sui, quod fœdius, ope continuata post Gallicum bellum militi stipendia, ut post evocatam Italiâ Margaretam Gubernatricem Caroli notham imperitam rerum, & Belgici regiminis, summa imperij, aut regni (nam hoc moliebatur) Cardinali Granvellano ministro, & assentatori Romanorum Pontificum cederet, conculcatâq; Status publici, & Belgicæ Nobilitatis autoritate, ponderosa negotia ad Philippum in Hispaniam, cæterosq; aulæ regiæ satellites devolverentur. Hoc modo horrente, & contremiscente populo, Ordinum quoque Principumque virorum mentes perculsæ, & quod peractâ non semel in Hispaniam legatione, (Montinius namque cæterique jam ante ad Philippum missi erant) velut circumdurato regis animo, nulla in melius rerum ægrescentium mutatio sequeretur. Itaq; Principes aurei Velleris in quorum numero Aurantius, Egmondanus, Hoogstratenus, Montmorentij cæterique erant, nutantium Provinciarum, & suæ juxta incolumitatis metu iv. Eid. Mart. ad Philippum regem litteras dedere, expositiq; immodestis Granvellani consilijs (quibus eum, per incuriam Principum, & quod plerique voluptatibus, atq; oblectamentis ludicris immersi gravem luxu ac socordi ignaviâ vitam agerent, usum fuisse Reidanus notat) tanquam civilium turbarum fomentis, revocandum eum in Hispaniam cum obtestatione fidei suæ proposuere. Alij addunt, adæsis per luxum facultatibus eosdem Principes impulsos, more mortalium, quibus gravis alieni æris sarcina, & recordatio veteris fortunæ esse solet, novas clam societates injisse, ijsdemq; subnixos de submovendo à procuratione Belgicarum rerum Granvellano præfervidis, neque injustis desiderijs laborasse. Ubi verò omne salutis, quietisque impetrandæ consilium inritum fuit, validâ, & flagrante apud Philippum Granvellani gratiâ, ne quid labentibus in deterius rebus ipsorum otio, ac privatæ fortunæ affingi posset, missionem oravere, & ut Philippus lubricos honores, quos Carolus pater, aut ipse, Belgicâ excedens concesserat, & simul in alios onera ac pericula transferret. Cæterum, ut lubricam Imperij semitam ingressis retrahere pedem fortuna non sinebat; ita honores ijs à Philippo continuati, ut stato tempore confortes principatus sui administros ex arduo, & præruptò honorum culmine præcipitaret. Qui propterea prævisâ nutantis fortunæ inconstantiâ concilio status abstinuerunt, potioremque regundæ, pacandæque (nam haud parum commota cernebatur) Belgicæ curam in cæteros dignationis suæ, & potentiæ æmulos rejecere.
units.tr: Temperies. MDLXIII. and to relieve the needy, which had been assigned for so many centuries, were to be diverted to the new luxury and splendour of the bishops. It was also added that the ordering of bishops was said to be put forward as a kind of veil to strengthen the Inquisition, and that the form of the episcopal charters did not differ from that suspicion. Hence, it seems, the power of granting prebends (as they put it) to nine canons was given to the Bishop of Friesland, so that the same prelate might use such assessors in the business of the Inquisition, and that these men might carry out the decrees of the See, and that domination over consciences, by the bishop's mandate. Although this had been devised under King Ferdinand to correct the pagans (who had migrated from Africa to Spain out of desire for wealth and trade), they said it was twisted against their consciences in such a way that they, shamefully driven out even from Germany and the chief coast of Italy and impatient of slavery, would stir up tumults and seditions, and, the law of obedience to their prince having been broken, would hasten their own ruin and furnish Philip with the occasion he was seeking, to crush the multitude by unhappy arms. For this reason they also hinted that their taxes, more shamefully, were used to keep paying the soldiers continuously after the French war. Margaret, the Governess, Charles's illegitimate daughter, inexperienced in affairs, had been recalled from Italy; the supreme power of the Belgian government, or of the kingdom (for this he was contriving), was to pass to Cardinal Granvelle, the minister and flatterer of the Roman pontiffs; the authority of the States and of the Belgian nobility would be trampled, and weighty business would be transferred to Philip in Spain and to the other attendants of the royal court. With the people thus horrified and trembling, the minds of the leading men of the Orders were also struck; and since an embassy to Spain had been carried out more than once (for Montigny and the others had already been sent to Philip earlier), and as if the king's mind had been hardened, no change for the better in the sickening state of affairs followed. Therefore the Knights of the Golden Fleece, among whom were Orange, Egmont, Hoogstraten, Montmorency and the others, wrote a letter to King Philip on 12 March, fearing for the wavering provinces and for their own safety. Setting out the wanton counsels of Granvelle (by whose negligence of the princes, and because most of them, immersed in pleasures and playful amusements, lived a life of heavy luxury and careless idleness, Reidanus notes he had made use of them), they proposed that he be recalled to Spain as a fomenter of civil disturbances, with an appeal to their good faith. Others add that the princes, their means exhausted by luxury, were driven, as mortals are when the heavy burden of debt and the memory of former fortune are wont to be, to form new secret associations, and, relying on these, laboured with passionate and not unjust desires to have Granvelle removed from the administration of Belgian affairs. But when every plan for obtaining safety and peace had come to nothing, and Granvelle's influence with Philip was strong and blazing, they begged for their dismissal, so that nothing could be imputed to their leisure and private fortunes as things slid into worse. They asked that Philip also transfer to others the slippery honours that Charles his father, or he himself, on leaving Belgium, had granted them, together with the burdens and dangers. Yet, just as fortune would not allow those who had entered the slippery path of empire to draw back their foot, so the honours were continued to them by Philip in such a way that at the appointed time he would cast down from the steep and precipitous height of honour the companions of his principate who served him. Therefore, foreseeing the inconstancy of their wavering fortune, they abstained from the council of state, and cast the chief care of governing and pacifying Belgium (for it was seen to be not a little disturbed) onto the others who were their rivals in rank and power.

units.la: Tum MARGARETA Gubernatrix, secessione Principum Equitumque aurei Velleris clam offensa, ne conciliandæ Granvellano invidiæ major procerum divulsio pararetur, legatum in Hispaniam propere amandavit, Antoniusq; post Perennottus Cardinalis Granvellanus mandato Philippi, sive ut Reidanus habet, ultrò injurijs Principum lacessitus, inexpiabili erga Belgicam nobilitatem odio, superstite adhuc sociorum factionis suæ potentiâ in Burgundiam, & mox Hispaniam concessit. Cæterum Principum Belgicæ secessio, ut inimicis paratura invidiem videbatur, ita econtra potentiam paravit. Submoto namque Belgicâ Granvellano evenit, ut quos ante consiliorum suorum participes fecerat, eosdem inlatæ sibi contumeliæ ultores relinqueret, omneq; publicæ autoritatis robur, in excusationem Granvellani, & oppressionem adversæ partis, & simul Belgicæ libertatis verteretur. Creditum fuit præclaros alios viros, & fortunam ex virtute nactos, ut ante dominatus, ita tum Granvellani famæ importunos defensores extitisse,. ipsumq; Philippum Granvellani è Belgica discessu exacerbatum, ardens sponte ingenium, & præcipitia suorum consiliorum exasperasse. Itaq; Senatus tum regius per secessionem Principum, sui juris, & potestatis factus in curam consecrandorum, introducendorumq; Episcoporum deflexit, quod ad negotium ocyus capessendum, Margareta Gubernatrix primores Senatus muliebri vehementiâ impellebat.
units.tr: Then Margaret the Governess, secretly offended by the withdrawal of the princes and the Knights of the Golden Fleece, lest a greater division of the nobles be prepared to foment hatred against Granvelle, quickly sent off an envoy to Spain. Antoine Perrenot, then Cardinal Granvelle, by command of Philip (or, as Reidanus has it, provoked by the injuries of the princes), with an implacable hatred towards the Belgian nobility, while the power of his faction's allies still survived, withdrew to Burgundy and soon to Spain. But the secession of the Belgian princes, though it seemed likely to stir up hatred against their enemies, on the other hand gained them power. For once Granvelle had been removed from Belgium, it came about that those whom he had earlier made partners in his counsels he left as avengers of the insult offered to them, and the whole strength of public authority was turned both to the defence of Granvelle and the oppression of the opposing party, and at the same time to the destruction of Belgian liberty. It was believed that other distinguished men, who had gained fortune through virtue, then stood as unwelcome defenders of Granvelle's reputation, just as they had done in his earlier dominance; and that Philip himself, exasperated by Granvelle's departure from Belgium, had inflamed his own ardent temper and the rashness of his counsels. And so the royal Senate, made by the secession of the princes into master of its own right and power, turned its attention to the consecration and introduction of bishops, since the Governess Margaret, with feminine vehemence, was urging the leading men of the Senate to take up this business more quickly.

units.la: Iam enim mense Iunio Fredericus Tauteburgius, qui Egmondano successerat, primus post Willibrordum Ultrajectinæ sedis ArchiEpiscopus totam constituendi per Frisiam Episcopatus rationem evulgaverat, missumq; in Frisios diploma Pontificum sanctione, ac Philippi mandato firmaverat.
units.tr: For already in June, Frederick Tauteburg, who had succeeded Egmont, the first archbishop of the see of Utrecht after Willibrord, had published the entire plan for establishing bishoprics throughout Friesland, and had confirmed the document, sent to the Frisians, with the sanction of the Popes and the mandate of Philip.

units.la: FREDERICVS, Dei & Apostolicæ Sedis gratiâ, Archi-Episcopus Trajectensis, Universis præsentes litteras nostras visuris Salutem in Domino. Cum dudum Sanctissimus Dominus noster Pontifex Maximus ad preces Serenissimi Principis PHILIPPI, Hispaniarum Regis Catholici, domini temporalis civitatis & patriæ Trajectensis, Domini nostri elementissimi, ad honorem & gloriam Dei omnipotentis, pro religionis Orthodoxæ conservatione, ac patriæ & subditorum salute, certos Archi-Episcopatus ac Episcopatus in provinciis suis inferioribus erexerit. Et præsertim novam Sedem Episcopalem in civitate Leovardiensi, cui tota provincia & populus Frisiæ de Oostergoo, Westergoo & Sevenwoolden, perpetuo tanquam suo Episcopo Diocesano subjiciantur, constituerit; & ab Ecclesiâ Trajectensi, cui antea suberant, separaverit. Notum facimus, quod nos, qui ex Sanctæ Sedis Apostolicæ clementiâ & dictæ serenissimæ regiæ maiestatis auspicio & favore, ad Archi-Episcopatus Traiectensis Præsulatum vocati & assumpti fuimus, eaque omnia quæ per eandem Sedem Apostolicam circa huiusmodi erectionem Episcopatus Leovardiensis salubriter decreta & ordinata exexistunt, quo ad nos & Archi-Episcopatum nostrum attinet, rata & firma esse volumus omnibus via, modo, forma, ac jure, quibus potuimus & possumus melioribus, creavimus, constituimus & deputavimus, creamusq;, constituimus & ordinamus, ac deputamus, per præsentes, nostros certos indubitatos, & legitimos procuratores & mandatarios ac nuncios speciales ac generales, ac negotiorum nostrorum infra scriptorum gestores irrevocabiles, videlicet Reverendum in Christo patrem, Nobiles & Magnificos viros, D. Iohannem Episcopum & Suffraganeum nostrum in Ecclesia Cathedrali Groningensi, &c. absentes tanquam præsentes, & eorum quemlibet (qui has deferet solum & in solidum specialiter & expressè) ad nostro nomine & sub titulo & qualitate Archi-Episcopi Trajectensis, ad quamcunque requisitionem dictæ regiæ Cathed. Majestatis ac Illustriss. & Excellentissimæ Principis Ducissæ Parmæ & Placentiæ, &c. Locum-tenentis & Gubernatricis generalis barum provinciarum, vel etiam ipsius Illustris Domini Comitis Arembergensis locum tenentis generalis patriæ Frisiæ, coram Senatu provinciali, seu statibus ac populis dictæ Frisiæ, aut civitate & Ecclesiâ Leovardiensi, aut alibi ubi opus, & necesse erit comparendum, ibique quo omnia, quæ circa erectionem & institutionem dictæ novæ Sedis Episcopalis Leovardiensis de nostro consensu, ut præditum est, sanctè ordinata existunt; nedum si necesse fuerit hoc ipsum declarandum, vel denuò consentiendum, sed assistendum quoq;& juvandum, ut constet mentis nostræ fuisse, & esse; ut negotium hoc pro dictæ Sedis Apostolicæ ac regiæ Majestatis intentione planè conficiatur, & executioni ac effectui mandetur, nec non specialiter ac generaliter ad omni jurisdictiomi autoritati & potestati Ecclesiasticæ & ordinariæ, quam nos ratione Ecclesiæ nostræ Trajectensis hactenus in dictâ provinciâ Frisiæ cum appendentijs supra dictis habuimus, & nobis competere potuit, ac imposterum quomodo prætendere possemus in favorem dicti novi Episcopi Leovardiensis si opus sit, cedendum & renuntiandum, quemadmodum etiam ex abundanti bonâ fide cedimus & renuntiamus per easdem præsentes, exceptâ duntaxat superioritate & jure nostro metropolitico, quod in Ecclesiâ & Diocesi Leovardiensi subjecta & subjicienda nobis & Archi-Episcopatui nostro Trajectensi perpetuò salvum, integrum & reservatum esse intendimus. Et generaliter omnia alia & singula faciendum, dicendum, agendum, declarandum, & procurandum quæ in præmissis & circa ea necessaria erunt, seu alias quomolibet opportuna, & quæ nos ipsi si præsentes & personaliter ibidem adessemus, facere, declarare & assistere possemus, etiamsi talia forent, quæ mandatum exigerent magis speciale, quam præsentibus est expressum, & majora forent prænarratis. Promittentes in fide Archiepiscopi totum id,* & quicquid per dictos nostros Procuratores & Mandatarios, seu eorum alterum actum, dictum, factum, gestumvè fuerit in præmissis ratum, firmum ac gratum perpetuò habituros. In cuius rei fidem & testimonium easdem præsentes manu nostra subscripsimus, sigillîq; nostri secreti jussimus appensione communiri. Datum in ædibus Archi-Episcopalibus civitatis Trajectensis, mensis Junij die secundo, Anno à nativitate Domini, millesimo quingentesimo sexagesimo quarto.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God and of the Apostolic See, Archbishop of Utrecht, to all who shall see these our present letters, greeting in the Lord. Whereas our most holy Lord, the Supreme Pontiff, at the petition of the most serene Prince Philip, Catholic King of Spain, temporal lord of the city and land of Utrecht, our most merciful Lord, for the honour and glory of Almighty God, for the preservation of the orthodox religion, and for the safety of the country and its subjects, had erected certain archbishoprics and bishoprics in his lower provinces; and especially had constituted a new episcopal see in the city of Leeuwarden, to which the whole province and people of Friesland, of Oostergo, Westergo and Sevenwolden, should be perpetually subject as to their own diocesan bishop, and had separated them from the Church of Utrecht, to which they had previously been subject. We make known that we, who by the clemency of the Holy Apostolic See and by the auspices and favour of the said most serene royal majesty have been called and assumed to the office of Archbishop of Utrecht, and who wish that all those things which have been wholesomely decreed and ordained by the same Apostolic See concerning the erection of the bishopric of Leeuwarden be ratified and confirmed so far as concerns us and our archbishopric, have, by the best way, manner, form and right by which we could and can, created, constituted and deputed, and do create, constitute and ordain and depute, by these presents, our certain, undoubted and lawful procurators, mandatories and special and general envoys, and irrevocable managers of our business written below: namely the Reverend Father in Christ, the noble and magnificent men, Lord John, our Bishop and Suffragan in the cathedral church of Groningen, etc., absent as if present, and any one of them (who shall bear these presents) solely and entirely, specially and expressly, to appear in our name, under the title and quality of Archbishop of Utrecht, at whatever requisition of the said royal Catholic Majesty and of the most illustrious and most excellent Princess, the Duchess of Parma and Piacenza, etc., Lieutenant and Governess General of these provinces, or also of the Lord Count of Arenberg, Lieutenant General of the country of Friesland, before the provincial Senate, or the States and peoples of the said Friesland, or in the city and church of Leeuwarden, or elsewhere where it shall be needful and necessary; and there to declare, and if necessary to consent again to, everything which concerning the erection and institution of the said new episcopal see of Leeuwarden has been holily ordained with our consent, as stated; and to assist and help, so that it may be plain that this was and is our intention, and that this business may be completed and carried into execution and effect according to the intention of the said Apostolic See and of the royal Majesty; and also, specially and generally, to cede and renounce to the said new Bishop of Leeuwarden, if need be, all ecclesiastical and ordinary jurisdiction and authority and power, which we have hitherto had in the said province of Friesland by reason of our Church of Utrecht with the appendages mentioned above, and which could belong to us, or which we might in future claim by any means; just as, also out of abundant good faith, we do cede and renounce by these presents, excepting only the superiority and our metropolitan right, which we intend to remain perpetually safe, whole and reserved to us and to our Archbishopric of Utrecht, in the Church and diocese of Leeuwarden, which is and shall be subject. And generally to do, say, act, declare and procure all other and single things which shall be necessary in the premises and about them, or otherwise fitting in any way, and which we ourselves, if present and personally there, could do, declare and assist in, even if such things should require a more special mandate than is expressed in these presents, and be greater than the foregoing. Promising on the faith of an Archbishop that we shall hold as ratified, firm and acceptable for ever everything and whatever shall have been done, said, made or transacted by our said procurators and mandatories, or either of them, in the premises. In witness and testimony of which we have subscribed these presents with our hand and ordered them to be confirmed by the appending of our secret seal. Given in the Archiepiscopal house of the city of Utrecht, on the second day of June, in the year from the birth of the Lord, one thousand five hundred and sixty-four.

units.la: FREDERICUS.
units.tr: FREDERICUS.

units.la: Quapropter Margareta, ut singulis Provinciarum Ordinibus consilium Philippi commendaret, litteras in Frisiam ad Ordines, Senatumque que Leovardiensem dedit, quibus docebat: Placuisse Philippo Regi Episcopum Frisijs designare, ac Leovardiæ Sedem constituere. Hac de causâ Philippum, Romam Franciscum Sonnium ad Paulum & Pium IV. Pontifices Romanos ablegasse, ne quid temerè statueret, adultæ temporum licentiæ, & manifestis ab Ecclesia secessionibus opportunum. Neq; enim aliud istâ Sonnij Legatione; & hoc ipso Decreto spectasse, quam ut ipse Hispaniâ suâ clausus, ita exigente regni statu, per Episcopos in Provincijs Belgicæ, & simul Frisiâ constitutos, religionem, tot sæculis receptam, & simul jus populi stabiliret, rerumque ultrò fluentium, ut in humanis constans nihil atque perpetuum esset, ordinem, confusionis vitio intactum conservaret. Et quoniam à longâ temporum memoriâ Ecclesiasticarum rerum summa per Frisiam cognitio, ac consecratio Antistitum penes præsulem Ultrajectinum fuisset, ita Philippum regem, hoc ipso erectæ Sedis beneficio cleri maxumè ærario prospexisse, ne tantis impendijs Legationes Ultrajectum fiant, cæterum intra Provinciam omnia habeantur, ordinationi, consecrationique religiosorum præscripta. Propterea Archiepiscopum Ultrajectinum jus suum, quo ante usus fuerat, Suffraganeo suo Frisiorum Episcopo cessisse, ut is simili potestate agat, commissumque sibi munus ex instituto veteri, bono populi Frisici tueatur. Rogare eapropter Frisiæ Ordines, & Senatum Leovardiæ urbis, ut omnem operam erigendæ Sedi præstent, quo Philippi regis voluntati, & conditioni simul temporum satisfiat. Litteræ Margaretæ Bruxellis v I. Kal. Aug. signatæ. His addebat Margareta, Sedem in Provinciâ constitutam agrarios, oppidanosque majore concordiâ junctūram, foreque ut divulsi ante Provincialium animi, eâdem communione sacrorum connexi, in unum corpus sepositâ dissensione coalituri sint.
units.tr: Therefore Margaret, so that she might commend Philip's plan to each of the provincial estates, sent letters to the estates of Friesland and to the senate of Leeuwarden, in which she explained that King Philip had resolved to appoint a bishop for Friesland and to establish the see at Leeuwarden. For this reason Philip had sent Francis Sonnius to Rome to the popes Paul and Pius IV, so that he would not decide anything rashly, given the unbridled licence of the times and the open secessions from the Church. For the embassy of Sonnius and this very decree aimed at nothing else than this: that Philip himself, shut up in his Spain, should, as the state of the kingdom required, establish through bishops set up in the provinces of Belgium and at the same time in Friesland the religion received for so many centuries, together with the right of the people. He would also keep the order of things, which flow on of their own accord, free from the vice of confusion, so that nothing among human affairs should be constant and perpetual. And since from long memory the supreme oversight of ecclesiastical affairs in Friesland, and the consecration of its bishops, had rested with the bishop of Utrecht, the king had provided, by this very benefit of the newly erected see, especially for the clergy's treasury, so that such great expenses for embassies to Utrecht would not be incurred, and everything within the province would be handled according to the rule prescribed for the ordination and consecration of the clergy. Therefore the archbishop of Utrecht had ceded the right he had formerly exercised to his suffragan, the bishop of the Frisians, so that he might act with the same power and, according to the ancient institution, guard the office committed to him for the good of the Frisian people. She therefore asked the Frisian estates and the senate of the city of Leeuwarden to make every effort to erect the see, so that the will of King Philip and at the same time the condition of the times might be satisfied. Letters of Margaret, signed at Brussels on 27 July. Margaret added that the see established in the province would bring the country folk and townspeople together in greater harmony, and that the minds of the provincials, previously divided, would be joined by the same communion of sacred rites and would unite into one body, with dissension set aside.

units.la: Invenio in archivis Provinciæ Deputatos Ordinum, suo & Magistratus Leovardiensium nomine Magaretæ Gubernatrici hunc in modum respondisse: Displicere sibi quam maxumè Philippi regis in constituendâ apud Leovardios Sede, consilium, neque è Rep. videri hoc institutum antiquandis patriæ legibus, & majorum immunitatibus repertum. Quas ipsas sartas tectas fore Carolus Cæsar publicâ Anni cIↄ. Iↄ. xxiv. conventione fidem fecisset. Neq; aliâ lege Philippum paterni Principatus hæredem, & successorem Frisico populo obstringi, quam quæ conservandis ijsdem privilegijs sit. Quorum propterea sanctum, atq; inviolabile jus nihil commune habere cum novo illius Ordinis instituto, quod inquietudinem populo, exitium Provinciæ daturum sit. Quapropter se operam, ac consilium commodare isti negotio non posse, nisi speciali Ordinum Frisiæ mandato instructos, quorum interfit; Ne quid detrimenti. Rogare interea Præfectum Aremberglum, pro eâ re apud Gubernatricem intercedat, interpreteturque responsum à libertate sua, & studio salutis publicæ profectum. Hoc in acta relatum, ac à Serapio Hania, C. Fonckio, Valerio Buma, Ruardo Roorda, Haringio Glinzio, Docone Martena, Iacobo Sibrandio, & Hessclo Aylma, v. Eid. Aug. signatum.
units.tr: I find in the archives of the province that the deputies of the estates, on behalf of their own body and of the magistrates of Leeuwarden, answered the governess Margaret in this manner: that King Philip's plan for setting up the see at Leeuwarden displeased them very much, and that this arrangement did not seem to them to serve the commonwealth, but to have been devised for overturning the laws of the fatherland and the immunities of their ancestors. That these same rights would remain whole and intact, Charles the Emperor had assured them by a public agreement in the year 1524. Nor was Philip, as heir and successor to his father's principality, bound to the Frisian people by any law other than one that preserves those same privileges. Therefore their sacred and inviolable right had nothing in common with that new institution, which would bring unrest to the people and ruin to the province. For this reason they could not lend their effort and counsel to that business unless they were instructed by a special mandate of the Frisian estates, whose concern it is, lest any harm be done. Meanwhile they asked the prefect Aremberg to intercede on this matter with the governess, and to interpret the reply as having come from their liberty and their zeal for the public safety. This was recorded in the acts and signed by Serapius Hania, C. Fonckius, Valerius Buma, Ruardus Roorda, Haringius Glinzius, Docon Martena, Jacobus Sibrandius, and Hesselus Aylma, on 9 August.

units.la: His duorum potentium cænobiorum validæ adversus ordinationem Episcopi contentiones, & juxta querimoniæ accedebant. Repetebat namque Horti Mariæ Antistes Regnerus Asperanus in consessu Delegatorum, Ordinem illum Honorio II. & post Calixto Pontifice institutum, illudque cænobium ab Anno cIↄ. Iↄ. LXIII. tenui fortunâ usum, pietatis & sanctimoniæ claritudine sensim increvisse. Datos ei ex inlustribus familijs Antistites, hominesque desiderio cælibis vitæ & fastidio terrenarum rerum correptos, locum hunc delegisse suo secessui, & pijs meditationibus commodum. Exinde censum, temporum progressu auctum, non alia donantium intentione, quam ut numen à mortalium turbâ secretis ritè coleretur, reliquumque census frugalitate cænobitarum corrogatum egestati pauperum inserviret. Hoc modo post trium ferè saeculorum ambitum jus cænobio integrum fuisse, donec intestina bella ambitione & discordiâ Principum, ac scissæ per Frisiam nobilitatis Saxonicis temporibus exorta, cum ipso Principis imperio occupatâ Provinciâ, vis quoq; cænobio inferretur. Tum quippe Tacone Æbingha viro nobili loci Antistite, cænobij agros maris alluvione pascendo pecori vicino littori adjectos à Georgio Saxone per vim occupatos, ac aggere circumductos annuos cænobij reditus minuisse. Antistitem ipsum dispendio suarum rerum, & imperio Saxonis potentis domini offensum, ac tempori obsecutum depositâ dignitate Lidlumum commigrasse, animiq; ægritudine, post pestilentiâ correptum diem vitæ clausisse. Neq; Carolo Cæsare meliorem cænobij fortunam fuisse. Ita sparsis per Provinciam Cæsarei exercitus reliquijs locaria agrorum intercepta, indutiis quoque cænobio præsidi s, ne quod sacrum religiosumque intactum armis aut saltem armorum incommodis haberetur. Tum militem contemptâ loci religione sadâ libidine & immundâ Venere sacrum polluisse, oppressaqve immunitate (quam à Pontificibus donatam Carolus Cæsar Anno cIↄ. Iↄ. x v. per Florentium Iselsteinium, post Vormatiæ ipsis Imperij comitijs, coram Legatis, integram fore promiserat) importunis exactionibus vexasse. Cæterum ista omnia bellicæ tum legi imputata. Nunc verò quietâ regione, & silentibus armis loci jus inverti, atque violari, eoq; robusto Principis imperio perventum esse, ut nec Senatus Philippi jus petentibus dicat, aut restitutionem in integrum poscentibus subveniat, cæterum supplici clero, tum ipsis Frisiæ Ordinum Legatis juris Ecclesiastici defensoribus silentium imponat. Id Renico Burmaniæ, & Francifco Camminghæ viris nobilissimis, & mandata Ordinum gerentibus à Senatu regio, Anno cIↄ. Iↄ. Lv. obvenisse, nihilque aliud in posterum sperari posse; quam ut leges per vim sileant, omneq; divinum, & juxta humanum dominatio Principis, & cupido majoris imperij profanet. Interim morem se gerere mandato Principis hac in re non posse, quin obtestari jus inveteratum, innocentiam Ordinis sui, morum atque Religionis integritatem, violenta hæc esse, perraro retinendis in fide mentibus diuturna. Neque absimilia Isbrandus Hardervicenus Lidlumanus, omnisque per Provincias antistitum ordo proferebant. Creditum fuit collegiorum istorum antistites molliori vitæ suetos, ut ægrios à jure suo, ita vivendi licentiâ dimoveri potuisse, difluentemque otioso luxu vitam nastos, metuentes disciplinæ, censuræ Episcopali periniquos extitisse. Notat Sibrandus Leo in Vitis Ab-babatum Horti Mariæ, Ioannem Hafseltanum loci illius Antistitem, cIↄ. Iↄ. Mariam Gubernatricem Caroli Cæsaris sororem Anno cIↄ. Iↄ. xlv. lxiv. Provinciam Frisiæ lustrantem unà cum Georgio Egmondano Episcopo Trajectensi, & Maximiliano Burano Frisiæ Præfecto, sumptuoso, & æmulo principum epulo excepisse, eundemque Antistitem immodico luxu jam ante usum, ne umbrá quidem virtutis in posteros transfusa, sex millia alieni æris Henrico Smeinzio successori reliquisse. Eundem quoq; Smeinzium socordis ignaviæ hominem, & domestico paratu nobilitati gravem æs alienum cumulasse, auctoque nexu creditoribus obligatum, & suarum rationum oblitum, curâ Petri Dekamæ Senatoris regij dignitate exutum, mox in squallidum carcerem detrusum, ac vix dimissum, attenuatum mærore corpus cum vitâ posuisse. Reperio in actis, Godefridum Sylvium Smeinsij successorem, implorato prius Curiæ decreto annuos hoc tempore prædiorum reditus, expungendis nominibus alienasse, ipsum; Smeinsium Volveganum tanquam conflati alieni æris autorem, in ipsis venditionum tabulis insignivisse. Reditus quoq; & prædia cænobiorum, quod in Philippi prætorum mandatis observo, rerum divenditarum onere exempta fuisse, solaq; proclamatione per tribunal factâ, emptorem in possessionem rei divenditæ immissum.
units.tr: To these were added the strong complaints of two powerful monasteries against the bishop's ordination, and their protests. For Regnerus Asperanus, abbot of Hortus Mariae, repeated in the assembly of delegates that that order had been founded under Pope Honorius II and afterwards under Calixtus, and that this monastery, which from the year 1163 had had a slender fortune, had gradually grown in the renown of its piety and holiness. Abbots from illustrious families had been given to it, and men seized by a longing for the celibate life and a disgust for earthly things had chosen this place for their retreat and as suitable for holy meditations. Thereafter its revenue, increased as time went on, was given not with any other intention on the part of the donors than that the deity might be duly worshipped apart from the crowd of mortals, and that the remainder of the revenue, gathered by the frugality of the monks, might serve the needs of the poor. In this way, over nearly three centuries, the monastery had its right whole, until internal wars arising in Saxon times from the ambition and discord of princes, and from the nobility of Friesland being split apart, together with the occupation of the province by the prince's power, brought violence upon the monastery too. For then Tako Ebinga, a nobleman and abbot of the place, saw the monastery's fields, which had been added to the pasture land near the shore by sea alluvium, forcibly seized by George of Saxony and enclosed by a dike, and the monastery's annual revenues diminished. The abbot himself, offended by the loss of his property and by the power of the Saxon lord, and yielding to the times, laid down his dignity and went to Lidlum, and, seized by a pestilence together with sickness of mind, ended his life. Nor under Emperor Charles was the monastery's fortune any better. Thus, with the remnants of the imperial army scattered through the province, the lands of the place were taken, and truces were granted to the monastery as a protection, so that no sacred and religious place would be left untouched by arms, or at least by their hardships. Then the soldiers, scorning the sanctity of the place, defiled the sacred ground with wanton lust and foul Venus, and, overriding the immunity (which the popes had granted and which Charles the Emperor had promised in the year 1515, through Florentius Iselsteinius, after the imperial diet at Worms, before the legates, would be kept whole), they harassed the monastery with burdensome exactions. But all these things were then imputed to the law of war. Now, however, in a quiet region and with arms silent, it has come about that the right of the place is overturned and violated, and by the strong power of the prince it has come to pass that the senate of Philip neither gives judgment to those seeking their right nor comes to the aid of those demanding restoration to the former state, but imposes silence on the suppliant clergy and on the very legates of the Frisian estates, the defenders of ecclesiastical right. This happened to Renicus Burmania and Franciscus Camminga, most noble men who carried the mandates of the estates, from the royal senate in the year 1555, and nothing else can be hoped for in future than that the laws be silenced by force and that everything divine and human be profaned by the domination of the prince and the desire for greater power. Meanwhile they said that they could not comply with the prince's mandate in this matter without protesting the long-established right, the innocence of their order, and the integrity of their morals and religion, since these violent measures are such as seldom leave minds lasting in their faith. Isbrandus Hardervicensis, the abbot of Lidlum, and the whole order of abbots throughout the provinces put forward things not unlike these. It was believed that the abbots of those colleges, accustomed to a softer way of life, could be moved away from their right just as much by the licence of living, and that men whose life flows away in idle luxury, fearing discipline, had been most unfair to episcopal censure. Sibrandus Leo notes, in the Lives of the Abbots of Hortus Mariae, that John Hafselt, abbot of that place, received Mary, the governess and sister of Emperor Charles, in the year 1545 (or 1564), when she was touring Friesland together with Bishop George of Egmond of Utrecht and Maximilian Buren, prefect of Friesland, with a sumptuous feast rivalling princes; and that this same abbot, already given to immoderate luxury, left, without even a shadow of virtue passed on to posterity, six thousand guilders of debt to his successor, Henry Smeinzius. The same Smeinzius, a man of slothful indolence, and burdened by a domestic display which was heavy for the nobility, piled up debt; bound ever more tightly to his creditors and forgetful of his accounts, he was stripped of his dignity through the care of Peter Dekama, royal senator, was soon thrown into a squalid prison, and, scarcely released, laid down his body wasted by grief together with his life. I find in the acts that Godefridus Sylvius, Smeinsius's successor, after first obtaining a decree of the court, at this time alienated the annual revenues of the estates by having the names erased, and that Smeinsius of Volvega, as the author of the accumulated debt, was marked in the very deeds of sale. The revenues and estates of the monasteries, which I observe in the orders of Philip's praetors, were also freed from the burden of the goods sold, and, by proclamation alone made at the tribunal, the buyer was put into possession of the thing sold.

units.la: Idem Sibrandus Leo tradit, Isbrandum Hardervicenum Præsulem Lidlumanum, ante dignitatem rectè ingenio usum, mox dignitate corruptum celebrandis quotidianis epulis, & geniali vitæ se dedisse, Præposituraeque insuper Bolsuerdiensis administrationem adeptum, mox eâ à Senatu regio privatum, dein munere Antistitis defunctum, & reddendis rationibus imparem, Embdam, post Francofurtum, dein Coloniam redijsse, destitutumque à suis, pestilenti aurâ attactum, mortalitatem implevisse. Ejusdem quoq; Antistitis electione biduum in ipso coenobij atrio largâ potatione exactum, precesque ad DEUM fusas, tum ceremonias isti actui solemnes infami ebrietate, & probrosis repotijs foedatas. Perscriptum commentarijs est, Præfectum Arembergium, Senatumque regium, tum ipsum quoque Gulielmum Lindanum Commissarium jam ante monasticorum collegiorum luxu inritatos, clàm illud consilium Philippo suggessisse, immutandoq; ordini occasionem commodasse. Eundem quoque ordinem suâ opinione Principis imperio exemptum, jus suum pertinaciter tutatum, de removendo Frisiâ Episcopo vehementius laborasse.
units.tr: The same Sibrandus Leo reports that Isbrand of Harderwijk, bishop of Lidlum, used his talents well before he held his dignity, but once in office he was corrupted. He gave himself over to daily feasting and a life of pleasure. He also obtained the administration of the provostship of Bolsward, was afterwards deprived of it by the royal Senate, and then gave up the office of bishop. Being unequal to rendering accounts, he returned to Emden, then went to Frankfurt and afterwards to Cologne. Abandoned by his own people and struck by a pestilential air, he died. At his election as bishop, two days were spent drinking heavily in the very courtyard of the monastery, and the prayers offered to God, and the ceremonies solemn for that act, were disgraced by shameful drunkenness and disgraceful carousing. It is recorded in the commentaries that the prefect Arenberg and the royal Senate, and also Willem Lindanus himself, the commissary, already provoked by the luxury of the monastic colleges, secretly suggested that plan to Philip and offered the order an occasion for change. The same order, believing itself exempt from the Prince's authority, stubbornly defended its own right and laboured more vehemently to have the Frisian bishop removed.

units.la: Ipsos quoque Oldehovios, Nyehovios & D. Catharinæ presbyteros totumque Leovardiæ civitatis clerum, expensis Margaretæ, quas memoravi, litteris liberiùs respondisse, Philippoq; ac Margaretæ Gubernatrici promovendæ Sedis operam denegasse.
units.tr: The Oldehove and Nijehove canons and the presbyters of St Catherine's, together with the whole clergy of the city of Leeuwarden, answered more freely in the letters of Margaret which I have mentioned, and refused to help Philip and Margaret, the Governess, to advance the See.

units.la: Neque enim (respondebant) beneficia nostra, quæ possidemus, ab aliys, quam à Magistratu Oppidano, interveniente electione & collatione, accepimus. Cum ipsis enim societate ac nexu juncti sumus, neque fas est nobis fœderi inter nos inito, nisi de voluntate Rectorum civitatis, ac ipsorum provinciæ Ordinum, renuntiare. Aquibus cum beneficia, cum emolumenta nostra proveniant, rectè faciet Gubernatrix, si apud Philippum regem responsum hoc, velut à libertate profectum, excusaverit.
units.tr: For (they replied) we hold our benefices not from anyone but the magistrates of the town, through election and collation. We are bound to them by fellowship and tie, and it is not right for us to renounce the covenant we have made among ourselves without the consent of the rulers of the city and of the Orders of their province. Since our benefices and our income come from them, the Governess will do well to excuse this reply before King Philip, as coming from a love of liberty.

units.la: Quare ipsi quoque Ordinum Delegati, ne soli clero odium pararentur, ijsdem fere, sed nonnihil acerbioribus decretis responderunt.
units.tr: Therefore the delegates of the Orders also answered with nearly the same decrees, though somewhat more bitterly, so that the hatred would not fall on the clergy alone.

units.la: Convelli novæ Sedis instituto, violarique jura, & privilegia gentis, cui libertatem à majoribus pace belloque partam Carolus Cæsar, & Philippus non unâ passione asseruissent. Neque tantum jus patrium tolli, caeterum ex illâ rerum novitate tempestates nasciturac provinciæ exitiosas. Se quoque ipsos ex illis discordiis turbisque in odium Philippi regis incursuros. Atque hanc esse sibi mentem, hæc esse Decreta Ordinum, mandataque, non consentire in Episcopi introductionem.
units.tr: The establishment of a new See would overthrow, and the rights and privileges of a people would be violated, which Charles Caesar and Philip had not once asserted to have been won by our ancestors in peace and war. Not only would the native law be abolished, but from that novelty of affairs storms would arise, destructive to the province. They themselves would also be drawn into those discords and disturbances out of hatred of King Philip. This is their mind, these are the decrees and mandates of the Orders: they do not consent to the introduction of a bishop.

units.la: Cui rei cum Præses Senatusque regius multa objecissent, & ex re provinciæ esse, ut religio, & cum eâ pax servetur, & ne regis voluntati ac mandato quid decedat, quod per Brabantiam, Geldriam, Transisulaniam, Groningananm civitatem & Omlandiam valuisset, ita denuò à Frisijs repositum: Scire se quid Romæ actum foret, & quantum incommodi nova Episcoporum electio per ðtinas provincias daret. Neque posse se (ita enim retinebant) sine totius populi Frisici conventu, in hoc consentire, cuius interesset, aliquid mutare. Ita res in suspenso mansit, donec tandem horrore Albani nominis, & simul feritatis spreti regij decreti vindictâ inardescentis conterritus, populus Episcopum reciperet.
units.tr: When the President and the royal Senate had raised many objections to this, and argued that it was for the good of the province that religion, and with it peace, be preserved, and that nothing be lacking to the king's will and command, which had prevailed throughout Brabant, Gelderland, Overijssel, the city of Groningen and the Ommelanden, the Frisians again rejected it in these words: They knew what had been done at Rome, and how much harm the new election of bishops would bring to these provinces. They could not (for so they kept insisting) consent to this without a general assembly of the whole Frisian people, whose interest it was to change anything. So the matter remained in suspense, until at last the people, terrified by the dread of the name of Alva and at the same time by the threat of vengeance flaring from the scorned royal decree, received the bishop.

units.la: Tum libellus supplex à Frisijs ad Margaretam, & dein ad Philippum in Hispaniam missus, in quo de cædium homicidiorumq; impunitate, & frequentibus per Frisiam in fraudem creditorum cessionibus conquerebantur, contraq; juris Saxonici, quod Georgius sanxerat, institutum, omnium rerum licentiam lenitate Iudicum increscere. Quare Philippus, aut Philippi nomine Margareta Gubernatrix, invalescente homicidarum multitudine, quæ ne à propinquis quidem fusi sanguinis crimen pretio redimebat, jus ad Saxonicum recurri jussit, Frisijsque, ut clariora istius decreti aut legis documenta ederent, mandavit. Quod cum propter locorum intercapedinem, agente in Hispaniâ Philippo, maturè fieri non posset, Margareta Saxoniæ principis constitutionem exhiberi sibi petijt. Igitur extracto apud Margaretam negotio postulata quædam, quos ante delegatos monui, Carolo Nitzenio Præsidi, Petro Dekama, Alexio Gelio Senatoribus tradita, quo nautici æris exactiones in sinu Scolbakhico cessarent, & ut homicidijs cessionibusq; bonorum increscentibus paci publicæ, & commerciorum prosperitati subveniretur. His addebant, ut quinque præturis, quod Harlinganæ arcis Satrapa impedire dicebatur, jus suum salvum esset, liceretque aggerum præfecto omne lignum contabulationibus littorum destinatum, pro recepto more vacuis juxta portam fossamque marginibus inlocare. Præterea ut prædiorum Ecclesiasticorum fructus, vacante ministerio, reparandis pastorum ædificijs, aut patrono, aut pauperum usui cederent, nulliq; lacerdoti beneficium conduplicaretur. Tum de Prætorum, in quos acriter tum invectum, licentiâ avaritiâque coercendis quædam addita, postulatumque, ut quoniam regiæ populique pecuniæ exactores, quæstoresq; forent, autoritate Senatus reddendas ad rationes cogerentur. Postremo de judicijs illorum reformandis actum, ac ut Leppæo aggeri, qui Oostergoam ab inundationibus tuetur, reliquisq; per Opsteranos, Smallingios, Scoterlandos, & Anver-dios aggeribus praetores istorum distrićtuum prospiciant: Quibus ab Arembergio, Nitzenio, Dekama, & Gelio responsum, Scolbalchicum sinum, nunquam tonnis vasisq; ligneis quae vadosum mare indicarent, natatum fuisse, neq; regi id oneris incumbere, caeterum regem perspecto maris atq; aestuarij discrimine, & ne naves Doccumanorum &c. Harlingensium in syrtes impingerent, naufragijsq; exponerentur magna aeris impensa securitati navigantium subvenisse. Quam si reponere regij aerarij tribuno Frisij velint, daturos se operam, ut diploma apud Philippum super hac re impetrent, & ut ista nautici aeris solutione mercatorum res exonerentur. Quod ad caedium immanitatem, & cessionum fraudes attineret, scripturos ad Regem & Margaretam, facturosque ut Edictorum quae aetate Saxonum viguissent, ratio habeatur. Idem de Praetoribus aggerum Praefectis rescriptum, dissimulatis aut elevatis illorum vitiis, qui regiae, quam obibant, functionis praetextu, libertate, & fortuna populi abutebantur. Tum Doccumani ne quid asperius paterentur, salvo Collumanorum aliorumq; jure, certis sub conditionibus cum delegatis regij Senatus transegere, seq; in singulas navium lastas dimidium sestertium soluturos recepere. Sex-viri quoque quos redarguendo Philippi imperio, quotannis constitutos dixi, morte Gulielmi Hissij, & Hesseli Aysmae, Barthium Idzaerda, & Tiepconem Oenema Iureconsultos surrogavere, quo autoritatis dignitatisq; suae vis morte praedecessorum non solveretur, & ne illorum sollicitudines pervigiliaq; intermitterentur, qui refrenandae Philippi potentiae, & tuendis legibus destinabantur. Quare & adversus praetores regios, & imprimis Pelgromium Indichium Ferverdicum, Emconem Genchenium Smallingium, & Simkonem Duconium Idardium, validae accusationes institutae, eaeq; majore cum acrimonia repetitae corrupta affectibus indicia, & fædatam peculatu avaritiam proferebant. Caeterum regiae dominationis fiducia, & quasi Philippi consilia praescirent, etiam inter publicas criminum insimulationes, & vehementiam actorum rei convictiq; securitatem immunitatemq; profitebantur, acerbisq; injurijs, tanquam fortuna ac potentia regis validi, in omnem superbiam proterviamq; dicendi se effundebant. Ut certe communi discordiae viam praestruere acerbitas partium videretur, omnisq; judiciorum vis in infelicium armorum rabiem transitura. Unde prodigia, notante in commentarijs Cornelio Gemma, rursum hoc anno enata, caelumq; chasmate, & horrendo hiatu, quasi maria terrasq; hausturus videretur, deforme, annorum quoque tristes inclementias aperuit. Quippe gelu mense Decembri ortum, inclinante eodem, ita ferocivit, ut multis mortalium, imprimis pauperioribus, manus, pedes, ipsaq; genitalia procederent, praterq; hominum mortes armenta quoq; & aves acerrimo frigore extinguerentur. Scribit idem autor, annosas etiam nuces, pyros, persicas, moros, ficus, rosarum frutices, vitesque emarcuisse, magnamq; annonae caritatem ex injuria hybernae asperitatis subsecutam. Pestilentiam quoq;, velut compressis corporum poris ac impedita transpiratione, enatam, malumq; scorbuti (scelotycen & stomachacem) Frisijs solis popalare per vicinas quoq; regiones se sparsisse. Idem quoq; gelu
units.tr: Then a supplication was sent from the Frisians to Margaret, and afterwards to Philip in Spain, in which they complained of the impunity for murders and manslaughters, and of the frequent assignments of goods made throughout Friesland to defraud creditors. They also complained that, contrary to the Saxon law which Duke George had sanctioned, the licence of all things was growing through the leniency of the judges. Therefore Philip, or Margaret the Governess in Philip's name, as the number of murderers grew, since they did not even redeem the crime of spilt blood from their own kin for money, ordered recourse to be had to the Saxon law, and commanded the Frisians to publish clearer documents of that decree or law. Since this could not be done promptly, owing to the distance between the places while Philip was in Spain, Margaret asked to be shown the constitution of the Saxon prince. Therefore, after the business had been drawn out with Margaret, certain requests were presented, through the delegates I mentioned earlier, to Karel Nitzenius the President and to the councillors Pieter Dekama and Alexius Gelius, that the exactions of sea-money in the Zuiderzee should cease, and that public peace and the prosperity of commerce, with the increase of murders and assignments of goods, should be provided for. To these they added that the right of the five praetorships should be kept safe, though the governor of the Harlingen castle was said to obstruct it, and that the prefect of the dykes be allowed to place in the empty margins by the gate and the ditch all the timber destined for the planking of the shores, as had been customary. Further, that the revenues of the church estates, while a ministry was vacant, should go either to the patron or to the use of the poor for repairing the ministers' houses, and that no clergyman should hold two benefices. Then some measures were added for restraining the licence and greed of the praetors, against whom they now inveighed sharply, and it was requested that, since they were collectors of the royal and public money and treasurers, they should be compelled by the authority of the Senate to render their accounts. Finally, the reform of their courts was discussed, and that the praetors of these districts should look after the Leppa dyke, which guards Oostergo from floods, and the other dykes through the Opsterlanders, Smallingers, Schoterlanders and Anvers. To these things Arenberg, Nitzenius, Dekama and Gelius replied that the Zuiderzee, a shallow sea, had never been navigable except by tuns and wooden vessels, and that this burden did not fall on the king. Rather, the king, having observed the danger of the sea and its sandbanks, and lest the ships of the Dokkum and Harlingen men should run aground on the shoals and be wrecked, had come to the aid of the safety of sailors at great expense to the treasury. If the Frisians wished to restore that money to the royal treasurer, they themselves would take care to obtain a charter from Philip on this matter, so that merchants' goods might be relieved of the sea-money payment. As for the monstrous slaughters and the frauds in assignments, they would write to the King and Margaret and see that the edicts that had been in force in the time of the Saxons were taken into account. A similar reply was given concerning the praetors, the prefects of the dykes, whose faults were overlooked or lightened, those who abused the freedom and fortunes of the people under the pretext of the royal office they held. Then the Dokkumers, so that they should suffer nothing harsher, agreed, saving the rights of the Collumers and others, to certain terms with the delegates of the royal Senate, and undertook to pay half a sestertium for each last of ships. The six men also, whom I said were appointed each year to resist the will of Philip, were replaced after the death of Willem Hissius and Hessel Aysma by the jurists Barthius Idzaerda and Tiepco Oenema, so that the force of their authority and dignity would not be dissolved by the death of their predecessors, and so that the anxieties and vigils of those who were destined to curb Philip's power and defend the laws would not lapse. Therefore strong accusations were brought against the royal praetors, and above all against Pelgrom Indichius of Ferwerd, Emcon Genchenius of Smallingerland and Simon Duconius of Idaarderadeel, and these charges, repeated with greater bitterness, set out evidence corrupted by partisan feelings and avarice stained by embezzlement. Moreover, trusting in royal authority and as if they foreknew Philip's plans, even amid the public accusations of crimes and the vehemence of the proceedings, the accused and convicted claimed security and immunity, and in harsh insults, as if relying on the fortune and power of a strong king, they poured themselves out in every kind of arrogance and insolence of speech. So that the bitterness of the parties seemed to pave the way for common discord, and all the force of the courts was about to pass into the frenzy of unhappy arms. Hence prodigies, which Cornelius Gemma notes in his commentaries, arose again this year, and the sky opened with a gap and a dreadful yawning, as if it would swallow up seas and lands, and it also revealed the grim harshness of the years. Indeed a frost that began in December grew so fierce towards its end that the hands, feet and even the private parts of many mortals, especially of the poorer sort, were lost, and beyond human deaths, herds and birds were also killed by the most bitter cold. The same author writes that even ancient walnut, pear, peach and mulberry trees, fig trees, rose bushes and vines withered, and that a great dearth of grain followed the harm of the harsh winter. A pestilence also arose, as if the pores of the bodies were closed and perspiration impeded, and the evil of scurvy (called scelotyce and stomachace) spread among the Frisians alone and also through the neighbouring regions.

units.la: Aprilem usq; in mensem & adultum ver protractum agricolarum labores & simul spem anni conturbasse. Tum Hesselus Aysma defuncti patruelis Ordinum Delegatorum cura recensendo Annalium operi, quod ex Saxonum Caroliq; actis Kempo Martenā vir nobilis concinnaverat, delectus, ne memoria priorum temporum interiret, & ut scirent posteri quantum inter antiquam gentis nostrae libertatem, ab Imperatoribus Regibusq; religiose habitam, & Saxonum Caroliq; dominationem interesset. Quam cum aut potentum assentatio, qui aulae honores ac simul opes ab imperatoria aut principali indulgentia affectabant, aut patientia percussi Caesaris majestate populi peperisset, ita erant, qui in priscae libertatis recordationem se reflecterent, acriorisque imperij, quam libertas ferre posset, metuentes vindicias indecentis regni ab ipsa inermium actorum fide requirerent.
units.tr: The unusually cold weather lasted until April and into a full spring, which upset the farmers' labours and their hopes for the year. Then Hesselus Aysma, a cousin of the late Aysma and one of the Delegates of the Estates, was chosen to review the work of the Annals, which the noble Kempo Martena had put together from the records of the Saxons and of Charles. He was to do this so that the memory of earlier times would not perish, and so that posterity would know how far apart were the ancient freedom of our people, which emperors and kings had respected, and the rule of the Saxons and of Charles. Flattery of the powerful, who sought court honours and wealth from imperial or princely favour, and the patience of a people struck down by the majesty of Caesar, had produced that situation. Yet there were some who turned back to remember their old liberty, and who, fearing a government harsher than freedom could bear, sought to justify the rights of an unbecoming kingdom from the very faithfulness of the unarmed records.

units.la: Traditum libris Editorum Provinciae reperio, Anglos inter Philippique subditos litem tum ortam, Philippumq; agente in humanis Maria conjuge Anglorum societate usum, ita populi Anglici aut Elisabethae reginae actionibus offensum, eandem tum rescidisse. Querebatur namque Philippus Belgicam gentem suae tutelae commissam, & commercia cum Anglis exercentem per Angliae regnum novis oneribus exactionibusque gravari, conventionesque inter Belgicae Principem & Anglorum regem jam ante initas, novo illius regni statuto infringi. Elisabetham quippe jam ante regio Edicto caviisse; Ne Belgae merces, & simul opificia in Angliam perferrent, caeterum commercijs ejusdem regni abstinerent. Addebat Philippus intutum Belgicis mercatoribus fretum Anglicum fuisse, Elisabethamq; reginam spreta Legatorum actione, & aequissimis conditionibus alio consilia vertisse. Et quoniam subditorum suorum non alia postulata essent, quam ut simili jure, quo Angli per Belgicam, ipsi in eodem regno fruantur, ita molestius ferre suorum subditorum jure imminuto commercia impediri, aut alio terrarum transferri. Ita Anglos pannorum forum e Belgica in fines Imperij Embdam transtulisse, non alio consilio, quam ut fortuna Belgicae gentis decresceret, & infida diu societas nova lite laxaretur. Quapropter velle ut Anglorum regno Frisij excedant, abstineantque similiter, dum Edictum Elisabetha rescindat, natāq; ex hac causa lites per arbitros dirimantur. Interea vetare, ne panni Anglici in Frisia recipiantur, vendanturve, quin econtra statuere, ut recepti, ac veno positi fisco cedant. Litterae Margaretae Gubernatricis iv. Kalend. Aug. Bruxellis in Frisiam missae, ac Leovardiae iii. Eid. publicatae. Constat ex ijsdem litteris, grassantem tum per Angliam luem atq; pestilentiam edictum promovisse, suspectisq; Anglorum mercibus, & negotiantium halitu commercia retardata. Tum repulsae Episcopalis injuriam tanquam contemptum imperij sui ulturus Philippus, litteras minarum plenas ad Margaretam Gubernatricem dedit, quibus severa jussa recipiendae Inquisitionis, & Concilij Tridentini continebantur. Quare Margareta convocato Status Belgici Senatu, ne quid clam haberet, litteras Philippi exhibuit, quas diversi, prout cuiusque animus, aut ingenium erat, dubijs illis asperisque temporibus variè interpretabantur. Erant, qui publicanda ocyus per Provincias Philippi decreta censerent, suadentibus econtra prudentioribus, & inter eos Viglio Zuichemo, differendam decretorum promulgationem esse, donec Senatus Belgicus de Provinciarum statu ad Philippum retulisset. Alij addunt Viglium Zuichemum, si quod è prolatatione rei incommodum, regiæve iræ periculum resultaret, id omne in se recepisse, præsentemq; Margareta sponsionem obtulisse. Cæterum Viglij salubre, & amans publicæ pacis consilium per aliorum suffragia evictum tum fuit. Itaq; laxata malis fræna, ac Margareta Gubernatrix xiii. Kal. Ian. litteras ocyus in Frisios perscripsit, quibus significabat: Velle Philippum suis de Religione Edictis populum parere. Monere quoque oppidanos Magistratus, ut sub poenâ in ijsdem Edictis comprehensâ è Senatorum Scabinorumve numero singulis trimestribus unum edant, eique potestatem faciant Concilij Tridentini Decreta sarta tecta curandi. Scribit Vir Clarissimus Abelus Franckena in Historicis suis fragmentis, Tridentinum Concilium à Paulo iii. Pontifice Tridenti ad Athesim flumen cæptum, ut omnium per Germaniam, ita Belgicam motuum matrem extitisse, Carolumque & mox Philippum reverentiâ procerum eiusdem Concilij tanquam inspiratione numinum actos, Perennottis patre & filio impulsoribus, omnem civilis imperij Legem, atque rationem neglexisse.
units.tr: I find it recorded in the books of the Editors of the Province that a quarrel then arose between the English and the subjects of Philip, and that while Philip was still alive, through his wife Mary, he had used the alliance with the English. Being offended by the actions of Queen Elizabeth and of the English people, he then broke it off. Philip complained that the Belgian nation, entrusted to his protection and carrying on trade with the English, was burdened through the English kingdom by new charges and levies, and that agreements between the Prince of Belgium and the King of England, made long before, were being broken by a new statute of that kingdom. Indeed Elizabeth had already provided, by royal edict, that the Belgians should not carry their goods and workmanship into England, and that they should otherwise abstain from the trade of that kingdom. Philip added that the English Channel had been unsafe for Belgian merchants, and that Queen Elizabeth, having ignored the action of the envoys and offered most fair terms, had turned her plans elsewhere. Since his subjects asked for nothing else than the same right by which the English enjoyed the use of Belgium, they were the more aggrieved that their commerce, with its rights diminished, should be hindered or moved to other lands.
