Worn down by delay and shortage of food, and broken afterwards by a mutiny of the soldiers (who had stained their hands with the murder of their prefect), he withdrew into Germany, and bore his own fortune, and that of his brother Louis, with the steadfastness of a prince. Then, after the battle of Jemmingen was fought, the forces were again drawn back into their garrisons, and ten cohorts of infantry, under the command of Ægydius Barlamontius Hyergius, marched through the town of Leeuwarden and its outlying places. Three cohorts also of the Walloon people spent the night at Leeuwarden, and the next day, sent off into Transfrisia, drove away from the doubtful town the anxiety that was then peculiar to it. Then, on the day before the Nones of August, a day of thanksgiving for Alva's victory at Jemmingen was appointed throughout all Friesland, and the names of those who had followed the party of Louis of Nassau in that war were reported to the royal senate. Thus prosperous and adverse matters were mingled and flowed up and down through Friesland, and the war, changeable and uncertain in its outcome, dragged on, its strength gradually growing. That Philip's spirit, long exasperated, had taken on greater hatreds in proportion to this great affair, the most sorrowful examples in Spain itself, and the deaths of the envoys he had ordered, showed. For all report affirmed that John, Marquis of Berg, was nearly consumed by imprisonment and a disorder of mind, and was afterwards killed by poison; and that Florent de Montmorency, having tried in vain to escape, was struck down by the sword at Segovia, and so fulfilled the unhappy fate of an envoy. This deed brought the worst reputation through all Europe and the courts of kings. Clearly it was left to Philip, after so many thousands had been shed in the provinces, and princes slaughtered, with every right, and soon also the rights of nations, violated, to add the murder of the envoys themselves. Presently a rumour spreading through Friesland, added to so many sad tidings, announced the death of Don Carlos, Prince of Spain. It was believed that, by his secret conferences with his stepmother, and then by his more familiar association with the Belgian envoys, the Marquis of Berg and Montigny, he had given rise to suspicion of an inclination toward the Netherlands, and had, being averse to his father Philip's harsher rule, devised a safer and milder remedy for settling the civil disturbances.

units.la: Borræus addit eum ab inimicis & paternæ aulæ assentatoribus fugæ aut similis consilij insimulatum, ac si per secreta cum Aurantio Principe literarum officiorumque commercia arripiendi per Belgicam, Principatus cogitationem cæpisset. Certè verisimile est, Carolum Principem in vigore ævi constitutum, nuperæque quo minus in Belgicam cum imperio iret, repulsæ haud oblitum, dignas filio regio curas agitasse, quibus inlatæ contumeliæ labem, æmulationesque inimicorum principe irâ, & opportunis vindicijs ulcisceretur. Cæterum Caroli arcanum per excusa, jussu patris, scrinia detectum infælici eum exitu, & juxta regiam domum magno infortunio multavit. Quippe severo patris imperio in carcerem datus, duriusq;, quam Principem filiumq; decebat, habitus incerto fine vitam clausit. Multi credidere eum fractâ per nervum gulâ, aut quod verius duxerim, lento veneno, ac mærore animi (nam utrumque tradunt) extenuatum, inlatumque præfervido balneo ruptis exolutisque venis exspirasse. Elisabetha Vallesia Philippi uxor, Caroli noverca, intellectâ (quo cum consuetudinem stupri habuisse Philippus suspicabatur) privigni cæde, dubium, suo an alieno jussu extincta. Ita regia Philippi domus duplicis parricidij non obscura suspicione fædata.
units.tr: Borrhaeus adds that he was charged by his enemies and by the flatterers of his father's court with flight, or with a similar design: that through secret correspondence and dealings with the Prince of Orange he had begun to plan to seize the government of the Netherlands. Certainly it is likely that Prince Carlos, being in the vigour of his years, and not forgetting the recent rebuff by which he was prevented from going to the Netherlands with authority, was turning over cares worthy of a royal son, by which he might avenge the stain of the insults offered him and the rivalries of his enemies with princely anger and fitting punishments. However, Carlos's secret plans were uncovered by the opening of his writing-cases, done by his father's order, and this brought him to an unhappy end and punished him with great misfortune within the royal house. Indeed, placed in prison by his father's harsh command, and treated more harshly than became a prince and a son, he ended his life, uncertain of its outcome. Many believed that he died by the cutting of the gullet by a sinew, or, as I think more likely (for both are reported), that he was worn away by slow poison and grief of mind, and that, when he was put into a very hot bath, he expired with his veins burst and loosened. Elisabeth of Valois, wife of Philip and stepmother of Carlos, having learned of her stepson's death (since Philip suspected she had an illicit affair with him), died, it is uncertain whether by her own command or another's. Thus the royal house of Philip was defiled by a suspicion, not obscure, of a double parricide.

units.la: Reperio in libris Editorum Frisiæ, Philippum Albanum, qui ad Trajectum Mosæ castra tum tenebat, VI. Kal. Iul. de morte Caroli perscripsisse, Carolumque poenitudine suæ imbecillitatis ductum, post applicata ei morientium solemnia, gloriosō & pio exitu decessisse. Philippi quoque jussu principi umbræ per omnem Frisiam ad v. Non. Octob. diem supplicationes decretas, Caroliqué exequias VIII. LXVIII.
units.tr: I find in the books of the Frisian editors that Philip, who then held his camp at Maastricht on the Meuse, wrote about the death of Carlos on the 26th of June, and that Carlos, moved by regret for his weakness, departed with a glorious and pious end, after the solemn rites for the dying were applied to him. By Philip's order, also, thanksgivings for the prince's shade were decreed throughout all Friesland until the 3rd of October, and the funeral rites of Carlos VIII. LXVIII.

units.la: Neq; Ferdinandus Albanus Iemminghanâ victoriâ ac prosperitate fortunæ elatior à statuendis quoq; immanibus exemplis cessabat. Quippe post præclaros per Brabantiam necatos viros, Culenborgiorum Comitum palatium quod Bruxellis visebatur, ob pactum in eo (de quo dixi) Fœdus, ac conventus Principum habitos, dirui jussit, & ut ipse in conscientijs non tantum temporum, sed & monumentis quoque perennaret, poni curavit hoc ipsum cum inscriptione:
units.tr: Nor did Ferdinand Alva, more lifted up by his victory at Jemmingen and the prosperity of his fortune, cease from setting up cruel examples. Indeed, after the distinguished men had been put to death throughout Brabant, he ordered the palace of the Counts of Culemborg, which stood at Brussels, to be pulled down, because of the covenant made in it (of which I have spoken) and the assemblies of the princes held there; and, so that he himself might endure in the memory not only of the times but also of monuments, he had this very thing set up with an inscription:

units.la: REGNANTE PHILIPPO II. CATHOLICO HISPANIARUM REGE, IN HÆREDITARIIS BELGII PROVINCIIS GUBER- NATORE FERDINANDO ALVARES TOLETANO, DUCE AL- VÆ, MARCHIONE CORIAE, &c. DECRETUM FLORENTII PAL- LANTIS, COMITIS CULEN- BURGII PALATIUM, PROPTER DETESTANDAM IN EO CONIV- ERATIONEM HABITAM, ADVER- SUS ROM. CATHOL. RELIG. RE- GEM HISPANIARUM, STATUMQUE BELGII, SOLO ÆQUANDUM.
units.tr: IN THE REIGN OF PHILIP II, CATHOLIC KING OF SPAIN, WITH FERDINAND ALVAREZ OF TOLEDO, DUKE OF ALBA, MARQUIS OF CORIA, ETC., AS GOVERNOR OF THE HEREDITARY PROVINCES OF BELGIUM: BY DECREE OF FLORENCE PALLANT, THE PALACE OF THE COUNT OF CULEMBORG, BECAUSE OF THE CONSPIRACY HELD WITHIN IT AGAINST THE ROMAN CATHOLIC RELIGION, THE KING OF SPAIN AND THE STATE OF BELGIUM, IS TO BE LEVELLED TO THE GROUND.

units.la: Deïn ne vestigia fœderis ullibi cernerentur, eiusque memoriam deleret necatis autoribus, omnes fœderi adscriptos qui in Erisiâ permanserant, VIII. Kal. Sept. edicto Antverpiam evocavit, intraq; trigesimum diem ad dicendam causam adesse jussit. In eorum numero, qui citati erant, Deitzius Wingia, Watzo Aylva, Wigerus Eelsma, Titus Hettingha, Tiepco Goslingha, Tetardus Iellersma, Taco Galama, Sixtus Emingha, Schelto Tiarda, Sixtus Donia, Scipio Meckama, Serapius Galama, Ridco Hysingha, Otto Herama, Oeno Grovensteinius, Lasius Heringa, Iorritius Hania, Upco Burmania, Edo Abbema, Idzardus Douma, Gellius Ridderma, Ioannes Bonga, Hesselus Emingha, Oeno Heringha, Horatius Unia, Ielto Eelsma, Gemma Burmania, Ægydius Iacobæus, Fredericus Offenhusanus, Franciscus Gerritius, Foppius Douma, Focco Eysingha, Erasmus Douma, Edo Gerbranda, Douwo Douma, Botto Emingha, Atteius Fernia, Alephus Iaersma, Aggæus Ofingha, & Auco Unia fuere. Quos omnes asperitate fori, & magnitudine periculi deterritos, Fecconem Rhalam, & Georgium Godefridum in suprema Curia causarum patronos Antverpiam misisse; qui suo nomine responderent, patriæ Historiæ jam ante scriptor Bernardus Furmerius annotavit. Mox Frisicæ Nobilitatis clarorumque virorum nomina pro rostris recitata, damnatăq; à Senatu Regio, & quo in populum exirent, templorum valuis, locisque publicis affixa, per omne Provinciæ Tribunal strepuere. Ita Epæo Doumæ, Francisco Eysinghæ, Wilconi Holdingæ, Piboni Haerdæ, Hommio Hettinghæ, Hesselo Oosthemio, Wigero Eelimæ, Siuckio Eminghæ, Foppio Camstræ, Deitzio Wingiæ, Epæo Bootsmæ, Douwoni Glinzio, Renico Gerlacio, Francisco Hugenio, Menenio Sceltamæ, Hesselo Feitzmæ Hufumano, & Hesselo Feytzmæ Peinsio, Edoni Heringhæ, Tarquinio Vallesio, Allæo Teiesio, Henrico Albartio, Petro Petræo, Gerardo Florentio, Focconi Aysmæ, Gabinio Selsmæ, Gualtero Coquillano, Ioanni Symonio, Sibrando Sibrandio, Cornelio Cornelij, Siboldo Aysmæ, Iepponi & Suffrido Vrielsmæ, Theodoro Gulielmio, Leoni Symonio, & Tiberio Oenamæ Iureconsultis, Ebeo Tinckenio, Carolo Roordæ, Siricio Fungero Iureconf. & Cornelio Fonckio ærarij Tribuno sarcina sædi in Regem criminis impositā, hominesque innocentiæ perfugium, & secretum tutioris vitæ extra patriam captantes, ne quid illorum miseriæ deesset, in ipsâ patriâ per Philippi Senatum damnati sunt. Alij codices Iulium Heringam, Ioannem Bongam, Oenonem Heringam, Ielsonem Eelsmam, Ægidium Iacobi virum consularem, Alefum Aggeniam, Gulielmum Bongam, Tiallengum Eysingam LL. Doctorem, Franciscum Hemmium, & Doconem Tetlæum Iureconsultos, Everardum Arckenium, Herconem Ruardum, Ludolphum Nautam, Theodorum Emskerckium, Ludolphum Sartorium, Petrum Textorium, Leonem Haniam ICum, Popconem Roordam, Popponem Aggæum, Aggæum Henricium, Thomam Chirurgum cæterosque addidere, eosdemque feralibus proscriptionum tabulis per Frisiam circumlatos sui in patriam studij iniquum præmium reportasse. Nobiles quoque, Consulares, & patritiæ fæminæ, ut maritorum fortunæ, ita exilij consortes eâdem lege damnatæ, conjugalis lecti societate communem cum maritis injuriam sustinuere. Ita per arma, & simul judiciorum metus oppresso fædere, plenam inter securitatem Ferdinandus Albanus agebat. Qui propterea, excusa omnis adversæ fortunæ curâ, more mortalium, fælicium prœliorum, & simul enormis sævitiæ gloriam duraturis monumentis consecrare aggressus, de erigendo sibi Trophæo cogitavit, quod ex merito bellorum, & pacatæ Belgicæ se consequutum opinabatur. Quare per omnes Provincias, ut & Frisios, publicas supplicationes indixit, ut extruendo quisq; monumento fœdæ Tyranni famæ votum nuncuparet. Theatrales quoq; ludi alibi locorum instituti, gymnasticaeq; concertationes concurrentium velut in pugnâ, militum triumphis atque ovationibus immistæ. units.tr: So that no traces of the covenant might be seen anywhere, and to wipe out its memory once its instigators had been put to death, he summoned by edict to Antwerp on 25 August all those enrolled in the covenant who had persisted in heresy, and ordered them to appear within thirty days to plead their cause. Among those cited were Deitzius Wingia, Watzo Aylva, Wigerus Eelsma, Titus Hettingha, Tiepco Goslingha, Tetardus Iellersma, Taco Galama, Sixtus Emingha, Schelto Tiarda, Sixtus Donia, Scipio Meckama, Serapius Galama, Ridco Hysingha, Otto Herama, Oeno Grovensteinius, Lasius Heringa, Iorritius Hania, Upco Burmania, Edo Abbema, Idzardus Douma, Gellius Ridderma, Ioannes Bonga, Hesselus Emingha, Oeno Heringha, Horatius Unia, Ielto Eelsma, Gemma Burmania, Ægydius Iacobæus, Fredericus Offenhusanus, Franciscus Gerritius, Foppius Douma, Focco Eysingha, Erasmus Douma, Edo Gerbranda, Douwo Douma, Botto Emingha, Atteius Fernia, Alephus Iaersma, Aggæus Ofingha, and Auco Unia. Daunted by the harshness of the court and the magnitude of the danger, all of them sent Fecco Rhala and Georgius Godefridus, advocates of the supreme court, to Antwerp to answer in their name; the earlier historian of our country, Bernardus Furmerius, has already noted this. Soon the names of the Frisian nobility and of famous men were read out from the rostra, condemned by the Royal Senate, and affixed to the doors of churches and to public places so that they might be cast out among the people; and they resounded through every tribunal of the province. Thus Epaeus Douma, Francisco Eysingha, Wilconus Holdingha, Pibo Haerda, Hommius Hettingha, Hesselus Oosthemius, Wigerus Eelima, Siuckius Eminga, Foppius Camstra, Deitzius Wingia, Epaeus Bootsma, Douwo Glinzius, Renicus Gerlacius, Franciscus Hugenius, Menenius Sceltama, Hesselus Feitzma of Hufum, and Hesselus Feytzma of Peins, Edo Heringha, Tarquinius Vallesius, Allaeus Teiesius, Henricus Albartius, Petrus Petraeus, Gerardus Florentius, Focco Aysma, Gabinius Selsma, Gualterus Coquillanus, Ioannes Symonius, Sibrandus Sibrandius, Cornelius Cornelii, Siboldus Aysma, Ieppo and Suffridus Vrielsma, Theodorus Gulielmius, Leo Symonius, and Tiberius Oenama, jurists; Ebeus Tinckenius, Carolus Roorda, Siricius Fungerus, jurist, and Cornelius Fonckius, tribune of the treasury, were charged with the stain of crime against the King. Since they sought refuge in innocence and a safer, secret life outside their homeland, they were condemned in their own country by the senate of Philip, so that nothing of their misery should be lacking. Other lists added Iulius Heringa, Ioannes Bonga, Oeno Heringa, Ielso Eelsma, Ægidius Iacobi, a man of consular rank, Alefus Aggenia, Gulielmus Bonga, Tiallengus Eysinga, Doctor of Laws, Franciscus Hemmius, and Doco Tetlaeus, jurists; Everardus Arckenius, Hercon Ruardus, Ludolphus Nauta, Theodorus Emskerckius, Ludolphus Sartorius, Petrus Textor, Leo Hania, jurist, Popco Roorda, Poppo Aggaeus, Aggaeus Henricius, Thomas the surgeon, and others, and they carried these men through Friesland on the deadly tablets of proscription, bringing back an unjust reward for their zeal for their country. Noble women too, of consular and patrician rank, were condemned under the same law as their husbands' fortunes and fellow exiles, and shared with their husbands the common injury of the marriage bed. Thus, with the covenant crushed by arms and at the same time by fear of the courts, Ferdinand of Alva carried on in full security. Therefore, having dismissed all anxiety about adverse fortune, he set about consecrating, in the manner of mortals, the glory of his successful battles and of his monstrous cruelty in lasting monuments, and he planned to erect a trophy for himself, which he believed he had won by the merit of his wars and the pacified Belgium. Accordingly he proclaimed public thanksgivings through all the provinces, the Frisians included, so that each man might vow to contribute to a monument to the foul tyrant's fame. Theatrical games were also staged in various places, and gymnastic contests in which the competitors fought as in battle, mingled with the triumphs and ovations of the soldiers. Scarcely able to contain his good fortune and prosperity, he ordered a trophy to be set up for himself, cast of solid captured bronze (for it was thought fitting to add this) by the sculptor's art, with a proud inscription:

units.la: FERDINANDO ALVAREZ à TO- LEDO, ALBÆ DUCI, PHILIPPI II. HISPANIARUM REGIS APUD BELGAS PRÆFECTO, QUOD EXTINCTA SEDITIONE, REBELLIBUS PVLSIS, REL.IG. PROCVR. IVSTIT. CVLTA. PACEM FIRMARIT, REGIS OPTUMI MINISTRO FIDELISSIMO POS.
units.tr: FERDINAND ALVAREZ OF TOLEDO, DUKE OF ALBA, GOVERNOR AMONG THE BELGIANS FOR PHILIP II, KING OF SPAIN, WHO, THE SEDITION BEING ENDED AND THE REBELS DRIVEN OUT, ESTABLISHED PEACE BY ENFORCING RELIGION AND JUSTICE; A MOST FAITHFUL MINISTER OF THE BEST OF KINGS, HAS SET THIS UP.

units.la: Quod monumentum ex æneis, ut multi putant, Ludovici Nassovij, quæ ad Iemmingham in Frisijs reliquerat, tormentis formatum, magnam ei invidiam paravit. Erant namque, qui arrogantis, & supra fortunam se habentis ingenii id factum interpretarentur, Ferdinandum Albanum, velut humanæ sortis oblitum, statuam æneam fallaci, & non stabili gloriæ, temerario & superbo consilio non prævisâ futuri adversitate consecrasse. Fluxas quippe & caducas rerum humanarum vices esse, nec eodem semper loco stare hominis fortunam, prosperis, ut plurimum, adversa miscentem. Idcirco XIII. Kal. Ian. grates, per omnem Frisiam Albani successibus in templis actæ, Trophæumque Duci velut debellatis partibus erectum, minuendæ invidiæ publicâ supplicatione cohonestatum est. Etiam ne per Frisiam novæ partes surgerent, (quæ haud procul Monachozilâ in Translavicanis à fugâ Ludovici Nassovij parabantur) litteræ Senatus Regii ad Prætores Grietmannorve per omnem Oostergoam datæ, quibus suorum finium curam gerere submovendis trans Lavicam Fæderatorum copijs jubebantur. Itaque campanum æs per confines Lavicæ annii Præturas pultatum, adactaque, ad sacramentum rusticâ plebe, dispositæ excubiæ ad claudendos viarum aditus stetêre. Ferdinandus quoque Albanus Nobiles Fæderatosij, Frisios ad VIII. Kal. Sept. jam ante Antverpiam evocatos, denuò citari per Edictum fecit, judiciumque subterfugientibus extrema pænarum denuntiavit. Creditores quoque, & hypothecarios actiones in res bonaque exulum habentes, intra decimum quartumque diem Ioanni Carolo Fisci advocato exhibere obligationum suarum tabulas jussit, repetitisque per mensium intervalla confiscationum edictis solitudinem provinciæ paravit. Quare ejectis Frisia fæderis socijs ut animos cæterorum quoque domaret, primarias civitates trans ac cis Lavicam, Leovardiam atque Groningam, cæteraque per Frisiam oppida validis præsidijs obsepsit, quæ conterrendis ijsdem provincialibus in omnem lasciviam, atque insolentiam nullo coercente effundebantur. Ablegatis namque in Transisulaniam quatuor Germanorum cohortibus, quas Groningæ post Iemminganam pugnam reliquerat, Gasparum Roblesium hominem Lusitanum, legionis Valonicæ Præfectum, cum VI. signis præsidio urbi esse jussit, eandemque gravi mille & ducentorum aureorum in singulas septimanas tributo assignandis militi stipendijs exhausit. Post Magistratum omnem annuum ante edicto perpetuum fecit, corrigendisque per universam Frisiam (quæ Hle-vo Amasoq; clauditur) fœderatis, Carolum Quarræum virum equestris ordinis, & Brabantinæ Curiæ Senatorem, in Frisios amandavit. Qui confecto Leovardiæ, ob quod venerat, negotio, factaque Ioanni Carolo cognitori regio inquirendi potestate, Groningam properavit, sumendisque supplicijs se dedit. Quod duri judicis officium perdomandæ gentis Frisicæ, ac Translavicani populi contumaciæ repertum nulli dubitabant. Tum de Elisabethæ Vallesiæ Philippi conjugis morte, fama in Frisiam perlata, confirmataque litteris Concilij Status Belgici continua tristium exemplorum nuntia ex Hispaniæ aulâ & Philippi domo vulgavit. Quamobrem ad vii. Eid. Ian. dies Elisabethæ exequijs per Frisiam præfinitus, imperatumque à Philippo, ut solemnia funeris, & apparatus pompæ anteactis Caroli Principis exequijs convenirent. Ut scilicet privignum & novercam à suspicione perpetrati incestûs non immunes, ut violentæ mortis, ita exequiarum communio esset, tragicij; regiæ stirpis exitus ijsdem officijs, & haud dispari fine signarentur. Tradit Everardus Reidanus scriptor eximius nimiam illam novercæ cum privigno familiaritatem fœdæ & secretæ consuetudinis non leve indicium fuisse, Elisabethamque Vallesiam virilis sexus fœtum immaturo, & quinquemestri partu ope medicantium, velut discutiendis uteri obstructionibus, clâm enixam, materiem sinistræ suspicioni præbuisse. Insolens namque & à lege artis alienum videbatur, fœminam utero gerentem, provectâ & jam vitali embrionis mole, sectionibus venarum, & purgantium pharmacorum exponi, motisque aut vacuatis corporis infirmi contentis, & fluxili humorum materie per violentas revulsiones vim visceribus inferri. Mox Ioannes Knyffius vir patritij apud Ultrajectinos sanguinis, profundæ eruditionis ac eximiæ autoritatis vir, Groningam missus, habitaque longâ cum Wittewerumano, mox Adoardico Præsule contentione, quod opulenta cænobia & jam temporum vitijs soluta luxu, suæ doti adjiceret in possessionem Groninganæ Sedis immissus est. Tradunt autores Knijffium antistitem modeste imperio suo usum, ducendisque populi animis validum flagrante apud Translavicanos gratiâ viguisse, factaque cum Abbate Morimontio (quem Cisterciensis Adoardici sumptibus quoq; Clarecampensium Præsulis Burgundiæ evocaverant) transactione annuam sex millium pensionem impetrasse. Apud Frisios verò, ut nuper Margareta Gubernatrice, ita illud negotium hoc quoque tempore de voluntate eorum protractum, qui Anno cIↄ. Iↄ. LXIV. patrio juri ac libertati adversum, publico decreto pronuntiaverant. Quare Ferdinandus Albanus erectæ apud Groningam Sedis exemplo, tum præfractis populi moribus impulsus litteras in Frisiam dedit, in quibus, ut locum facerent Episcopo, severè hortabatur. Prolatam diu quippe rem pietati gentis & juxta saluti dicatam aiebat, hominesque publicè inquietos, velut in licentiæ regno, immodestis moribus & solutiore vitâ usos reverentiam excussisse Romanæ Sedi, & juxta Carolo Cæsari à majoribus tributam. Quod malum quia divinum omne atque humanum temerasset, clero etiam ipso per ubertrina otia in luxum atq; supersuperbiam prolapso', disciplinâ opus esse, quâ animorum illi morbi coërceantur, & in viam redeant humanæ mentes in devia errorum nimiâ licentia effusæ. Et quoniam antiquæ Ecclesiæ morbis non alio remedio quam ordinationibus Episcoporum, Censorumque subventum fuisset, ita rectè & prudenter Paulum, & Pios Pontifices Romanos cavisse, ut Provinciæ Belgicæ, quas frequentia populi ac commerciorum fortunâ ad magnitudinem rerum & simul vitiorum extulisset, crescente per prospera pravitate plures quoque Episcopi ordinarentur, Friscæque genti multâ cænobiorum opulentia, & cleri otio in lubidinem ac luxum effuso, Cunerus' Præsul decerneretur. Quare ne Philippi regis autoritati, ac sanctionibus Romanorum Pontificum quid decedat, hortari se, ac munitum mandato regio jubere, ut eundem Antistitem Frisij recipiant, & quidem ocyus, pareantque ei è formulâ ac præscripto Episcopalium tabularum, quas ipso Sedis natali in conventu Ordinum Frisiæ exhibiturus esset.
units.tr: This monument, which many believed was cast from the bronze cannon that Louis of Nassau had left at Jemmingen in Friesland, brought him great hatred. For there were some who interpreted the deed as the work of a proud mind that presumed too much on its fortune: they said that Ferdinand of Alba, as if forgetful of the human lot, had with a rash and arrogant plan dedicated a bronze statue to a false and unstable glory, not foreseeing the coming reversal. Indeed, the changes of human affairs are fleeting and transient, and a man's fortune does not always stand in the same place, since prosperity is mostly mixed with adversity. For this reason, on 19 December, thanksgivings for Alba's successes were offered in the churches throughout Friesland, and the trophy, erected as if the provinces had been subdued, was honoured with a public supplication, so as to lessen the hatred. Also, so that new factions should not rise up in Friesland (which were being prepared not far from Makkum among the people beyond the Lauwers, after Louis of Nassau's flight), letters of the royal Senate were sent to the praetors and to the Grietmen throughout Oostergo, by which they were ordered to take care of their own borders by keeping the forces of the Confederates out beyond the Lauwers. And so the bell of the district was rung along the borders of the Lauwers, and the rural population was bound to an oath; guards were posted to close the approaches of the roads. Ferdinand of Alba also had the nobles and the Frisians of the Confederacy, who had already been summoned to Antwerp by 6 August, cited again by edict, and he announced the extreme penalties to those who evaded trial. He also ordered creditors and those holding mortgage claims on the goods and property of the exiles to present the records of their obligations to John Charles, the advocate of the treasury, within fourteen days, and by repeating the confiscation edicts at intervals of several months he brought about the desolation of the province. Therefore, when the allies of Friesland had been expelled, to subdue the minds of the rest too he fortified the chief cities on both sides of the Lauwers, Leeuwarden and Groningen, and the other towns of Friesland, with strong garrisons, since the inhabitants, terrified by these measures, were pouring out into every licence and insolence with no one to restrain them. For after sending away into Drenthe the four German cohorts that he had left at Groningen after the battle of Jemmingen, he ordered Gaspar Robles, a Portuguese man, prefect of the Walloon legion, to hold the city with six standards as a garrison, and he drained the same city by a heavy tax of 1,200 gold pieces each week, to pay the soldiers' wages. After this he made the magistracy annual, and he decreed beforehand that it would be perpetual; and to correct the confederates throughout Friesland (which is bounded by the Lauwers and the Ems), he sent Charles Quarré, a man of the equestrian order and a senator of the Brabant court, into Friesland. Having finished the business at Leeuwarden for which he had come, and having given John Charles, the royal investigator, power of inquiry, he hastened to Groningen and gave himself up to inflicting punishments. This harsh judge's office, men did not doubt, had been devised to tame the Frisian race and the obstinacy of the people beyond the Lauwers. Then news of the death of Elisabeth of Valois, wife of Philip, spread into Friesland, and, confirmed by letters from the council of the Belgian State, it made known a continuous series of sad events from the Spanish court and Philip's house. Therefore, for 7 January a day was appointed throughout Friesland for Elisabeth's funeral rites, and Philip commanded that the solemnities of the funeral and the preparations of the procession should match the earlier funeral rites of Prince Charles. So that the stepson and stepmother, who were not free from suspicion of committed incest, might share in the same manner of violent death and funeral rites, and the tragic ends of the royal stock might be marked with the same duties and no unlike fate. Everard Reidanus, an outstanding writer, relates that that excessive intimacy of the stepmother with the stepson was no slight sign of a foul and secret liaison, and that Elisabeth of Valois, secretly delivering by the help of physicians a male fetus, born prematurely in the fifth month, as if to clear obstructions of the womb, gave cause for a sinister suspicion. For it seemed unusual and contrary to the rules of the art that a pregnant woman, with the embryo already far advanced and nearly viable, should be subjected to bloodletting and purgative drugs, and that by violent revulsions force should be inflicted on her vital organs, the contents of the weakened body being moved or drained and the fluid matter of the humours being dragged out. Soon afterwards John Knijff, a man of patrician blood among the people of Utrecht, of deep learning and outstanding authority, was sent to Groningen; after a long dispute with Wittewerum, and soon with Bishop Adolf, who wished to add the rich monasteries, now loosened by the vices of the age and by luxury, to his own endowment, he was put in possession of the see of Groningen. Authors relate that Knijff exercised his office with moderation and, being strong in guiding the minds of the people, was held in high favour, blazing among the people beyond the Lauwers; and that, after an agreement with the Abbot of Mont-Saint-Martin (whom the Cistercians, at the expense also of Adolf, had summoned from the bishop of Clairvaux in Burgundy), he obtained an annual pension of six thousand. Among the Frisians, however, as lately under Margaret the governess, so at this time too that business was delayed by the will of those who by public decree had, in the year 1564, pronounced against the paternal law and liberty. Therefore Ferdinand of Alba, following the example of the see established at Groningen, and urged by the stubborn habits of the people, sent letters to Friesland, in which he sternly urged them to make room for the bishop. He said that the matter, long deferred, was dedicated to the piety of the nation and to its welfare; that men publicly restless, as if in a kingdom of licence, using immodest manners and a looser life, had cast off reverence for the Roman See and for the authority that the ancestors had granted to Emperor Charles. Since this evil had corrupted everything divine and human, and since the clergy themselves, having fallen through abundant leisure into luxury and excessive pride, needed discipline by which those diseases of mind might be restrained, and human minds, poured out into the wilds of error by excessive licence, might return to the right way. And since the diseases of the ancient Church had been remedied by no other means than by the ordinances of bishops and censors, Paul and the pious Roman pontiffs had rightly and prudently provided that in the Belgian provinces, which the crowded population and the prosperity of commerce had raised to great size and at the same time to vices, as wickedness grew with prosperity, more bishops should also be ordained; and that, since the Frisian nation was given over to lust and luxury through the great wealth of its monasteries and the idleness of its clergy, a bishop should be appointed. Therefore, lest anything be taken from the authority of King Philip and the sanctions of the Roman pontiffs, he urged them, and by royal mandate commanded, that the Frisians should receive the same bishop, and that quickly, and should obey him according to the form and prescription of the episcopal records, which he was to present at the assembly of the estates of Friesland on the feast of the see's establishment.

units.la: Quod Ferdinandi Albani mandatum, Margaretæ nuper Gubernatricis, validius tum fuit propterea, quod Albanus quæ decrevisset exequi etiam per vim, & arma certus confusionem omnium rerum, & tristes vindicias spreti imperij minaretur. Quare fundamentum ab eo tempore Sedi per Frisiam substructum, ipseq; clerus, etsi quam maxime animis adversaretur, Ferdinandi Albani decreto post obsecutus est. Qui ut exercitum Philippi, cui cum imperio præerat, per Provincias sparsum, arctius sibi per stipendia pignoraret, de novo per Belgicam tributo cogitavit, populumque opibus validum, ac commercijs florentem, suis quoque viribus atterere conatus est. Igitur conventu omnium procerum Ordinumque Belgicæ (quo & Frisij advenerant) vergente Martio mense, indicto, multa de inopiâ regij aerarij & egentiâ subsidiorum præfatus, centesimam immobilium mobiliumque bonorum, & eorum quidem divenditorum vigesimam, mobilium verò commerciorumque decimam postulavit. Post de modis corrogandi per Provincias tributi latè disseruit, animosque præsentium Ordinum (quod in Hispaniâ suisq; ditionibus, magno principatus sui stabilimento haberi assereret) ad rei novæ famam percussos pavore ac metu complevit. Itaque eorum nomine Viglius Zuichemus ex Aytanâ apud Frisios familiâ, vir regij Senatus præses, verba facere jussus est. Is erudita oratione; Non esse eam Belgicarum Provinciarum, quæ Hispaniæ sit, conditionem ostendebat, variandasque leges pro varietate locorum, aut naturâ gentium esse. Hispaniam namque vasto Oceano, & altissimis montibus clausam, suis è terrâ proventibus, latifundijsque fœlicem esse, Belgicæ econtra provincijs per vicina sibi invicem emporia circumseptis, quorum fortuna non aliunde quam à commercijs & facili annonâ esset. Ideo Philippum Burgundum, laudatæ memoriæ Principem, commercijs ac annonæ omnibus modis prospexisse, quod amoto vectigalium onere parvo sumptu florens populus victitaret, & ubere commercio subditorum suorum opes, atq; divitiæ increscerent. Inde namq; factum esse, ut in infrequentes primum habitatoribus Provincias, novæ velut omnium gentium coloniæ confluerent, omnesque nationes Gadibus & ipso Bosphoro, velut ut terminis Europæ, conclusæ, in hoc terrarum centro, tanquam orbis latissimi emporio coirent. Ita sciret Albanus Philippi Burgundi & Lxi posterorum curâ, ac populi immunitate res Belgicæ evectas, non aliter robur suum atque potentiam amissuras, quam si advectæ ex omni orâ merces decimâ parte onerum augeantur. Inde fore ut plurimæ familiæ in Angliam aut Germaniam migraturæ sint, desertâ Belgicâ, & ditissimis mercatorum novâ lucri cupidine novas sedes quærentibus. Idcirco, remedium supplendi ærarij regij non eo modo, sed à precario populi tributo (antiqui rogas appellabant) haberi posse, quod Principes summa semper necessitate accepissent, & quidem eorum assensu quorum interesset, salvas Provincias esse. Neque enim hoc peregrinum, ut imperare pecuniam Rex non queat, nisi convocatis proceribus, & consensu populi interveniente, quod longa temporum serie in Angliæ regno etiam ab Eduardi IV. ætate obtinuisse Cominæus fidus autor annotasset. Quod verò ad arcium (de quibus etiam Albanus monuerat) structuras attineret, eas modico sumptu pro ratione ærarij habendas, quin curandum potius ut refectis prioribus, quas tutandis finibus majores extruxissent, novarum cura evilescat, roburque regij imperij à fide, & obsequio subditorum potius, quam damnosâ exactione, & operoso munitionum sumptu habeatur. Hæc ferè Albano Viglium Præsidem reposuisse autor Demetrius. Famâ ferunt responso Viglij itaq; Ducem excanduisse, ut istiusmodi Præsides Vilvordam custodiam perduellium ablegandos diceret, Vigliusque aspectu ac horrore Tyranni, velut ultimam necessitatem denuntiantis, syderatione aut apoplexiâ feriretur. De Frisijs seorsim addi potuisset, Carolo Cæsari cessione Saxonicâ hæreditariâ Frisiæ Præfecturâ donato in subsidium, & dignitatem imperij afferendam, censum annuum, vectigales agros, portoria assignata, ut modus exactionibus, & avaritiæ Principum esset, & ne Provincialium facultates, ac ipsius quoq; ærarij opes, sola tuendæ servandæque adversus omnem vim libertatis remedia subverterentur. Interim fidem populi voluntario sæpe tributo detectam, Frisiosque, etsi juris sui retinentes, gratuitâ sæpe liberalitate affectas Principum res, atque impendia rerum præjuvisse. Hac tamen cautione interpositâ; Ne quid fraudis juri publico fieret, & ut omne validâ Principis autoritate, sive adulatione assentantium concessum, per attributam donationem, & beneficium populi rescinderetur.
units.tr: This mandate of Ferdinand of Alba was the stronger, since Alba was resolved to carry out by force and arms whatever he had decided, threatening total confusion and sad punishment for contempt of his authority. Therefore the foundation was laid from that time for the see throughout Friesland, and the clergy themselves, though they were most strongly opposed in mind, afterwards submitted to Ferdinand of Alba's decree. And so that he might bind more tightly to himself by wages the army of Philip, which was scattered through the provinces and which he commanded, he planned a new tax throughout Belgium, and he tried to wear down with his own forces a people strong in resources and flourishing in commerce. Therefore, at an assembly of all the nobles and estates of Belgium (to which the Frisians too had come), summoned for the month of March, after speaking at length about the poverty of the royal treasury and the lack of funds, he demanded a hundredth of all immovable and movable goods, and a twentieth of such goods when sold, but a tenth of movable goods and of commerce. Afterwards he spoke at length about the means of raising the tax through the provinces, and he filled the minds of those present with fear and dread, struck by the report of a new thing, which he asserted was held in Spain and in its dominions as the great foundation of the prince's rule. Then, on their behalf, Viglius Zuichemus, of the Aytta family from Friesland, a president of the royal Senate, was ordered to speak. In a learned speech he showed that the condition of the Belgian provinces was not that of Spain, and that laws must vary according to the variety of places or the nature of the peoples. For Spain, shut in by the vast Ocean and by very high mountains, was blessed with the produce of its own soil and its wide estates, whereas the Belgian provinces, surrounded by neighbouring markets, had their prosperity from nothing but commerce and cheap grain. Therefore Philip the Burgundian, a prince of praiseworthy memory, had provided for commerce and the grain supply in every way, so that the people might live well at small cost once the burden of taxes was removed, and that by a rich trade the resources and wealth of his subjects might grow. For from this it had come about that, at first, the provinces thinly peopled by their inhabitants, as if new colonies of all nations, had flocked together, and all the peoples, enclosed between Cadiz and the Bosphorus, as if at the boundaries of Europe, came together in this centre of the lands, as in the market of the widest world. Thus Alba should know that the affairs of Belgium, raised up by the care of Philip the Burgundian and of his heirs, and by the freedom of the people, would not lose their strength and power in any other way than if the merchandise brought from every shore were burdened with an added tenth of charges. From this it would follow that many families would emigrate to England or Germany, leaving Belgium deserted, and the richest merchants, seeking new seats for a new greed for gain. Therefore, he said, a remedy for filling the royal treasury could be found not in that way, but in a tax on the people granted by favour, which the ancients called precarium, which princes had always received in the greatest necessity, and indeed with the assent of those whose interest it was that the provinces be safe. For it is not a foreign practice that the king cannot levy money unless the nobles are summoned and the consent of the people is obtained; the faithful writer Commines had noted that this had prevailed in the kingdom of England for a long succession of times, even from the age of Edward IV. As for the building of fortresses (about which Alba had also given advice), these should be regarded as a small expense in proportion to the treasury; indeed, care should rather be taken that, by repairing the older ones which their ancestors had built larger to guard the frontiers, the care of new ones should not grow overgrown, and that the strength of royal rule should be sought in the loyalty and obedience of the subjects rather than in a ruinous exaction and a costly outlay on fortifications. Such, the writer Demetrius reports, was the substance of Viglius the president's reply to Alba. They say that by report Alba flared up at Viglius's answer, and that he said such presidents should be sent away to Vilvoorde, the prison of traitors; and that Viglius, at the sight and horror of the tyrant, who was threatening the utmost extremity, was struck by a stroke or apoplexy. Separately about Friesland it might have been added that, since the hereditary Saxon prefecture of Friesland had been granted to Emperor Charles by cession as a subsidy, and the dignity of the empire was to be brought forward, an annual census, tax-bearing lands and assigned customs duties should be fixed, so that there might be a limit to the exactions and avarice of princes, and so that the resources of the provincials and the wealth of the treasury itself should not be overturned, leaving only remedies for defending and preserving liberty against every force. Meanwhile, the loyalty of the people had often been shown by voluntary taxes, and the Frisians, though retaining their own right, had often by free generosity assisted the affairs and expenses of princes. Yet this caution was added: that nothing of fraud be done against public law, and that whatever had been granted by the strong authority of the prince, or by the flattery of sycophants, be annulled by the gift and benefit of the people that had been assigned.

units.la: Itaque tum populus immodicæ exactionis fastidio, per omnem Provinciam inquietus, majora consilia agitavit, sepultamque ante, velut torpidis animis, virtutem odio superbi Ducis exerere conatus est. Sic quos nec ante, ut Reidanus notat, sociorum fædera; aut exilia, tum vel maximè puræ veræque religionis oppressio ad implorandum armorum subsidium excitaverant, sola fortunæ, & caducarum rerum cura ad defensionem patriæ instigavit, libertasque veteri mortalium ingeniorum morbo, infra opulentiam habita, conservandarum rerum familiarium cupiditate, & simul sævitiâ dominantium revaluit. Quainobrem Senatus per Frisiam regius perceptâ populi per omnem Belgicam nova inquietudine præpediendis clandestinis conventibus se dedit, omneque cum profugis reformatisque commercium Edicto iterum sustulit. Ca-vit
units.tr: Therefore the people, restless throughout the whole Province and weary of excessive exactions, began to consider bolder plans, and tried to rouse their courage, which had lain buried until then as if their spirits were numb, against the hatred of the proud Duke. Thus those whom neither the alliances of allies, as Reidanus notes, nor exile, nor above all the oppression of pure and true religion had earlier stirred to seek armed help, were now roused to defend their country by the sole care of fortune and perishable things. Liberty, which mortals in their old disease had held of less worth than wealth, revived through the desire to keep their household property and at the same time through the savagery of their rulers. Accordingly, the royal Senate at Friesland, having perceived the new unrest of the people throughout all Belgium, set itself to prevent secret meetings, and by another edict again abolished all dealings with exiles and reformed persons. He also provided

units.la: cIↄ. Iↄ. LXIX. vit quoque, Ne peregrinis ullis aut advenis, nisi quibus testimonia Magistratuum Presbyterorumve data essent, ulli per Frisiam agri aut praedia locarentur, adducereturque in discrimen Regis imperium deletis partibus securum. Reperio in notis incerti autoris, Iulium Bonniam virum nobilem ex hoc ipso Edicto à fisci regij patrono accusatum damnatumque multae loco totum praedium dependisse.
units.tr: that no outsiders or newcomers, unless they had certificates from magistrates or elders, should be let land or estates anywhere in Friesland, lest the royal authority, with its parts destroyed, be brought into danger of being secure. I find in the notes of an unknown author that Julius Bonnia, a nobleman, was accused by the royal fiscal advocate under this very edict and condemned, and that in place of a fine he paid over his entire estate.

units.la: Mox Albanus PHILIPPI decreto Madriti in Hispania VI. Eid. Maij perscripto, Edictum in causa Religionis à CAROLO Caesare Anno cIↄ. Iↄ. L. publicatum, ac à Philippo primis Principatus sui annis confirmatum, renovari per Frisiam jusit, omneque rescriptum spem, aut saltem speciem clementiae prae se ferens, ob retardatam exactionis gravissimae consilium rescidit. Ut scilicet titillante gloria ferox, & inflatus regni sui, aut futuri dominatus imaginem ostenderet, fatalemque & praefractam feritatem desperationi, & post virtuti gentium, Principumque praesterneret.
units.tr: Soon afterwards Alva, by a decree of Philip written at Madrid in Spain on the sixth day before the Ides of May, ordered the edict on religious matters, published by Emperor Charles in 1550 and confirmed by Philip in the first years of his reign, to be renewed in Friesland; and he annulled every rescript that showed any hope, or at least the appearance, of clemency, because of his plan of delaying the most grievous exaction. Clearly, fierce and puffed up by the glory that tickled him, he wished to display an image of his present rule or of future dominion, and to spread out before despair and the courage of peoples and princes his fatal and unyielding savagery.

units.la: Quamobrem Aurantius notato populi per omnem Provinciam murmure, ad alia consiliorum se convertit, damnatque exautorati ad Mosam exercitus reparaturus, relicta continente mari experiri constituit. Creditum fuit Casparum Colignium Gallici maris Praefectum istud consilium suggessisse, ac si de liberandae Belgicae remedio opportunitate maris portuumque benignior Natura prospexisset. Itaque Aurantius misso in omne confinium ad exules foederatos, qui Embdae, ac Vesaliae Cliviorum latitabant, Ioanne Basio Iureconsulto homine Frisio subsidia gerendis rebus flagitavit, novique consilij prudens secretum apud exules sociosque exposuit. Quorum res etsi duorum annorum exilium, & erogata jam ante in Principem subsidia accidissent, tamen amor patriae, & in eam reditus praeconceptae spes, ad officia pietatis exulum populum accendebant. Idcirco Aurantius pecunia turbae exulantis, tum suo, ac propinquorum aere sublevatus navalem expeditionem adornavit, validamque classem toto mari, quod Balthicum Caledoniumque tangit, adulto autumno sparsit. Tum ne nautica pubes, aut clasiarius quisque sine disciplina ageret, peiraticaeve se daret, leges classi suae praefixit, sociorumque rebus abstinere jusit. Eorum quippe nomine Romani Imperij, Galliae, Angliae, Sueciae, Daniae, & Vandalorum subditi censebantur, quod pro ijs aut religio foederum, aut spes auxiliorum intercederent. Caeterum libero mari increscens libertas mox licentiam facturà alieni cupiditatibus nauticam, & efferam pubem implicuit. Quare haud procul Flevi ostio, qua in mare delabitur, majores Frisios, & Flevolandiam interluens, Vandalicae naves direptae, fususque late per terras & maria terror, omne confinium implevit.
units.tr: Therefore Orange, having noted the murmuring of the people throughout the whole province, turned to other plans. Having been dismissed from the army at the Meuse, and about to rebuild it, he decided to make trial of the sea, leaving the mainland. It was believed that Gaspard de Coligny, admiral of the French sea, had suggested this plan, as if nature, more kindly, had provided the sea and its harbours as a remedy for freeing Belgium. So Orange, sending to the exiles who had joined the cause, who were hiding at Emden and at Wesel in Cleves, asked for support for carrying out the affair through John Basius, a jurist and Frisian by birth, and he set out his prudent new plan in secret to the exiles and allies. Although the exiles' affairs had suffered two years of exile and subsidies already spent on the Prince, love of country and the hope of return they had long conceived kindled the exiles and the people to acts of duty. Therefore Orange, relieved by the money of the exiled crowd, and by his own and his relatives' funds, fitted out a naval expedition, and in the ripe autumn spread a strong fleet over the whole sea that touches the Baltic and the Caledonian coast. Then, so that the sailors or any ship's crew might not act without discipline or turn to piracy, he prescribed laws for his fleet and ordered that they abstain from the property of allies. For under that name they were counted as subjects of the Roman Empire, of France, England, Sweden, Denmark and the Vandals, since either the bond of treaties or the hope of help stood between them and these. But freedom, growing on the open sea, soon made the sailors and the wild crews, whose desires were not their own, into a licence of their own. Hence, not far from the mouth of the Vlie, where the sea flows in, and along the greater Frisian and Flevoland coasts, Vandal ships were plundered, and terror, spread widely over land and sea, filled the whole coast.

units.la: Quare non uno comitio instruendis praesidiarijs navibus instituto, magnae exactiones factae, & imprimis à populo civico quem Senatus Philippi, tutando à praedonibus mari, istà tributi specie praegravaverat. Qui idcirco libellum supplicem, evulgatâ per civitates ac oppida decreti oneris famâ Carolo Brimaeo Praefecto, & Senatuj regio offerri jusit, deq; rei iniquitate prolixe conquestus omne civilis concordiae vinculum istâ onerum inaequalitate tolli criminatus est. Nimios quippe in sumptus illud adornandæ classis consilium excrescere, qui- bus sustinendis oppidani pares non forent. Multa namq; per Frisiam oppida annuis reditibus destitui, mercaturam ab urbibus in agros transferri magno illorum incommodo, quos præter pecuniæ nauticæ subsidium, militare quoque tributum, & grassantis pestilentiæ lues exederet. Interesse tam agrariorum, quam civium, ut mare liberum sit, ac commercijs floreat, & ut piratæ circa ostia fluminum, & per æstuaria grassantes præsidiariâ classe, & per vim militum comprimantur. Ita per Hollandiam & Translavicanos fieri, quo publica maris securitas publico & communi ære præstetur. Cæterum Senatus regius illud sustinendæ classis impendium oppidanis assignavit, solamq; subsidij ab agrarijs præstandi spem ac pollicitationem fecit. Invenio in actis eosdem agrarios, salvo tamen jure suo, quinque aureorum millia, præter ordinarium tributum regiæ quoq; necessitati decrevisse, magnasq; contentiones in causâ tributi exercitas, modo regium Senatum, modo Deputatos Ordinum fatigasse. Sex quoq; Carolæorum millia mense Octobri petente Carolo Brimæo, regijs usibus decreta, eiusdemq; Brimæi interventu in collatione tributorum urbicos Magistratus cum agrarijs convenisse. Eundem quoque Brimæum trium millium honorario donatum, sive conciliando novi rectoris favori, sive ut prima imperij initia liberalitate populi probarentur
units.tr: Hence, not at one assembly, but on the initiative of arming garrison ships, great levies were made, and above all upon the citizens, whom the Senate of Philip had overburdened with this kind of tax for protecting the sea against pirates. These therefore ordered a supplicating petition to be offered to Charles Brimaeus, the Prefect, and to the royal Senate, when the news of the decreed burden had spread through the cities and towns. They complained at length of the injustice of the matter, and charged that every bond of civil harmony was destroyed by this inequality of burdens. For the plan for equipping the fleet, they said, was growing into costs that the townsmen could not match. Many towns in Friesland, they argued, were deprived of their annual revenues, and trade was being transferred from the cities to the countryside, to the great loss of those who, besides the money for the naval subsidy, were also wasted by military taxes and the plague of the pestilence raging about. It was in the interest of country folk as of citizens that the sea be free and commerce flourish, and that pirates raiding about the mouths of rivers and through the estuaries be checked both by a garrison fleet and by the force of soldiers. This was how things stood in Holland and the Trans-Vlie districts, where public safety at sea was secured by public and common money. But the royal Senate assigned the expense of maintaining the fleet to the townsmen, and made to the country folk only a hope and promise of contributing. I find in the records that the same country folk, saving however their own right, decreed five thousand gold pieces, beyond the ordinary tax, for the royal need as well, and that great disputes arose over the matter of the tax, wearying now the royal Senate, now the deputies of the orders. Likewise six thousand Carolus-coins were decreed for royal uses at the request of Charles Brimaeus in October, and through the same Brimaeus' mediation the town magistrates came to an agreement with the country folk over the levying of taxes. The same Brimaeus was also given an honorarium of three thousand, either to win the favour of the new governor, or so that the first beginnings of his rule might be approved by the generosity of the people.

units.la: Albanum verò ut exigendæ centesimæ decimæq; pertinax studium, ita constituendæ per Frisiam Sedis acre tum desiderium incitabat. Quamobrem inversis metu periculi, an potentiâ jubentis dubium, populi Frisici ingenijs, Cunerum Petrum, natione Zelandum, & Lovanij tum docentem Episcopum è Bullâ Pij iv. Pontificis (quam is Romæ viii. Eid. Mart. Anno cIↄ. Iↄ. xli. Francisco Sonnio Legato Regis communicaverat) ordinavit, eique diploma, & administrandæ Sedis rationem xviii. Kal. Decemb. Bruxellis præscripsit: Ea istiusmodi erat:
units.tr: Alva, however, was spurred on by a stubborn eagerness to exact the hundredth and tenth, and by a keen desire at that time to set up a bishopric in Friesland. Therefore, with the people of Friesland uncertain whether to fear danger or the power of the one who commanded, he appointed Peter Cunerus, a Zeelander by birth, then teaching at Louvain as bishop, on the basis of the Bull of Pope Pius IV (which he had communicated at Rome on 8 March 1561 to Francis Sonnius, the royal legate), and on 14 November at Brussels he prescribed for him the charter and the manner of administering the see. It was of this kind:

units.la: EPiscopo fiduciariæ à Philippo Rege, & Ferdinando Albano, ad Archiepiscopum Vltrajectinum, & Monasteriensem litteræ dabuntur, quibus de Sanctione Pontificis, & iurisdictione novi Episcopi doceantur.
units.tr: The bishop-designate shall be sent letters by Philip the King and by Ferdinand Alva, addressed to the Archbishop of Utrecht and to the Archbishop of Münster, by which they shall be informed about the Pontiff's sanction and the jurisdiction of the new bishop.

units.la: Episcopus mandatorum Tabulas exhibebit Præfecto, & Senatui Regio, qui eum coram religiosis D. Viti, & præsente Magistratu Oppidano in possessionem Sedis mittent, & ad quos isto nomine litteræ dabuntur.
units.tr: The bishop shall show the mandates to the Prefect and the royal Senate, who shall put him in possession of the see in the presence of the religious of St Vitus and the town magistracy, and to whom letters shall be given for this purpose.

units.la: Episcopus introductioni suæ diem præsiniet, deductusque, clero a Præfecto, Senatu Regio, Magistratu, ac vicinâ Nobilitate in Cathedrale D. Viti sanum juramentum dicet, è formulâ isti actui præscriptâ.
units.tr: The bishop shall fix the day of his introduction, and, escorted by the clergy, the Prefect, the royal Senate, the magistracy and the neighbouring nobility, he shall take the solemn oath in the Cathedral of St Vitus, in the form prescribed for that act.

units.la: Religiosi ad D. Vitum obedientiam vicissim Episcopo promittent; si gravati id fecerint, quod Vltrajectino obligatos se censeant, litteris approbatoriis Vltrajectini, & bullâ Pontificis se muniet.
units.tr: The religious of St Vitus shall in turn promise obedience to the bishop. If, burdened by it, they should do so because they consider themselves bound to Utrecht, he shall protect himself with letters of approval from Utrecht and with the Pontiff's bull.

units.la: In possessionem Sedis missus conciones habebit, populum in Catholica Religione erudiet, visitabit Ecclesias, inque cleri oppidani mores, & doctrinam Presbyterorum inquiret, cum potestate morum religionisve suspectos corrigendi, degradandique.
units.tr: Once put in possession of the see, he shall hold sermons, instruct the people in the Catholic religion, visit the churches, and inquire into the morals of the town clergy and the teaching of the elders, with the power to correct and depose those suspected in morals or religion.

units.la: Ordinem quoq; mendicantium curabit, ut rite doceat, scandalaq; ac errores Religionis emendabit.
units.tr: He shall also take care of the mendicant orders, that they teach properly, and he shall correct scandals and errors of religion.

units.la: Locis vacantibus pios eruditosque pastores aditusque dabit, scholarumque non tantum Leovardiæ, sed per omnem Frisiam curam geret, ac quid doceatur, expendet.
units.tr: He shall grant access to vacant posts to pious and learned ministers, and he shall take care of the schools not only at Leeuwarden but throughout all Friesland, and weigh what is taught.

units.la: De consilio Pastorum, Magistratus oppidani Seminarium è præscripto Concilij Tridentini constituet.
units.tr: With the advice of the ministers, the town magistrates shall set up a seminary according to the prescription of the Council of Trent.

units.la: Librariorum officinas lustrabit, dabitque operam ne quid habeatur tolerabile, præterquam quod Edicto Regis congruat.
units.tr: He shall inspect the bookshops, and shall take care that nothing be tolerated except what agrees with the King's edict.

units.la: Concilij Tridentini decreta promulgabit, si non omnia, saltem ea quæ Doctrinam spectabunt, & ad captum populi erunt.
units.tr: He shall promulgate the decrees of the Council of Trent, if not all of them, at least those which concern doctrine and are suited to the understanding of the people.

units.la: Et quoniam, quo minus id jam ante ab Archi-episcopo Vltrajectino factum esset, per Senatum regium stetisset, aliter hac de re edoctum, ita velle ut Concilium Tridentinum pro sanctione Pontificis, & ex Decreto PHILIPPI Regis vulgetur.
units.tr: And since it had been the Senate's doing that this had not already been done by the Archbishop of Utrecht, he is to know that the King wishes the Council of Trent to be published in this matter, by the Pontiff's sanction and by the decree of King Philip.

units.la: Dabit operam Episcopus, ut Clerus Edictis PHILIPPI regis de Religione pareat, contumaces in carcerem mittat.
units.tr: The bishop shall see to it that the clergy obey King Philip's edicts concerning religion, and he shall send the obstinate to prison.

units.la: Magistratum aliosve ijsdem Edictis non parentes, ad Senatum Regium, eo tardo aut connivente ad Præfectum Provinciarum deferet.
units.tr: He shall refer magistrates and others who do not obey the same edicts to the Royal Senate, or, if the Senate is slow or connives at them, to the Governor of the Provinces.

units.la: Episcopus Abbatias collegiaque monastica utriusque sexus visitabit, tam ordinario jure Episcopo subjecta, quam è potestate sibi à Romano Pontifice data.
units.tr: The bishop shall visit the abbeys and monastic communities of both sexes, both those subject to the bishop by ordinary right and those placed under his authority by the Roman Pontiff.

units.la: Vetustate, aut incuriâ collapsas ædes sacras refici curabit.
units.tr: He shall take care that sacred buildings collapsed through age or neglect are restored.

units.la: Officium facienti Episcopo Præfectus Senatusque Regius omne subsidium præstabunt, & si res exigat, plures nomine Regis adjungentur.
units.tr: The Governor and the Royal Senate shall give the bishop every assistance in performing his office, and if the matter requires it, more men shall be added in the King's name.

units.la: Laurentius Decanus ad D. Godelam comitem Episcopo se dabit, eique dum singula paret, à consilijs erit.
units.tr: Dean Laurentius shall place himself at the service of Lord Godelus, Count of the bishop, and shall advise him in each matter as it arises.

units.la: Episcopus in omnes Fidei ac hæreseos suspectos inquiret, juxtaque cum ijs aget.
units.tr: The bishop shall inquire into all who are suspected of faith or heresy, and shall proceed against them accordingly.

units.la: Integros ab infectis discernet, regioque Senatui in Magistratuum creatione operam commodabit, delectumque præscribet.
units.tr: He shall separate the sound from the infected, shall assist the Royal Senate in the appointment of magistrates, and shall prescribe the selection.

units.la: Et quia Sanctitas sex beneficia Sedi assignavit Cathedrale D. Viti fanum, Abbatiam Horti-Mariæ, tum Canonicorum Regularium Cænobium apud Bergumanos, & Præposituram Bolsuerdiensem, admitetur Episcopus ut beneficia Sedi applicet, exigenteque necessitate, tueatur se procuratore fisci, & diplomatis Pontificum, ac ipsius Regis mandato.
units.tr: And since His Holiness has assigned six benefices to the See, namely the cathedral church of St Vitus, the abbey of Hortus Mariae, the house of Regular Canons at Bergum, and the provostship of Bolsward, the bishop is authorized to apply the benefices to the See, and, if necessity requires, to defend himself by the procurator of the treasury, by the papal bulls, and by the King's own mandate.

units.la: Episcopus omnia singulaque faciet, quæ ad conservationem Catholicæ Religionis, quietem & pacem publicam spectare judicaverit.
units.tr: The bishop shall do all and each thing that he judges to pertain to the preservation of the Catholic religion and to public quiet and peace.

units.la: Hæc Ferdinandi Albani manu signata, & è Bullâ Pij iv. Pontificis excepta, eidem Cunero tradita. Itaque Cunerus mandatis Pontificum, Philippi regis, & Ferdinandi Albani instructus x. Kal. Febr. Lovanio Grudiorum civitate excessit, confectoque decem dierum itinere Leovardiam pervenit, quâ in urbe primus post tot sæculorum ambitum Episcopatum inchoaturus erat, nullo populi favore, cæterum sola dominantium potentiâ subnixum. Mox à Segero Grosbecio viro Nobili, (qui agente apud Tanfisulanos Carolo Brimæo Comite Megano Frisiæ Præfecto vicarium per Provinciam imperium gerebat) in arcem regiam evocatus, noctem in eâ egit, dieque postero in urbem effusus, stipatusque; multâ procerum frequentiâ in Cathedrale D. Viti templum à Grosbecio deductus est. Deïn celebrato postridie sacro, diem epulo clausit, ad quod ex omni Provinciæ orâ primores gentis evocaverat. caverat. Ut scilicet novi & diu Frisiâ arciti muneris invidiem geniacIↄ. Iↄ. li festivitate elevaret, spectarentque Frisij hominem sacris operatum à lxx. vino, aut convivalium dierum cultu non abhorrere.
units.tr: These instructions, signed by the hand of Ferdinand of Alva and taken from the bull of Pius IV, were handed to the same Cunerus. Accordingly Cunerus, furnished with the mandates of the Pontiffs, of King Philip and of Ferdinand of Alva, left the city of Louvain on the tenth day before the Kalends of February, and after a ten-day journey reached Leeuwarden, where he was about to begin the episcopate, for the first time after so many centuries, supported not by any favour of the people but solely by the power of those in authority. Soon he was summoned to the royal citadel by Seger Grosbeek, a nobleman, who, while Charles Brimaeus, Count of Megen and governor of Friesland, was acting among the Tanfisulans, was exercising the deputed rule over the province. He spent the night there, and on the following day he went out into the city, surrounded by a large crowd of nobles, and was led by Grosbeek into the cathedral church of St Vitus. Then, after Mass had been celebrated the next day, he closed the day with a banquet, to which he had summoned the leading men from every part of the province. He did this clearly so that the festivity might soften the resentment aroused by a new office long withheld from Friesland, and so that the Frisians might see that a man engaged in sacred duties did not shun wine or the customs of festive days.

units.la: Mox Bergumanum in Cænobium, quod doti Sedis applicatum, istius loci Præsul & vicina Nobilitas indignabatur, secessit, litterasq; Ferdinandi Albani manu vii. Kal. Decembr. signatas, Præsuli exhibuit. Litterae habebant.
units.tr: Soon he withdrew to the monastery at Bergum, which the bishop of that place and the neighbouring nobility resented as having been assigned to the endowment of the See, and he presented to the prelate a letter signed by the hand of Ferdinand of Alva on the seventh day before the Kalends of December. The letter read:

units.la: Misimus litteras nostras ad regis Senatum, eiq; potestatem fecimus, quaedam exponendi, quae ad utilitatem publicam & simul Regis spectare videntur. Quapropter peto, & nomine regis mando, ut ijs, quae denuntiabuntur, pareas, faciasq; fidelis subditi erga regem officium, quod id è re sua esse censuit.
units.tr: We have sent our letter to the Senate of the King, and have empowered it to set forth certain matters which seem to pertain to the public advantage and at the same time to the King's interest. Therefore I ask, and in the King's name I command, that you obey those things which shall be announced, and that you perform the duty of a faithful subject toward the King, which he has judged to be to his own advantage.

units.la: Quas litteras & simul Senatus regij declarationem, etsi ut iniquam respueret, Præsul ita rescripsit.
units.tr: This letter, together with the declaration of the Royal Senate, the prelate rejected as unjust, and he replied in these words:

units.la: Cænobium nostrum Episcopo tradere nostrae potestatis non est. Subjecti Capitulo Windesimano cuius membra sumus, multa à Pontificibus privilegia, multas immunitates obtinuimus à sacris Concilijs & ipso Carolo Cæsare, post ab ipso Concilio Tridentino approbatas. Quod ad sacramentum attinet, id Præsidj nostri ordinis diximus, quod separari nos ab eo societasq; non finit. Adhæc Ordinibus Frisiæ innexi antiquâ & veteri societate, & ita quidem, ut nostro arbitrio hoc negotium agi non queat, & quoniam Regi eiusq; Præfectis & administris semper ab officys fuimus, ita periniquum est, Cænobium hoc everti, plurium familiarum nutricatui, qua in solo hoc sterili numerantur, iterq; Groningam versus facientibus inserviens. Taceo reditus nostros largitionibus pauperum accisos, & ita quidem ut vix duo aureorum millia quotannis faciant. Itaq; frugalitatem professi, & inculpatum vitae otium obeundis sacris dedimus egimusq; ut ad exemplum exorbitantis alibi cleri decens disciplina hoc in loco vigeret. Nullius criminis factiq; conscij sumus. Quare jus nostrum Episcopo cedere, neq; Ordinis nostri regula, nec Pontificum Conciliorumq; diplomata admittunt. Libellus quoq; supplex pro Præsule regio Senatui ab Ulpio Heemstra, Frederico Arnoldio, Bruchtio Altæo & Adriano Cronenburgio oblatus, invalidis in totum rationibus, quæ irati regis imperio & super-bi dominantis asperrimo jussu subvertebantur. Ex quo etiam factum est, ut in ipso quoq; Philippi Senatu juris quasi dicundi officia cessarent, partiumq; odio, aut gratiâ corruptum judicium culpabili mora, sicuti per Iustitium, extraheretur. Quod cum in Pelgromio Indikio prætore nuper regio, multorum criminum facinorumq; insimulato, fieret, litteræ ab Ordinibus ad Philippum & illius Proregem datæ, quæ Senatum regium puniendis improbis tardum non vanâ neglecti juris suspicione gravabant. Itaq; Albanus Philippi nomine Senatum in-crepavit, datisq; Antverpiâ xiii. Kal. Febr. litteris eundem aspere sui officij commonuit. Tum ne ipse frequentioribus judicum suorum accusationibus fatigaretur, ipsi quoq; Pelgromio, quamvis severius Philippi imperium odio libertatis probaret, jus dici à Senatu mandavit, integritatemq; regio judicio, etsi, ut multa istorum temporum acta arguunt, partium affectibus obnoxio, adstruere conatus est. Reperio
units.tr: It is not in our power to hand over our monastery to the bishop. Subject to the Chapter of Windesheim, of which we are members, we have obtained many privileges and many immunities from the Pontiffs, and from the sacred councils and from Charles Caesar himself, afterwards approved by the Council of Trent itself. As for the sacrament, we have said that this belongs to the President of our order, since it does not permit us to be separated from it and from the society. Moreover, we are bound to the orders of Friesland by an ancient and long-standing fellowship, and in such a way that this business cannot be transacted at our discretion. And since we have always been at the service of the King, his governors and his officials, it is very unjust that this monastery should be overthrown, which nourishes many families, and which is reckoned among the few in this barren region, serving those travelling towards Groningen. I say nothing of our revenues, which have been reduced by the gifts to the poor, so that they barely amount to two thousand gold pieces a year. Having therefore professed frugality, and given a blameless leisure of life to sacred duties, we have also worked to ensure that, in contrast to the unrestrained clergy elsewhere, a becoming discipline flourishes in this place. We are conscious of no crime or wrongdoing. Therefore neither the rule of our order nor the decrees of the Pontiffs and councils allow us to cede our right to the bishop. A humble petition was also presented on behalf of the prelate to the Royal Senate by Ulpius Heemstra, Frederick Arnold, Bruchtius Altaeus and Adrian Cronenburg, whose reasons were wholly without force, and were overturned by the harsh command of an angry king and a haughty ruler. As a result, even in Philip's Senate the duties of administering justice ceased, and judgment, corrupted by party hatred or favour, was dragged out by culpable delay, as if by a suspension of the courts. When this happened in the case of Pelgrom, the recent royal magistrate of Indikium, who was accused of many crimes and offences, letters were sent by the Estates to Philip and to his Governor, which charged the Royal Senate with being slow to punish the wicked, with a not vain suspicion of neglect of law. So Alva, in Philip's name, rebuked the Senate, and by letter dated at Antwerp on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of February sharply reminded it of its duty. Then, so that he himself might not be wearied by the frequent accusations against his judges, he also commanded the Senate to administer justice to Pelgrom himself, though he approved of the harsher rule of Philip out of hatred of liberty; and he tried to establish the integrity of the royal judgment, although, as many acts of those times show, it was open to the influence of party feelings. I find

units.la: in actis Episcopalibus nobilem quendam, & in dignitate prætoriâ constitutum, nobilissimæ virginis amore captum, eam contracti secum matrimonij insimulavisse, Quæsitoremq; rerum fiscalium utriq; reo in foro Episcopi actionem intentasse. Episcopum quoq; ipsum in Divæ Annæ Cænobio, quod urbi Leovardiæ in ortum Solis æstivum est, pro Tribunali sedisse, invocatoq; Christi nomine, utrumq; reum, demandato in futurum silentio, absolvisse. Quæ res, quia amplitudinem regij supremiq; judicij, quod Carolo Philippoq; regnantibus, matrimoniales controversias cognoverat, minuere, & simul licentiam juvenilium ac sæpè inanium amorum videbatur, primo quoq; dominatus Episcopatis tempore odium eï conciliavit.
units.tr: in the episcopal records that a certain nobleman, holding a magisterial dignity, captivated by love of a most noble maiden, had accused her of a marriage contracted with him, and that the examiner of fiscal affairs had brought an action against both defendants in the bishop's court. I find also that the bishop himself sat in judgment in the convent of St Anne, which lies to the east of the city of Leeuwarden, and, invoking the name of Christ, acquitted both defendants, with silence enjoined for the future. This affair, because it seemed to diminish the authority of the royal and supreme court, which under Charles and Philip had taken cognizance of matrimonial disputes, and at the same time seemed to license youthful and often empty loves, won him hatred at the very beginning of his episcopal rule.

units.la: Post v. Kal. Mart. promulgatis, ut jussus erat, Concilij Tridentini Sanctionibus Cathedralem Sedem ad D. Vitum posuit, locumque velut nupero motu populi profanatum lustro adspersit. Senatus quoq; regius Antonium Lavailium, Petrum Frittemam Senatores, & Ioannem Carolum Fisci Advocatum è suo cætu delegavit, qui de dignitate & persona Episcopi apud populum agerent. Scribit Suffridus Lavailium speciosâ & gravi oratione verba fecisse, ac ad obedientiam Sedis quoq; hortatum, præsidium Regij Senatus eidem Episcopo addixisse. Idem Ioannes Carolus vir eruditus nomine Philippi fecit, modo ne Principis jurisdictio, aut jura Majestatis regiæ arctarentur. Ita in possessionem Sedis immissus Cunerus, beneficia doti suæ adjecit, capitulumque, ut vocant, decem & sex Canonicorum, quos Laurentius Metrius Sylvæ-Ducensis introduxerat, suspectis populo solemnibus, erexit. Post iii. Non. Martij Statuta quoque & ordinationes erecti Capituli vulgavit, faciendisque sacris, tum fundendis ad Deum precibus, hymnisque tempora constituit. Tum vii. Kal. Maij Synodus per Provinciam omni clero indicta, ac tridui spatio Leovardiæ celebrata, designatis è regio Senatu Senatoribus, Petro Frittema, & Foccone Rommartio, qui sanctiones Concilij Tridentini fartas tectas curarent, Præsulque Cunero una cum Archi-Diacono Dominico Benedixio per universam Frisiam in visitandis Ecclesijs operam, atque autoritatem præstarent. Ita Episcopus, mense Iulio, adscitis in comitatum Senatoribus regijs, Ooftergoos, Weftergoos, Sylveftres, ac Oppidanos adijt, intactamq; tam diu invidiâ Sedem habuit, donec in luxum, ludicraque, ut memorabo, prolapsus, suam juxta & novæ Sedis existimationem fædiore vitâ indignisq; Episcopo moribus attaminaret. Ivo Ioannis, de quo ante dixi, quod Anno cIↄ. Iↄ. lxvi. in Romanâ religione perstitisset, Cathedralis Ecclesiæ Decanatu ornatus est, quam Poftrid. Non. Iul. subsecutâ nocte audaci sacrilegio expilatam è Tiaræ notis Borræus meminit. Refert quippe argenteas capsulas duas, cum quatuor vasculis olearijs argenteis sacrario extractas, perpetratumque crimen, tentatâ nequicquam inquisitione, velut eâ, quâ acciderat, nocte conte&ctum manifisse. Quod facinus confirmando edicto causam post dedit, Carolumque Brimæum Frisiæ tum Præfectum, ut & ante Grosbecium, in sacrilegos statuere compulit. Circa quod temporis exules Frisios (ut & è cæteris Belgicæ Provincijs) Spiram Nemetum ad comitia Imperij, quæ Maximilianus II. eo in loco ordinavenaverat, profectos Borraeus tradit, Caesariq; Maximiliano & Germaniae Electoribus hunc in modum supplicasse:
units.tr: After the fifth day before the Kalends of March, as he had been ordered, he published the sanctions of the Council of Trent and set up the cathedral see at St Vitus, and purified the place, as though profaned by the recent movement of the people, by sprinkling it. The Royal Senate also delegated from its own number the senators Antonius Lavailius and Petrus Frittema, and John Charles, advocate of the fisc, who were to speak to the people about the dignity and person of the bishop. Suffridus writes that Lavailius spoke with a splendid and weighty oration, and also exhorted them to obedience to the See, and that the Royal Senate assigned its protection to the same bishop. The same John Charles, a learned man, did this in the name of Philip, provided only that the prince's jurisdiction and the rights of royal majesty were not narrowed. Thus Cunerus, installed in possession of the See, added benefices to his endowment, and with solemn ceremonies, which were suspect to the people, established the so-called chapter of sixteen canons whom Laurentius Metrius of Zwolle had introduced. After the third day before the Nones of March he also published the statutes and ordinances of the established chapter, and fixed the times for the performance of sacred rites, and for pouring out prayers and hymns to God. Then on the seventh day before the Kalends of May a synod was summoned throughout the province for all the clergy and was held at Leeuwarden over three days, with senators Peter Frittema and Foccon Rommartius chosen from the Royal Senate, whose task was to see that the decrees of the Council of Trent were carefully observed, while the bishop, together with the archdeacon Dominic Benedixius, gave their labour and authority to the visitation of the churches throughout all Friesland. So the bishop, in July, with royal senators taken into his retinue, went to the Oostergo, the Westergo, the Sylvestres and the townsmen, and he held the See, untouched by envy for so long, until he fell into luxury and frivolity, as I shall relate, and by a more disgraceful life and unworthy conduct stained both his own reputation and that of the new See. Ivo Johannis, of whom I spoke before, who in the year 1566 had persisted in the Roman religion, was adorned with the deanery of the cathedral church, which, on the night following the day after the Nones of July, was plundered by a bold sacrilege, as Borraeus records from the notes of the Tiara. For he reports that two silver caskets, together with four small silver oil vessels, were taken from the sacristy, and that the crime, after an inquiry had been tried in vain, was clearly revealed as having been concealed by the very night on which it had occurred. This outrage gave occasion afterwards for the confirmation of an edict, and compelled Charles Brimaeus, then governor of Friesland, as also Grosbeek before him, to take measures against the sacrilegious. At about this time, Borraeus relates, the exiled Frisians, as also those from the other provinces of Belgium, set out for Speyer, where the Diet of the Empire had been ordered by Maximilian II, and made supplication in this manner to Emperor Maximilian and to the Electors of Germany:

units.la: C
units.tr: C

units.la: VEnimus ad te Maximiliane Caesar, & Electores Principes, ut, quoniam horrenda Ferdinandi Albani tyrannide compulsi, exuti bonis ac patria extorres agimus, tuum subsidium & juxta clementissimorum Principum imploraremus, defenderemusque causam nostram adversus eos, qui speciem religionis, & sanctimoniae praeferentes, ambitiosis Romanorum Pontificum ingeniis subnixi Regum Principumque consiliis se intulerunt. Ab iis namq; profectum est, ut Inquisitio corrigendis Iudaeis paganisque reperta, in Christianos, & hodie in nos Frisios detorqueatur, eademque ipsa Carolo V. Caesare, post Philippo filio regnante, introducta, omnem nobis miseriam atque calamitatem advexerit. Ita qui spem acceperamus vitae libertatis, & ut ad exemplum Germanorum vestrorum, aut Gallici populi nullo discrimine sacra ac religiones nostras profiteremur, ita maxime in servitutem incidimus, nostris conscientiis intentatam, proclamatiq; sumus haeretici, rebelles, & seditiosi, ut nostrae innocentiae non unum crimen affingeretur. Tum in bona nostra, ac fortunas saevitum, & ne iis terminis inexplebilis saevitiae furor staret, postquam expilatas res nostras, fusum innocentium concivium sanguinem, denique temerata divina atque humana jura conspeximus, nostras cervices cruento adhuc tyranni gladio subtraximus, dulcissimaeque patriae, hoc, quod videtis, Caesar, Principesque, exilium antepositimus. Quod ipsum quoque, singulari patientia huc usque toleravimus, & quidem non alia fide, quam quod a Deo aeterna Providentiae ordinatione obvenire nobis crederemus, Deumque daturum aliquando rebus nostris eventum, & in hoc ipso exilio solatia tolerata adversitatis.
