Sed cruentis eius consilijs, sola, qui Leovardiæ erant, exulum intercessio tum obstitit. Quare jussum imperatumque militi, ferro parceret. Postquam illud vario sanguine pollutum in vaginas reconditum, tum licentia rapinis data, posteriora quoque scelera patefecit. Itaque fœdæ cædi, & flebili incendio miserrimæ etiam urbis sectio accessisset, nisi adventantium copiarum advolans rumor, quas fœderati ducebant, ab ulteriore nocendi decreto sanguinarium Valonum gregem revocasset.
units.tr: Henricus Bra relates that those soldiers who, as I mentioned, had withdrawn into the tower, reported the country folk's flight to their fellow soldiers, and, seeing the weakening of the citizens, abandoned the tower and joined the victors. Then, with a straw band fixed to their caps, a password was given for slaughter, and sixty horsemen who had come quickly from Groningen increased it with monstrous savagery. For, most of those who bore arms being slain, almost no one was spared, not even by age or sex, and bodies, mangled and wounded, were scattered through the streets, and much blood was poured into the flowing Ee. Then a fire shone forth worse than the slaughter itself, and many who, fleeing the danger of the sword, had taken refuge on the rooftops, driven down by the fumes and smoke of the fires burning beneath, fell into the hands of the most cruel enemies. They report that half-naked and still sickly, and then women in childbirth with their infants, were dragged into the open and shared the lot of the common danger; and that Roblesius himself, immoderate in anger, planned to destroy the town by sword and flame. But against his bloody designs, only the intercession of the exiles who were at Leeuwarden then stood in the way. Therefore it was ordered and commanded to the soldiers that they should spare the sword. When that blade, stained with various blood, had been returned to its scabbard, licence for plunder was then given, and it revealed the later crimes as well. And so the shameful slaughter and the lamentable fire would have been joined by the sack of the most wretched town, had not the rumour, flying in of the approaching forces which the Federated men led, called back the Walloon band of bloodthirsty men from the further decree of harm.

units.la: Doccomium Roblesium invadit.
units.tr: Roblesius attacks Dokkum.

units.la: Ferocia hostium.
units.tr: The ferocity of the enemy.

units.la: Doccomium capitur. set. Urbs in medijs flammis deserta, relicto tantum in præsidio, cum centum & quinquaginta armatis Montjoio.
units.tr: Dokkum is taken. The city, deserted in the midst of the flames, was left with only a garrison of one hundred and fifty armed men under Montjoie.

units.la: Interea fœderati, ductoribus pedestrium copiarum Ioanne Bonga, & Siccone Tyesfenio, ad tertium ab urbe lapidem noctem agebant, criminatiq; tarditatem suam, & sociorum simul fortunam Valones opperiebantur. Qui propterea refocillatis somno ac alimonia militum corporibus, victores & incendiarios assecuti, in ripa Eæ fluminis non parva strage fuderunt, prædaque spoliarunt. Cæteris non ausis resistere præceps fuga profuit, quâ palantes, & sparsi Leovardiam rediere, ubi Roblesius magnarum rerum consilia animo versans, ad iv. Kal. Sept. conventum Ordinum indixerat. Ea laniena istius vera facies fuit, quam jam ante prævisam in illius temporis commentariis fidissimus testis Henricus Bra annotavit. Quare nocturnos rumores, & ungularum pulsationes, hinnitusq; equorum auditos, visaque jam ante incendia commemorat. Fama fuit, Gisbertum, de quo dixi, Hollandum istius expeditionis auspicem, recedente æstu in vado Lavicæ amnis post circumventum, naso auribusq; mutilatum, dein confossum fuisse. quod Gerardum Deccomiensem hominem impensè regiæ parti deditum à Douwone Glinzio viro nobili captum, maloque navis adligatum glande plumbeâ confecissset. Glinzium ipsum mari res infæliciter gerentem, ac hostibus traditum porrectâ percussori cervice gloriosam mortem Groningæ oppetijsse. Tum Roblesius coacto Ordinum conventu, ad quem ex Oostergoïs Gerardum Iacobi, Antistitem Clarecampensem, Sceltonem Sceltamá, Gerbrandum Aytam, Heronem Burmaniam, è Westergoïs Ioannem Geelmuydanum, Præsulem Lidlumanum, Edzardum Grovensteinium Sceltonem Lyauckamam, Martinum Nitzenium, Sceltonem Tiardam, è Sylvestribus Fredericum Occonium Pastorem Oelanum, Annam Tarquinium, & Tinconem Andringham, ad viii. Kal. Sept. evocaverat, multa præfatus, tributa per Provinciam poposcit.
units.tr: Meanwhile the allies, under the foot commanders Johannes Bonga and Siccho Tyesfenius, were spending the night three miles from the city. They blamed their own slowness and waited for the Walloons, who were also their allies' fortune. Having refreshed the soldiers' bodies with sleep and food, the Walloons caught up with the victors and the arsonists and, on the bank of the river Ea, slaughtered a considerable number and plundered their spoils. Since the others did not dare to resist, headlong flight served them well; scattered and straggling, they returned to Leeuwarden, where Roblesius, turning over great plans in his mind, had called an assembly of the Estates for the 4th of the Kalends of September. That butchery was the true face of the man, which the most faithful witness Henricus Bra had already foreseen and noted in the records of that time. Hence he also records the nocturnal rumours, the beating of hooves, the neighing of horses heard, and the fires seen before. There was a report that Gijsbert, whom I mentioned, the Hollander who led that expedition, was captured by Douwe Glins, a nobleman, after being surrounded in the ford of the river Lauwers as the tide receded; that he was then mutilated of nose and ears and finally stabbed. It was said that Glins, a man deeply devoted to the royal party, had bound Gerard of Dokkum, who had been captured, to a mast and killed him with a leaden bullet. As for Glins himself, when he was ill-fated at sea and handed over to the enemy, he met a glorious death at Groningen, offering his neck to the executioner. Then Roblesius convened the assembly of the Estates, to which he had summoned from the Oostergo districts Gerard Jacobi, the abbot of Klaarkamp, Schelto Schelttama, Gerbrand Ayta, Hero Burmania; from Westergo Johannes Geelmuyden, the provost of Lidlum, Edzard Grovenstein, Schelto Liauckama, Martin Nitzen, Schelto Tiarda; and from the Sylvestri district Frederick Occo, the minister of Oeland, Anna Tarquinius, and Tinco Andringa, on the 8th of the Kalends of September. After a long preface he demanded taxes throughout the province.

units.la: Jam diu quippe perspectam fuisse erga Philippum Regem fidem atq; industriam suam, cum in comprimendis rebellibus, tum in conferendis de suo in publicum pecunijs. Cæterum nunc belli mole per Frisiam ardescentis exhaustum, sine majoris tributi subsidio opitulari rebus labantibus non posse. Ingressum quippe Provinciam Bronchorstium tria mox oppida, sedem bello, fœderi sociasse. Exin ne solâ Westergoâ se concluderet, Doccomium urbem portu commodam suam fecisse, jactoq; ibidem magnarum rerum fundamine, duo prælia non sine utriusq; partis clade sustinuisse. Fœderatos intra ipsa urbis mænia, suos ad Eam flumen deletos, neque dubitandum esse, quin atrocius post bellum cæsorum manes pro inferijs exacturi sint. Quod ut veris robustisque in posterum nervis trahi queat, non supplementis tantum imbecillium copiarum, sed novo milite, & adhoc pecuniâ opus esse, sine quâ nulla temporum ætas magnum aliquod & memorabile gesisset. Eius penuriâ licentiam militum, contemptum disciplinæ suboriri, bellumq; ipsum languore quodam & segniter tractum velut marcore, aut tabe suâ deficere. Quod ne deserere magno Philippi damno, ac infamiâ regij imperij cogatur, impulsas ærarij res grandi tributo levandas, sine quo CIↄ. Io. quo nec bellum geri, nec quies populo Frisico esse posset. Hæc fere LXXII. Roblesius. Cæterum Ordinum nomine, qui comparuerant, auditis Roblesij postulatis, tempus deliberandi petiere, eoque, ut præceps Roblesius erat, negato, in hunc modum responderunt.
units.tr: He said that his loyalty and diligence towards King Philip had been long observed, both in putting down rebels and in contributing money from his own resources to the public cause. But now, with the country exhausted by the weight of war blazing through Friesland, the failing cause could not be helped without a larger tax subsidy. Bronchorst had entered the province and had soon brought three towns, the seat of war, into alliance with the rebels. Then, so that he would not confine himself to Westergo alone, he had made Dokkum, a city convenient for its harbour, his own, and, laying there the foundation of great enterprises, had sustained two battles, not without loss on both sides. The allies, within the very walls of the city, had destroyed his men at the river Ea, and there was no doubt that after the war they would exact more savagely, as an offering to the dead, the blood of those slain. So that this might be drawn out with strong and lasting sinews in the future, not only reinforcements for the weakened troops were needed, but new soldiers and, besides, money, without which no age had ever accomplished anything great or memorable. For lack of it, the soldiers' licence and contempt for discipline would arise, and the war itself, dragged on in a kind of languor, would wither away from its own rot. Lest he be forced to abandon it, to the great loss and disgrace of the royal government of Philip, the finances of the treasury had to be relieved by a large tax, without which neither could the war be waged nor could the Frisian people have peace. These were roughly the words of Roblesius. Then the Estates, speaking through those who had appeared, after hearing Roblesius's demands, asked for time to deliberate; when this was refused, as Roblesius was headlong, they replied in the following manner.

units.la: Nec Statum exhaustæ Provinciæ nova onera, nec mobiles per Provinciam hominum animos nova tributi imperata ferre posse. Vastatam enim armis jam diu partium miserrimam patriam, tum fluctibus maris immersam, gravem annonam, & vix alendis familijs parem accepisse. Itaque curandum quam maxime, ne omnium rerum inopiæ, recens malum exactio Tributi accedat, exacerbandis illorum ingenijs, quibus omne immoderatum molestum esset, & qui per exempla edocti, expendere Præfecti imperia, & juxta consilia constituent. Esse enim in populo non tantum, sed & in Ordinum consessu, qui exigendas potius veteres accepti expensique tabulas, quam gravandam Provinciam novis exactionibus, censeant. Ærarium etiam ipsum tot annorum tributis auctum secreta dispendia pati, conversis in alios usus populi pecunijs, & promptissimâ largitione. Itacentum & viginti octo aureorum millia, non aliâ lege dependisse, quam ut amotâ ulteriori exactione, ingruente bello, aut aliâ gravi necessitate, infælici patriæ sanctius ærarium subveniret. Quapropter durum esse obliteratâ recentis liberalitatis memoriâ, novis adhuc tributis Provinciam gravare, regiumque militem adæsis per luxum stipendijs, per agros vagari privatorum possessionibus & domesticæ quieti gravem. Quæ incommoda cogitaret Roblesius Caroli Cæsaris actis, ac libertati adversa, quâ si redonare Frisiam posset, intestinis armis commotam, non defuturos Ordines adhibendis novæ temporum fælicitati fomentis. Paratos interim, in spem publicæ pacis tranquilitatisq; 24000. aureorum, quinq; cohortium stipendijs, intra trimestre assignare, cæteraq; facere quæ suæ potestatis, & debiti in Regem officij essent. Ita Ordinum nomine Scelto Scheltama, Valerius Cammingha, Scelto Liauckama, Edzardus Grovensteinius, Hero Burmania, Hector Abinga, Martinus Nitzenius, Gerbrandus Ayta, & Scelto Tiarda responderunt.
units.tr: The state of the exhausted province could bear no new burdens, nor could the minds of its people, easily stirred, bear new orders for taxes. For the wretched homeland, long laid waste by arms and by factions, and then submerged by the waves of the sea, had received a heavy harvest, barely enough to feed its households. Therefore great care must be taken that the recent evil of a tax levy not be added to the general scarcity, to exasperate the minds of those to whom everything immoderate is burdensome, and who, taught by experience, weigh the commands of their governors and shape their plans accordingly. For there are among the people, and also in the assembly of the Estates, men who think that old accounts of receipts and expenditures should be demanded rather than the province burdened with new exactions. The treasury itself, enlarged by the taxes of so many years, suffers secret wastes, its money being diverted to other uses of the people and to very ready largesse. Thus 28,000 gold pieces had been paid out under no other condition than that, with further exaction set aside, the sacred treasury would come to the aid of the unhappy homeland in the event of an impending war or some other grave necessity. Therefore it was hard, with the memory of recent generosity forgotten, to burden the province with yet more taxes, and for the royal soldier, with his pay squandered in luxury, to wander through the fields, a burden upon private estates and upon domestic peace. Roblesius should consider these disadvantages, which are contrary to the acts of Charles Caesar and to liberty; if he could restore Friesland to its quiet, the Estates, who would not be lacking, would apply the means to the new happiness of the times. Meanwhile they were ready, in hope of public peace and tranquillity, to assign 24,000 gold pieces within three months for the pay of five cohorts, and to do the other things that were within their power and due from their office towards the King. Thus on behalf of the Estates responded Schelto Schelttama, Valerius Cammingha, Schelto Liauckama, Edzard Grovenstein, Hero Burmania, Hector Abinga, Martin Nitzen, Gerbrand Ayta, and Schelto Tiarda.

units.la: Tum Roblesius dolore repulsæ, ac responso Ordinum turbatus, ad sueta bellorum conversus est, hostiliumque animorum faces, instar erratici ignis, per omnem Provinciam luxere. Quare & per Dongrios, direpto incensoq; Doccomio, non rusticæ tantum plebis civiumque, cæterum & religiosi ordinis notata, qui inter arma ne sacris quidem secessibus locisq; se tuebatur. Invenio in actis Henricum Kesselium, Doccomiensium Præsulem, cum cænobij, quod, D. Bonifacio erectum erat, primoribus Leovardiam se contulisse, usumque multorum præsulum, qui isthuc confugerant, conversatione in spem melioris tutiorisque fortunæ, sub armis Roblesij latuisse. Eundem quoque Kesselium ob intuta temporum, cuidam Taconi Haringio, qui Prioris titulo cænobio inter-erat, conferendi se in Omlandiam veniam fecisse, mutandæq; habitus potestatem concessisse. Adeo publicæ privatæque res, in tanto discriminum metu, necessitatis imperio subjacebant.
units.tr: Then Roblesius, troubled by the grief of rejection and by the answer of the Estates, turned to his customary methods of war, and the torches of hostile spirits, like wandering fire, blazed through the whole province. Hence, through the Dongeradeel districts, with Dokkum plundered and burned, the mark of the outrage fell not only on the country folk and citizens but also on the religious order, which even amid arms did not protect itself even in sacred retreats and places. I find in the records that Henricus Kessel, the abbot of Dokkum, had withdrawn with the leading men of the monastery, which had been founded in honour of St Boniface, to Leeuwarden, and that, living in company with many abbots who had fled there in hope of a better and safer fortune, he lay hidden under the arms of Roblesius. The same Kessel granted to a certain Tako Haring, who was prior of the monastery, permission to betake himself to Ommeland, and gave him power to change his habit, because of the unsafe condition of the times. So far public and private affairs, in such great fear of dangers, lay under the command of necessity.

units.la: Advenerat jam in Frisiam, cum septem Germanicarum cohortium auxilijs, iv. Eid. Sept. Iustus Scouwenburgius. Qui Snecæ magno cicivium applausu exceptus, obvias populi gratulationes in omen prosperi, actaelicis imperij vertebat. Neq; absimile studium alijs in locis, sed praesertim apud Franequeranos sibi augurabatur, quo contendere, ut aulae suae ac juxta bello per Frifiam sedem figeret, omni cum aulico comitatu & praesidio militari parabat. Sed itineri accinctum novae Praefecturae negotia Snecae attinuerunt. Itaq; datis confestim litteris foederatarum civitatum Legatos Snecam evocavit, ut de potestate sibi ab Aurantio assignata e diplomate cognoscerent, quod regium Philippi nomen declinandis illorum temporum odiis adhuc praeferebat. In eo namque praedicabat Aurantius, non alia de causa susceptum a fe bellum esse, quam ut a Ferdinandi Albani, & Hispanorum immani dominatu populum Belgicum liberaret, omniaq; gentis jura, & immunitates a majoribus integras, incorruptasque aslereret. Ita tot annorum curas, & impendia principem animum sustinuisse, eoq; tandem propitia divini numinis ordinatione rem perductam, ut plurimae per Brabantiam, Hannoniam, Hollandiam & Zelandiam urbes, exclusis, aut ejectis praesidijs, libertatem amplexae sanctissima, & carissima quaeq; pignora suae fidei commiserint. Et quoniam compertum gentem Frisicam peregrinae dominationis insolentiaeq; pertaesam, cupidine quoque potiundae libertatis ferri, ac auxilia rogare, idcirco Justum Scouwenburgium affinem suum virum militiae egregium, & multo rerum usu exercitatum in Frisiam misisse. Qui quoque ut effectum dare idipsum commodius queat, potestatem ei fecisse contrahendi copias, ut ijs adjutus commodare auxilium possit libertatis desideria profesis. Tum ne miles stipendia per Frisiam faciens, aut post autorandus licentiae proximus, & sine disciplinae sit metu, eidem Scouwenburgio jus atque autoritatem dedisse, tam autorandi, quam recensendi, & corrigendi milites, caeteraque curandi, quae e commodo ac usu publico videbuntur. Rogare se propterea Consules, Scabinos, Rectores urbium, cives, singulosque Provincialium, tribunis vero militiique mandare ut morem ei gerant, praestentque subsidia desideratae diu libertati opportuna. Diploma in castris ad Aldkerckam Geldrorum Prid. Eid. Iul. perscriptum. Quo perlecto Snecenses caeterique foederatorum legati voce acclamarunt, Iustusque Scouwenburgius Propraefectus majoris inter Flevum Lavicamque Frisiae renunciatus est. Aurantius ipse, sive quod proxumas majoribus Frisijs ditiones Philippi nomine trans Flevum teneret, seu quod ex pacto cum Carolo IX. Gallorum rege Lutetiae inito Frisiam sortitus esset, potius sibi per Provinciam imperium reservavit. Tum Scouwenburgius, juramento, quod ipse dixerat, a foederatis civitatum Legatis accepto, relicta Sneca Bolsuerdiam contendit, magnoq; rerum apparatu una cum Diderico Bronchorstio per Arenariam portam urbem ingressus, in Heramaea arce consedit. Bronchorstius subdelegato post Scouwenburgium imperio usurus Jongamaea se clausit. Ubi dum bellum segnius trahunt, Gaspar Roblesius, cuius ipsem jam ante praeconceperat, occupandae Franequerae consilium admovit. Quare praesidiario milite Harlinga clam evocato, medio fere Septembri, naves quasdam cohortibus peditum complevit, ac Franequeram ablegavit, quam
units.tr: Justus Schouwenburg had already arrived in Friesland, on the 4th of the Ides of September, with the help of seven German cohorts. Received at Sneek with great applause from the citizens, he turned the people's congratulations that met him into an omen of prosperous and happy government. He expected a similar zeal in other places, but especially among the Franekerers, to whom he hastened, intending to set up his court there and to fix the seat of his government in Friesland, and he was preparing with the full court retinue and military guard. But the business of his new prefecture kept him at Sneek, girded for the journey. Therefore, sending letters at once, he summoned the delegates of the confederated states to Sneek, so that they might learn from the charter the authority assigned to him by Orange, a document which still bore the royal name of Philip, to avoid the hatreds of those times. For Orange had declared in it that the war had been undertaken by him for no other reason than to free the Belgian people from the monstrous domination of Ferdinand of Alba and the Spaniards, and to keep intact and uncorrupted all the rights and immunities of the nation from their ancestors. Thus, he said, the prince had sustained the cares and expenses of so many years, and at last, by the favourable ordering of divine providence, the matter had been brought to such a point that many cities throughout Brabant, Hainault, Holland and Zeeland, having expelled or ejected their garrisons, had embraced liberty and entrusted to its good faith their most sacred and dearest pledges. And since it had been learned that the Frisian nation, weary of foreign domination and insolence, was also carried by the desire to gain liberty, and was asking for aid, he had therefore sent Justus Schouwenburg, his kinsman, an outstanding man in war and practised in much experience of affairs, into Friesland. So that he might the more conveniently carry this out, he had given him power to raise troops, so that, aided by them, he could bring help to those who professed desires for liberty. Further, so that the soldier serving in pay throughout Friesland should not, after being discharged, be close to licence and without fear of discipline, he had given the same Schouwenburg the right and authority both to discharge, to review and to correct the soldiers, and to take care of other matters that seemed for the public advantage and use. He therefore asked the consuls, the magistrates, the governors of the cities, the citizens and each of the provincials, and ordered the tribunes and soldiers, to comply with him and to give the aid suitable to the long-desired liberty. The charter was drawn up in the camp at Aldekerk in Guelders, on the day before the Ides of July. When it had been read, the delegates of Sneek and the other confederated states acclaimed it with one voice, and Justus Schouwenburg was proclaimed governor of the greater Friesland between the Vlie and the Lauwers. Orange himself, either because he held the districts nearest to greater Friesland across the Vlie in the name of Philip, or because he had been allotted Friesland by agreement made at Paris with Charles IX, king of the French, kept the government of the province for himself. Then Schouwenburg, having received the oath, which he himself had dictated, from the delegates of the confederated states, left Sneek and made for Bolsward; with a great array of equipment, together with Dirk Bronckhorst, he entered the city through the Sand Gate and took up residence in the castle of Hemaa. Bronckhorst, intending to exercise a subordinate command after Schouwenburg, shut himself up in Jonghema. While they dragged out the war rather sluggishly, Gaspar Roblesius, who had already conceived the plan beforehand, brought forward his purpose of seizing Franeker. Therefore, having secretly summoned the garrison soldiers from Harlingen, about the middle of September he filled some ships with cohorts of foot soldiers and sent them to Franeker, which the allies, with the small garrison that Bronckhorst had placed there, were defending. Roblesius had ordered the Harlingen garrison to attack the city from the west at a signal, and the others, whom he had sent from Leeuwarden, to attack from the east, while the waterways, blocked or dammed on every side, by which the approaches...

units.la: Scouwenburgius Praefectus cIↄ. Io. LXXII. quam non numeroso praesidio, quod Bronchorstius ibi posuerat, fa-derati tuebantur. Roblesius praesidiarios Harlinganos dato signo ad occidentem, caeteros, quos Leovardia miserat, ab ortu oppugnare urbem jusserat. Caeterum obseptis undiq; aut oppilatis rivis, per quos aditus ad urbem non patebat, inritum omne negotium fuit, copiaeq; Valonum Aengiumano ac Lidlumano caenobijs, tum Berlicomio vico tumulutario opere circumducto, ijs in locis praesidia egere.
units.tr: Scouwenburgius, Governor, 1572: the confederates held Franeker, which Bronchorstius had garrisoned with no large force. Roblesius ordered the Harlingen garrison to attack the city from the west at a given signal, and the rest, whom Leeuwarden had sent, to attack it from the east. But the roads and streams through which access to the city lay were blocked or obstructed, so the whole enterprise came to nothing. The Walloon troops took up positions at the monasteries of Aengium and Lidlum and at the village of Berlikum, which they fortified with makeshift earthworks.

units.la: Igitur Roblesius spe sua frustratus, ut Bolsuerdiorum naves, quae stationem in portu Maccumano habebant, diriperet, ac annonae, qua maxime premebatur, consuleret, adornatis Harlingae liburnicis militem imposuit, Maccomiumque devexit, quo & Iustus Scouwenburgius, perceptâ istarum rerum famâ, sexcentos quoque pedites Bolsuerdiâ amandaverat. Quorum adventu territi Valones in altum se receperunt, regressisque Bolsuerdiam Scouwenburgicis, mox littus praelegentes naves depraedati sunt. Emissarium ipsum depressis per onera navigijs obtuiatum est.
units.tr: Roblesius, disappointed in his hope, then fitted out warships at Harlingen. He put soldiers aboard them and sailed to Makkum, intending to plunder the Bolsward ships that lay at anchor in that harbour and to relieve the food shortage, which pressed hard on him. Justus Scouwenburgius, on hearing of these moves, had also sent six hundred foot soldiers from Bolsward. Frightened by their arrival, the Walloons withdrew to the open sea. Then, returning to Bolsward, the Scouwenburgians plundered the ships that were sailing along the coast. The outlet of the river was blocked by ships sunk under their cargo.

units.la: Dein Scouwenburgius Bolsuerdiam nova munitionum forma circumscribi fecit, habitoque Senatus oppidani conventu Dominicum Hottingham, & Iacobum Iacobaeum ad Gulielmum Aurantium Hornam in minores Frisios misit, qui de statu urbis rerumq; per Frisiam referrent, auxiliaque orarent. Quae cum ad manum Aurantius non haberet, Gallici furoris interventu, & universi exercitus missione debilitatus, solam spem praestandi subsidij fecit, Legatosque dimisit.
units.tr: Next Scouwenburgius had Bolsward fortified anew in a new style of defences. He held a meeting of the town council and sent Dominicus Hottinga and Jacobus Jacobaeus to William of Orange at Horn in Lower Friesland, to report on the state of the town and of affairs throughout Friesland and to beg for help. Since Orange did not have help at hand, and was weakened by the French madness and by the disbanding of his whole army, he held out only the hope of assistance and dismissed the envoys.

units.la: Fama traditum est Tiallengum Eysingham virum Nobilem, & juris scientiâ eximium Ludovici Nassovij expeditionis, & fortunae consortem Vesaliae Clivorum in exilio tum agentem, auditâ Galliae laniena perturbatione mentis concussum, nefarijque sceleris indignatione apoplexiâ, quod de Philippo Burgundo Meierus scribit, correptum, repentinâ morte exspirasse. Tum Iustus Scouwenburgius responso Legatorum accepto, & ordinatis Bolsuerdiae rebus Franequeram properavit, ingressusque urbem, victoris magis, quam recentis praefecturae fortunâ usus est. Miles quippe modestiae, aut disciplinae nullius retinens, ac in omnem insolentiam effusus, rapinis urbem & juxta imperium Praefecti foedavit, suburbanis locis saedo incendio vastatis. Unde multorum odijs expositus, metuensque conspirationis, regiae partis plerosque edicto urbe expulit, bonis eorum, nisi saniora consilia induerent, fisco adjudicatis. Caeteris Pontificijs, arma detracta sunt, ipseque Scouwenburgius perdomatâ urbe, & validiore praesidio impo-sito Siardamea arce se tutatus est, in quâ Sedem imperio, & simul Praefecturae destinabat. Mox missó in Geesterlandiam, ac Stellinguerfios milite crates gerrasque muniendis locis comparari jussit, Bolsuerdijsque praecingendorum firmo opere maenium curam imposuit.
units.tr: It is reported that Tiallingius Eysinga, a nobleman distinguished in law, who had shared the fortunes of Louis of Nassau's expedition and was then living in exile at Wesel in Cleves, was struck by the news of the slaughter in France and the disturbance of mind it caused, and, moved by indignation at the wicked crime, was seized by apoplexy, as Meierus writes of Philip of Burgundy, and died suddenly. Then Justus Scouwenburgius, having received the envoys' reply and settled affairs at Bolsward, hurried to Franeker. On entering the town he made use of the fortune of a conqueror rather than of a newly installed governor. For the soldiers, retaining no discipline or restraint and given over to every kind of insolence, laid waste the town with plunder, and, by the governor's command, ravaged the outlying districts with fire and sword. Thus exposed to the hatred of many, and fearing a conspiracy, he expelled most of the royalist party from the town by edict, and had their goods confiscated to the treasury unless they adopted more sensible views. The other Papists were disarmed. Scouwenburgius himself, having subdued the town and left a stronger garrison in it, secured himself in the citadel at Sneek, where he intended to set up his seat of government and at the same time the seat of the governorship. Soon after, he sent men into Geesterland and the Stellingwerf district and ordered hurdles and wicker frames to be made to fortify the places, and he put in charge of the work the strengthening of the walls of Bolsward and its surroundings with solid masonry.

units.la: Senatum quoq; Provincialem tam dicundi juris causâ, quam ne rude imperium peregrinis arbitris staret, Franequerae constituit, Harinstumque Glinzium Ripensem virum Nobilem & eruditum, Praesidem istius Ordinis autoravit. Praeclaros quoque viros & peritiâ legum eximios Barthium Idzardam, Econem Isbrandum, Fecconem Rhalam collegas ei adjunxit, Fredericumque Inthimam Iureconsultum procuraratorem fisci designavit. Mox Bolsuerdiæ, quæ tum octo pedestrium cohortium præsidio tenebatur, edictum recitari fecit, tribunosque copiarum, ut & militem sarcinas colligere, ac extemplo ad signa convenire jussit. Cæterum miles, secreto, ut creditum fuit, centurionum instinctu stipendia, & residuum æs contumaciæ obtendens, seditiosis consilijs occupabatur, metumq; direptionis omnium animis inferebat. Quare Magistratus litteras Franequeram ad Scouwenburgium ocyus dedit, quibus remedium orabat sedandis militum animis conveniens.
units.tr: He also set up a provincial senate at Franeker, both for the administration of justice and so that the new government would not stand without experienced judges from outside. He appointed as its president Harinus Glinzius, a nobleman of Rippen (?) and a learned man. He also added to him as colleagues the distinguished men, eminent in legal learning, Bartius Idzarda, Econ Isbrand and Feccon Rhala, and he appointed Frederick Inthima, a jurisconsult, as procurator of the treasury. Soon after, he had an edict read out at Bolsward, which was then held by a garrison of eight companies of foot, and ordered the tribunes of the troops to make the soldiers pack their baggage and assemble at once at the standards. But the soldiers, it was believed, were secretly stirred up by the centurions, and, pretending that their pay and the remaining money owed them was the reason for their obstinacy, they were occupied with seditious plans and spread fear of plunder among everyone. Therefore the magistrates quickly sent a letter to Scouwenburgius at Franeker, begging for a remedy suited to calming the soldiers' minds.

units.la: Itaque Scouwenburgius quatuor cohortes Bolsuerdiâ Ripam, ubi stativa castrorum posuerat, evocavit, seditiosamque multitudinem ex instituto veteri locorum spatiis discrevit. Castra verò quæ Ripæ tantum sex cohortium habebat Scouwenburgius, ut luxu diffluebant, ita nullis ferè excubijs vigilijsq; asservabantur. Quippe miles potare, aleam ludere, & somnum ducere, Præfecti procul signis pavidi & inertes suffugia periculis facere. Itaq; Valones, cito agmine Beriicomio, ubi præsidium tenebant, egressi, in somno ac luxu graves Scouwenburgicos impetum fecere, pugnâque tumultuariè commissâ, castris exutos in fugam dedere. Cæsorum par ferè numerus, gloria dispar fuit, Valonesque prædam, quam nacti erant, & simul cadavera sociorum Berlicomium devecta, sepulchrali honore terræ mandavere.
units.tr: So Scouwenburgius called four companies from Bolsward to Rijp, where he had established the camp's quarters, and he separated the seditious crowd by the old custom of assigning them places. Scouwenburgius held at Rijp a camp of only six companies, but, as it was dissolute in its luxury, so it was guarded by almost no sentries or night watches. For the soldiers drank, gambled with dice and slept, while the governor, timid and idle, far from the standards, made hiding places out of danger. So the Walloons, leaving quickly from Berlikum where they held a garrison, fell with great force on the Scouwenburgians, heavy with sleep and luxury; the battle was joined in disorder, and they drove them from the camp in flight. The number of the slain was nearly equal, but the glory was unequal. The Walloons carried off the booty they had taken and the bodies of their comrades back to Berlikum, and gave them burial with funeral honours.

units.la: Heymannus notat Tiallengum Andringam virum nobilem isto conflictu cecidisse, sparsaque ignobili fugâ in diversa cohortes sub ipsos Bolsuerdiæ muros suggressos, fædi pavoris ignominiâ, & per nuperæ seditionis memoriam urbe prohibitas cænobium Oeganum expilasse.
units.tr: Heymannus notes that Tiallingius Andringa, a nobleman, fell in that clash, and that the scattered cohorts, having rushed under the very walls of Bolsward in disgraceful flight, and being shut out of the town because of the memory of the recent mutiny, plundered the monastery at Oegeum, shamed by the disgrace of their foul panic.

units.la: Mox sacrâ supellectile stipendijs applicatâ eosdem Scouwenburgicos non petita missione, exleges & sacramenti oblitos omni vi ac insolentiâ perpetratâ Cuneram perfugisse. Ita defectione imbellium copiarum Scouwenburgici exercitus robur enervatum. Quâ re perceptâ Iustus Scouwenburgius inter luxum, & epulas tempus apud Franequeranos trahens, metuensque ne Valones victoriâ elati Snecam aut Bolsuerdiam occuparent, ad Didericum Bronchorstium & Titum Hettingham, qui Snecæ præsidium tenebat, ocyus litteras dedit, quibus fidelem locorum custodiam imperabat. Quamobrem Bolsuerdiæ militaribus vigilijs excubiæ civium commissæ, copiarumque reliquiæ, jam ante Ripâ fugatæ, tutandis suburbanis locatæ.
units.tr: Soon after, having applied the sacred furniture of the churches to pay the soldiers, the same Scouwenburgians, without asking for discharge, lawless and forgetful of their oath, committed every kind of violence and insolence and fled to Kuinre. Thus by the desertion of the unwarlike troops, the strength of the Scouwenburgian army was sapped. When Justus Scouwenburgius learned of this, spending his time among luxury and feasting at Franeker, and fearing lest the Walloons, elated by victory, should seize Sneek or Bolsward, he quickly sent letters to Didericus Bronchorstius and Titus Hettinga, who held the garrison at Sneek, ordering them to guard the places faithfully. For this reason the night watches of Bolsward were entrusted to the citizens with military sentries, and the remnants of the troops, already put to flight from Rijp, were stationed to defend the outlying districts.

units.la: Bronchorstius quoque ne Valones circumjacentia loca munirent, commeatumque aut annonam urbi præcluderent, cænobium Floridi Campi, quod in ortum Solis æstivum situm est, diripi fecit, seditiosamque & infidam multitudinem facta prædandi veniâ placavit. Tum Scouwenburgius, etsi torpido otio, & diurno luxu attineretur, more eorum, qui commessationibus consilia belli immiscent, tribunos militarium cohortium in Siardamæam arcem VIII. Kal. Nov. convocavit, eosque hoc modo allocutus est.
units.tr: Bronchorstius also, so that the Walloons might not fortify the surrounding places and cut off supplies or food from the town, had the monastery of Floridus Campus, which lies towards the summer sunrise, plundered, and he appeased the seditious and faithless multitude by granting them leave to plunder. Then Scouwenburgius, although held back by sluggish idleness and daily luxury, in the manner of those who mix plans of war with drinking parties, summoned the tribunes of the military cohorts to the citadel at Sneek on the 8th day before the Kalends of November, and addressed them in this way.

units.la: Res nostras, Commilitones, non parum accisas Ripensis clades, & flagitiosæ, quæ Cuneram petiit, multitudinis desertio fecit. Reparare collapsa, quam tueri parta majoris semper gloriæ apud fortes viros fuit, quibus animus ex periculo increvit. Nec detrimenta cladis istius
units.tr: Our affairs, fellow soldiers, have been not a little damaged by the defeat at Rijp and by the desertion of the disgraceful multitude which made for Kuinre. It has always been a greater glory among brave men to repair what has fallen than to defend what has been won, for their courage grows out of danger. Nor do I dwell only on the losses of that defeat

units.la: tius tantum retenseo. Spectate socios vestros eadem sacramenta vobiscum profes-sos, campis dispersos jacere, & inhumata cadavera tabo squallentia, vulnerumque notis deformia longiorem vobis ignaviam exprobrare. Virtute ac animis, Commilitones, opus est, ut mearum rerum fortunam reparetis, sociorum vero manes cede hostium ultum eatis, quos non magno numero Aengiumano Cænobio conseptos vobis ostendo. Expedito itinere opprimetis imparatos, ac nuperâ prosperitate securos.
units.tr: I dwell only on the losses of that defeat. Look at your comrades, who took the same oaths with you, lying scattered over the fields, their unburied corpses rotting with filth and disfigured by the marks of their wounds, and reproaching you with your long inaction. Courage and spirit are needed, fellow soldiers, so that you may repair the fortune of my affairs; and that you may avenge the shades of your comrades by the slaughter of the enemy, whom I show you enclosed in small numbers at the monastery of Aengium. By a quick march you will overwhelm them unprepared and secure in their recent success.

units.la: Itaque tum præsidiarij justo agmine in cænobium Aengiumanum non segni itinere effusi sunt, congressique cum Valonum cohorte, ducentos ad internecionem delevere.
units.tr: So the garrison troops, in a proper column, poured out with no sluggish march towards the monastery of Aengium, and, engaging the Walloon cohort there, destroyed two hundred of them to the last man.

units.la: Scribit fidus autor vix superfuisse, qui editæ stragis nuntium ad socios perferrent, cæterosque Valones præsidium Berlicomij habentes, metu ferè exanimatos Leovardiam confugisse. Victores Scouwenburgici Franequeram regressi, quod oppidum ut gravi tum præsidio, ita annonæ quoq; penuria premebatur. Quapropter Scouwenburgius comparatis ad id navigijs, amotoq; Leovardiam Valones ratus, in Biltanum agrum progredi copias jussit, frumentationemque militi imperavit. Ubi verò obseptos per hostem viarum aditus idem miles intellexit, omisso frumentandi consilio, pavore correptus pedem retulit, ac in urbem se recepit, nuperæque victoriæ decus in eodem loco, quo quæsitum erat, turpi fugâ fædavit.
units.tr: A trustworthy author writes that scarcely anyone survived to carry news of the slaughter to their comrades, and that the other Walloons, who held the garrison at Berlikum, fled to Leeuwarden, almost dead with fear. The Scouwenburgian victors returned to Franeker, a town then pressed both by a heavy garrison and by a shortage of food. Therefore Scouwenburgius, having prepared ships for the purpose and thinking that the Walloons had withdrawn to Leeuwarden, ordered the troops to advance into the Biltan country and commanded the soldiers to forage. But when the same soldiers learned that the approaches to the roads were blocked by the enemy, they gave up the plan of foraging, were seized with panic, turned back and withdrew into the town, and by a shameful flight they disgraced the glory of their recent victory on the very spot where it had been won.

units.la: Heymannus notat, partium manus eo quoque tempore commissas, ac ducentos schlopetos à fugientibus Scouwenburgicis projectos Valonibus obvenisse. Tum Franequerani omissis in remotiora expeditionibus domesticæ securitati consuluere. Itaque miles per Provinciam sparsus in hyberna passim reductus est; ac Franequera Præfecti & juxta belli primaria sedes amplo præsidio firmata. Cui rei asperum vel maximè gelu v. Eid. Octob. flante Cæcia, dein Euro surgens causam dedit. Tanto quippe & tam immani frigore adultum autumni tempus desævijt, ut tentoria militem non terrent, ullisq; operimentis ab ambientis injuria corpora præservarentur. Quare continui frigoris intemperie fluens aër molestiam militi, civi verò periculum attulit, quod post solidissimam glaciem cælo decidua altissimæ nives auxerunt. Opertis namque fossarum incilium-que cavitatibus Euri vehementiâ muris urbium adjecta nix, adsurgentes clementer colles, & simul metum adferebat, qui sparsis de adventu Roblesij rumoribus Franequeram per urbem magno tum terrore grassabatur. Igitur Senatus Oppidani Edicto, quod Scouwenburgius suasisse credebatur, omnis fossæ urbicæ glacies transversim secta, collectæq; haustris aquæ, dein præruptô valli adjectæ inibique concretæ, glabritiem simul & securitatem ab hostibus dedêre.
units.tr: Heymannus notes that at this time too the forces of the opposing party engaged, and that two hundred muskets, thrown away by the fleeing Scouwenburgians, fell into the hands of the Walloons. Then the Franeker men, giving up distant expeditions, looked to the safety of their homeland. So the soldiers, scattered through the province, were led back to their winter quarters everywhere, and Franeker, the governor's seat and the chief base of the war, was strengthened with a large garrison. The harsh frost, especially fierce on the eve of the Ides of October with the wind blowing from the north-east and then from the east, gave cause for this. For the autumn season raged with such a severe and monstrous cold that tents did not protect the soldiers, and bodies were not kept safe from the harm of the air even with any coverings. Thus the air, flowing with the constant bitterness of the frost, brought discomfort to the soldiers and danger to the citizens; and after the solid ice, the falling snow from the sky increased it, the deepest snows. For the snow, driven by the violence of the east wind against the city walls, filled the hollows of the ditches and moats and the gently rising hills, and at the same time brought a fear which, since rumours of Roblesius's approach had been spread, was then spreading with great terror through Franeker. Therefore by an edict of the town council, which Scouwenburgius was believed to have advised, all the ice of the city moat was cut across, the collected water was drawn off, and then, after a steep rampart was added and the water froze in it, the smoothness and safety from the enemy were given.

units.la: Tum Scouwenburgius longioris moræ incapacem rerum suarum angustiam reputans, mittendos denuò, etsi media brumâ, ad Aurantium Legatos censuit, qui auxilia rogarent. Quare è fœderatâ nobilitate populoque Franequerano Serapius Galama, Iulius Bottnia, Siuckius Emingha, & Sibrandus Richæus Iureconsultus designati. Qui acceptis Iusti Scouwenburgij sociorumque fiduciarijs litteris Bolluerdiam profecti tabulas mandatorum signari per Bolsuerdios fecere, adscitisq, in comitatum eius urbis, ut & Snecensium, primarijs viris, conducto Mac- comij navigio Enchusam adpulere, littora majoris Frisiæ contra sitam. Deïn facto per glaciem (adulta namque hyems erat) pedestri itinere Harlemum perrexere, quo in loco Gulielmus Aurantius momenta rerum versabat. Quo pro more salutato fiduciarias litteras legati exhibuere, ac Sibrandus Richæus vir insignis & juxta facundus, hunc in modum disseruit.
units.tr: Then Scouwenburgius, reckoning that his straitened affairs could not bear a long delay, resolved to send envoys again to Orange to ask for aid, although it was the middle of winter. Accordingly, from the allied nobility and the people of Franeker, Serapius Galama, Iulius Bottnia, Siuckius Emingha and Sibrandus Richaeus, a jurist, were chosen. Having received the letters of trust from Justus Scouwenburgius and his associates, they set out for Bolsward and had their letters of commission sealed by the Bolsward men. They took on as companions in that city, and also from Sneek, leading men, hired Maccomius's boat, and landed at Enchusa, on the shore of Greater Friesland opposite. Then, across the ice (for the winter had grown hard), they went on foot to Haarlem, where William of Orange was at that time directing affairs. There, after greeting him in the customary way, the envoys presented their letters of trust, and Sibrandus Richaeus, a distinguished man and a fluent speaker, made the following speech.

units.la: DE conditione suorum temporum quesli sæpe plurimi, Princeps, sed privatis querelis, ac mulicbribus lamentis ægritudinem publicam non savere. Namque quod alij direptas domos, exustas villas plorent, privatis damnis dedere, non versis animis in publici discriminis contemplationem. Prudentiores verò quique postpositâ rerum familiarium jactura patriæ juxta suæ, & avitæ, in quâ nati essent, libertatis curam habuere, ne quid ea mali per civiles discordias, aut vim externam pateretur. Hac ratione ab excessu etiam Philippi regis in Hispaniam sub Arembergio Præsecto caterisque extiterunt, qui Episcopi ac Inquisitorum ordinationibus obloquerentur, nobilique virtute arma armis opponerent. Ab eo tempore varià fortunâ habiti Frisij sumus, quos in quantum Scouwenburgij ac Bronchorstij adventus erexerat, tantum Doccumanæ Stauricæque clades nos depressere. Quas reparare nostræ potestatis non est, Princeps, nedum retinere quod nostrum per arma fecimus sine auxilijs, quorum causa hæc Legatio instituta. Nam plures copias per Provinciam colligere, ut nec tutum, ita ærarium, & impulsæ res non ferunt, quas rapina hostium, & infestum fluctibus mare exhausit. Istis malis defectio cohortium accessit, quæ sacramentum, & simul Frisiæ terminum transgressæ animos perfidos alio terrarum, atque signa verterunt. Quæ nisi suppleantur ocyus, Princeps, de patriâ nostrâ actum erit. Eius rei testes nostras & simul Iusti Scouwenburgij affinis tui litteras exhibemus, ne videamur famâ auxisse periculum, & nostræ imbecillitatis iniqui æstumatores esse. Cæteri mortales adversa sæpe silentio texere, nobis prospera tacentur, quoniam omnium rerum maxime autem auxiliorum egentes sumus. Quæ si procures Princeps, spe melioris fati nos donabis, mori paratos non servire.
units.tr: Prince, many people have often complained about the state of our times, but with private grievances and womanish laments they have not relieved the public sickness. For while some weep over plundered houses and burned farms, they have treated these as private losses, and have not turned their minds to considering the public danger. The wiser men, however, have set aside the loss of their property and cared for the freedom of their country, which is as much their own and their fathers', where they were born, so that it may suffer no harm from civil discord or foreign force. On this principle, since the departure of King Philip for Spain, under Arenberg as governor and others, men arose who opposed the decrees of the bishops and inquisitors and met arms with noble courage. From that time we Frisians have been held in varied fortune: as the coming of Scouwenburgius and Bronchorst raised us up, so the defeats at Dokkum and Stavoren have cast us down. We are not able, Prince, to repair these losses, much less to keep what we have won by arms, without help, and it is for this reason that this embassy has been undertaken. For we cannot gather larger forces throughout the province; our treasury will not allow it, and our circumstances, shattered by enemy plunder and a sea hostile with its floods, will not bear it. To these evils has been added the desertion of the cohorts, who, breaking their oath and crossing the boundary of Friesland, have turned their faithless minds and standards elsewhere. Unless these losses are quickly made good, Prince, our homeland will be lost. As proof of this we present our letters and those of your relative Justus Scouwenburgius, so that we may not seem to have exaggerated the danger by rumour, or to be unfair judges of our own weakness. Other people often hide their misfortunes in silence, but we conceal our prosperity, since we are in the greatest need of everything, and especially of help. If you provide it, Prince, you will give us hope of a better fate, and we are ready to die rather than live in servitude.

units.la: Cæterum Aurantium ut ante Gallici fæderis tristissima concussio, ita tum hostium res prosperæ, fuga quoque & desertio Gulielmi Bergensis incapacem mittendis auxilijs faciebant. Quare Scouwenburgius habere intra Provinciam delectus constituit, datisque ad Bolsuerdios litteris, de conscribendis ocysime equitum peditumque copijs velut extremi periculi remedio hortatus est. Modum quoque cogendi auxilia non ineptè perscripsit, quo è gente aut familiâ suâ fœderata nobilitas, & potentissimi agrariorum cogere, ac armare rusticæ plebis delectos jubebantur. Tum de tributis addidit, quæ nobili viro Edoni Heringæ & Iacobo Iacobæo ærarij tribunis pendi ocyus jubebat, quod sine ijs magnarum rerum, quas animo agitaret, inritos conatus duceret. Quibus omnibus Vibrandus Aylva vir clarorum natalium, & Snecensium Oldermannus, fidem in Senatu faciebat, ac duas equitum turmas apud Scotanos in Sylvestribus fœderatæ militiæ, adscriptas menstruo sti- penpendio autorandas esse. Rationes quoque eius rei in aerarium perse-rendas, ne quis defectioni seditionique locus esse possit, & ne bellum sine disciplinâ habeatur, perennitatis & boni ordinis custode.
units.tr: Meanwhile, just as the disastrous shock of the French alliance had kept Orange from sending help earlier, so now the enemy's successes, and also the flight and desertion of William of Bergen, made it impossible to send aid. Accordingly Scouwenburgius resolved to hold levies within the province, and by letter to the men of Bolsward urged them to raise horse and foot as quickly as possible, as the remedy for extreme danger. He also set out, not unskilfully, the method of raising troops: the allied nobility and the most powerful landholders were ordered to levy and arm picked men from their own clans and households, and from the rural commons. He added a note about taxes, which he ordered to be paid promptly to the noble Edo Heringa and Jacob Jacobaeus, treasury officers, since, without this money, he considered his great projects would come to nothing. Vibrandus Aylva, a man of distinguished birth, and the alderman of Sneek, vouched for all these matters in the council, and declared that two troops of horse were to be enlisted among the Scotani in the woodlands of the allied militia and paid a monthly wage. The accounts of this matter were also to be entered in the treasury, so that no one might have grounds for rebellion or sedition, and so that the war might not be conducted without discipline, the guardian of order and lasting peace.

units.la: Quod postulatum Scouwenburgij approbasse Bolsuerdios reperio, pactumque eâ de re inter agrarios fæderatosq; oppidanos initum, subscriptione publicâ roborarum fuisse. Sed ut nihil constans ac stabile in rebus humanis, ita concordiam fæderis, & spem surgentis Reipub. Iusti Scouwenburgij perfidia concussit. Qui cumulato grandi per Frisiam tributo, sex cohortibus peditum stipatus, desertâ velut in incendio Franequerâ Maccomium duxit, novoque ibi & tumultuario opere inchoato per Worcomios tendens signa Sylvestribus intulit, ac si equitum, de quibus dixi, turmis adjutus, de obsidendâ Leovardia Provinciae metropoli, aut magnarum rerum caeptandis consilijs cogitaret. Neque aliud plenae fiduciâ hominum mentes suspicabantur, cum is relicto Bolsuerdiae in praesidijs Diderico Bronchorstio Nedermormterio, Franequerae Docone Martna, Snecae Tito Hettingha, Praefecturae suae & muneris desertor, post gravissimas exactiones instar fugitivi, decesit. Direpta cohortium vexilla, & militum in diversa se spargentium furor parvo aere redemptus est. Ipse inglorius, & diffisus etiam suis, celerrimo equo per Tencteros vectus, nocte illuni in interiorem Westphaliam se abdidit, passurus alias discrimen, ac enormis perfidiae illustres poenas daturus. Cuius faedum è Provincia discessum magna rerum per Frisiam mutatio secuta. Gasparus namque Roblesius de fuga Iusti Scouwenburgij certior factus, relictis mediterraneis ac Leovardia urbe, copias Harlingam confestim duxit, positoque ibidem pro ratione loci praesidio cohortes aliquot Valonum Maccomium praemisit.
units.tr: I find that the Bolsward men approved Scouwenburgius's demand, and that an agreement on this matter was made between the landholders and the allied townsmen and confirmed by public signature. But just as nothing in human affairs is constant and stable, so the treachery of Justus Scouwenburgius shook the harmony of the alliance and the hope of the rising commonwealth. He imposed a heavy tax across Friesland, and, escorted by six cohorts of foot, abandoned Franeker as if it were burning and led his men to Makkum. There, starting a new and hastily made work, and moving through the Workum district, he turned his standards against the woodlands, as if, aided by the troops of horse I mentioned, he were thinking of besieging Leeuwarden, the capital of the province, or of undertaking great enterprises. Men full of trust suspected nothing else. But he left Bolsward under the protection of Dirk Bronchorst of Nedermormter, Franeker under Doco Martena, and Sneek under Tito Hettinga, and then, after the most severe exactions, deserted his command and his office like a fugitive. The cohorts' standards were plundered, and the fury of the soldiers, scattering in all directions, was bought off for a small sum of money. He himself, inglorious and distrusted even by his own men, was carried away on a swift horse through the Tencteri, and that same night hid himself in inner Westphalia, destined to face other perils and to pay the well-known penalties for his monstrous treachery. After his shameful departure from the province, a great change of affairs followed throughout Friesland. For Gaspar Robles, informed of Justus Scouwenburgius's flight, abandoned the inland districts and the city of Leeuwarden, and at once led his forces to Harlingen. Having placed there a garrison of some cohorts, suited to the position of the place, he sent ahead to Makkum a number of Walloon companies.

units.la: Erat apud Gasparum Roblesium Harlingae tum vir magnae autoritatis Hector Dekama, qui minus fæderi æquus Philippi, & Praefectorum partes procacibus studijs sectabatur. Is datis Harlinga ad Dominicum Hottingham Oldermannum Bolsuerdiam litteris urbi excidium denuntiavit. Esse plerisque cum copijs in armis Roblesium, cuius arbitrio nisi se permittant, eum pro lubidine more victoris actarum. Ita cogitarent Mechliniam, Zutphaniam, socias fæderi urbes, regijs nuper armis expugnatas, direptioni, caedi & infaelicibus flammis patuisse. Neque aliud Bolsuerdiae urbi instare, quam ut eadem lege habeatur, tum demum miserationem victricis dexterae imploratura, cum revocare animos manusque à caede praeceps furor non permittat. Suadere itaque deditionem faciant, quam maturrime, quod eâ solâ declinare periculum queant, miserae urbi decretum. Quibus litteris recitatis, ac in vulgus sparsis affectibus immodicum, magna consternatio totam urbem frequentavit. Fuere, qui per puerorum faeminarumque lamenta & ejulatus lachrymas profunderent, consulentesque publicae securitati Roblesium honesta legatione exorandum, & tempestivis blandicijs censerent. Igitur decreto publico Botto Gellius, Hobbius Douwonius, Legispeeritus, Gulielmus Cornelius, & Abbaeus Petraeus etiam inclinante die ad Roblesium misi, qui expeditis per marinum littus copijs castra jam ad Maccomium posuerat. Horatius verò Buma, & Haringus Haersma tribuni cohortium praesidiario milite tuebantur.
units.tr: At Harlingen, at that time, Gaspar Robles had a man of great authority, Hector Dekama, who, being less than fair to the treaty, pursued the cause of Philip and the governors with aggressive zeal. From Harlingen he sent a letter to Dominicus Hottinga, the alderman of Bolsward, and threatened the city with destruction. Robles was at the head of many troops under arms, he said, and unless the townsmen placed themselves at his discretion, he would act as the victor pleased. The cities of Mechelen and Zutphen, allied to the treaty and recently taken by royal arms, had thought the same, and had been exposed to plunder, slaughter and unhappy fires. Nothing else threatened the city of Bolsward than that it would be treated by the same law, and would then at last implore the pity of the victorious hand, when headlong fury would no longer let the minds and hands be restrained from slaughter. He therefore urged them to make surrender as soon as possible, since this alone could avert the danger, and that was the destined fate of the unhappy city. When this letter was read out and spread among the common people, great dismay, with excessive emotion, filled the whole city. Some poured out tears with the lamentations and wailing of boys and women, and, consulting the public safety, thought that Robles should be won over by an honourable embassy and by timely flatteries. So, by public decree, Botto Gellius, Hobbius Douwonius, a lawyer, Gulielmus Cornelius, and Abbaeus Petraeus were sent to Robles even as the day was declining; he had already brought his forces by the seashore and pitched camp at Makkum. Horatius Buma and Haringus Haersma, tribunes of the cohorts, held the city with the garrison.

units.la: Quorum primus non vanus hostilis potentiae aestumator, metuens ne obsessos morâ aut inedia Roblesius consumeret, litteras clàm Bolsuer- diam ac Franequeram misit, ut commeatum praestarent, sociosq; ac foederatos ad mittenda mature auxilia hortarentur. Caeterum ista Maccomium nullo fructu transmissa. Quippe nuntiati excidij metus tantum Bolsuerdijs pavorem incusserat, ut missus civibus miles, tum Dux atq; Imperator partium Bronchorstius vacuam fere urbem relinqueret. Qui ubi Snecam, quo se receperat, advenit, captus à Pontificijs per fisci regij procuratorem Leovardiam abductus est. Tum consternatum captivitate Bronchorstij praesidium Maccomio excesit. Bolsuerdia ipsa ad turpissimas conditiones adacta, veniam tandem impetravit, ducentique Valonum facto per Schettanum aggerem itinere, & emissario Marnio superato, erectis signis Bolsuerdiam intravere. Qua tempestate plurimas familias insolentiae Valonum pertaesas Embdam se recepisse comperio, in quâ urbe vicarium Edzardi imperium Occo adhuc Frisius Satrapa, vir crudelis animi & osor foederis Belgici administrabat. Memoriae traditum est, Haringium Glinzium Scouwenburgici Senatus Praesidem, cum caeteris exulum Embdam petentem strato glacie Amalo flantis adversum Euri vehementiâ correptum, ambustisque frigore artubus Embdam progressum triduano morbo decessisse. Sed adversitate fatorum ut ante cIↄ. Iↄ. LXVIII. acta rursum libertas tutius exilium patriae fortunâ reputabat. Itaque per oppida Frisiae praelucentibus cereis amburbia rursum, & supplicationes decretae, lustratisque fanis Romanae Sedis cultus per omnem Provinciam stabilitus. Civium quoq; foederatorum arma in publicum comportata usui partium serviere, foederatique à Praesidiarijs Valonibus in omnem vim, & licentiam effusis contumelia affecti. Bolsuerdiae quoq; consularium, civiumque aedes dirutae, areaeque lustro conspersae redintegrandis fanis sacrisque locis applicatae sunt. Omnis quoque ordinis sexusve homines ad Pontificiam religionem redire jussi, vetito omni cum foederatis profugisq; commercio, quibus captivitates, carceres & supplicia asperrimis edictis decernebantur. Mox Franequera sociarum urbium fortunâ suam aestumans minore foederis studio contempuit, civesque Pontificij, liberâ à foederato praesidio civitate, ad sua ingenia conversi sunt. Magistratum namque regium nupera exautoratio, caeteros, urbe eiectos propinquos, & recens exilij memoria stimulabat. Quare clandestinos per coetus primum inermes, post armati convenere, non ignaro Senatu foederato res novas molientibus secreta domorum compleri. Inde pavor per Curiam, mox ubi ex metu ejusdem defectio subsecuta, habiti intra urbem conflictus Pontificijs victoriam attulere. Foederati per vim portis ejecti in proxima loca suffugium fecere. Tum supplicatoriae litterae ad Gasparum Roblesium Leovardiam missae, & ne quid in morâ periculi, Delegati Magistratus civiumq; nomine Hero Ockingha, Æmylius Adama, Bernardus Rodmersius, Ioachimus Symonius Iureconsulti, cum Iacobo Abbaeo, qui veniam anteactorum peterent. Illi innuebant post occupatam à foederatis civitatem fidem se semper in occulto professos saevis victorum imperijs paruisse. Detentos namque per vim partis adversae, neque loricam urbis, aut spatia portarum facturis transfugia patuisse. Quare alio modo captatam rem, versaque in virtutem patientiâ armis foederatos ejecisse, manifesto erga Philippum Regem constantis animi fideique indicio. De cuius integritate si quid delibatum foret per necessitatem, rogare se supplices indignationis regiæ temperamentum, & clementiam victoribus non negandam. Quorum precibus evenit, ut nihil abnuentibus veniam daret Roblesius, ipseque accessione tot urbium auctus magnarum rerum spes, & victorias agitaret. Quare Valonum Germanorumque copijs, quas per Frisiam autoraverat, stipendia popposcit, conferrique ab agrarijs in singulos reditmeans aureos, qui è solo proveniunt, quatuor per Provinciam sestertios imperavit. Dies quoque pendendo confestim tributo dictus, ne perdomatâ Provinciâ gerendarum rerum, & occasio atterendi populi elaberetur. Tum Germanus miles maturandæ solutioni planos per agros sparsus, foederatarumque nuper urbium tutela, (quarum muros dirui ac solo æquari Ferdinandus Albanus imperaverat) Valonum fidei commissa.
units.tr: Of these, the first, who was no mean judge of the enemy's power, fearing that Robles would wear out the besieged by delay or starvation, secretly sent letters to Bolsward and to Franeker, urging them to furnish supplies and to exhort their allies and confederates to send help promptly. But this effort, sent to Makkum, achieved nothing. Indeed, the fear of the announced destruction had struck such terror into the men of Bolsward that, the citizens having sent away the soldiers, Bronchorst, the commander and leader of their party, left the city almost empty. When he came to Sneek, where he had retired, he was seized by the Papists through the royal treasury's procurator and carried off to Leeuwarden. Then the garrison, dismayed by Bronchorst's captivity, left Makkum. Bolsward itself, driven to the most shameful terms, at last obtained pardon; and the Walloon troops advancing by the road made over the Schettan dyke, and Marnius having been overcome, the standards were raised and they entered Bolsward. At this time I find that many families, weary of the insolence of the Walloons, withdrew to Emden, a city where Occo, the Frisian satrap, a man of cruel temper and hater of the Belgian alliance, administered the vicarious rule of Edzard. It is recorded that Haring Glinzius, president of the Stavoren council, on his way to Emden with the other exiles, was seized by a violent east wind blowing over the ice of the Ems; his limbs were burned by the cold, and after a three-day illness he died when he reached Emden. But, as in the earlier year 1568, fortune's adversity had restored freedom, so the exiles now reckoned that exile was safer than the fortunes of their homeland. Accordingly, in the towns of Friesland, with candles burning, thanksgivings were again proclaimed and supplications decreed; the temples were purified, and the worship of the Roman See was re-established throughout the province. The arms of the citizens and allies were gathered into public stores and served the use of the party, while the allies were treated with insult by the Walloon garrisons, who had let loose all violence and licence. In Bolsward too, the houses of the consuls and citizens were pulled down, and the areas, sprinkled with lustral water, were assigned to the restoration of the churches and sacred places. Men of every rank and sex were ordered to return to the Papist religion, with all dealings with the allies and exiles forbidden, and for them captivity, prisons and punishments were decreed by the harshest edicts. Soon Franeker, weighing its fortunes against those of the allied cities, showed less zeal for the alliance; and the Papist citizens, now that the city was free of the allied garrison, turned to their own inclinations. For the recent dismissal of the royal magistrates, and the memory of the recent exile of their relatives driven from the city, spurred them on. Hence they first gathered secretly in small groups, unarmed, and afterwards met under arms, with the allied council unaware, and filled the private houses with plots for revolution. Then fear spread through the council chamber, and soon, when defection followed upon that fear, the clashes within the city brought victory to the Papists. The allies, driven from the gates by force, took refuge in nearby places. Then letters of supplication were sent to Gaspar Robles at Leeuwarden, and, lest any delay bring danger, delegates of the magistracy and the citizens, Hero Ockinga, Aemilius Adama, Bernardus Rodmersius and Joachim Symonius, lawyers, with Jacob Abbaeus, went to seek pardon for past deeds. They pleaded that, since the city had been seized by the allies, they had always secretly professed their loyalty and had obeyed the cruel commands of the victors; for, held by force of the opposing party, and with the city's walls and gates guarded, they had no way of escape. Therefore, they said, the matter had been undertaken in another way; and by patient endurance turned into courage, they had driven out the allies by arms, a clear sign of their constant spirit and fidelity toward King Philip. If anything of this integrity had been impaired by necessity, they begged as suppliants for a moderation of royal indignation and for a clemency not to be denied to the victors. By their prayers it came about that Robles, granting pardon to those who asked nothing, and himself enlarged by the addition of so many cities, pursued hopes and victories on a larger scale. Accordingly he demanded pay for the Walloon and German troops he had taken into service throughout Friesland, and ordered that, from the landholders, four sesterces per province be collected on each gold coin (aureus) produced from the soil. He also appointed a day for prompt payment of the tax, lest, with the province subdued, the opportunity of carrying on war and wearing down the people should slip away. Then the German soldiers, scattered over the flat fields to hasten payment, and the safeguarding of the recently taken allied cities (whose walls Ferdinand of Alba had ordered to be torn down and levelled with the ground) were entrusted to the good faith of the Walloons.

units.la: Reperio in Notis Feiconis Nicolaï, viri apud Staurios eâ ætate Consularis, totum illud biennium, quod à septuagesimi anni per Frisiam diluvio effluxit, ut prægnans novorum motuum, ita variâ fortunâ exactum fuisse. Direptum à foederatis Worcomium oppidum, Ioannemque Lindanum, Cænobij Hemelumani Præsulem, domo Presbyteri Worcumani extractum Nordam in Transfamalanos abductum, lytro scx mille dalerorum sub comminatione suspendij eî impositio. Antistitem eundem ab Haïone Manningha viro Nobili, nullo impendio liberatum, habitumque pro dignitate, honesto post comitatu suo cænobio restitutum. Eosdem quoque foederatos Texelam insulam, & haud procul eâ viginti oneraria naves depraedatos, regiasque post naves Amstelodami instructas, in Amafo fluvio cum foederatis congressas post longum, & dubij exitus conflictum victoriâ potitas. Plurimos taederatorum, quod in fluvium præcipites dati, nando evaderent, vitæ servatos, cæterosque & in ijs ultra quinquaginta suspendio necatos, aut Amstelodamum abductos. Regiam classem Flevum ingressam divisâ apud Enchusa prædâ Angliam petijsse. Ibi circa Tamesis fluvij ostium, & post haud procul Doverâ castello, quod littori imminet, xvii. foederatas naves fugasse, ac in Zelandiam se recepisse. Foederatam verò classem quatuor Hamburgensium naves diripuisse, prædàque divite onustam, & strangulato jussu Archithalasi primario Hamburgensium navarcho, Amasum ingressas. Regis naves ingruente brumâ Enchusæ in portum subductas, eandemq; hyemem nullo frigore, aut gelu asperam rarâ cæli clementiâ notabilem fuisse.
units.tr: I find in the Notes of Feiko Nicolai, a man who was then a consul at Staveren, that the whole two-year period which ran from the flood of the seventy-first year in Friesland was, like a pregnant mother of new disturbances, spent in changing fortune. The town of Workum was plundered by the confederates, and John Lindanus, prelate of the monastery of Hemelum, was dragged from the house of the Workum minister, carried off to Noordwijk in Transfamalan territory, and threatened with hanging unless he paid a ransom of six thousand daalders. The same prelate was freed without expense by Haio Manninga, a nobleman, and, treated with the honour due to his rank, was restored to his monastery with a respectable retinue. The same confederates also raided the island of Texel and nearly twenty transport ships off it; afterwards the royal ships, fitted out at Amsterdam, engaged the confederates in the river Amstel after a long and doubtful battle, and gained the victory. Many of the confederates, thrown into the river, escaped by swimming and were saved alive; the rest, more than fifty of them, were hanged or taken to Amsterdam. The royal fleet entered the Vlie, and after dividing the booty at Enkhuizen sought England. There, near the mouth of the Thames and not far from the castle of Dover, which overlooks the shore, it put seventeen confederate ships to flight and withdrew to Zeeland. The confederate fleet, however, plundered four Hamburg ships and, laden with rich booty, entered Amsterdam, after the chief Hamburg admiral, Archithalasius, had been strangled by order. As winter drew on, the royal ships were drawn up into the harbour at Enkhuizen; and that winter, though not harsh with cold or frost, was remarkable for the rare mildness of the sky.

units.la: Anno sequente xiii. foederatas naves relicto Flevo partim Wiringiam, partim in sinum Austrinum provectas Hornensium navibus damna dedisse. Decimæ exactionem ab Albano tum institutam pacatas fermè partes ad bellum resuscitasse. Foederatos quoque cum classe circa Flevi ostium stantes Enchusam revocatos, & post captum Enchusæ Franciscum Boshusium Archithalassum regium, domosque plurimas incendio datas, cum regijs triremibus navali pugnâ, & nullo successu decertasse. Principem Aurantium Enchusam, deïn Medenblicum ingressum. sum, fœderatosque premendis Amstelodamensibus de obturandâ Tya fluvio consilium iniisse. Gaspárum Roblesium cum quadringentis Valonum Stauriam profectum castello præsidium imposuisse, gerendarum rerum imperio in Fredericum Hornium, Hornani Comitis nothum, Prætorem Hemelolpherdium, & Satrapam arcis, tum Martinium Baiartum cohortis Valonicæ tribunum devoluto. Pedestres quoque fœderatorum cohortes Asingha Ripperda, Ennone Poppenio, & Nicolao Bremense ductoribus occupatâ urbe castellum circumvenisse, tormentisque Sneca & Bolsuerdia adductis protractâ in x. Sept. obsidione locum naturâ & opere munitum nequicquam oppugnasse. Sex signa Germanorum Valonumque Leovardia Stauriam à Roblesio missa, medio noctis, cæsis qui obstarent, urbem occupasse. Fœderatos urbe ejectos, decemque & quatuor civibus per pontes strangulatis reliquam multitudinem nulla conjugum, aut liberorum cura fugæ datam vitæ consuluisse. Multos quoque fugientium scaphis Enchusam devectos, alios occultis ædium locis obtectos periculis subductos. Prædam LX. navibus impositam, ac Leovardiam transportatam una cum damno urbi dato centum M. dalerorum superasse. Fœderatos quoque recuperandæ prædæ avidos ad Galedamum vires collegisse, cæterum dissipatos sparsosque in avia Valonum prosperis non obstitisse. Ducentos quoque Valones in Flevi insulam enavigasse, expugnatisque quibus Gerardus Gorcomius & Ielmerus Flevolandius præerant, navibus, capita cæsorum truncis avulsa pinnis imposuisse. Cæteros captivorum Groningam abductos, & capitis damnatos. Gasparum quoque Roblesium tergo fugientis Scouwenburgij inhærentem VIII. Kal. Dec. Stauriam pervenisse. Ita pericula audaciam sæpe atque virtutem dabant, partiumque consilia varios eventus pro arbitrio fortunæ sortiebantur.
units.tr: In the following year, thirteen confederate ships left the Vlie, some sailing to Wieringen and some into the southern bay, and inflicted losses on the ships of Hoorn. The collection of the tithe, then instituted by Alva, revived the war in parts that were now almost pacified. The confederates, who were stationed with their fleet near the mouth of the Vlie, were also recalled to Enkhuizen; and after Francis Bossu, the royal admiral, had been captured at Enkhuizen and many houses had been burned, they fought a naval battle with the royal galleys with no success. Prince William entered Enkhuizen, then Medemblik, and the confederates, intending to crush the people of Amsterdam, formed a plan to block the river Ij. Gaspar Robles, having set out for Staveren with four hundred Walloons, placed a garrison in the castle, and the command of the operations was handed over to Frederick Horn, the natural son of Count Horn, the praetor of Hindeloopen and governor of the citadel, and to Martin Bajart, tribune of a Walloon cohort. The confederate infantry cohorts under Asinga Ripperda, Ennon Poppen and Nicolas Bremen also seized the town and surrounded the castle; with cannon brought up from Sneek and Bolsward, the siege was prolonged until 10 September, and they attacked the place, strong by nature and fortification, in vain. Six standards of Germans and Walloons, sent from Leeuwarden to Staveren by Robles, at midnight, after cutting down those who stood in their way, occupied the town. The confederates were driven out of the town, and with fourteen citizens strangled on the bridges, the rest, allowed to flee without any care for wives or children, saved their lives. Many of the fugitives were carried to Enkhuizen in boats, and others, hidden in secret places of houses, were rescued from danger. The booty, loaded on sixty ships and carried to Leeuwarden, together with the damage done to the town, exceeded one hundred thousand daalders. The confederates, eager to recover the booty, gathered their forces at Galedam, but, scattered and dispersed, they did not stand in the way of the Walloons' successes in the open country. Two hundred Walloons also sailed across to the island of the Vlie, and having overpowered the ships commanded by Gerard Gorcum and Jelmer Vlieland, they set the heads of the slain on pikes on the stumps of masts. The rest of the captives were carried off to Groningen and condemned to death. Gaspar Robles, too, following closely on the heels of the fleeing Schouwenburg, reached Staveren on 24 November. Thus dangers often gave rise to daring and to courage, and the plans of the parties drew their various outcomes as fortune chose.

units.la: Mox Nova Stella per Frisiam conspecta. Quæ in Cassiopæa surgens & præter legem superi corporis immota, varie, ut solet rebus afflictis, mortalium ingenia affecit. Itaq; diversa ratione rerum cælestium periti de rariore naturæ ostento differebant, existimantibus nonnullis, Stellam Novam, quod vagis sparsisque per aërem Ignibus non arderet, lucidissimo fulgore novæ fælicitatis ventura tempora indicare. Alij verò, quod eversâ Philosophorum sententiâ in ipso cælo, & æternorum corporum compage quid natum deprehenderetur, tristiorem rerum statum ex inversa Naturæ lege ominabantur. Ita sua quisque, non aliena pericula horrore ac aspectu inusitati syderis æstumabat. Post suspectam prodigij fidem intumescens mare auxit, ruptisque iterum aggeribus in proxumam continentem effusum, omnem ferme Frisiam infælicibus undis operuit. Plurimi credidere recrudescens elementum, & insoluto æstu tumefactum, æmulæ gentis discordiam castigasse, lacerique ac jam ante disiecti littoris derupta, obstantiaque locorum opprobrio discordis populi demolitum.
units.tr: Soon a new star was seen over Friesland. It rose in Cassiopeia and, contrary to the law of the heavenly bodies, stood motionless; and, as is usual in afflicted times, it stirred the minds of mortals in different ways. Accordingly, experts in celestial matters, reasoning in different ways, disputed about this rarer portent of nature: some held that the new star, since it did not burn like the wandering fires scattered through the air but shone with the brightest light, announced times of new happiness. Others, because, the opinion of the philosophers being overturned, something newly born had been detected in the heavens themselves and in the structure of the eternal bodies, foretold a sadder state of affairs from the inverted law of nature. Thus each person reckoned his own dangers, not those of others, by the dread and the sight of the unusual star. After the credibility of the omen was doubted, the swelling sea grew, and, the dykes breaking again, it poured out onto the nearest mainland and covered almost all of Friesland with unhappy waves. Many believed that the element, reviving and swollen with a surge that would not subside, had punished the discord of a rival nation, and that the shore already torn and broken, and the obstacles of the land, had been demolished as a reproach to a discordant people.

units.la: Finis Libri Secundi.
units.tr: End of the Second Book.

units.la: P. W I N.

units.la: P. WINSEMI Historiarum LIBER TERTIUS.
units.tr: The Histories of P. Winsemius, Book Three.

units.la: XORTUM novæ Stellæ magna rerum per Frisiam mutatio præcesserat, major sequebatur. Quippe laceratam Principis, populiq; concordiam fortuna adhuc trahebat, velut dubia & fluctuans, an ex voto Regi dominatum, an libertatem populo destinaret. Itaque anxiæ & suspensæ ad incerta mentes, cum nec vulgus tantum futuri avidum, sed peritos quoque cœlestium prodigij secretum, & sollicitudo imminentium fatigaret. Neq; enim defuere, qui motiones syderum edocti, ipso verno Æquinoctio, quo conversio & flexus stellarum fieri solet, finem rebus humanis assignarent, ipsoque Belgicæ libertatis deliquio novissimum terris diem adesse superstitiosius magis, quam verius occinerent. Alij credebant novum gentibus regnum hoc ipso sydere portendi, aut, quod in Cassiopeæ signo, turbidis, ut plurimum, stellis circumfuso, luceret, popularium furorum incrementa consentientibus astrorum judicijs præsagiret. Magnum certe quid obnuntiare Cornelius Gemma gravis autor censuit, idemque ostentum nullâ naturæ lege genitum supra ordinariam prodigiorum fortem, atque indicationem timendo spectaculo exsurrexisse.
