units.tr: A great upheaval in the affairs of Friesland had preceded the appearance of the new star, and a greater one followed. Fortune still dragged along the torn concord between prince and people, wavering and uncertain whether it would grant the king dominion as he wished or liberty to the people. Minds were therefore anxious and held in suspense by doubtful expectations. The common people were eager to know the future, and the learned, too, were troubled by the hidden meaning of the heavenly portent and by the anxiety of impending events. Nor were there lacking men skilled in the movements of the stars, who, at the very spring equinox, when the stars usually turn and change their course, fixed an end to human affairs. With more superstition than truth, they foretold that the last day for the earth was at hand, the day on which Belgian liberty would fail. Others believed that this star, shining in the constellation of Cassiopeia, which is commonly surrounded by turbid stars, portended a new kingdom for the nations, or foretold, by the agreeing judgments of the stars, an increase of the rage of the citizens. Cornelius Gemma, a serious author, certainly thought that it signified something great, and he held that this portent, born from no law of nature, had risen above the ordinary lot of prodigies and was a sign to be feared as a terrifying spectacle.

units.la: Idem scriptor tradit, haud multum ab exortu novæ Stellæ, chasma lucidæ exhalationis circa VI. Kal. Febr. in cœlo observatum, certioribus malorum obnuntiationibus initia anni insigniviße. Itaque eundem gentium irruptionibus, per excidia urbium, & civilium cladium funera feralem fore, sagacissimus cœlestium contemplator judicabat, omnenque provincialium oculis, & ad horrorem ostentui in illo superiore convexo expositum, non nisi funesta & adversa paci, ac rerum ordini decernere.
units.tr: The same writer relates that, not long after the rise of the new star, a gap in a bright exhalation was observed in the sky about the sixth day before the Kalends of February, and that this marked the beginning of the year with more certain announcements of evils. The most sagacious observer of the heavens therefore judged that the invasions of the nations, the destruction of cities, and the deaths in civil disasters would be deadly, and he held that this sign, displayed in that upper vault for all the provinces to see and for a shudder of horror, decreed nothing but what was dire and adverse to peace and to the order of affairs.

units.la: Mihi consilium, exponere secuti temporis memoriam, procul affectibus, nec absimili fide, quâ majores nostri impollutos adulationibus, aut odijs annales clarissimis posteris legavere.
units.tr: My purpose, in following the memory of the times, is to set it out free from partisan feeling, and with a fidelity not unlike that with which our forebears bequeathed their annals, untainted by flattery or hatred, to the most illustrious posterity.

units.la: FVgas, & proscriptiones civium, ac redactam fermè in formam regni Provinciam. Anniversaria inundationum damna communibus impendijs sarcita, & maris æstuaria tempestate aut diurno æstu littus resorbentia, molibus aggerum clausa. Morte proregis admotos regundis Provin-
units.tr: Flights and proscriptions of citizens, and the province brought almost into the form of a kingdom. Yearly losses from floods were made good by common expenses, and the estuaries of the sea, which by storm or by long tide swallowed up the shore, were closed off with dykes and embankments. On the death of the viceroy, men were brought in to govern the provinces.

units.la: cIↄ. Iↄ. LXXIII. Provincijs patres, & Reip. statum lenioribus consilijs inversum. Sequestras pacis conditiones sistendis armis perscriptas, & paucorum inquietudine bellum fœdere involutum. Stipendiorum inopiâ, & cohortium seditione regios Præfectos custodiæ datos, ac novorum successione validas urbes duriorì imperij tædio regijs partibus subductas. Funestum sydus cælo ardescens mali prænuntium. Inde sollicitata regum, nationumque auxilia, quæsitumque libertati exteras apud gentes patrocinium, & difficulter repertum. Accitos aliunde provinciarum rectores, asperum propinqui regis imperium novâ lenitate attemperantes. Mox libertatem conscientijs in spem civilis concordiæ indultam, & consilium sanandis malis repertum, secessionibus accommodatum. Divulsis provincijs sicta seorsim fœdera, & utrinque partibus robur bello quæsitum. Cástigatam reciprocis cladibus concordiam, & provinciarum Præsides subdolis artibus sacramenta variantes. Repentinas violentasque mortes fato desciscentibus immissas, & perfidiam eorundem cælestibus iris expiatam.
units.tr: In 1573, the provincial fathers and the state of the commonwealth were overturned by milder counsels. Conditions of peace were drawn up for laying down arms, and by the restlessness of a few men the war was entangled in a covenant. Through lack of pay and a mutiny of the cohorts, royal prefects were given to the garrisons, and powerful cities were withdrawn from the royal side by the successive appointment of new men and by the harsher weariness of rule. A baleful star burned in the sky, a herald of evil. Thence the aid of kings and nations was sought, and protection was sought, and with difficulty found, among foreign peoples for liberty. Governors were summoned from elsewhere, tempering the harsh rule of the neighbouring king with a new mildness. Soon freedom of conscience was granted, in hope of civil concord, and a plan was found for healing the evils, suited to the secessions. The provinces were divided, and separate treaties were feigned, and on both sides strength was sought for war. Concord, chastened by mutual disasters, and the provincial governors, varying their oaths by deceitful arts. Sudden and violent deaths were sent by fate upon those who went over, and their treachery was expiated by the heavenly rainbow.

units.la: Igitur attritâ per Frisiam, fugâ Justi Scouwenburgij, fœderatarum partium fide, Gasparus Roblesius, commorante apud Geldros Ægidio Barlamoutio Hyergio, vicariam provinciæ Præfecturam gerens, ardua magis, ac infensa fœderi meditabatur. Quippe portentosæ asperrimæque hyemis commoditate (quam conjunctionibus quorundam Planetarum, inerrantiumque stellarum Mathematici adscripserant) quaquaversum signa per Provinciam sparsit, adjutusque Senatus regij consilijs, formandis, more victorum, ex arbitrio rebus incubuit.
units.tr: Therefore, with Friesland worn down and Justus Scouwenburg in flight, and with the faith of the confederate party broken, Gaspar Robles, who was staying among the Gelderlanders with Egidius Barlaimont Hyergius and holding the deputy governorship of the province, planned more severe and hostile measures against the Union. Taking advantage of the portentous and most harsh winter, which the mathematicians had ascribed to the conjunctions of certain planets and fixed stars, he scattered his signs everywhere through the province. Aided by the counsels of the royal senate, he set to work on arranging affairs at his own discretion, after the manner of victors.

units.la: Cæterum in Hollandiam à Frederico Albani filio, qui castra ad Harlemum posuerat, evocatus, cum parte Legionis provinciâ excessit, reliquasque cohortes per præsidia civitatum disposuit. Jam enim fœderis socios, ut ante sub Albani adventum, alijs terris fortuna absconderat, utraque Amasum, ac Visurgim, tum cis ac trans Rhenum longinqua, & infida suffugia fœderato & exuli populo delegerat. Itaque mœsta per plerâsque Frisiæ urbes passim solitudo, & triste silentium, nisi quod regiarum partium multitudinem alienæ infœlicitatis domesticum spectaculum, aut externa fama oblectaret. Quippe oppressum Fœdus, Gallias, & Germaniam dubias, Philippo assertum imperium lætabatur, Fredericumque Albanum, etsi ingenio immanem, & paternæ ferociæ æmulum, clarissimarum per Hollandiam, Geldriamque urbium excidia, & simul spolia secum trahentem Harlemum Hollandiæ oppidum regio exercitu circumvenisse. Roblesium quoque illius urbis oppugnatione ampla decora commeritum, amisso Doppio, & vulnerato Gantonio cohortium tribunis, retinendæ in fide regis provinciæ benignitate fati servatum.
units.tr: Meanwhile, summoned into Holland by Frederick, son of Alba, who had pitched his camp at Haarlem, he left the province with part of the legion and distributed the remaining cohorts among the garrisons of the towns. For fortune had by now hidden the confederates, as before at Alba's arrival, in other lands; the exiled people had chosen as refuges, on either side of the Rhine, the distant and unfriendly places beyond the Ems and the Weser. Hence a sad solitude and gloomy silence lay here and there over most of the towns of Friesland, save that the crowd of royalists was cheered by the spectacle of another's misfortune at home or by the news from abroad. For they rejoiced that the Union had been crushed, that France and Germany were unsettled, and that power had been secured for Philip; and they rejoiced that Frederick of Alba, though savage by nature and a rival of his father's ferocity, had surrounded with the royal army the Dutch town of Haarlem, and was dragging with him the destruction and plunder of the most famous towns of Holland and Gelderland. Robles too, who had earned great distinction in the siege of that city, had been preserved by the kindness of fate for keeping the province in loyalty to the king, though Doppio had been lost and Gantonius, a tribune of the cohorts, wounded.

units.la: Tradit V. Cl. Joannes Arcerius Theodoretus gentis nostræ scriptor, qui inter obsessos tum fuit, in Ephemeride suâ Fredericum Albanum destinatâ oppugnandæ urbi noĉte circa Prid. Kal. Febr. diem stratas glacie fossâ & diruto fermè muro velut potiundi oppidi certum fuisse, dignoscendisque partibus suos lineis indumentis coopertos & quidem ex opinione virtutis delectos Joanniiarum portam rariore asservantium custodiâ sub ortum lucis occupasse. Cæterum oppidanos perspecto discrimine eo loci consisse, hostemque tanto progressu rerum, & secunundis suis elatum multa cœde, & reportatis in urbem vexillis reppulisse. Eadem vexilla animandis obsessis per ubem circumlata, generoso ultrò sanguini incitamentum ad præclara addidisse. Hostes quoq; repetito infultu murorum editis imminentes subsidente humo, quam obsessi excavaverant, & subjecto pulvere succenso, igne ac voragine diductæ telluris absumptos, reliquosque subsequentes velut reparandis detrimentis suffectos sociæ cladis spectaculo de præcipiti fuga cogitasse. Eorum etiam plurimos ferentariorum virtute oppressos, præterq; faucios, quos crudo vulnere adhuc calens sanguis subducebat, post re-pulsum cum suis Roblefium, fortissimos quosq; & è legionum tribu-nis cecidisse. Addit Cl. Arcerius ex interceptis Stephani Dynaræ (is Frederico Albano ab Epistolis) ad Albernoum Ferdinandi patris Actua-rium litteris, solos Hispanos istâ oppugnatione suis partibus defuisse, cæterarumq; nationum legiones plurimum gloriæ ex illo conflictu, Hispanorum gentem æternum dedecus reportasse. De se Dynara scribit, ob rem male ab Hispanis suis gestam, præ mærore attabescere, indignantemque, nec falsò, suæ gentis infamiam ægritudine animi, & læsæ mentis vertisse. Addunt nostrates scriptores, Sole Aquarij signum ingresso, primoque Harlemensis obsidij tempore, incrustatâ velut con-tinuis Etesijs terrâ, & altissimis nivibus contectâ, tam immite acer-bumque gelu extitisse, ut multorum artus frigore ambusserit, militumque plurimos, diurnis castrorum operis intentos, extincto vitali calore exanimaverit. Plurimum quoque sanguinis illâ obsidione utrinq; fusum, obsessosq; ultimâ necessitate ad deditionem compulsos, hostiarumque ritu mactatos, suo sanguine infaustam urbem, & proxumos lacus imbuisse. Cætera abijs scriptoribus non enarrata pertexere nostri instituti non est.
units.tr: Our fellow countryman, the most distinguished Joannes Arcerius Theodoretus, a writer who was among the besieged at that time, relates in his journal that Frederick of Alba had planned to assault the city by night, about the day before the Kalends of February, when the ditch was paved with ice and the wall was almost broken down, as if he meant to capture the town. Having marked the difference between the parties by their coverings, he occupied the Johannes Gate, which was guarded more carelessly, at dawn; these were men chosen for their supposed courage, clad in linen. But the townsmen, seeing the danger, took up their position in that place, and, with a great slaughter, drove back the enemy, who was elated by such progress and his own successes, and they carried the enemy's standards back into the city. These standards were carried about the city to encourage the besieged, and gave a further spur of their own to noble blood, eager for deeds of glory. The enemy also, renewing the assault, with the ramparts raised over them, were struck when the ground subsided, which the besieged had hollowed out, and gunpowder was set alight beneath; by fire and the chasm of the torn earth they were swallowed up, and the rest who followed, as if sent to make good the losses, thought of headlong flight at the sight of their comrades' ruin. Most of them were overcome by the valour of the light-armed troops, and besides the prisoners whom blood still warm from the raw wound drew away, after Robles was driven back with his men, the bravest men and some of the tribunes of the legions fell. Arcerius adds, from letters intercepted by Stephen Dynara (who was secretary to Frederick of Alba) sent to Albernoz, the actuary of Ferdinand the father, that the Spaniards alone had failed their side in that assault, and that the legions of the other nations had gained much glory from that encounter, while the Spanish nation had brought back eternal disgrace. Dynara writes of himself that, because of the disaster his Spaniards had suffered, he was wasting away with grief, and that, indignant, and not falsely, at the infamy of his nation, he had turned it into an illness of mind and a wounded spirit. Our own writers add that, when the sun entered the sign of Aquarius, and at the first time of the siege of Haarlem, the earth, encrusted as if by constant north winds and covered with deep snows, was so cruelly harsh and bitter with frost that it burned the limbs of many, and that it deprived of life, by extinguishing their vital warmth, many soldiers who were busy all day with the work of the camp. Much blood was also shed on both sides in that siege, and the besieged, driven by final necessity to surrender, were slaughtered like victims, and with their own blood they stained the ill-fated city and the nearby lakes. It is not my purpose to recount in full what those writers did not tell.

units.la: Hoc tantum subjungunt, fœderatos exules, & Scouwenburgicæ societatis, subvertendis Amstelodamensium, & regij ad Harlemum exercitus commeatibus, quibusdam triremibus, liburnicisque Dimenum lacum occupasse, pugnâque navali, cum regia classe, (cui Focco Sibrandius Staurius vir fortis cum imperio præerat) commissâ, illustrem sibi prædam ac victoriam peperise. Triremes quoq; & naves regias, aut undis haustas, aut in potestatem Fœderatorum redacstas. Ipsum Si-brandium classis regiæ Præfectum vestibus exutum, & non uno vul-nere confossum, è triremi sua præcipitem datum, cadaverque vadosis post annum aquis erutum, solenni funeris apparatu apud Amstelodamenses humatum. Legatum quoque mille aureorum ejus testamento Staurijs scriptum.
units.tr: They add only this: the exiled confederates of the Scouwenburg company, to cut off supplies to the royal army at Haarlem and to the Amsterdammers, seized the Dimmer lake with some triremes and light galleys, and in a naval battle with the royal fleet, which was commanded by the brave Focco Sibrandius Staurius, they won for themselves an illustrious prize and victory. They also seized the triremes and royal ships, which were either swallowed by the waves or brought into the power of the confederates. Sibrandius himself, the prefect of the royal fleet, was stripped of his clothes, pierced with more than one wound, and thrown headlong from his own trireme; his body, dragged out of the shallow waters a year later, was buried with solemn funeral rites among the Amsterdammers. A legacy of a thousand gold pieces was also left to the Stauri by his will.

units.la: Neque per Frisiam, etiam amoto trans Visurgim in ditiones suas Justo Scouwenburgio, & dissipato fœdere, tuta adhuc per provinciam quies erat. Senatus namque regius, agente in castris Frederici Roblefio, imperium gerens, præsidiorum adhuc insolentiæ alimentum dabat, suspestiqué adhuc partium non obscuris odijs memoriâ fotæ toleratæque societatis atterebantur. Itaque conducendis huc illuc co-pijs æs imperatum, provisumque edicto commeatui, ne asperrimâ hyeme, ultro militi per inclementiam cœli infestâ, imbecillo inopiâ pabuli equite subjugandæ provinciæ præceps, & opportunum confilium retardaretur. Traditum memoriæ est, Arnoldum Gemenium Prærem Stellinguervium Tranfisulanæ Curiæ decreto quadringentos dale-ros pendere jussum, mandatoque contumacem, quod exhaustam tributis præturam obtenderet, à Petro Acuna Hispano alæ equitum levis armaturæ ductore Stenvicum pertractum. Ibi custodiæ datum inter minas, & territamenta mortis diu anxium non ante dimissum, quam extortam per cruciatus & tormenta pecuniam insolentissimo militi asignaret. Montjoium quoque virum nobilem, & cohortis regiæ præfectum, occasione belli (quod per Hollandiam, & in Kenhemarijs Fredericus Albanus gerebat) Stauriæ præsidium agentem, corruptum otio militem per domos civium disposuisse, eundemq; adæsis per luxum stipendijs alieni avidum patrandis flagitijs habuisse. Itaque non domesticæ tantum quieti gravis miles, cæterum ab insolente & nescio disciplinæ diurnus civium victus, in luxuriem, lasciviemque quotidianis commessationibus vertebatur. Parietinæ quoq;, & exustarum ædium, quæ ante annum hostili igne conflagraverant, rudera Montjoï jussu muniendo castello regio applicata, privatarumque rerum dispendia publicam secum servitutem traxere. Florentissimus quoque Stauriæ urbis splendor, qui jam ante magnificentiâ ædificiorum, structurarumque, superbo foecundis commercijs luxu, omne confinium provocaverat, fato suo, &, ut cuncta mortalium solent, vetustate temporum decrescens, magis magisque injuriâ civilis belli deformatus est. Josephus vero Talimerius Hispanus triremi regiæ apud Stauros præfectus vicina æstuaria, & Flevi alveum infestabat, fœderatosque, intutâ continente, per infidum mare errantes horrendâ immanitate divexabat. Scribit F. Nicolaus, vir apud Stauros consularis, tam barbarum, & crudele viro ingenium fuisse, ut Harder-vicenum quendam navarchum fœderi addictum, spoliatâ & exustâ navi scaphæ injectum, vinctumque ac vimine & stramento circumfusum in altum miserit, injectoq; igne, dubium quo mortis genere, sustulerit. Quod immane facinus, velut omnem temporum memoriam superans, etiam regiæ factionis administris improbatum fuit, damnantibus scilicet, virum amissa navi spoliatum, non vulgari morte, sed pugnantibus inter se naturæ odio elementis commissum, novæ crudelitatis fœdissimo commento exspirasse.
units.tr: Nor was there yet any safe peace throughout Friesland, even though Justus Scouwenburg had been removed beyond the Weser into his own lands and the Union was dispersed. For the royal senate, which was exercising power through Frederick Robles in the camp, still gave fuel to the insolence of the garrisons, and suspicion, still unhealed, was wearing down those who remembered the disguised and endured alliance, with its open hatreds. Therefore money was demanded for raising troops here and there, and provision was made by edict for supplies, lest the province, to be subdued headlong in the harshest winter, when the inclemency of the sky was hostile to the soldier, be delayed by a shortage of fodder for the horses, and an opportune counsel be held back. It is recorded that Arnold Gemenius, the prefect of Stellingwerf, was ordered by decree of the Trans-Sul court to pay four hundred daler; and when he refused, pleading that his office was drained by taxes, he was dragged to Stenvik by Peter Acuña, a Spaniard, leader of a light-armed cavalry wing. There he was thrown into custody amid threats and terrors of death, and, anxious for a long time, he was not released until he assigned to the insolent soldier the money he had extorted through torments and tortures. Also Montjoy, a noble man and prefect of a royal cohort, who was holding the garrison of Stauri on the occasion of the war which Frederick of Alba was waging through Holland and in the Kennemerland, placed soldiers, corrupted by idleness, in the homes of citizens, and kept them, greedy for the pay that had been spent in luxury, ready to carry out crimes. Hence the soldier was a burden not only to domestic peace; the daily sustenance of the citizens, drawn by the insolent and unskilled discipline, turned into luxury and wantonness through daily feasting. Ruins too, of houses burned by enemy fire the year before, were applied by Montjoy's order to fortifying the royal castle, and the losses of private property brought public slavery in their train. The flourishing splendour of the city of Stauri, which before had surpassed all its neighbours in the magnificence of its buildings and in the luxury of its fruitful commerce, declined by its own fate and by the age of times, as all mortal things do, and was more and more disfigured by the injury of civil war. Josephus Talimerius, a Spaniard placed in command of the royal trireme at Stauri, harassed the neighbouring estuaries and the channel of the Vlie, and grievously tormented the confederates who wandered over the treacherous sea, since the mainland was unsafe. Friar Nicholas, a man of consular rank at Stauri, writes that the man's nature was so barbarous and cruel that, having stripped and burned the ship of a certain Harderwijk captain attached to the Union, he threw him, bound and wrapped round with wicker and straw, into a small boat, and sent it out to sea; then, setting fire to it, he destroyed him by a death that is uncertain in kind. This monstrous crime, surpassing as it does all memory of the times, was condemned even by the agents of the royal faction, who judged that the man, stripped of his ship, had not died an ordinary death, but had perished, committed to elements at war with each other in nature's hatred, by the most foul invention of a new cruelty.

units.la: Neq; alia per Hispaniam consilia in secreto regni, & Philippi aula habebantur. Quippe fovendæ Albanorum patris & filij per Belgicam sævitiæ, & ne divisam pluribus bellis potentiam luxaret Philippus, biennales cum Elisabethâ Anglorum reginâ inducias depactus est, vulgatoque per omnem provinciam restitutorum commerciorum edicto, duorum regnorum diu infidam societatem, & simul fortunam Belgici fœderis repressit. Scribit Thuanus, conterrendis Harlemensibus tabulas istius Hispanum inter & Anglam conventionis, per castra, & exercitum jussu Albani publicatas, eandemque velut pacem certius per provincias bellum, & præclusa ex Angliæ regno fœderatis auxilia arrectis ad edictum legionibus promisisse. Quare Ferdinandus Albanus, ut exteras, & præsertim Germaniæ gentes, quæ ad bellum merendis sub Aurantio stipendijs confluxerant, à fœderatæ militiæ sacramento alienaret, omomnibus singulisque in sua redeundi potestatem edicto fecit, concessoque libero per provincias commeatu, desertorum armis assignari pretium jussit. Ne scilicet Germanus miles inops aeris patrandis per agros flagitijs se daret, aut sustentandae animae avidus ad sacramentum Aurantij Principis rediret. Frumenta quoque, ac annonam ex omni Frisia, quae Flevo, Lavicâ, & Amalo alluitur, submi-nistrari foederatis copijs vetuit, praepeditisque sociarum urbium commercijs, castra regia compleri commeatibus jussit. Sic omne consilium atterendo foederi pronum, fovendaeque regij militis licentiae, omne per forum ac tribunalia Philippi edicta recitabantur. Itaque exulum reditus novis quoque decretis intercepti, patrimoniaque profugae nobilitatis, ac proscriptorum civium innovatis tabulis fisco regio, sanciente Senatu, adjudicata. Tum, ne facili vertendis rebus fortunâ, confecti per provinciam foederis societas revivisceret, Gasparus Roblesius copias suas, quae in Albani castris semestre stipendium fecerant, sex navium classe in Frisiam reduxit, dispositisque Harlingae & Franequerae, ad coercendam multitudinem praesidijs, Leovardiam properavit. Ibi Cuneri Episcopi, & primariae Nobilitatis, tum Magistratus oppidani, ac salutationibus occurrentium civium exceptus, navatae in castris regijs ad Harlemum virtutis & fidei insignem gloriam tulit. Mox potissimâ legionis parte Leovardiae collocatâ, caeteras cohortes faciendis stipendijs per plana agrorum, atque municipia sparsit, populumque conferendis tributis contumacem, & saepè invalidum, duriore imperio, & solutis dominantium moribus exercuit.
units.tr: No other plans were being made in Spain, in the king's secret councils or in Philip's court. To foster the cruelty of the Alvas, father and son, in the Netherlands, and so that Philip would not weaken the power he had divided among several wars, he concluded a two-year truce with Elizabeth, Queen of the English. He published the edict restoring trade throughout the whole province, and so broke the long-standing and unreliable alliance of the two kingdoms and at the same time the fortunes of the Belgic confederacy. Thuanus writes that, to terrify the people of Haarlem, the Spanish printed the terms of this agreement between Spain and England and had them posted throughout the camp and army by Alva's order. He claimed that this so-called peace was in fact a surer war throughout the provinces, and that the legions, roused by the edict, had promised to cut off the help the confederates were receiving from the kingdom of England. For this reason Ferdinand Alva, in order to turn away foreign troops, and especially the Germans who had flocked to fight under Orange for pay, from their oath of service to the confederate army, issued an edict to each and all of them that they might go home, and, granting them free passage through the provinces, ordered that a price be set on the arms of deserters. This was so that a German soldier, without money, would not turn to crime in the countryside, or, eager to keep himself alive, return to the service of Prince Orange. He also forbade grain and provisions to be carried from all Friesland, which is washed by the Vlie, the Lauwers and the Amel, to the confederate forces, and, cutting off the trade of the allied towns, ordered the royal camp to be stocked with supplies. Thus every plan that tended to weaken the confederacy, and every licence granted to the royal soldiers, was proclaimed through the market and the tribunals by Philip's edicts. Accordingly, the return of the exiles was blocked by new decrees too, and the estates of the fled nobility and of the proscribed citizens were, by renewed registers, adjudged to the royal treasury by the decree of the Senate. Then, lest the confederate society, worn down by these shifts of fortune, should revive throughout the province, Gaspar Robles led his troops, who had been paid for six months in Alva's camp, back to Friesland with a fleet of six ships; and, posting garrisons at Harlingen and Franeker to restrain the populace, he hurried on to Leeuwarden. There he was received by the bishop of Cuneri, the leading nobility, and the town magistrates, and by the greetings of the citizens who met him, and he carried away the distinguished glory of the courage and loyalty he had shown in the royal camp before Haarlem. Soon, having posted the greater part of the legion at Leeuwarden, he spread the remaining cohorts across the flat countryside and the towns to collect the payments, and he harshly ruled over the people, who were stubborn in paying taxes and often unable to pay, with a heavier command and with the unrestrained manners of masters.

units.la: Quippe crebrae terrarum inundationes opulentiam gentis non parum acciderant, mareque, diurni aestus, & in continentem se effundentis salsedine, ferendis frugibus utilem glebam corruperat. Cui malo diuturnae provincialium lites accedebant, quae reparandis aggerum molibus, Carolo Caesare sub Georgio Scenco, quadraginta ante annos coeptae, illum usque in diem pertinaciâ litigantium trahebantur.
units.tr: Indeed, the frequent floods of the land had not a little diminished the wealth of the people; and the daily tides of the sea, pouring into the mainland and laden with salt, had spoiled the soil, which was useful for bearing crops. To this evil were added the long-running lawsuits of the provincials, which had been begun forty years earlier under Charles Caesar, under Georg Scenco, over the repair of the dyke-works, and were dragged on to that very day by the obstinacy of the litigants.

units.la: Quippe maritimi, gubernante Frisiam Carolo Caesare, proxumum mare, continuas inundationes, & natam ex ijs egestatem querebantur. Nudatos littore agros, elisas, aut consumptas vetustate tabulationes, quas refici afflictae res non ferrent, nisi à mediterraneis praejuventur, in commune Westergoae exitium, & mox provinciae iturae. Aequum esse communi ope isti malo occurri, quod promiscuam perniciem, aut saltem metum incolentibus Westergoam daret. Non disceptandam eam litem in foro esse, quae proferri non quiret, exhaustâ agrorum fecunditate, & mari continuis diluvijs infesto. Nec Senatum Caesaris maritimis satis aequum, & esse in eo, qui privatae rei respectu publicam morentur. Inofficiosi suspectos submoveri per Caesarem debere, curandumque, ut, partium actis ad supremum Caesaris per Belgicam Senatum transmissis, diuturna lis sopiatur.
units.tr: Indeed, the people of the coast, while Charles Caesar governed Friesland, complained about the nearby sea, the constant inundations, and the poverty born from them. Their fields were stripped of their shores, and the embankments were ruined or worn away by age; and since their afflicted resources could not repair them unless the inland people helped, this would bring ruin on all of Westergo, and soon on the whole province. It was only fair, they said, that this evil be met by common effort, since it brought a shared destruction, or at least fear, to the inhabitants of Westergo. The matter, they argued, was not one to be argued in court, since the fertility of the fields was exhausted and the sea, with its continual floods, was a menace. Nor was Caesar's Senate fair to the coastal people, since in it were men who put their private interests before the public good. Those who were suspected of being partial should be removed by Caesar, and care should be taken that, once the records of both sides had been sent up by Caesar to the highest Senate in the Netherlands, the long-running dispute should be settled.

units.la: Reperio in actis istorum temporum, Carolum, velut miseratione maritimae per Westergoam gentis motum, rescriptum ex voto ijsdem maritimis tum indulsisse, mandasseque, ut suspecti partium Senatores judicio abstinerent, actaque litigantium Mechliniam, aut ad se perferrentur. Eosdem quoque Westergoos tam maritimos, quam mediterraneos cio. Io. neos, intercesione Georgij Scenci Præfecti, & Senatus Cæsarei consensus LXXXIII. venisse, ut aggerum refectio intra v. Kal. Mart. & octavum à festo Paschatos diem pro quantitate, & onere aureorum florenorum fieret, consultarentque interea Westergoi, an componi ex se litem, an deferri arbitrio Præfecti, & Senatus vellent.
units.tr: I find in the records of those times that Charles, moved as it were by pity for the coastal people of Westergo, granted them, by a rescript as they had asked, and ordered that the Senators who were suspected of partiality should refrain from judging, and that the records of the litigants should be carried to Mechelen or to him. The Westergoes, both coastal and inland, came with the mediation of Georg Scenco, the prefect, and with the consent of Caesar's Senate, in the year LXXXIII, on the agreement that the repair of the dykes be carried out within the period from the fifth day before the Kalends of March to the eighth day after Easter, in proportion to the amount and burden of the gold florins; and meanwhile the Westergoes were to consider whether they wished to settle the dispute among themselves or to refer it to the judgment of the prefect and the Senate.

units.la: Cæterum mediterraneis Westergois inveteratum jus acerrimam in defensionem vertebatur. Quippe majores suos nullis marinorum aggerum impendijs agros suos coluisse, hoc tantum adnixos, ne quid damni ex inundationibus terrarum, aut vicinis maritimis sentirent. Ideo privatos aggeres possessionibus suis præduxisse, quibus aquæ in interiora Westergoæ se effusuræ crebros per æstus certis obicibus sisterentur. Ijs vero sustinendis tributum quotannis conferri, nullo subsidio à maritimis Westergois petito, quibus fertiles agros, æque ac mediterraneis, colendos natura dedisset. Non esse maritimos Westergoos pecuniæ, aut virorum inopes, quo minus reficiendo aggeri pares sint, marinis diluvijs, relicto agris limo, nova fœcunditate injuriam pensantibus. Neque omnem Frisiæ populum mediterraneis locis agere posse, suisseque semper littorum accolas, sua forte & conditione nascendi, ijs locis ascriptos. Ita de sedibus suis maritimæ gentis majores non conquestos, fælicibus temporum ætatibus, suis agris ac latifundijs tam diu usos, donec intumescens Flevus, arrosis sensim ripis, & crepidine lacuum, lata per ostia, influxum maris lacesseret. Inde pro ratione æstuum, & tempestatum modicum littus Oceano objecisse, si pejora incommoda sentiat, majore opere muniendum. Iniquum scilicet esse, ex alieno discrimine, mediterraneos Westergoos nova onera sentire, & cum ex conventione, aut jure non obligentur, rescripto Cæsaris, aut per nova judicia gravari. Sed nec Carolum Cæsarem, etsi maritimis æquiorem, aliud eo rescripto voluisse, quam ut partium acta conficerentur, confectaque ac consignata ad supremum tribunal, aut ad se, finiendæ controversiæ mitterentur. Paratos se mediterraneos esse, eventum litis opperiri, sed hac cautione, ut pendente causa, maritimorum opere ac sumptu, agger ex consuetudine reficiatur, dum certas agendi, præstandique vices reis aut actoribus judicium assignaverit. Cæterum pertinacia & contatione partium, (quæ ut plurimum publica salubriaque consilia privatis ex odijs retardavere) & post interveniente civili bello, omne negotium prolatum, donec stupendo anni 1570. diluvio, miseratione supplicum maritimorum, quos illa præcipuè clades attriverat, communibus Westergoæ impendijs, salvo partium jure, reficiendum marinum aggerem Rex Philippus decerneret. Itaque discordiam populi trium quasi annorum diluvijs castigante Oceano, factum est, ut divulsæ partes coirent, dilationumq; forensium pertæsæ, præceps forum, & expedita judicia crescentibus instantibusque malis flagitarent.
units.tr: Moreover, the inland Westergoes defended their long-established right most fiercely. Their ancestors, they said, had cultivated their fields without any expense on the sea-dykes, relying only on this, that they should suffer no loss from the floods of the land or from the neighbouring coasts. For this reason they had extended private dykes along their estates, by which the waters that were to pour into the interior of Westergo were held back at fixed barriers during the tides. To maintain these, a tax was paid every year, without any help being asked from the coastal Westergoes, to whom nature had given fertile fields to cultivate just as it had to the inland people. The coastal Westergoes, they said, were not lacking in money or men, so that they could not repair the dyke equal to the task; the sea floods had left mud on their fields, and new fertility made up for the damage. Nor could the whole people of Friesland live in inland places; there had always been dwellers on the shores, who by their own chance and condition of birth were assigned to those places. Thus the ancestors of the coastal people had not complained about their homes; in the happy ages of the past they had enjoyed their fields and broad estates for as long as the swelling Vlie, gradually eating away its banks and the ridge of the lakes, had not yet pressed upon them through its broad mouths the inflow of the sea. Then, according to the force of the tides and storms, they had set a modest shore against the Ocean; if they now felt worse troubles, it must be fortified with greater labour. It was surely unjust, they argued, that the inland Westergoes should bear new burdens from another's danger, and that, since they were not bound by agreement or by law, they should be oppressed by a rescript of Caesar or by new judgments. But neither did Charles Caesar, though more favourable to the coastal people, wish anything by that rescript except that the records of both sides be drawn up, and that, once drawn up and sealed, they be sent to the highest tribunal, or to him, to end the controversy. The inland people were ready to wait for the outcome of the suit, but on this condition: that while the case was pending, the dyke be repaired as usual at the expense and labour of the coastal people, until the court should assign fixed turns of acting and of paying to the defendants or the plaintiffs. Yet the obstinacy and quarrelling of the parties (which, for the most part, had delayed public and wholesome plans by private hatreds), and afterwards the civil war that intervened, deferred the whole business, until, in the astonishing flood of 1570, in pity for the coastal suppliants, whom that disaster in particular had worn down, King Philip decreed that the coastal dyke should be repaired at the common expense of Westergo, with the rights of the parties preserved. Thus, since the Ocean, for about three years, had punished the discord of the people with its floods, the divided parties came together, and, weary of the delays of the courts, demanded a swift tribunal and quick judgments as the threatening evils grew and pressed upon them.

units.la: Unde conventio à mediterraneis, maritimisque Westergois x. Kal. Ianuar. scripta, omneque controversum, quod maritimos mediterraneosque Westergoos, etiam à Caroli Cæsaris ætate exercuerat, certis arbitris commissum. In eos Gasparus Roblesius Frisiæ Propræfectus, Balduinus Ronius Transisulaniæ Cancellarius, Gerardus Oftendorpius Senator, Joannes Fonckius Præpositus Ultrajectinus, ac secretioris Concilij Senator, & Igramus Achlenius Præses, delecti. Hoc vero cIↄ. Iö. cavebatur, ne à latâ sententiâ ulla provocatio esset, & ut ea Philippi regis assensu, & ratihabitione firmaretur. Ita pro mediterraneis Westergois Edzardus Sickingha, Senator regius, Hero Ockingha, Julius Dekema, H. Ebingha, Siricius Donia, Hector Dekama, Hesselus Hania, S. Dekama, J. Watnia, A. Tiessema, D. Fogelsangus, Fecco Rhala, Ruardus Hilconius Attiema, Roimerus Tiallengius pro Minnertsgais, Isbrandus Slotius Præpositus Aengiumanus, Foppo Grovesteinius, Lollius Ockingha, Hotso Aysma, Mintsius Buma, Tiallengus Sydsius pro Berlicomijs, J. Tritsum, Valerius Ockingha, Ruardus Petri, Hero Aggæus pro Dronrypijs, Gellius Gellij pastor Oosterlittanus, D. Fogelsangus pro Oosterviremijs, Livius Sibæus pro Oosterlittanis, Otto Galama, Gerlacus Ulpius Rispens, Oph. Imsvaldius, Julius Saclæus pro Oosterendijs, Leo Vibenius, Sixtus Tiallengius pastor, & Franciscus Tallum pro Tiumanis, Franciscus Wopconius Popta, Joannes Foppius pastor Weidumanus, Petrus Valta, Dion Hania, Serapius Bonga pro Huinsijs, & Lionsijs, Oedsius Petri pro Baardijs, Simon Nicolaus pro Winsemijs, S. Theodorus pastor Buranus, Petrus Widmarsius, Cornelius Joannis pastor in Slappeterp, Abbæus Tetardius, Diorræus Sipconius pro Schingensibus, Fomcko Wibenius pro Deinumanis, Poppo Burmania pro Edensibus, Rodmerus Regneri pro Wommelijs, Otto Galama, Franciscus Ulpius pro Wielsoripijs, Tiebbo Tabonius pro Boxumanis, Arnoldus Hardervicenus pro Regnero Anskio legato Hitsumano, Julius Hoffius pro Itenijs, Jorritius Wiarda pro ijsdem, Ruardus Roorda, Foppo Wopconius, Sixtus Leo pro Cubardijs, Epo Taconius pro Waxumanis, Edgerus Ruardus, Petrus Cammingha, R. Hemmema, Vitus Cammingha, & Titus Cammingha signavere.
units.tr: Hence an agreement was drawn up by the inland and the coastal Westergoes on 22 December, and every controversy that had troubled the coastal and inland Westergoes since the time of Charles Caesar was committed to chosen arbiters. For this purpose were chosen Gaspar Robles, deputy prefect of Friesland; Baldwin Ronius, chancellor of Transisulania; Gerard Oftendorp, senator; John Fonck, provost of Utrecht and senator of the more secret council; and Igram Achlen, president. It was provided, however, that there should be no appeal from the sentence pronounced, and that it should be confirmed by the assent and ratification of King Philip. Thus on behalf of the inland Westergoes signed: Edzard Sickingha, royal senator; Hero Ockingha; Julius Dekema; H. Ebingha; Siricius Donia; Hector Dekama; Hesselus Hania; S. Dekama; J. Watnia; A. Tiessema; D. Fogelsang; Fecco Rhala; Ruardus Hilconius Attiema; Roimerus Tiallengius for Minnertsga; Isbrand Slotius, provost of Aengwirden; Foppo Grovesteinius; Lollius Ockingha; Hotso Aysma; Mintsius Buma; Tiallengus Sydsius for Berlikum; J. Tritsum; Valerius Ockingha; Ruardus Petri; Hero Aggaeus for Dronrijp; Gellius Gellii, minister of Oosterlittens; D. Fogelsang for Oosterwierum; Livius Sibaeus for Oosterlittens; Otto Galama; Gerlach Ulpius Rispens; Oph. Imsvald; Julius Saclaeus for Oosterend; Leo Vibenius; Sixtus Tiallengius, minister; and Franciscus Tallum for Tzummarum; Franciscus Wopconius Popta; John Foppius, minister of Weidum; Peter Valta; Dion Hania; Serapius Bonga for Huins and Lions; Oedsius Petri for Baard; Simon Nicolaus for Winsum; S. Theodorus, minister of Buren; Peter Widmarsius; Cornelius Joannis, minister in Slappeterp; Abbaeus Tetardius; Diorraeus Sipconius for Schingen; Fomcko Wibenius for Deinum; Poppo Burmania for Eaddens; Rodmerus Regneri for Wommels; Otto Galama; Franciscus Ulpius for Wieuwerd; Tiebbo Tabonius for Boksum; Arnold Hardervicenus for Regnerus Anskius, the legate of Hitsum; Julius Hoffius for Itens; Jorritius Wiarda for the same; Ruardus Roorda; Foppo Wopconius; Sixtus Leo for Kubaard; Epo Taconius for Waaxens; Edgerus Ruardus; Peter Cammingha; R. Hemmema; Vitus Cammingha; and Titus Cammingha.

units.la: Pro maritimis vero Westergois, Cunerus Petri Episcopus Leovardiensis, Scelto Liauckama, Leo Syricius, V. Hiddama, L. Watnia, Haio Sibæus. Et nos pro tribus pagis, salvo jure nostro, Iacobus Formadler, Jacobus Abbæus, L. Walckama, Edo Garbranda, A. Cronenburg, Wilhelmus Ioannis, Sintius Popma, Dothias Bonga, Sibrandus Pierius, Upco Hajonius, D. Albertus Hesselus Reen pastor in Midlum, Nicolaus Folckertius, Edo Nicolai, D. Imo Simonides vicarius Harlinganus, D. Heino Nicolaus vicarius ibidem, Elco Lollius, Hobbius Regneri, Wopco Taeclesius, Sicco Nicolai Bramsius, Gerardus Intenius, Vibius Andreæ, D. Nicolaus Sixti vicarius, Marcus Marci, D. Sibrandus vicarius in Petersbierum, Wibrandus Suffridus Not. Pub. D. Wilhelmus Noviomagus, D. Wibrandus Harlinganus pastor in Petersbierum, D. Martinus Welmi pastor in Pingum, Bauco Rommarda pro Pingumanis, Pierius Aggæus pastor Wonsius, Suffridus Franciscus pastor in Winaldum, Douwo Hesselius pro Abbingaverijs, H. de Pau pro Maccomijs, Thomas Hiddius pro Sirichijs, Sibrandus Wibranda pro Petersbyremijs, Abbæus Rotterus, Ioannes Duyshenius, Petrus Medenblicanus Prior Luinckerckius & Achlemius, Petrus Douwonius & Siricius Leo subscripsere.
units.tr: As for the maritime Westergoers, Cunerus Petri, Bishop of Leeuwarden, Scelto Liauckama, Leo Syricius, V. Hiddama, L. Watnia, and Haio Sibaeus signed. For ourselves, on behalf of the three districts, saving our right, Jacobus Formadler, Jacobus Abbaeus, L. Walckama, Edo Garbranda, A. Cronenburg, Wilhelmus Ioannis, Sintius Popma, Dothias Bonga, Sibrandus Pierius, Upco Hajonius, D. Albertus Hesselus, minister in Midlum, Nicolaus Folckertius, Edo Nicolai, D. Imo Simonides, vicar of Harlingen, D. Heino Nicolaus, vicar there, Elco Lollius, Hobbius Regneri, Wopco Taeclesius, Sicco Nicolai Bramsius, Gerardus Intenius, Vibius Andreae, D. Nicolaus Sixti, vicar, Marcus Marci, D. Sibrandus, vicar in Petersbierum, Wibrandus Suffridus, notary public, D. Wilhelmus Noviomagus, D. Wibrandus Harlinganus, minister in Petersbierum, D. Martinus Welmi, minister in Pingum, Bauco Rommarda on behalf of the Pingumers, Pierius Aggaeus, minister at Wons, Suffridus Franciscus, minister in Winaldum, Douwo Hesselius on behalf of the Abbingaveri, H. de Pau on behalf of the Maccomers, Thomas Hiddius on behalf of the Sirichers, Sibrandus Wibranda on behalf of the Petersbyremers, Abbaeus Rotterus, Ioannes Duyshenius, Petrus Medenblicanus, prior, Luinckerckius and Achlemius, Petrus Douwonius and Siricius Leo subscribed.

units.la: Mox quo cæteri mediterranei Westergoi assensum conventioni darent, rent, Iulio Dekama, & Heroni Ockingha arbitrorum delegatis reliquam nobilitatem, & proprietarios agrorum convocandi potestas facta, recitatumque per templa, & post praeconis voce edictum, quo ad iv. Ian. sistere se contumaces, & a publico dissentientes jubebantur. Igitur Petrus Boimerus Iureconsultus & Oldermannus Franequerensium, Hero Ockingha pro Eduarda Hoxveriâ, Geroldus Cammingha, Carolus Sternzaeus, Poppo Doiemus, Allardus Ottonius, & Gerardus Tetlaeus in Curiâ oppidanâ comparuere, auditisq; Julij Dekama Senatoris Regij postulatis conventionem ratam fecêre. Inde acta ei rei scripta, ac à Petro Boimero, Amelià Grombachiâ, Herone Ockingha, Eduardâ Hoxveriâ, Carolo Sternzeo, Geroldo Cammingha, Fokelâ Martenià, Catharinâ Gratingiâ, Allardo Ottonio, & Gerardo Tetlaeo signata.
units.tr: Soon afterwards, so that the rest of the inland Westergoers might give their assent to the agreement, the power was granted to Julius Dekama and Hero Ockingha, delegates of the arbiters, to summon the remaining nobility and the owners of the land. A proclamation was read in the churches and afterwards announced by a herald's voice, ordering the obstinate and those dissenting from the public good to appear by the fourth of January. Accordingly Petrus Boimerus, jurisconsult and alderman of the Franekerers, Hero Ockingha on behalf of Eduarda Hoxveria, Geroldus Cammingha, Carolus Sternzaeus, Poppo Doiemus, Allardus Ottonius and Gerardus Tetlaeus appeared in the town hall. After hearing the demands of Julius Dekama, royal senator, they ratified the agreement. Thereupon a written record of the matter was made and signed by Petrus Boimerus, Amelia Grombachia, Hero Ockingha, Eduarda Hoxveria, Carolus Sternzeus, Geroldus Cammingha, Fokela Martenia, Catharina Gratingia, Allardus Ottonius and Gerardus Tetlaeus.

units.la: Pactionem quoque à maritimis, mediterraneisque Westergois initam Ferdinandus Albanus nomine Philippi regis ratam habuit, eaque de re, petentibus patribus, rescriptum indulsit. Hoc in acta relatum Noviomagi v. Kal. April. ac Albani manu signatum. Tum pactione rescripto firmatâ Kal. April. diem caeptando apud Leovardios arbitrorum conventui praefinivit, animumque ferocem sola urbium excidia, & sanguinem foederati populi spirantem, velut continuo furori intervallum largitus pacis negotio exercuit. Caeterum arbitris in diversa distractis, & fatali velut partium mora salubria consilia, etiam asperrimi Ducis, praepediebantur. Quare maritimi Westergoi metuentes malorum, ac ut mare prolatis aggerum curis tempestate, aut aestu intumesceret, supplicationem hunc in modum ad Ferdinandum Albanum misere.
units.tr: Ferdinandus Albanus also ratified, in the name of King Philip, the pact entered into by the maritime and inland Westergoers, and at the request of the fathers he granted a rescript on this matter. This was entered in the records at Noviomagus on the fifth day before the Kalends of April, and signed by Alba's hand. Then, the pact having been confirmed by the rescript, he appointed a day on the Kalends of April at Leeuwarden for a meeting of the arbiters, and, granting a brief respite to his fierce spirit, which breathed only the destruction of cities and the blood of the confederated people, as if to a pause in his continual fury, he occupied himself with the business of peace. However, the arbiters were pulled in different directions, and as if by a fatal delay of the parties, wholesome counsels were hindered, even those of the most harsh Duke. Therefore the maritime Westergoers, fearing evils, and that the sea might swell by a storm or a tide because of the neglected care of the dykes, sent a petition to Ferdinandus Albanus in this manner.

units.la: ILLUSTRISSIME PRAEFECTE.
units.tr: MOST ILLUSTRIOUS PREFECT,

units.la: MUltis ab hinc annis reficiendo marino aggeri gravia onera sustinuimus. Ideo ad Carolum Caesarem olim supplices devoluti remedia nostris malis, ac subsidia oravimus. Caesar vero rescriptum indulsit, mandavitque Hyppolito Persinio Senatus tum Praesidi, caeterisque per Frisiam Senatoribus, (ad quos aggerum res non spectaret) ne actorum judicialium quae comperendinationes essent, caeterum acta partium à Frisiae Senatu visitata Bruxellas ad Senatum Secretiorum transmitterentur. Et quoniam, actis confectis, mare anno 1570. in Westergoam, aut saltem potissimam Westergoae partem se effudit, ita aggeres, tabulationes, cateraque littorum praesidia vi ac impetu fluctuum dissecit. Damnis vero datis, quia succurrere nostrarum virium non erat, placuit tibi, Illustrissime Dux, regio Philippi nomine decernere, ut communibus Westergoae impendijs pristinam in molem à Bildâ in Maccomanum emissarium agger erigeretur, conciliandisque interea partibus à Senatu regio, aut à te jure Principis leges scriberentur. Caeterum quoniam aliud rescriptum mediterraneis post concessisti, quo differri anterius decretum jubebas, ita Roblesium, Romum & Ostendorpium delegasti, qui rescriptorum tuorum interpretes essent, eoque facto omne inter maritimos mediterraneosque Westergoos controversum, evocatis ex Hollandiâ, Zelandiâque Senatoribus, & aggerum Praefectis definirent. Postquam vero turbae per Hollandiam, Zelandiamque increvere, interceptis commeantium itineribus, mediterranei, maritimique Westergoi in conventionem condescenderunt, definienda litis potestate, Gasparo Roblefio, Baldvino Ronio, Gerardo Ostendor- pio, Ioanni Fonckio, & Igramo Achlenio factâ. Nos vero maritimi non a-liam in spem conventioni nos submisimus, quam ut omnes Westergoi iisdem pactis se obligarent, omnesque lites, ad rem aggerum spectantes, concordi Westergoæ populo finirentur. Cæterum pervicaciâ eorum, qui exercere odia & lites, quam suis, & reipub. commodis consulere maluerunt, spes nostræ elula, interverso amicæ compositionis fructu, qui haud dubie ad omnem Westergoam perventurus fuisset. Idem scias, Illustrissime Dux, Roblefium, idem Fonckium, ac cæteros arbitros sentire. Hoc interim restat, ut, illorum arbitriis lite commissâ, salaria habeant, ac ut ea specie tributi colligi per Westergoam sinas, dum, qui lite cadant, sumptus & impendia refundant. Maritimos certe nos ulterioribus expensis gravari, nec turbæ, quibus præcipuè infestamur, nec alluens mare permittunt. Neque enim pendendo levi tributo, quod ante annum reficiendo aggeri decrevimus, pares nos egestas facit, incrementum haud dubie factura, nisi omnium inter Westergoos litium finis sit, aggerumque damna communibus subsidiis sarciantur. Tuum erit, Illustrissime Præfecte, potestatem arbitris facere, lites etiam quascumque finiendi, statuendique, ut vim ac robur illorum judicia sortiantur, ac si Senatus Secretiorum determinandis controversiis præsedisset. Et quia ordinariæ jurisdictionis incapaces arbitri sunt, rogamus, ut jus illis ac potestatem facias è florenis aureis modicum tributum cogendi, ne damnosa iisdem arbitris sua officia sint, & ne defectu aris nostræ lites moram ferant. Id si facias, Illustrissime Dux, saluti tuæ vota nuncupabimus.
units.tr: For many years we have borne heavy burdens in repairing the sea wall. Therefore, having once humbly appealed to Emperor Charles, we begged for remedies for our troubles and for aid. The Emperor indeed granted a rescript and charged Hippolytus Persinius, then president of the Senate, and the other senators throughout Friesland (to whom the matter of the dykes did not pertain), that the judicial records, which were matters for adjournment, should not be sent, but that the records of the parties, examined by the Senate of Friesland, should be transmitted to the Secret Council at Brussels. And since, when the records were completed, the sea in the year 1570 poured into Westergo, or at least into the greater part of Westergo, and so broke through the dykes, embankments and other coastal defences with the force and violence of the waves, and since, the damage having been done and our own resources not being sufficient to help, it pleased you, most illustrious Duke, to decree in the king's name Philip that the former dyke should be rebuilt from Bilda to the Maccomer outlet at the common expense of Westergo, and that meanwhile, with the parties being reconciled, laws should be written by the royal Senate or by you with the authority of a prince. However, since you afterwards granted another rescript to the inland districts, ordering the earlier decree to be deferred, you appointed Roblesius, Romus and Ostendorpius to be interpreters of your rescripts, and by this means they were to settle every dispute between the maritime and inland Westergoers, summoning senators from Holland and Zeeland and the prefects of the dykes. But after the disturbances spread through Holland and Zeeland, and the roads of travellers were cut off, the inland and maritime Westergoers came to an agreement, with the power of settling the dispute given to Gaspar Roblesius, Baldwin Ronius, Gerardus Ostendorpius, Joannes Fonckius and Igramus Achlenius. We maritime folk submitted to the agreement with no other hope than that all the Westergoers would bind themselves by the same terms, and that all lawsuits concerning the dykes would be settled by the united people of Westergo. But by the obstinacy of those who preferred to pursue hatreds and lawsuits rather than to look to their own and the public advantage, our hopes were cut short, and the fruit of a friendly settlement, which would undoubtedly have reached all Westergo, was lost. You should know, most illustrious Duke, that Roblesius, Fonckius and the other arbiters think the same. It remains, then, that, since the dispute has been committed to their judgment, they should have salaries, and that you allow them to collect this under the name of a tax throughout Westergo, while those who lose the suit repay the costs and expenses. For we maritime people are certainly burdened by further expenses, which neither the crowds that chiefly trouble us nor the sea washing our shores allow. For the light tax which we decided, a year ago, to pay for repairing the dyke does not make us equal to these burdens, and it will undoubtedly grow, unless there is an end to all the lawsuits among the Westergoers and the losses to the dykes are made good by common funds. It will be your task, most illustrious Prefect, to give the arbiters power to settle and decide any lawsuits whatever, so that their judgments may have the force and strength of those of the Senate of the Secret Council, had it presided over the decision of the disputes. And since the arbiters are not competent in ordinary jurisdiction, we ask that you grant them the right and power to levy a small tax from the gold florins, so that their offices may not be a loss to them and that lawsuits may not be delayed for lack of money. If you do this, most illustrious Duke, we will offer vows for your welfare.

units.la: Hæc à Cunero Episcopo, Ulpio Hiddama, Jacobo Herbajo, L. Watnia signata.
units.tr: These were signed by Cunerus, the bishop, Ulpius Hiddama, Jacobus Herbajus, and L. Watnia.

units.la: Rescriptum Albani tale erat.
units.tr: The rescript of Alva was as follows.

units.la: QVandoquidem è supplicatione maritimorum Westergoorum certior factus sum, eam, ut bono publico, conciliandæque inter Philippi regis subditos concordiæ, ita conservandis præmuniendisque adversum maris violentiam agris spectare, Regisque etiam, ut id fiat, quam maxime interesse. Ita Philippi nomine potestatem facio Billio, Fonckio, Cancellario Transisulaniæ, Ostendorpio & Præsidi Frisiæ, litem, processumque judiciarium, visitandi, definiendique. Itaq; eosdem arbitros Senatui Secretiorum, quem huic rei cognoscendæ delegeram, substituo, voloque ut eorum sententia idem ponderis habeat, ac si Senatus Secretiorum pronuntiasset. Salariis vero corrogandis, jus facio iisdem arbitris tributum per Westergoam colligendi, ne quid morâ interveniat, mandoque ut rei judicatæ partes ex æquo pareant. Datum Noviomagi VI. Kal. Iul. Anno cIↄ. Iↄ. LXXIII.
units.tr: Since I have been informed by the petition of the maritime Westergoers that it concerns the public good and the establishment of concord among King Philip's subjects, and that the fields must be preserved and fortified against the violence of the sea, and that it is also very much in the King's interest that this be done: therefore, in Philip's name, I grant power to Billius, Fonckius (chancellor of Overijssel), Ostendorpius and the President of Friesland to examine and decide the dispute and the judicial proceedings. I substitute these same arbitrators for the Council of Secret Affairs, which I had appointed to hear this matter, and I wish their judgment to carry the same weight as if the Council of Secret Affairs had pronounced it. To raise their salaries, I grant the same arbitrators the right to collect a tax throughout Westergo, so that nothing is delayed, and I order that the parties obey the judgment equally. Given at Nijmegen, the 6th day before the Kalends of July, in the year 1573.

units.la: F. Dvc de Alva.
units.tr: F. Duke of Alva.

units.la: Ad Mandatum
units.tr: By order.

units.la: Berti.
units.tr: Berti.

units.la: Igitur, vergente Augusto mense, arbitrorum conventus Leovardiæ in arce regiâ indictus. Ibi Roblefius expositâ coram arbitris sui consilij ratione, hunc in modum disseruit.
units.tr: Therefore, as August drew to a close, the arbitrators were summoned to meet at Leeuwarden in the royal citadel. There Roblesius, having set out before the arbitrators the reasons of his council, spoke to this effect:

units.la: On unius anni calamitate exagitamur, ceterum intestino bello diu attriti, non minus periculum à circumfuso fermè mari habuimus. Majores hujus gentis non unâ temporum ætate ijs malis obnoxij fuere, cum Flevus, Rhenum flumen latissimo alveo, & immensis lacubus difficulter claudens, crepidine ripæ à continente sensim avulsâ, non agris tantum hisce, ceterum pagis, vitisque diluvia attulit. Sed libertate olim ante Principum tempora usis diuturna factiones curam provincia excussere, probatumque fuit, studia pacis grassantibus armis vilescere. Vbi vero salutaris Principis dominatio civiles discordias sedavit, experti fuere quanta publici boni apud Principem desideria essent, & quantum interesset inter maris æstus ac eluviones terram incolentibus donari. Hoc modo Biltanis agris munimentum curâ Prineipis obductum, qui ne alieni littoris contiguitate damnum sentirent, ceteris quoque præductæ moles Oceanum reppulere. Sic agros coluêre ab inundationibus tutos, intraque littora conseptum mare fecundam annonæ provinciam, & simul affluentiam opum dedit. Post vero luxuriâ fortunæ corrupta gentes, ut ostenderent, quam difficilis ac ardua felicitatis possessio esset, sumptis in Principem armis, & simul discordijs civilibus agitata pacis iterum consilia, & fructus neglexere. Itaque mare, velut civilis dissidij ultrix, ante triennium, & post ruptis fluctuum repagulis omnem provinciam adflixit. Neque frumenta tantum, & pecora in profundum acta, ceterum multorum millium internecione surgens diluvium, cultissimis terris solitudinem, regio ærario inopiam, egestatem privato censui dedit. Protrahi longius reprimendi maris consilia sine ultimi exitu metu non possunt. Nisi forte Biltanos quoque agros novo cultu, & alluvione felices infensanti rursum Oceano permittimus. Qui diurnis æstibus vada & obices reserbens, mox procellâ æstus, plenilunijs novilunijsque tumidior, perpetuum velut naturæ bellum cum hac ipsâ continente adhuc exercet. Cujus ferocia quoque factum est, ut populus ante litium & discordiarum ferax, suis sedibus metuens, &, si mare latius terminos extendat, necessario coloniam facturus, nostris arbitrijs ac judicijs se permiserit, extremisque malis præceps remedium poposcerit. Nostrum erit, pacem ac securitatem volenti populo dare, munitosque Philippi regis rescripto provincialium desiderijs, & simul discrimini publico subvenire. Hoc agendo æqui in Principem, in commissum nobis populum erimus, tutiores terras post compositam litem habituram. Vt eam finiamus non actis, rescriptisque Principum, sed solâ conscientiâ egebimus. Hac consultâ æquitatem spectabimus. Sin vero querimonijs supplicum, aut eorum importunitati auscultemus, trahemus conventum, & simul offensiones partium, quæ judicaturo posthabendæ sunt. De me testor, nihil affectibus daturum, ceterum faveris, aut odij immunem publica commoda privatis utilitatibus anteposituram.
units.tr: We are harassed by a calamity of one year, and, worn down for a long time by civil war, we have also been in no less danger from the sea that surrounds almost the whole land. The ancestors of this people were exposed to these evils not only in one age; for the Flevus, a river that discharges the Rhine through a very wide channel and immense lakes, tearing away from the mainland by degrees along the bank, brought floods not only to these fields but to villages and vineyards. But in ancient times, when they enjoyed liberty before the rule of princes, long-lasting factions shook the province from its care, and it was proved that the aims of peace grow worthless while arms rage. But when the beneficial rule of a prince calmed civil discord, they learned how greatly the people desired the public good from the prince, and how much it mattered that those who dwell on the land be shielded from the tides and inundations of the sea. In this way, by the prince's care, a bulwark was drawn across the Biltani fields, and so that they might not suffer harm from their neighbourhood to a foreign shore, the dykes that were built forward also drove back the ocean. Thus they cultivated fields safe from floods, and the sea, enclosed within the shores, gave the province fertility of crops and at the same time an abundance of wealth. But afterwards the peoples, their fortunes corrupted by luxury, to show how difficult and arduous the possession of prosperity is, took up arms against the prince, and, stirred by civil discords, neglected both the counsels of peace and its fruits. And so the sea, as the avenger of civil dissension, a little less than three years ago, after the barriers of the waves were broken, afflicted the whole province. Not only were grain and cattle swept away into the deep, but the flood, rising with the slaughter of many thousands, reduced the most cultivated lands to desolation, the royal treasury to poverty, and private property to want. The plans for restraining the sea cannot be postponed any longer without fear of final ruin. Unless perhaps we are to surrender the Biltani fields, made happy by new cultivation and by alluvial soil, again to the raging ocean, which, opening its shallows and barriers by daily tides, and then fiercer with the storm of the tide at full and new moon, still wages what is almost a perpetual war of nature against this very land. Because of its ferocity, the people, once rich in lawsuits and quarrels, fearing for their homes, and about to make a colony necessarily if the sea should extend its bounds more widely, have placed themselves under our judgment and decisions, and, rushing toward the greatest evils, have sought a remedy. It is for us to give peace and security to a people who wish it, and by the rescript of King Philip to fortify the desires of the provincials and at the same time to help the public danger. By doing this we shall be just toward the Prince and toward the people entrusted to us, and the lands will have greater safety once the dispute is settled. To end it we shall need not the acts and rescripts of princes, but only our conscience. Having consulted this, we shall look to equity. But if we were to listen to the complaints of the suppliants, or to their importunity, we would drag out the meeting, and at the same time the offences of the parties, which ought to be set aside by the one who is to judge. Concerning myself I testify that I will give nothing to passions; rather, free of hatred or favour, I will place public advantages before private interests.

units.la: Hæc Roblesius.
units.tr: Thus spoke Roblesius.

units.la: Mox evolvendis partium actis consumpto triduo, bono exitu litem clausit, dimissoq; conventu Joannem Fonckium unum ex arbitris ad Ferdinandum Albanum amandavit, qui adornandæ classi, & maturandis in minores Frisios expeditionibus Amstelodami tum agebat. Ibi Fonckius gesti negotij, & definitæ inter Welbergoos litis certiorem Albanum fecit, populumque Westergoum ante discordiam, & judicia novis dissensionibus morantem, laudabilem in concordiam coaluisse. Nihil verò aliud desiderari, quam ut Westergoi fructum judicij sen-tiant, publicenturque acta, quorum desiderio avidæ partes teneantur. Quare Albanus vir imperiosæ severitatis, litteras Amstelodamo VII. Eid. Sept. in Frisiam ad Roblesium dedit, quo, curante adhuc Philippi res per Geldriam Ægidio Barlamontio Hyergio, per arbitros decreta omnem in populum vulgarentur:
units.tr: Soon, after three days spent going through the parties' records, he brought the dispute to a good conclusion, and, the meeting being dismissed, he sent John Fonckius, one of the arbitrators, to Ferdinand Alva, who was then at Amsterdam, busy with equipping the fleet and hastening the expeditions against the Lesser Frisians. There Fonckius informed Alva of the business carried out and of the dispute settled between the Westergoers, and that the people of Westergo, who before had been delayed by discord and lawsuits from new quarrels, had joined in a commendable concord. He said that nothing else was wanted but that the Westergoers should feel the fruit of the judgment, and that the records should be published, whose desire held the eager parties in suspense. Therefore Alva, a man of imperious severity, gave letters from Amsterdam on the 7th day before the Ides of September to Roblesius in Friesland, by which, while King Philip's affairs were still being managed through Gelderland by Egidius Barlaimont Hyergius, the decisions of the arbitrators were to be made known to the whole people:

units.la: Præpositus Ultrajectinus Ioannes Fonckius mihi apud Amstelodamenses hoc tempore agenti fidem fecit, definitam vos per arbitros aggerum litem esse. Ego vero Regi Philippo, & vobis gratulor, ejusque nomine acta vestra rata habeo, testesque regiæ & meæ fidei litteras subjungo. Tibi mando, Roblesi, ut extemplo Cancellarium, Ronium, Ostendorpium, (neque enim Fonckium hoc tempore dimittere queo) Leovardiam voces, obsignataque per vos arbitros publicari cures ocyus.
units.tr: John Fonckius, provost of Utrecht, has assured me, while I am at present dealing in Amsterdam, that the dispute over the dykes has been settled by you as arbitrators. I indeed congratulate King Philip and you, and in his name I hold your acts valid, and I append letters of the king's and my own faith as witnesses. I order you, Roblesius, to summon at once to Leeuwarden the Chancellor, Ronius and Ostendorpius (for I cannot release Fonckius at this time), and to see to it that what has been sealed by you arbitrators is published as quickly as possible.

units.la: Hæc ALBANI manu signata.
units.tr: These things, signed by the hand of Alva.

units.la: Itaque ad v. Eid. Novemb. diem partes Leovardiam, audiendam ad sententiam, citatæ, litteræque isti rei scriptæ Gasparis Roblesij, ac Præsidis manu signatæ. Cæterum omisså in ijs omnium litium, quæ universis Westergois communes essent, mentione, Westergoorum delegati, qui tum adesant, in arcem regiam vocati.
units.tr: Accordingly, on the 5th day before the Ides of November (9 November), the parties were summoned to Leeuwarden to hear the sentence, and the letters written on this matter, signed by the hand of Gaspar Roblesius and the President, were read. However, omitting any mention in them of those lawsuits which were common to all the Westergoers, the delegates of the Westergoers who were then present were called into the royal citadel.

units.la: Ibi ACHLENIUS.
units.tr: Here Achlenius.

units.la: Itari (inquit) vos fecimus, ut audiretis quæ à nobis arbitris decreta sint, & quæ dirimendis maritimis, mediterraneisque Westergois tantum spectabant. Nos vero, quoniam omne controversum, inter vos Westergoos, definivimus, id vobis indicandum duximus, quo de nostris in vos officijs vobis constaret. Et quoniam Cancellarium Ronium, Fonckium, & Ostendorpium abesse non ignoratis, deliberabitis inter vos, an pronuntiari à nobis decretum velitis, an differri, dum reliqui arbitri præsto sint. Vestrum erit id nobis significare, ac per acta nos docere, quo diem præsiniamus promulgandis decretis opportunum.
units.tr: We have had you come, he said, so that you might hear what has been decided by us as arbiters, and what concerned only the maritime and inland Westergoers in settling their disputes. Since we have settled every dispute among you Westergoers, we thought it right to inform you of this, so that you may know what we have done for you. And since you know that Cancellarius Ronius, Fonckius and Ostendorpius are absent, you will deliberate among yourselves whether you wish the decision to be announced by us now or postponed until the remaining arbiters are present. It will be for you to tell us this and to let us know by the record which day we should fix as suitable for publishing the decisions.

units.la: Mox pro maritimis Westergois rescriptum.
units.tr: Soon a reply was given on behalf of the maritime Westergoers.

units.la: Placere compendium temporis, ne quid mali prolatis decretis interveniat. Neque esse necessariam reliquorum arbitrorum præsentiam, quos aliorsum turbidi temporis tædium, aut sollicitudo vocaverit. Roblesij Pro-præfecti, & Achlenij Præsidis fidem solemnibus interponi. Ea rata se habere.
units.tr: They were pleased to save time, so that nothing bad might come of the decisions being announced. The presence of the remaining arbiters was not necessary, whom the weariness or anxiety of the troubled times might have called elsewhere. They confirmed with the solemn pledge of Roblesius, the Pro-prefect, and Achlenius, the President, that they regarded the decision as binding.

units.la: Sic pro maritimis Cunerus Petri Episcopus, Scelto Liauckama, Ulpius Hiddama, Dothias Bonga, L. Watnia, Leo Syricius, Tzommo Mantgumanus procurator coenobij Achlomani rescripsere. Idem à mediterraneorum delegatis Sixto Tiallengio Presbytero Tiumano, Francisco Tallumio, Petro Boimero, & Æmylio Adama pro Franequeranis, Serapio Bonga, & Simone Nicolao pro Baerderanis, Jovio Lyclesio, & Gerlaco Rispenio pro Hinnardijs, Siccone Gerritio, & Jetsone Gerconio pro Menaldumanis, Livio Jacobi pro Minnertsgais, Jacobo Formadler pro Tiumarumanis & Firdgumanis, Jacobo Hobbio pro Osterbiremijs factum. Tum assensus nobilium quorundam subsecutus, actaq; à Julio Dekama, H. Ebinga, Herone Ockingha, Hector ctore Dekama, & Ruardo Roorda signata. Cæteri quoque Australes Westergoi una cum Sylvestrium Legatis, qui nec maritimis, nec mediterraneis quinque præturarum Westergois accensebantur, octiduo effluxo, velut tempore ad deliberandum capto, omne quod ab arbitris gestum, scriptum, judicandum, publicandumque esset, approbravere, potestate vulgandi Roblesio, & Achlenio Præsidi facta. Ita per Petrum Frittema Senatorem Regium pro Wimbritserijs, Paulum Costerium priorem in Thabor, Joannem Wittenium priorem in Haska, Douwonem Roordam pro Snecanis, Bernardum Romckenium pro Bolsuerdijs, Vibium Douwonium pro Hindelopijs, Ulpium Nicolaum pro Worcumanis, Gerardum Olphartium pro Hemelum-olpherdijs, Nordvoldijs & Staurijs, Hoitonem Tenium, Gellium Tarquinium pro Geesterlandis, Geroldum Herama, Douwonem Herama, Folpardum Titum Baard pro Wonseranis, Titum Suffridæum pro Ilstanis, Annam Tarquinium, Hoitonem Hinnesium pro Donieverstallijs, Gerbrandum Mintium pro Lemsteranis quinque pagicis signatum. Hæc in Jacobæorum æde Leovardiæ gesta. v. Kid. Nov.
units.tr: Thus on behalf of the maritime people Cunerus Petri, Bishop, Scelto Liauckama, Ulpius Hiddama, Dothias Bonga, L. Watnia, Leo Syricius, and Tzommo Mantgumanus, procurator of the monastery of Achlomanus, replied in writing. The same was done by the envoys of the inland people: Sixtus Tiallengius, presbyter of Tiuma, Franciscus Tallumius, Petrus Boimerus and Aemylius Adama for the Franequerani; Serapius Bonga and Simon Nicolaus for the Baerderani; Jovius Lyclesius and Gerlacus Rispenius for the Hinnardi; Siccho Gerritius and Jetso Gerconius for the Menaldumani; Livius Jacobi for the Minnertsgai; Jacobus Formadler for the Tiumarumani and Firdgumani; and Jacobus Hobbius for the Osterbiremi. Then the assent of certain nobles followed, and the document was signed by Julius Dekama, H. Ebinga, Hero Ockingha, Hector Dekama and Ruardus Roorda. The other southern Westergoers too, together with the envoys of the Sylvestri, who were counted neither among the maritime nor among the inland Westergoers of the five districts, approved after eight days had passed, as if that were the time taken for deliberation, everything that had been done, written, judged and to be published by the arbiters, and they gave Roblesius and Achlenius the President leave to make it public. So through Petrus Frittema, royal senator, for the Wimbritseri; Paulus Costerius, prior in Thabor; Joannes Wittenius, prior in Haska; Douwo Roorda for the Snecani; Bernardus Romckenius for the Bolsuerdi; Vibius Douwonius for the Hindelopi; Ulpius Nicolaus for the Worcumani; Gerardus Olphartius for the Hemelum-olpherdi, Nordvoldi and Stauri; Hoito Tenius; Gellius Tarquinius for the Geesterlandi; Geroldus Herama; Douwo Herama; Folpardus Titus Baard for the Wonserani; Titus Suffridaeus for the Ilstani; Anna Tarquinius; Hoito Hinnesius for the Donieverstalli; and Gerbrandus Mintius for the Lemsterani, the five districts signed. These things were done in the church of the Jacobites at Leeuwarden, on the fifth day before the Kalends of November.

units.la: Quare cum litteris citatorijs in omnem non solum Westergoam, sed Sylvestrium tractum tabelliones missi, partesque ad xiv. Kal. Dec. adesse Leovardiæ jussæ. In ijs Menaldumæi, Antistes Aengiumanus, Baerderani, Monachobajumenses Cœnobitæ, Hennardij, Franequerani, Minnertsgai, Barrani, Bolsuerdij, Cœnobitæ Wonserani, Antistes Floridi Campi, Oegani Cœnobij, Snecenses, Cœnobitæ Winbritserij, Cœnobitæ Thaboritani, Hospitalij, Nazareni, Groendiceni, Neoclosterij, Woldseindij, Ilstani, Carmelitæ, Worconiani, Cœnobitæ, Hindelopij, Staurij, Hemelumolphardij, Nordvoldij, Antistes Hemelumanus, Geesterlandi, Donieverstallij, Slotenses, Lemsterani, Haskerij quinque pagici, Prior Haskerius, Scoterlandi, Commendator Cœnobij Opsterlandi, Anguirdij, Cœnobitæ Steenkerkani, & Utingerani fuere. Itaque in Basili à confidente Roblesio Pro-præfecto, & Senatu regio sententia recitata.
units.tr: Therefore, with citation letters, messengers were sent into the whole of Westergo, and not only there but also into the Sylvestri district, and the parties were ordered to appear at Leeuwarden on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of December. Among those who came were: the Menaldumaei; the abbot of Aengium; the Baerderani; the monks of Monachobaju; the Hinnardi; the Franequerani; the Minnertsgai; the Barrani; the Bolsuerdi; the monks of Wonsera; the abbot of Floridus Campus; the monastery of Oega; the Snecenses; the monks of Winbritseri; the monks of Thabor; the Hospitalii; the Nazareni; the Groendiceni; the Neoclosterii; the Woldseindi; the Ilstani; the Carmelites; the Worconiani; the monks; the Hindelopi; the Stauri; the Hemelumolphardi; the Nordvoldi; the abbot of Hemelum; the Geesterlandi; the Donieverstalli; the Slotenses; the Lemsterani; the five districts of Haski; the prior of Haska; the Scoterlandi; the commendator of the monastery of Opsterland; the Anguirdi; the monks of Steenkerk; and the Utingerani. Then, in Basel, the decision was read out by Roblesius, the Pro-prefect, with the royal senate present.

units.la: EA cautum fuit, ut actiones utrinque cessarent, nulloque actoris, aut rei respectu diuturna litis impendia reciprocâ compensatione sanarentur. Rescripta quoque Principis, Præfectorumque, quæ jam ante miseratio recurrentium inundationum, aut preces supplicum extorserant, post terminatam litem rescinderentur, valeretque pronuntiatum à Georgio Scenco Gubernatore Cæsaris Anno 1533. cæterisque arbitris definitum. Itaque aggerum spatia, quæ à Bilta Harlingam versus mari objacent, mediterraneis Westergois, reliqua ab Harlingâ in Austrum ad emissarium Maccumanum excurrentia, maritimis assignata. Decretum quoque, ut tabulationes post inundationem Anni 1570. factæ, aut faciendæ, pro situ agrorum partibus cederent, Lidlumanique Cœnobitæ cum Tjumarumanis, Firdgumanis, & Oosterbiremijs ex edicto Scenci subsidia partibus præstarent.
units.tr: It was provided that actions on both sides should cease, and that, with no regard to plaintiff or defendant, the long expenses of the dispute should be made good by mutual compensation. The rescripts too of the Prince and of the prefects, which earlier pity for the recurring floods or the prayers of suppliants had extorted, were to be annulled once the dispute was ended, and the pronouncement made by George Scencus, governor of the Emperor, in the year 1533, and defined by the other arbiters, was to stand. So the stretches of embankment that lie along the sea from Bilta towards Harlingen were assigned to the inland Westergoers, and the rest running from Harlingen southward to the outlet at Maccum to the maritime people. It was also decreed that the surveys made, or to be made, after the flood of 1570 should be divided among the parties according to the position of the fields, and that the monks of Lidlum, together with the Tjumarumani, Firdgumani and Oosterbiremi, should pay their shares to the parties in accordance with Scencus's edict.

units.la: Reperio in actis Hemelumolpherdios & Nordvoldios, maritimis Westergois sociatos, eandem Sylvestribus litem tum intentasse, eosdemque maritimos, velut lite temere institutâ fiduciâ causæ, & simul spe boni eventus, ex decreto eorundem arbitrorum, excidisse. Quae cIↄ. Iↄ. a Philippo solemni edicto confirmata in usu mansere. Haec in arce regia Leovardiae perscripta, ac Gaspari Roblesij, Igrami Achlenij, Baldiuini Ronij, Gerardi Ostendorpij, & Joannis Fonckij manu signata. Hoc modo lite aggerum, quam conjunximus, confecta, diploma quod regium, quod erigendo, reficiendoque marino aggeri a Philippo scriptum erat, Gasparus Roblesius ratum efficaxque esse jussit, contumacemque adhuc populum, sua & simul publica exitia neglectu aggerum trahentem, severioribus imperijs agressus est.
