units.la: Reperio in actis istorum temporum, Bolsuardios etsi introducendis in civitatem indictionum legibus industrios, de suorum criminationibus & immodestia onerum apud præsides rationum provinciæ questos, præter civium damna terra ac mari inlata, immunitatem, aut contumaciam vicinorum municipiorum suæ impotentiæ obtendisse. Adeò difficile est legem ex necessitate latam conditioni temporum aptare paucisque in exemplum immunitatis opiniore aut ingenij vitio peccantibus, omnium modestiam imperare. Hoc vero maxumè eosdem Bolsuerdios premebat, quod præter res quas usus consumeret, corpora quoque & personas civium publico censui egestas aut avaritiâ Ordinum subjecisset, quas in libertate natas servilibus oneribus conditio nascendi eximeret. Quibus criminationibus per eos fomenta subministrabantur, qui ex discordijs civium, ex Ordinum secessionibus nova commoda, antiquas dignitates sperabant, populumque in ipso libertatis ortu servitij pertæsum regias ad partes exuto fœderis obsequio rediturum.
units.tr: I find in the records of these times that the people of Bolsward, although zealous in introducing the levy laws into their town, complained before the provincial governors about the accusations made against their own men and the excessive burdens of the levies. Besides the damage done to citizens by land and sea, they pleaded in defence of their weakness the immunity or obstinacy of neighbouring towns. So hard is it to adapt a law made from necessity to the condition of the times, and so hard to impose moderation on all, when a few who sin from a reputation for immunity or from a fault of character set an example. What most oppressed these same Bolsward people was that, besides the goods which use consumes, the public assessment had also subjected their persons and bodies to the poverty or greed of the Estates, when the condition of their birth had freed them, born in liberty, from servile burdens. Such accusations were supplied with fuel by those who hoped for new advantages from the quarrels of the citizens and from the secession of the Estates, and for their old dignities; and who expected that the people, weary of servitude at the very dawn of their liberty, would return to the royal side once the obedience of the covenant was cast off.

units.la: Quamobrem Lalainius non ignarus quantis artibus partium odia per provinciam tegerentur, datis vi. Non. Oct. ad præsidem Senatumq; lit- teris, nes. teris, convocari ad viii. Eid. Octobr. Ordines, præscriptumque ad diem regio adhuc Philippi nomine usurpato, adesse frequentes jusit quo de postulatis Ordinum generalium suis ex Legatis cognoscerent. Itaque dicto die præter Frisiæ Ordines Cortenillius & Gruterus cum mandatis adfuere. Ista habebant; Ut communibus Belgicæ indictionibus locum in provincia facerent, singulasq; in cerevisiæ, que 12. stuferos excederet tonnas binos penderent. Ut mille & quingenti carolæi signati æris, commeatus & pulveris tormentarij sex lastæ præstarentur.
units.tr: Therefore Lalaing, not unaware by what arts the hatred of the parties was concealed throughout the province, on 2 October sent letters to the governor and the Council, ordering the Estates to be summoned for 8 October, and a date set for them to attend in numbers, still in the name of Philip, so that they might learn from their own delegates the demands of the General Estates. Accordingly, on the appointed day, besides the Estates of Friesland, Cortenilles and Gruter came with their mandates. They brought these proposals: that they should make room in the province for the common levies of the Belgic provinces, and pay two tuns for each tun of beer exceeding twelve stuivers; and that one thousand five hundred Carolus coins of minted money, supplies and six lasts of gunpowder should be furnished.

units.la: Heymannus addit de fœdere quoq; cum Geldris, Hollandis & eorum Socijs ineundo propositum in eodem comitio fuisse, innuente Gruteo (nam is verba faciebat) sociali fide per Flandriam & Artesiam lubricâ inferiores provincias propriore concordiâ connectendas. Quæ quamvis in incertum adhuc dicerentur, spe conciliandarum provinciarum necdum excussa, ita tamdiu protracta, donec anno sequenti, ut memorabo, fœdus apud Ultrajectinos ictum, non sine animorum motu invalesceret.
units.tr: Heymann adds that a proposal was also made at the same assembly about entering into a covenant with Gelderland, Holland and their allies. Gruter, who was speaking, hinted that the lower provinces, unsettled through Flanders and Artois, should be bound together by a closer concord of allied faith. Although these matters were still spoken of as uncertain, with the hope of winning over the provinces not yet given up, they were so long delayed that the covenant, struck at Utrecht the following year, as I shall recount, came into force not without a stirring of spirits.

units.la: Igitur legatorum studijs, qui Antverpiam advenerant, effectum est, ut Senatus ordinum Belgicæ cogeretur, Matthiasq; Gubernator augusti confessus princeps & Aurantij Consilio subjutus, perrogatis sententijs permittenda civibus castella decerneret. Quare litteræ ad Leovardiæ, Harlingæ & Stauriæ oppidorum Magistratus hunc in modum datæ.
units.tr: So, through the efforts of the delegates who had come to Antwerp, it was brought about that the Council of the Belgic Estates was convened, and Matthias, the governor, a prince of Augsburg confession and supported by the counsel of Orange, decided, after the votes had been taken, that the castles should be entrusted to the citizens. Accordingly, letters were written in this manner to the magistrates of the towns of Leeuwarden, Harlingen and Stavoren.

units.la: PETIERE Ordinum Frisiæ Legati, ut castella potestatis vestræ faceremus. Quod cum vestro bono & amovendis similibus suspicionibus speciet, ita de Consilio Aurantij Principis & suffragationibus ORDINUM generalium constituimus atque sanximus, ut in manus vestras castella traderentur. Vos quoque arcium custodiæ vestro ex corpore deligeretis dum de diruendis abolendisque decretum perscribatur. Itaque rogamus & pro auctoritate nostrâ decernimus, ut castellis regundis asservandisque viros fidos & patriæ amantes præficiatis & qui parati erunt nobiscum & cum Ordinibus generalibus pro majorum libertate & causâ publicâ fortunas, corpora atque animas impendere. Quod si feceritis & certi esse ac securi amoto suspicionum metu poteritis, dum admunitis vestris oppidis destrui castelli & solo æquari publica auctoritas & occasio præceperint. Atque id vestro bono sancitum credite.
units.tr: The delegates of the Estates of Friesland have asked that we make the castles subject to your power. Since this appears to be for your good and for removing such suspicions, we have, by the counsel of Prince William of Orange and by the votes of the General Estates, decreed and sanctioned that the castles be handed over into your hands. You too are to choose from your own body guardians for the fortresses, until the decree about demolishing and abolishing them is drawn up. Therefore we ask, and by our authority we order, that you appoint to the governing and keeping of the castles men who are loyal and love their country, and who are ready to devote their fortunes, bodies and souls with us and with the General Estates to the liberty of their elders and the common cause. If you do this, and can be sure and safe with the fear of suspicion removed, then, once your fortified towns are secured, the public authority and occasion will lay the castles low and level them with the ground. Believe that this has been sanctioned for your good.

units.la: Litteræ 8. Eid. Oct. signatæ à MATTHIA Gubernatore & in Frisiam ocyus missæ. Similes quoque ad Præfectos arcium datæ, quibus easdem tradere civibus eodem decreto jubebantur.
units.tr: The letters, sealed on 8 October by Governor Matthias, were sent quickly into Friesland. Similar letters were also given to the commanders of the fortresses, ordering them by the same decree to hand the same over to the citizens.

units.la: Igitur Renico Camminga legato Antverpiam progresso, qui ex fiduciarijs suis subsidia & affectum gentis angustis provinciarum rebus offerebat, omnia in lenius mutata decretumque imprimis. Ut Castella Leovardiæ, Harlingæ atque Stauriæ oppidorum peregrinis commissa provincialibus traderentur arciumque Satrapæ à Magistratibus è corpore civium creati illarum custodiæ vacarent, dum ipsa oppida munitionibus circumducta securitatem populo fecissent.
units.tr: So when Renicus Camminga, the delegate, went on to Antwerp, offering from his trustees subsidies and the goodwill of the people for the straitened affairs of the provinces, everything was changed to a milder course, and above all the decree was altered: the castles of Leeuwarden, Harlingen and Stavoren were to be entrusted to provincial men rather than to outsiders, and the governors of the fortresses, chosen by the magistrates from the body of citizens, were to take charge of their keeping, while the towns themselves, surrounded by fortifications, provided security to the people.

units.la: Litteræ vero Archiducis ad Magistratus oppidorum ejusmodi erant.
units.tr: The letters of the Archduke to the magistrates of the towns were of this kind.

units.la: ORDINES Frisiae petiere ut vestrae potestatis castella faceremus. CIↄ. Iↄ. Nos vero, quo illorum postulato & vestris commodis amovendam ad LXXVIII. inofficiosi de nobis suspicionem satisfieret, de consilio AURANTIJ Principis ac Ordinum Generalium id lubentes indulsimus sanximusq́, ut vestri juris ac arbitrij essent. Quapropter rogamus & pariter mandamus gubernatorio nomine, ut istiusmodi Satrapas arcibus ac castellis praeficiatis, quorum fides apud vos probata erit & qui nobiscum ac Ordinibus generalibus parati erunt bona, corpora atq; vitam libertati & saluti publicae impendere. Atque haec valebunt quo securi malorum esse posititis, dum permunitis oppidis vestris castella diruantur.
units.tr: The Frisian Estates asked that we hand over castles to your authority. 1578. We, however, so that their request might be granted, your interests served, and suspicion of disloyalty toward us removed, have on the advice of Prince William of Orange and the General Estates gladly agreed and decreed that they should be under your right and control. Therefore we ask and likewise command, in the governor's name, that you place such governors in the citadels and castles whose loyalty has been proved among you, and who are ready with us and the General Estates to devote their goods, bodies and lives to liberty and the public safety. This will help you to be safe from harm, while the castles are demolished and your towns kept well fortified.

units.la: Litterae quoque seorsim ad Satrapas & praesidiarios Harlinganae arcis datae, quibus castello cedere de voluntate sua & Ordinum jubebantur. Eae Antverpiae VIII. Eid. Octobr. signatae.
units.tr: Letters were also sent separately to the officers and garrison of the Harlingen fort, ordering them to yield the castle according to their own will and that of the Estates. These were signed at Antwerp on the eighth day before the Ides of October.

units.la: F. Nicolaus scribit Matthiae Gubernatoris litteris Stauriam perlatis Magistratum urbanum Gulielmum Petraeum concivem suum Satrapam arci praefecisse, publica omnium laetitia custodiam castelli & simul urbis diu vim & insolentiam externi praesidij passae rectori civico committi. Caetera quoque per oppida plebes gaudio immodesta ex novae libertatis indulto licentiam acuebat. Itaq; Leovardiae factum est, ut VII. Eid. Octob. Iulij Dekamae Senatoris regij, qui a fuga Senatus Daventriam concesserat, hortum suburbanum, amoenitate & cultu celebrem, caederet locumque tanquam in speciem insidijs peropportunum, odio magis domini quam ex metu periculi vastaret. Scriptores tradunt magnitudine sua septem agri jugera complexum frugiferarumque arborum compta serie consitum antiqui decoris pulchritudinem repentina foeditate mutasse. Mox furore populi necdum sedato, per urbem ipsam partium foecundam templa ruinis atq; spoliis foedata, statuaeq; & imagines sacrarum aedium ornamenta tanquam obnoxia superstitionibus visentium oculis submota. Heymannus addit, ex Hocano districtu, qui urbi in ortum solis aestivum est, tempestatem emanasse populumq; illius orae prae caeteris aut turbidum aut zelo religionis correptum templorum cultum & quietem urbis conturbasse. Itaque Nyhovae & Praedicatorum sana enormius direpta librique rituales per vicos sparsi ac discerpti pro animorum captu miserationi aut ludibrio fuere. Adeo verum est Religionis odium, cum desinere ex lege & mandato supremae potestatis debuisset, a proclamata pace civilem magis immodestiam efferasse. Interim Lalainius, quo novi foederis negotium promoveret, litteras ad Ordines dedit, quibus petebat; Ut ad Eid. Octobr. legatos Ultrajectum mittant, quo inter ambigua temporum illa in civitate habendo conventui destinata, de praeconcepto ocyus foedere consultarent. Sed angustia temporis & per omnia domi praesertim inter agrarios turbida salubre Lalainij consilium praepediebatur. Igitur Georgio Grutero Ioto legato suo in Frisiam ocyus remisso, ut ad XIV. Kal. Nov. adessent, praecepit, excusantibus modeste agrarijs in tam arduo negotio cautius deliberandum esse, neque praecipitandas consultationes, quas sicut omnia rerum opportunum temporum sanaret. Unde protracti apud Ultrajectinos conventus fama mox in Frisiam perlata tanto gratius accepta, quanto magis publicae utilitates privatis ex aemulatio-
units.tr: Brother Nicolaus writes that once Matthias's letters had been brought to Stavoren, the city magistrate appointed his fellow citizen Willem Petersz as commander of the garrison. To general rejoicing, the keeping of the castle and of the city, which had long suffered the force and insolence of a foreign garrison, was entrusted to the civic governor. Elsewhere too, the common people, immoderate in their joy at the grant of new liberty, were inflaming their licence. So it happened at Leeuwarden, on the seventh day before the Ides of October, that the suburban garden of Dekama, a royal senator who had withdrawn to Deventer after the flight of the Senate, famous for its pleasantness and cultivation, was laid waste. The place, very convenient as if for ambushes, was devastated more from hatred of its lord than from fear of danger. Writers relate that the garden, covering seven acres and planted with fruit trees in an orderly arrangement, was suddenly changed from its former beauty to foulness. Soon, with the people's fury not yet calmed, churches throughout the city, which was fertile in factions, were defiled with ruins and plunder, and statues and images, the ornaments of the sacred buildings, were removed from the eyes of onlookers as liable to superstition. Heymannus adds that a storm had burst out of the Hogeland district, which lies to the north-east of the city, and that the people of that shore, more turbulent than others or seized by religious zeal, disturbed the worship in the churches and the peace of the city. Therefore at Nijehove and at the house of the Dominicans, the sacred furnishings were plundered more excessively, and the ritual books, scattered and torn through the streets, were given over to pity or mockery according to the capacity of each mind. So true it is that hatred of religion, which ought to have ceased by the law and command of the supreme authority, after the proclaimed peace stirred up civil lawlessness all the more. Meanwhile Lalaing, to advance the business of the new covenant, sent letters to the Estates asking them to send delegates to Utrecht by the Ides of October, to meet in that city, appointed amid those uncertain times, and to deliberate more quickly on the covenant already conceived. But the shortness of time, and the turmoil everywhere, especially at home among the agrarians, hindered Lalaing's salutary plan. So he quickly sent his legate, Georgius Gruterus Iota, back into Friesland, ordering the delegates to attend by the fourteenth day before the Kalends of November. The agrarians modestly excused themselves, saying that in so arduous a business more cautious deliberation was needed, and that consultations must not be rushed, since the opportune time heals all things. Hence the meetings at Utrecht were protracted, and the news of this, soon carried into Friesland, was received all the more gladly because public advantages were being delayed by private rivalries.

units.la: lationibus tardabantur. Itaq; Oppidani, acribus in novum fœdus studijs, suo ex corpore legatos, creavere designatis Julio Bottniâ Oldermanno Franequerensium & Douwone Sixma Consule, qui legatione fungerentur. Illis in mandatis datum erat. Ut Ultrajectum ituri Hollandis, Zelandis, Ultrajectinis, Geldris, Zutphaniensibus, Trans-Isulanis & provinciis Præfecturæ Lalainij subjectis sese jungerent fœdusque facerent, cæterum sub hac conditione, si superiorum provinciarum secessio propiorem concordiam & societatem harum gentium postularet. Hoc etiam additum, ut de formulâ fœderis ad Matthiam Belgicæ Gubernatorem, Principem Aurantium & Generales Ordines referretur firmatumque illorum assensu & ratihabitione vim atque efficaciam justi fœderis sortiretur. Hæc Leovardiæ ix. Kal. Non. sigillo Leovardiensium & manu Jarichi Wopconij pro ijsdem, pro Eloftanis à Ieltzone Galama pro Doccomiensibus à Cornelio Jacobi, pro Snecanis & Slotensibus à Gysberto Oenaeo, pro Worcumianis ac Hindelopijs à Douwone Petræo, pro Harlingensibus Nicolao Folkersio signata. Quæ caute & prudenter reperta, ut sanandis provinciarum secessionibus erant, ita sanctionem Belgici fœderis non abolebant, modeste censentibus oppidanis vetera fœderum ex novis non tollenda & quæ non violari præterquam sociali defectione Frisiæ gentis interesset.
units.tr: Therefore the townsmen, eager for the new covenant, chose from their own body delegates, namely Julius Bottnia, alderman of Franeker, and Douwe Sixma, consul, to carry out the embassy. They were given these instructions: on going to Utrecht they were to join with Holland, Zeeland, Utrecht, Gelderland, Zutphen, Overijssel and the provinces subject to Lalaing's prefecture, and make a covenant; but on this condition, that the secession of the upper provinces demanded a closer concord and fellowship of these peoples. It was also added that the form of the covenant should be referred to Matthias, Governor of Belgium, to the Prince of Orange and to the General Estates, and that once confirmed by their assent and ratification it would acquire the force and efficacy of a lawful covenant. These things were drawn up at Leeuwarden on the ninth day before the Nones of November, sealed with the seal of the Leeuwardeners and signed by the hand of Jarich Wopkes for the same, for the people of Eloft by Jeltzo Galama, for the people of Dokkum by Cornelis Jacobs, for the people of Sneek and Sloten by Gijsbert Oenema, for the people of Workum and Hindeloopen by Douwe Pieters, and for the people of Harlingen by Nicolaas Volckertsz. These measures, devised cautiously and prudently, were suited to healing the secessions of the provinces, and so they did not abolish the sanction of the Belgic covenant. The townsmen modestly judged that old covenants should not be removed by new ones, and that nothing should be violated except what would serve the interest of the social defection of the Frisian nation.

units.la: Invenio in actis istorum temporum, morte cujusdam Stintiemæ Prætoris & aggerum à Feenhusâ ad Clivum promontorium præfecti, quendam Sibrandum Benckenium pro successione obtinendâ apud Lalainium vehementer neq; damnatis artibus laborare, interventuque Caroli Roorda provinciæ ad Lalainium legati arcitum dedecus repulsæ & ex vitiatâ patriâ lege ignobilem contemptum reportare. Id namq; voluerat Benckenius, ut nullâ præviâ trium nominatione & jure populi faciendis nuncupationibus antiquato, Lalainius præfecti potestate de prætoriâ dignitate aut Saltem ejus provisione disponeret, solusque aulicorum gratiâ & fiduciâ sui imperij nixus, solenni ritu & autoritate Collegij spretâ, beneficia petenti assignaret. Regerente Roorda Legato retinendos curiosè provinciæ mores esse, neque clam & contra jus publicum elargiendas dignitates quas conferre Præfectus non jure, violatâ jurisjurandi religione, nec quisquam accipere nisi perduellis & exlex posset. Obtinuisse scilicet consuetudine ac statutis majorum ut vacantes Præturæ à loco proxumis administrarentur, dum defuncto successorem electio populi & collegij autoritas suffecisset. Itaque factum est, ut Lalainius se nihil contra datam fidem aut juris publici sanctionem acturum coram Legato testaretur seque provincialium legibus reverenter habitis privatæ potentiæ aut aucupandæ dominationis studia commodis populi postpositurum. Quæ à Legato ad viii. Viros perscripta animum viri patriæ amantis nascenti reip. commendavere.
units.tr: I find in the records of those times that, on the death of a certain praetor of Stiens and of the prefect of the dikes from Feenhuis to the headland of Clivum, a certain Sibrandus Benckenius laboured vehemently to obtain the succession with Lalaing, and not by honourable arts. Through the intervention of Karel Roorda, the province's legate to Lalaing, he brought back the shameful disgrace of rejection and the ignoble contempt that came from the corrupted law of the country. For Benckenius had wished that, with no prior nomination of three candidates and with the right of the people to make nominations set aside, Lalaing by the prefect's power should dispose of the praetorship, or at least of its provision, and relying solely on the favour and trust of the courtiers of his rule, should assign benefices to whoever asked for them, disregarding the solemn ritual and authority of the College. Roorda the legate replied that the customs of the province must be carefully kept, and that dignities must not be bestowed secretly and against public law. The prefect could not confer them lawfully without violating the sanctity of his oath, and no one could accept them unless he were a traitor and outlaw. It had clearly prevailed, by custom and the statutes of the ancestors, that vacant praetorships should be administered by the nearest officer until election by the people and the authority of the College supplied a successor to the deceased. And so it came about that Lalaing declared before the legate that he would do nothing against the faith given or the sanction of public law, and that, with the laws of the province reverently observed, he would put the pursuits of private power or the desire to win dominion behind the convenience of the people. The legate wrote these things down for the eight men, and commended the mind of a man who loved his country to the nascent commonwealth.

units.la: Tantum abest, inquiebat, (nam id litteræ habent) ut pignerare, officium homini improbo & legirupæ voluerim, qui mavelint reliquum vitæ in exilio agere, quam ferre privilegia populi neglecta aut imminuta transgressoribus legum cedere, quos patriâ suâ & honoribus indignos majestatis crimen & sacrissimi ambitus fecisset. Cui rei Deum advoco, qui conscientia mea & navatæ pro rep. operæ testimonium dabit. Itaque & vestrum erit, jus publicum & privilegia cum gloriâ majorum parta constanter tueri, ne hoc libertatis nostræ ortu ante eorum usu privemur, quam in possessione adempti juris benignitas temporum locaverit. Quod certè fiet P. C. si aditum ad remp. istiusmodi legum ruptoribus faciamus, quas connivendo ad turpia & per incuriam ante perdemus quam recuperatæ sint. Et cogitate quanta id cum infamiâ, si evenieat, vicini & posteri vestri agnituri aut dolituri sint, si viderint vos providentiæ munere malè usos obviam libertatem sædis moribus & servili indulgentiâ attamiânasse. Quæ à me scripta scitote ab illo viro, ab illo animo profecta, qui post Dei cultum primùs in boni libertatem habeat, quam sanguine & vitâ sancire patriæ amantium est.
units.tr: So far am I, he said (for so the letter has it), from wishing to act as surety, as the duty of a wicked man and a breaker of the laws, that I would rather spend the rest of my life in exile than endure the privileges of the people neglected or diminished, or yield to those who transgress the laws, whom the crime of treason and the most sacrilegious ambition have made unworthy of their country and of its honours. I call God to witness this, who will bear testimony to my conscience and to the work I have undertaken for the commonwealth. Therefore it will be your task to defend constantly the public law and the privileges won with the glory of your ancestors, lest we be deprived of them at the very dawn of our liberty, before the kindness of the times has restored a right that has been taken away. This will certainly happen, Conscript Fathers, if we open the way to the commonwealth for breakers of such laws, whom we shall lose to baseness through connivance and carelessness before those laws are recovered. And consider how great the infamy will be, if it comes to pass, when your neighbours and descendants recognise, or lament, that you misused the gift of foresight and sullied liberty, as it was offered, with foul morals and servile indulgence. Know that these things written by me come from that man and that mind which, after the worship of God, first holds the liberty of good men dear, and which it belongs to lovers of the fatherland to sanction with blood and life.

units.la: His de morte Austriaci ad v i. Nov. Oct. subjunctum, & illustrium virorum funera longâ serie connexa, Reuxium, Fonckenbergium, Mondragonium, Scharenbergium, Detrionem, Assonvilium & Bertium humanis exemisse. Roblesium quoque olim Frisiæ Gubernatorem ex literis Baronis Hohensaxij Arnhemo datis mortalitatem implevisse Binsiumque Alençonio deditum Gallorum auxilia secundis initijs honestasse. Tum jura ac beneficia, quæ anno LXIII ex sanctionibus Pontificum rex Philippus indulserat, novis Episcopis & Archiepiscopis decreto Matthiæ Gubernatoris & de voluntate Ordinum abrogata, quo primæ civilium turbarum causæ & inter principem populumq; serendis discordijs & mox armis repertæ ex jure fœderum paci atq; concordiæ servirent.
units.tr: To these things is added the death of the Austrian, on the sixth day before the Ides of October, and the funerals of illustrious men, linked in a long series: Reux, Fonckenberg, Mondragón, Scharenberg, Detrion, Assonville and Berti were taken from human life. Robles, once governor of Friesland, also completed his mortal course, according to letters of Baron Hohensax given at Arnhem. Binche, surrendered to Alençon, had honoured the French auxiliaries with favourable beginnings. Then the rights and benefices which King Philip had granted in the year 1563 by the sanctions of the Popes were abrogated by decree of Matthias the Governor and with the will of the Estates, in respect of the new bishops and archbishops. Thus the first causes of civil troubles, the discords sown between prince and people, and soon found in arms, were to serve, by the law of the covenants, for peace and concord.

units.la: Formulâ Editi MATTHIAE Gubernatoris hæc erat:
units.tr: The form of the edict of Governor Matthias was this:

units.la: CUm Hispanorum consiliys atq; factionibus per has inferiores provinciás novi Episcopatus atque Archiepiscopatus erecti, illisq, dignitates canonicatus, præbendæ, divinæ pensiones & alia beneficia, officia bonaq; tam sæcularia quam Ecclesiastica assignata sint, per vim magis quam consensum Ordinum & populi cujus interesset, contra privilegia provinciarum & jus scriptum nihil statui. Cùmq; pacificatio Gandavensis ejus ratihabitio, jura, privilegia, consuetudines atq; statuta tam provinciarum quam civitatum restituì sanxerit, Ordinesq; generales illas bonorum & dignitatum acquisitiones & ordinationes infirmari jam ante diversis actorum indicijs fecerint, itâ hoc ipso decernunt, ut omnes dignitates, beneficia, decimæ, pensiones, per Episcopos aut Archiepiscopos acquisitæ aut usurpatæ de facto cessent habeanturq; in posterum nullæ & inefficaces, salvo tamen jure supplicandi, quod unicuiq; læso liberum erit. Hæc Antwerp. Prid. Kal. Nov. MATTHIAE manu signata.
units.tr: Since, by the counsels and factions of the Spaniards, new bishoprics and archbishoprics have been set up through these lower provinces, and dignities of canons, prebends, divine pensions and other benefices, offices and goods, both secular and ecclesiastical, have been assigned to them, by force rather than by the consent of the Estates and of the people whose interest it was, and against the privileges of the provinces and the written law, let nothing be decided. And since the Pacification of Ghent, ratifying it, has decreed that the rights, privileges, customs and statutes of the provinces and of the cities be restored, and the General Estates have already before, by various indications in their acts, weakened those acquisitions and ordinations of goods and dignities, they therefore decree by this very act that all dignities, benefices, tithes and pensions acquired or usurped de facto through bishops or archbishops shall cease, and shall be held in future as null and ineffective, saving however the right of appeal, which shall be free to anyone who is injured. Given at Antwerp, the day before the Kalends of November, signed by the hand of Matthias.

units.la: Itaq; evenit ut quod ante annum Frisiæ Ordines per Sceltonem Tiardam, Nitzenium & Tatmannum legatos postulaverant, provinciâ tum obtineret, patrimoniumq; sed contra jus ac fas quæsitum cœnobiorum rectoribus & ut post memorabo reip. gerendis rebus assignaretur. Mox Rennebergius xvi. Nov. die comitium Leovardiæ ordinavit, sub eâ cautione ut nulli ad consulendum admitterentur præterquam qui in patriæ & optimatum partibus erant & qui eas vivâ voce in comitio professi externæ dominationis odia amore libertatis induissent. Itaque in Austriacum & Hispanos detestationes innovatæ, quibus neque illi eximebantur, qui conditionibus temporum serviendo odia ac amicitias partium suspectis simulationibus velabant. Igitur de Ultrajectino fœdere, de recipiendis indictionibus ac agendo censu repetitum, urgen- tibus Rennebergij legatis ut postulatis decretum perscriberetur, temporumq; dilationibus prolata maturatæ consultationes desinerent. Caeterum omnia partium plena lentis deliberationibus trahebantur. Quippe Gandavensium motus jam ante ex dissidio religionis orti (post direptas ditium coenobiorum opes & Pontificios ritus turbidæ civitati damnatos) plurimos sponte mobiles etiam per Frisiam ostendebant, Erantque qui ex ruptâ per Flandros & Hannonios religionis pace, occasionem impellebant defectionibus, bello materiam captarent.
units.tr: So it came about that the province obtained what the Frisian Estates had demanded a year earlier through their envoys Sceltonem Tiardam, Nitzenius and Tatmannus: the monastic patrimony, which had been acquired against law and right, was assigned to the heads of the monasteries and, as I will relate later, to the conduct of public affairs. Soon afterwards Rennenberg convened the assembly at Leeuwarden on 16 November, on the condition that only those admitted to deliberate who stood on the side of the country and the nobles, and who had declared by voice in the assembly that, out of love of liberty, they had taken up hatred of foreign domination. Thus hatred of the Austrians and the Spaniards was renewed, and it spared not even those who, serving the circumstances of the times, veiled their hatreds and friendships with suspect pretences. So the matter of the Utrecht union, the receiving of levies and the collecting of the tax was taken up again, with Rennenberg's envoys pressing that the decree be drawn up as they demanded. Deferrals of time prolonged the matter, so that mature consultations came to nothing. Meanwhile everything, full of partisan strife, was dragged out by slow deliberations. Indeed the disturbances of Ghent, which had already arisen earlier from religious dissension (after the wealthy monasteries had been plundered and the Papist rites condemned in the turbulent city), were showing many people moved to revolt, even through Friesland. And there were those who, from the religious peace broken by the Flemings and Hainaulters, seized the occasion to push for defections and sought material for war.

units.la: Quare legiones ex cessantibus stipendijs ultra ægras Ordinumq; generalium imperijs coutumaces, Montinio Lalainioq; ducibus sollicitatas & involutas seditionibus lætabantur, ipsosq; Gandavenses Casimiri auxilijs subjutos Ordinum Exercitum distractis copijs extenuasse. Casimiro quoque æmulationem & mox invidiem conflatam, quod à Matthiâ Gubernatore ac Ordinibus Belgicæ è Germaniâ specie auxiliorum evocatus, suo magis ingenio quam ex mandatis Ordinum discordias & arma partium subministratis copijs fovisset. Deniq; Aurantium sopiendis dissensionibus & sistendæ vi Gandavum profectum ex immodestis civitatis moribus à turbido statu parum ad concordiam profecisse, omniaque in urbe sanciendo provinciarum fœderi jam ante destinata arma & bellum comminari. Infesta scilicet Gandavensium in Hannonios cæterosque vicinos ex religione odia esse; neque Ordinum imperijs aut partibus satis æqua, qui haud dubiè vastandis Flandriæ terris seditiosas Montinij legiones incitavissent. Neque displicebat quod Alençonius nulla Ordinum legatione, aut æquitate conditionum emolliretur, fideiq; per Ordines læsæ vulnus alius exercitus missione Montinianas partes præjuvissent.
units.tr: Hence they rejoiced that the legions, whose pay had stopped and who were insubordinate to the orders of the sick Estates-General, had been enticed by the leaders Montigny and Lalaing and entangled in sedition, and that the men of Ghent, supported by the aid of Casimir, had weakened the army of the Estates by dividing its forces. Rivalry and soon envy were also kindled against Casimir, because he had been summoned from Germany under the pretext of auxiliaries by Governor Matthias and the Estates of Belgium, and by his own disposition rather than by the mandates of the Estates he had fostered discord and armed the parties with the troops supplied to him. Finally, Orange had gone to Ghent to quell the dissensions and check them by force, but had achieved little toward concord, because of the city's unrestrained morals and turbulent state; and in the city, arms and war threatened, already decided beforehand for the union of the provinces. Clearly the hostility of Ghent towards the Hainaulters and other neighbours arose from religion; nor were the commands or the party of the Estates quite fair, since they had undoubtedly incited Montigny's seditious legions to lay waste the lands of Flanders. Nor was it displeasing that Alençon was softened by no embassy of the Estates and no fairness of terms, and that the wound inflicted on faith by the Estates had aided Montigny's party by sending another army.

units.la: Itaque Pontificij erectis animis Leovardiæ ad exercitia suorum ritium redierunt, sacrisque ad Nyehovam pro more celebratis prædicatore quoque restaurandos ad cultus impulere. Quare vergente Novembri per illos campanum æs pulsatum, resq; divina pontificio ritu peracta ne triumphalibus quidem ob expugnatam Daventriam ovationibus interrupta est. Heymannus scribit Iulium Dekamam Senatorem cum Germanorum præsidio, quod capta urbe excesserat, in Germaniam abijsse magnæq; rerum mutationis per Frisiam & vicina ægritudine tactum, externa locorum patriæ desiderio & suorum consuetudini prætulisse.
units.tr: So the Papists, with raised spirits, returned at Leeuwarden to the exercise of their rites; at Nyehove they celebrated the sacred rites as usual and, with a preacher too, pressed for the restoration of worship. Hence, as November drew on, bells were rung by them and divine service was performed by the papal rite, not even interrupted by the triumphal ovations for the capture of Deventer. Heymann writes that Julius Dekama, a senator, withdrew into Germany with the German garrison which had left once the city was taken. Touched by the great change of affairs in Friesland and by the sickness of the neighbouring region, he preferred foreign places to longing for his homeland and the customs of his own people.

units.la: Tradunt Scriptores viginti equitum, peditum quadraginta millia in exercitu Ordinum tum numerata stipendiorum inopiâ & per discordias ducum attabuisse. Everardus Reidanus decem & quatuor millibus equitum, triginta quinque millibus peditum censum notat, eundemque reprimendis Turcarum armis validum solo procerum velut diversa pro concipientium dissensu & ex impulso Ordinum ærario spem virtutis & gloriæ fœdâ ignominiâ mutasse. Idem addit novies centena milliarum-mum in menstruum æs assignata, provinciarum vastatione aut egestate semestri spatio mediam menstrui aeris partem non æquasse. Itaq; factum est, ut florentissimus provinciarum Exercitus castra moveret, externisque legionibus ad continendam fidem discretis provinciarum copiæ in hyberna ac præsidia conducerentur. Caeterum Exercitu per præpræsidia aut opportuna lccorum distributo, alia malorum subnascebantur. cIↄ. Iↄ? Quippe Casimiri suspectis actionibus, quas Angliæ legatus Davisonus tanquam Reginæ mandatis & datæ fidei adversas, Ordinum & provinciarum rebus damnosas exagitaverat, etiam hoc accedebat, quod Andinus de deserendis provinciis clam agitaret ipsâq; Gandavensium civitate adhuc impacatâ Montinij & hostium partes accessione virium regiæq; Philippi gratiæ invalescerent.
units.tr: Writers report that the army of the Estates then numbered twenty thousand horse and forty thousand foot, but that through lack of pay and the dissensions of its commanders it had wasted away. Everard Reidanus records fourteen thousand horse and thirty-five thousand foot, and the same man, strong enough to repel the Turkish arms, was turned from hope of virtue and glory into foul disgrace by the sole impulse of the nobles, whose opinions differed in forming their dissensions, and by the impulse of the Estates' treasury. He adds that nine hundred thousand (florins) had been assigned monthly for pay, but through the devastation or poverty of the provinces, over a half-year, the money paid had not equalled even half the monthly sum. And so it came about that the flourishing army of the provinces broke camp; foreign legions were detached to keep faith, and the provincial forces were led into winter quarters and garrisons. But when the army had been distributed among outposts or convenient places, other evils sprang up. Indeed, to the suspect actions of Casimir, which the English envoy Davison had denounced as contrary to the Queen's orders and to the faith given, and as harmful to the affairs of the Estates and the provinces, was added this: that Anjou was secretly planning to desert the provinces. With Ghent still unpacified, the party of Montigny and of the enemies grew stronger by the accession of forces, and by the favour of King Philip.

units.la: Igitur Casimiro in Angliam profecto pro retinendo in provinciis Andino laboratum, velut plurimum interesset, regij sanguinis principem à provinciarum societate non alienari, qui funestissimos Galliarum motus optimo remedio & laudabili exitu pacasset. Neq; enim nuda auxilia spectanda esse caeterum curandum ut tanto intercessore seditiosi & defectores in fidem Ordinum redeant, pacemq; provinciæ sicut fratris regnum, illius moderatione & interventu accipiant. Caeterum Andinus etsi conciliandis partibus omne studium polliceretur, præcipuam sui discessus causam per Legatum hoc modo exposuit.
units.tr: Therefore, when Casimir had gone to England, efforts were made to keep Anjou in the provinces, as it greatly mattered that a prince of royal blood should not be alienated from the union of the provinces, he who had pacified the most deadly movements of France by an excellent remedy and a praiseworthy outcome. For mere auxiliaries were not to be regarded; rather care had to be taken that, through such a mediator, the seditious and the defectors would return to the faith of the Estates, and receive peace for the provinces as the kingdom had received it, through his moderation and intervention. Yet Anjou, although he promised every effort toward reconciling the parties, set out his chief reason for leaving through the envoy in the following way.

units.la: ABIRE à vobis ORDINES, quorum socius atq; amicus veteram, animus non fuit. Caeterum quoniam à fratre Rege jam pridem revocor, exigentibus regni turbis, fratris Regis imperio & simul desiderio matris obsequi cogor. Quibus & hoc accedit, quod intelligam esse qui mea præsentia non egere provincias censeant, tanquam paci obstem quæ cum PHILIPPO Hispano in gratiam redire vos faciat. Igitur actione pacis irrita habebor & isti impedimentum & bello consilium attulisse. A quo quam alienus sim principem animum testem habeo, neque aliud voto cupio, quam ut in tali pace statu res vestræ collocentur & meis non egeant. Quas ipsas amore vestri ac miseratione vestris quoque posthabui paratus pignori à vobis data, aut armis meis parta ultro redhibere. Neque ijs tantum in summa necessitate vos juvi, qui nullo dominationis aut potentiæ studio medium me insuper discordijs inter vos & defectores ingessi, prater morem ambitiosorum principum, quibus provinciarum res angustæ ac discordes commodo ac usui cessissent.
units.tr: I MUST DEPART from you, Estates, whose companion and friend, as of old, my heart was never unwilling to be. But since I have long been recalled by my brother the King, as the troubles of the realm require, I am bound to obey my brother the King's command and, at the same time, my mother's desire. To this is added that I understand there are those who think the provinces do not need my presence, as though I stood in the way of a peace which would bring you back into favour with Philip of Spain. Therefore my action for peace will be counted vain, and they will say that I have brought hindrance to it and counsel for war. Of how far I am from such a purpose, I have a witness in my own mind; nor do I desire anything more than that your affairs be placed in such a peaceful state that they no longer need me. Those very things I have put behind my own interests, out of love for you and pity for you, ready to return freely the pledge given by you or won by my arms. Nor have I helped you only in your greatest need, I who, with no desire for lordship or power, have thrust myself into the midst of your discords between you and the defectors, beyond the custom of ambitious princes, to whom the narrow and discordant affairs of the provinces would have been convenient and useful.

units.la: Addebat Legatus ut interim principis sui beneficia serio expenderent & quo animo provincijs excederet, qui suâ autoritate eas maxumè præjuvisset. Id vel ipsis dissimulantibus cæteros Principes & vicinos agnituros Ordinumq; gratitudinem cum beneficijs Andini collaturos. Postremum petijt ut Ordines ratione suarum rerum habitâ illius amicitiam ac societatem religiose colerent, in cujus potestate esset damna pro beneficijs reponere.
units.tr: The envoy added that they should meanwhile weigh seriously the benefits of his prince and with what spirit he was leaving the provinces, he who by his authority had most greatly aided them. Even if they dissembled this, the other princes and neighbours would recognise it, and would bestow their gratitude on account of Anjou's benefits. Lastly he asked that the Estates, having regard to their own affairs, cultivate his friendship and alliance faithfully, since it lay in his power to repay harms in return for benefits.

units.la: Reidanus tradit, Elisabetham Angliæ Reginam datis litteris vehementi quoq; indignatione apud Ordines expostulasse, quod Andini beneficia non agnoscendo, nec respectum tanti principis, nec suorum pactorum habuissent. Itaq; avertendis à Belgica tam Andini quam aliorum principum animis & pro exemplo fore. De se testari illâ ex actione (etsi aliud sinisteriore famâ ferret) voluptatem non hausisse neq; ejus animi & morum esse, ut ex injuriâ Regis Galliarum filio ac fratri inlatâ gaudium sensura sit.
units.tr: Reidanus relates that Elizabeth, Queen of England, also complained to the Estates by letter with great indignation, because by not acknowledging Anjou's benefits, nor showing regard for so great a prince or for their own agreements, they had acted badly. Thus, to turn the minds of Anjou and of the other princes away from Belgium, it would serve as an example. She testified of herself that from that action (although rumour in a more sinister sense reported otherwise) she had drawn no pleasure, nor was it her nature and character to feel joy at an injury inflicted on the son and brother of the King of France.

units.la: Quod velum etsi Elisahethâ suæ indignationi præferret, tamen erant qui crederent illam ab Andini connubio non alienam multum personæ & regio sanguini ex affectu amoris dedisse. Isti fini Simierum hominem Gallum & Andini familiâ diu usum urgendo reginæ matrimonio in Angliâ reliquisse, quo scenicos & aulæ mores, supra quam multorum conditio ferret, edoctus facili ad omnia ingenio muliebre quoque pectus amatorijs artibus expugnaret. Igitur Ordines allevandis Reginæ & Andini offensionibus honestissimâ legatione institutâ Elostum Flandriæ oppidum cum præsidio obtulere, de cæteris facile conventuri ubi more recepto quisque ad provincias de arcanis rerum retulisset.
units.tr: Although Elizabeth put this veil before her indignation, there were nonetheless those who believed that she, not unfavourable to Anjou's marriage, had given much to his person and royal blood out of affection. To these people, Simier, a Frenchman long employed by Anjou's household, had been left in England, urging the Queen's marriage; and he, instructed in theatrical and courtly manners beyond what the condition of many people bore, with a disposition easy towards everything, would conquer even a woman's heart by amorous arts. Therefore the Estates, to relieve the offences of the Queen and of Anjou, instituted a most honourable embassy and offered the Flemish town of Alost with a garrison, expecting to agree easily on the rest once each had reported the secrets of affairs to his province according to the accepted custom.

units.la: Ista erant, ut si Andinus, sicuti ante conciliandis Gandavensibus & Valonibus operam navaret, si copias Gallicas ab ijsdem Valonibus revocaret, religionem utramque; ex pacis publicatæ formulâ, quantum occasio & quies publica permitteret, per provincias stabiliret aut stabilitam confirmaret, paxque cum rege Hispaniarum intra Kal. Martias proxumas fieret, Andinus pro autore pacis, tranquillitatis & salutis publicæ haberetur. Ordines quoque Provinciarum testandæ gratitudinis & quo Andini beneficia solenni & anniversariâ agnitione recognoscerent, statuam ex ære celeberrimis in locis Antverpiæ & Bruxellis æternæ Andini & masculorum hæredum memoriæ erigerent. Legatos quoq; pro statu Ordinum ex Ecclesiasticis, nobilitate & civitatum Magistratibus die constituto ad Andinum mitterent, coronamque ex oleæ ramulis contextam cæteris cum donarijs offerrent quæ centena millia æris pretio æquarent. Pacem vero si ante Kal. Martias æquas conditiones regi Hispaniæ offerendo non obtinerent, regem tanquam à pace & incolumitate suarum provinciarum alienum & juris-jurandi immemorem, jure suo excidisse declararent, provinciales sacramentis exsolverent, deliberarentq; quibus modis deferri Andino principatus Belgicæ posset.
units.tr: These were the terms: if Andinus, as he had before, worked to reconcile the Ghentese and the Walloons, and if he recalled the French troops from those Walloons, then the Estates would establish both religions throughout the provinces, according to the formula of the published peace and as far as circumstances and public tranquillity allowed, or would confirm them where already established. If peace with the king of Spain were made before the first of March, Andinus would be regarded as the author of peace, tranquillity and public safety. The Estates also, to testify their gratitude and to acknowledge Andinus's benefits with a solemn annual observance, would erect a bronze statue to the eternal memory of Andinus and his male heirs in the most famous places of Antwerp and Brussels. They would also send envoys, on a fixed day, to Andinus on behalf of the Estates, drawn from the clergy, the nobility and the civic magistrates, and offer him, along with other gifts worth a hundred thousand in coin, a crown woven of olive twigs. But if they did not obtain peace by offering fair terms to the king of Spain before the first of March, they would declare the king alien to the peace and safety of their provinces, forgetful of his oath, and to have forfeited his right; the provincials would release themselves from their oaths, and they would deliberate by what means the principality of Belgium could be conferred on Andinus.

units.la: Cæterum Andinus etsi secus simularet, injuriæ memoriam atq; sensum ex oblatione principalis gloriæ ac imperij non exuerat, tanto magis validâ veteri indignatione, quanto secretius principe animo & cum modestiâ tegeretur. Igitur oppidis, quæ præsidio copijs suis aut pignori acceperat, Ordinibus provinciarum traditis curatoq; ne Gallica auxiliâ Valonum in partibus manerent provinciarum finibus excesit.
units.tr: Meanwhile Andinus, though he pretended otherwise, had not laid aside the memory and resentment of the injury caused by the offer of princely glory and rule. All the more strongly did his old indignation burn, the more secretly and modestly it was concealed beneath a princely bearing. So, having handed over to the Estates of the provinces the towns which he had taken with his troops as a garrison or pledge, and having seen to it that the French auxiliaries of the Walloons did not remain within the provinces, he left the borders of the provinces.

units.la: Invenio in archivis abiturienti Andino, qui tum Montibus Hannoniæ erat, dubium adhuc animum apparuisse illumq;, etsi pronis auribus de affectu Ordinum ex Carolo Gauræo cognovisset, consilium tamen decreti in Galliam itineris non mutasse.
units.tr: I find in the archives that when Andinus was departing, who was then at Mons in Hainaut, his mind still appeared undecided; and although he had learned from Charles Gauraeus, with ready ears, of the disposition of the Estates, he nevertheless did not change his settled plan of journeying into France.

units.la: Iulius Bottnia provinciæ nostræ Antverpiam legatus in litteris v ii. Kal. Ian. datis, scribit se ex Secretario Andini, quo cum divertebat, de ejus primum abitu intellexisse Andinumq; rectà ad Quintini fanum, quod ad sabim flumen est, itinere facto suo discessui turbatum Galliæ regnum obtendisse.
units.tr: Julius Bottnia, our province's envoy at Antwerp, in a letter dated 26 December, writes that he first learned of Andinus's departure from Andinus's secretary, with whom he was lodging; and that Andinus, having made his journey directly to Saint-Quentin, which lies on the Somme, pleaded as his reason for leaving the disturbed state of the kingdom of France.

units.la: Itaque quantum ægritudini ex consilio Andini provinciæ acceperant, tantum gaudij pacatæ Gandavensium res adferebant, quod populus ultro inquies & ex dissidio immodestior ex recepta pace & utraque religione in civilem concordiam redijsset. Hoc vero paci suspectum erat, quod captivos jam ante custodiæ datos conventio non liberasset, discordiq; temporum ætate vinculis inditi squalloribus carcerum, etiam facta conventione, consumerentur.
units.tr: So, as much sorrow as the provinces had received from Andinus's plan, so much joy did the settled affairs of the Ghentese bring; for the people, restless of their own accord and more unbridled through discord, had returned to civil concord after the peace and both religions were accepted. But this was suspicious to the peace: the agreement had not freed the prisoners already given into custody earlier, and, in the discord of the times, they would be worn away in chains by the squalor of the prisons even though the agreement had been made.

units.la: Quare pro ijs dimittendis etiam, ab Elisabetha Anglica litterae petente reginâ, ut captivi judicio sisterentur, legibusq; provinciae damnati aut absoluti culpam criminum aut innocentiam missione vel poenâ exsolverent. Litterae Elisabethae in archivis repertae III. Kal. Jan. datae. His subjungebat regina ut satiandis Valonum & Gandavensium factionibus Ordines porro incumberent pacemque provincijs à discordiâ partium curarent.
units.tr: Therefore, for their release also, letters were sought from Elizabeth of England, the queen asking that the captives be brought before judgment, and that those condemned or acquitted under the laws of the province should settle the guilt or innocence of their crimes by release or punishment. Letters of Elizabeth, found in the archives and dated 30 December. To these the queen added that, to satisfy the factions of the Walloons and the Ghentese, the Estates should apply themselves further and take care to secure peace for the provinces against the discord of the parties.

units.la: Mox convulsae per Frisiam Sedis censu & dignitate imminutâ Rennebergius de amovendis Episcopi Canonicis agitavit, pensionesque ex proventu Sedis assignatas interverti reddique coenobijs jussit. Sed Matthiae Gubernatoris rescripto monitus, ne ambigua temporum ultro odijs exposita acerbioribus factis atq; decretis irritaret, ducentos florenos aureos Canonicorum alimentis dari fecit, dum illorum otio de subsidijs vitae autoritas patrum dispositum esset. Controversiam quoq; de Leppaeo aggere, qua Oostergoae partem à Sylvestribus disterminat, regio jam ante Senatui communissam, definiri per Deputatos Ordinum voluit, forique munia, velut ex interregno & per discordias novi veterisque Senatus compedita, ad judicia Ordinum transferri. Itaque per eorum apparitorem audiendam ad Sententiam Vitum Pibonis Abbema tanquam causae actorem & cum eo Leovardios, Idardios, Tietzerckios, Utingeranos una cum Nicolao Iselmudeno viro Nobili citari jussit judicioque ferundo v. Decembris diem praefinivit. Caeterum quid pronunciatum fuerit, in indigestis illorum temporum actis non invenid. Hoc tantum observo, aemulationes jam ante inter optimates & Senatores regis exercitas, isti rei occasionem dedisse, censentibus patribus accidendas provincialium lites & simul Senatorium numerum esse, agerumque controversias allevandis fori molestijs arbitrijs Ordinum aut Delegatorum permittendas.
units.tr: Soon, with the Frisian see shaken, its revenue and dignity diminished, Rennenberg considered removing the canons of the bishop, and ordered that the pensions assigned from the income of the see be diverted and returned to the monasteries. But, warned by a rescript of Governor Matthias not to provoke with harsher acts and decrees times already uncertain and exposed to hatred, he had two hundred gold florins given for the maintenance of the canons, while the authority of the fathers was arranged for their subsistence from subsidies during their leisure. He also wished the dispute over the Leeuwarden dike, by which part of Oostergo is separated from the Sylvestrians, already earlier committed to the senate by the king, to be decided by deputies of the Estates; and the judicial functions, as if shackled by the interregnum and by the discords of the new and old senate, were to be transferred to the courts of the Estates. Accordingly, through their summoner he ordered Vitus Pibonis Abbema, as plaintiff in the cause, to be summoned to hear the sentence, together with Leovardius, Idardius, Tietzerck and Utinger, along with Nicolas Iselmuden, a nobleman; and he set 5 December as the day for pronouncing judgment. But what was pronounced I do not find in the unarranged records of those times. I observe only this: rivalries already earlier exercised between the optimates and the king's senators gave occasion for the matter, since the fathers judged that the lawsuits of the provincials should be settled and at the same time the number of senators reduced, and that the controversies should be left to the decision of the Estates or their delegates, to relieve the annoyances of the courts.

units.la: Tum Rennebergius VI. Eid. Decembris à Matthiâ Gubernatore evocatus provinciâ Antverpiam celerrimo itinere contendit, ingravescentibus sensim inter illum & optimates suspicionibus, quod bona patrum consilia trahendo secreta & in pectus demersa suis non populi commodis reservaret. Igitur ne Ordinum generalium & Matthiae Gubernatoris animum malis artibus infrueret Iulius Bottnia, ut ante dixi, Antverpiam cum mandatis confestim missus, tum observandis Rennebergij actionibus, tum ut legatos regij Senatus secretiore ad hoc custodiâ clausos mole criminum & suspectorum consiliorum oneraret. Itaque consulto Ufkenio, qui Antverpiae negotia provinciae quoq; pro Trans-Lavicanis curabat, hoc effectum dedit, ne xi. mensis, qui dies isti actioni tractandae dictus erat, custodiâ liberandi pronunciarentur, ipsiusq; Rennebergij ad diversa respicientis consilia non procederent. Unde Rennebergius, quod suspicionibus gravaretur, acribus verbis in legatum invectus est, proque castellis regijs retinendis, quorum diruendorum causâ legatum Harlingae diu egisse objiciebat, acerbè locutus est beneficiorum suorum memoriam excidisse patribus criminabatur.
units.tr: Then Rennenberg, summoned by Governor Matthias on 8 December, hastened from the province to Antwerp by the swiftest journey, while suspicions were gradually growing between him and the optimates, because he was delaying the good counsels of the fathers, keeping them secret and buried in his breast, and reserving them for his own advantage rather than the people's. So, lest he deceive the mind of the general Estates and of Governor Matthias by bad arts, Julius Bottnia, as I said before, was sent at once to Antwerp with instructions: both to watch Rennenberg's actions and to burden the envoys of the royal senate, who were held in custody for this purpose, with a load of crimes and suspected counsels. Accordingly, having consulted Ufkens, who at Antwerp also looked after the province's business on behalf of the Trans-Lavicans, he brought it about that the eleventh day of the month, which had been set for dealing with this matter, should be declared the day for release from custody, and that Rennenberg's own plans, which looked in different directions, should not go forward. Whereupon Rennenberg, weighed down by the suspicions, inveighed against the envoy in sharp words, and, objecting that the envoy had long been working at Harlingen to have the royal castles demolished, while he himself wished them kept, he spoke bitterly, complaining that the fathers had forgotten his benefits.

units.la: Itaque (inquiebat) quos ego juvi, ab illis mihi male rependitur, regerente & petente Legato, ut si in illis esset, sacramento exsolveretur, ne pro patriâ loquendo vocis libertatem cum publicâ amitteret. Quare recepto in gratiam legato omne invidiæ onus in Hesselum Aysma Iureconsultum à Rennebergio rejectum, factumque est, ut conscientiæ testimonio & constantiâ Legati evictus Rennebergius reip. se addiceret. Quod vero ad fœdus Ultrajectinum attineret, in eo nihil agi posse coram legato obtestabatur, nisi copiâ fœderis à Joanne Nassovio Geldriæ Præfecto ad Matthiam Gubernatorem transmissâ.
units.tr: "Therefore," he said, "those whom I have helped repay me with evil." The envoy replied and asked that, if he were among them, he be released from his oath, lest by speaking for the fatherland he lose the freedom of his voice along with public favour. Hence, when the envoy had been received back into favour, the whole burden of odium, which Rennenberg had shifted onto the jurisconsult Hessel Aysma, was taken up; and it came about that Rennenberg, overcome by the testimony of his conscience and by the constancy of the envoy, submitted himself to the commonwealth. As for the Treaty of Utrecht, he protested that nothing could be done in the envoy's presence unless a copy of the treaty was sent to Governor Matthias by John of Nassau, governor of Gelderland.

units.la: Reliqua quoque Legati mandata communicanda Gubernatori suafit, ne derivatas ultro in se suspiciones tergiversando aut mandatis satisfaciendo manifestioribus odijs implicaret. Legatus vero pro diruendis castellis Ordinum generalium mandatum implorabat, ac ut Matthias Gubernator cautione de non præjudicando admissâ datam fidem principalibus promissis interponeret. Itaque libello supplici de sinistris Rennebergij in remp. suspicionibus conceptis quædam inserta delegatique Aldegondius & Leoninus ex consessu Ordinum, qui regij per Frisiam Senatus causam & mandata legati examinarent. Cæterum per absentiam Aurantij Principis omnia tardius expediebantur; Unde factum est, ut rebus etiam necessarijs moræ necterentur, dubiaque quarundam provinciarum fide singularum jus autillius curandi studium evanesceret. Bossuvius, qui cum imperio Exercitum Ordinum duxerat, fato tum functus sequiorem belli & reip. fortunam sua morte afflixit.
units.tr: He also advised that the remaining instructions of the envoy be communicated to the Governor, so that they would not entangle themselves, by evasion or by satisfying their mandates, in suspicions that had been drawn against them, and in more manifest hatreds. The envoy, however, begged for a mandate from the general Estates to dismantle the castles, and that Governor Matthias, once a caution against prejudicing the matter had been admitted, would pledge his word to the principal promises. Accordingly, a supplicating petition was inserted, containing some points about the sinister suspicions conceived against Rennenberg concerning the commonwealth; and Aldegonde and Leoninus were chosen from the assembly of the Estates to examine the case of the royal senate in Friesland and the envoy's instructions. But because the Prince of Orange was absent, everything was dispatched more slowly; hence it happened that even necessary business was held up, and the zeal for managing it faded with the doubtful loyalty of some of the provinces. Bossu, who had led the army of the Estates with command, died at that time, and by his death he added to the worse fortune of the war and of the commonwealth.

units.la: Mox percrebescente fama binas militum cohortes in provinciam inruisse, Deputati Ordinum de removendis decrevere, potestate Doconi Martnæ viro nobili & collegæ factâ, qui de causâ inruptionis cognosceret, dubijsque temporum & suspecta sacramenta populationibus ac licentiæ venditantes excedere finibus cogeret. Quod etsi etiam à Caroli Cæsaris per Frisiam Gubernatione præfectorum provinciæ ossicium fuisset (quos prohibendis Præfecturâ suâ externis copijs majores nostri speciali mandato & sub jurisjurandi religione adegerant) ita per absentiam Rennebergij Antverpiæ agentis finium tuendorum curam Delegati Ordinum suscepere, ne terrarum limites olim gentibus sacri, tum agri atque villæ vastationibus hostium ac suspectarum legionum exponerentur. Quæ ideo sinisterius quoque Deputati Ordinum interpretabantur, quod Rennebergius jam pridem inefficiosi insimulaaretur gloriamque prioris imperij & fiduciam patrum suffectis suspicionibus minuisset. Mandati tabulæ Epaei & Erasmi Doumæ, Barthij Idsaerdæ, Dirici Fogelsangij, Douwonis Syxmæ & Gellij Sibæi manu signatæ. Quas ipsas hoc etiam maximè prægravabat, quod Senatui regio, qui Leovardiæ domesticâ adhuc custodiâ attinebatur, judicia ac defensiones detulisset, Matthiæque Gubernatoris mandatum, agente apud Gaudavos directore rerum Aurantio, admittendis Senatorum patrocinijs impetrasset. Itaque rescripto in Frisiam misso eundi Antverpiam Senatoribus veniam fecit, Petroque Frittema viro nobili ac Senatorio, Joanni Damero Senatori ac à fisci advocato legatis commeatum procuravit. Hoc etiam cavit, ne quis manum legatis injiceret, neve molestiam crearet, pacisque publicæ sponsionem interceptâ securitate subverteret. Rescriptum Rennebergij xiii. Kalend. Ianuar. Antverpiæ indultum.
units.tr: Soon, as the report spread that two companies of soldiers had made an incursion into the province, the deputies of the Estates decided on removals, granting the power to Doco Martena, a nobleman and colleague, who was to inquire into the cause of the incursion and compel those who, taking advantage of the doubtful times and of suspect oaths, were plundering and bullying with impunity, to leave the borders. Although this had also been the office of the prefects of the province under the government of Charles the Emperor in Friesland (whom our ancestors, by special mandate and under the sanction of an oath, had bound to forbid foreign troops within their prefecture), so, in Rennenberg's absence while he was acting at Antwerp, the deputies of the Estates took up the care of guarding the frontiers, lest the boundaries of lands once sacred to the peoples, and then the fields and villages, be exposed to the devastation of enemies and suspect legions. The deputies of the Estates interpreted these measures all the more unfavourably because Rennenberg had long been accused of inefficiency and had diminished the glory of the former rule and the trust of the fathers by casting suspicions on his subordinates. The mandate tablets were signed by the hands of Epaeus and Erasmus Douma, Bartius Idsaerda, Dirk Fogelsang, Douwo Syxma and Gellius Sibaeus. These weighed on him especially, because he had handed the judgments and defences over to the royal senate, which was still held under domestic custody at Leeuwarden, and had obtained, through Governor Matthias's mandate, with Orange directing affairs at Ghent, the admission of the senators' advocacy. Accordingly, by a rescript sent into Friesland he gave the senators leave to go to Antwerp, and he procured a safe passage for the envoys: Peter Frittema, a nobleman and senator, and John Damerus, senator and advocate of the fisc. He also took care that no one should lay hands on the envoys or cause them trouble, and that the pledge of public peace should not be undermined by a broken guarantee of safety. The rescript of Rennenberg was granted at Antwerp on 20 December.

units.la: Itaque per Frisiam procerum animi sicuti superiores per provincias, ut antè contedis æmulationibus, ita tum discordijs dissociabantur.
units.tr: Thus in Friesland too the minds of the leading men were divided by discord, just as in the provinces above they had been split by earlier rivalries.

units.la: Mox reposcendis ab Episcopo tabulis permutatione agrorum inter Episcopum & Achlenios Lunckerkiosq; coenobitas scriptis Doco Martna delegatus, petente Pompeio Roorda Ecclesiasticorum bonorum quaestore ut tabulae praestarentur. Quibus exhibitis parante abitum delegato Episcopus pro annua pensione sustentandae vitae obtinendâ legatum ut intercederet oravit, qui pridem in dignitate & affluentia rerum constitutus reliquum aevi, quod breve esset, procul contemptu egestatis transfigeret. Quae quamquam Delegato Martnae viro prudenti & humanitatis artibus imbuto ultra commendata, quo vir Pontificio & regio cum diplomate in provinciam missus ab extremis fortunae abesset, ita Delegatus criminabatur Episcopum mandatis Ordinum non paruisse, jussumque lustrandis templis caeterisque Episcopalibus ceremonijs abstinere antiquam potestatem odio Ordinum & concitandis turbis exercuisse. Igitur suadere Episcopo ut in posterum ab hujusmodi potestate usurpandâ cessèt, ne secus faciendo laesae autoritatis publicae severitatem experiatur.
units.tr: Soon, when the records were to be recovered from the Bishop concerning the exchange of lands between the Bishop and the Achlenians and the monks of Lunckerk, Doco Martna was appointed commissioner by letter, at the request of Pompeius Roorda, quaestor of ecclesiastical property, so that the records would be produced. When these had been handed over and the commissioner was preparing to leave, the Bishop asked him to intercede for an annual pension to sustain his life, since he had formerly been placed in dignity and plenty and would spend the rest of his short life far from the contempt of poverty. Although these requests were commended to the commissioner Martna, a prudent man versed in the arts of courtesy, and although he had been sent into the province with papal and royal authority and was not in the extremes of fortune, the commissioner accused the Bishop of not obeying the orders of the Estates. He charged that, though ordered to refrain from purifying churches and other episcopal ceremonies, the Bishop had exercised his old authority out of hatred for the Estates and to stir up disturbances. Therefore he advised the Bishop to cease from usurping such power in future, lest by doing otherwise he experience the severity of the injured public authority.

units.la: Caeterum Episcopum, quo inanis solatij fallacem eventum praeveniret, veterisque fortunae memoriam alens constantiae gloriam etiam in adversis retineret, pauca delegato regesserit testatusq; SE (verba sunt) IN MANIBUS HOMINUM ESSE, retinendae nihilominus potestatis non difficilem fiduciam sumpsit. Itaque juri meo (inquiebat) renuntiare, & supersedere obeundis sacris ministerijs in animum non induxi, nisi jubear illorum mandato quorum autoritatem & beneficium meis factis obtendo. Quae ab Episcopo praesentibus praesule Achlenio, Iacobo Cronenburgio, Gosuino Foppio & Ludovico Foxio actuario publico, delegato Martna repositâ causam magis Episcopi & post Ordines exacerbavere. Haec Nonis Jan. facta.
units.tr: However, the Bishop, to anticipate the deceptive outcome of an empty consolation, and to keep the glory of constancy even in adversity by nourishing the memory of his former fortune, replied briefly to the commissioner and declared of himself (these are the words) "IN THE HANDS OF MEN"; nevertheless he took up, with no small confidence, the task of keeping his power. "Therefore," he said, "I have not made up my mind to give up my right or to refrain from performing the sacred ministries, unless I am ordered to do so by the command of those whose authority and favour I claim to be acting under in my deeds." These words, spoken by the Bishop in the presence of the prelate Achlenius, Jacob Cronenburg, Gosuin Foppius and Ludovicus Foxius, public notary, were reported to the commissioner Martna, and they made the cause worse, first for the Bishop and afterwards for the Estates. This was done on 5 January.

units.la: Tum pacatâ Gandavensium urbe & simul inquietudine, conciliandis Valonum dissensionibus omne studium adhibitum, quo provinciarum Belgicae corpus jam ante innovatis tot foederum rogationibus connexum, compositis partium discordijs coalesceret. Cujus boni spem etsi alerent qui concordiae & paci consilium suggerebant, ita erant qui simultatibus immutrebantur regique & Romanis sacris fervidè ac serviliter dediti, Ordinum imperijs & licentiâ religionum offenderentur. Ita quod extirpandis civilium animorum odijs inventum credebatur serendis usurpatum est, eo provectâ infelici discordiâ ut apertis secessionibus pararetur. Cui malo à praecipuis autoribus Episcopo Atrebatense & Ioanne Norcarmio (qui spiculatorum Philippi per Hispaniam ductor incertas conditiones pacis haud pridem attulerat) caeterisque fomenta subministrabantur, quanquam mihi actorum fide deprehensum sit, ipsum quoque Farnesium Limburgi agentem, dignitate regij imperatoris vix acceptâ, mobiles Valonum animos rumpendis provinciarum foederibus & conventionibus sollicitasse. Igitur secretis illorum conventibus quos faciendis secessionibus agitaverant, regis sui commodum includebat, quasi in eo positum esset, ut repudiatâ provinciarum societate, imminutam Philippi & Romanae sedis autoritatem obtendendo, de novâ cogitarent. De se vero fidem faciebat, nihil magis
units.tr: Then, with the city of Ghent pacified and its unrest at the same time settled, every effort was made to reconcile the disputes of the Walloons, so that the body of the Belgic provinces, already bound together by the many covenants renewed earlier, might unite once the discords between the parties were composed. Although those who offered counsel of concord and peace nourished hope of this good, there were others who were fed by animosities, devoted with zeal and servility to the king and the Roman rites, and offended by the rule of the Estates and the licence of the religions. So what had been thought devised for extirpating the hatreds of civil minds was used instead for sowing them, and the unhappy discord advanced to the point that open secessions were being prepared. To this evil, fomentations were supplied by the chief authors, the bishop of Arras and John Norcarmius (who had lately brought uncertain conditions of peace as leader of Philip's lancers through Spain), and by others. Yet I have ascertained from trustworthy records that Farnese himself, acting at Limburg, having scarcely received the dignity of royal commander, had stirred the fickle minds of the Walloons to break the covenants and agreements of the provinces. Thus their secret meetings, in which they planned the secessions, included their king's advantage, as if it lay in this: that, rejecting the union of the provinces, they should think of something new, alleging the diminished authority of Philip and the Roman see. Their own assurance was that nothing could be more pleasing or acceptable to him than for them to persevere in the worship of the Roman religion and in obedience to the kingdom, and by inciting others, to expect from themselves the king's advantage, glory and honour, as the rich fruits of their counsels.

units.la: cIↄ. Iↄ. magis gratum sibi acceptumque esse posse, quam si in cultu Romanæ religionis, in obsequio Regni perseverent, aliosque instigando opimos consiliorum fructus regis commodum, ex se gloriam atque decus expectent. Itaque evenit ut fidem legatis Ordinum datam violando à societate provinciarum desciscerent, fœdusque clandestinum VIII. Eid. Ian. Attrebati ictum recepto omnium Belgicæ nationum fœderi obtruderent. Quod quamvis superficie tenus intuendo à religionis odio & diversis in Philippum regem studijs profectum diceretur, tamen fato magis accidisse mihi verisimile est tantamque rerum perturbationem, cum humanâ ope & consilio persanari nequierit, immutabili providentiæ necessitate infœlicibus provincijs obvenisse.
units.tr: Thus it came about that, violating the faith pledged to the envoys of the Estates, they deserted the union of the provinces and forced upon the union of all the Belgic nations, which had been accepted, a secret treaty concluded at Arras on the eighth day before the Ides of January. Although on the surface this was said to have arisen from hatred of religion and differing zeal toward King Philip, it seems to me more probable that it befell by fate, and that such great disorder, which could not be cured by human help and counsel, came upon the unhappy provinces by the unchangeable necessity of providence.

units.la: Præsertim cum ea mutationum omnium his in terris lex atq; conditio sit, ut à supernis tanquam causis proficiscantur stellarumque motibus aut influentijs ascriptæ fati magis, supra astra adsurgentis inelucta-bile imperium, quam humanæ voluntatis arbitrium agnoscant: Igitur Hannoniæ, Artesiæ sociorumque fœdere continebatur, ut justum legitimumque esset, Romanæque Religionis & Philippi regis cultum atque obedientiam, denique pacis apud Gaudavos ictæ fidelem observantiam includeret. Hoc etiam additum, ut istud fœdus promiscuæ religionis tolerandæ decreto (quod IV. Eid. Iul. Antverpiæ perscriptum erat) adversum esset, unaque religio majorum traditionibus & autoritate Romanæ Sedis fulta per provincias & in Philippi ditionibus doceretur.
units.tr: Especially since it is the law and condition of all changes in this world that they proceed from heavenly causes, and that they acknowledge, rather than the decision of human will, the inescapable rule of fate ascribed to the motions or influences of the stars, rising above the stars. Therefore the treaty of Hainault, Artois and their allies contained that it should be just and lawful, and should include the worship and obedience of the Roman religion and of King Philip, and finally faithful observance of the peace struck at Ghent. It was also added that this treaty was to be contrary to the decree for tolerating a mixed religion (which had been drawn up at Antwerp on the fourth day before the Ides of July), and that one religion, supported by the traditions of our ancestors and the authority of the Roman See, should be taught throughout the provinces and in Philip's dominions.

units.la: Quibus attemperandis etsi egregiâ animorum moderatione & illustium virorum legationibus Ordines generales intercederent, ita econtra illorum studiâ pronis odijs accipiebantur, regerentibus Hannonijs & eorum socijs Ordines eosdem primos fœderum ruptores ex religionis pace discordiam sevisse remediaque civilibus malis quærendo incremento suffecisse. De se vero testabantur, Gandavense fœdus veneratos pacem tam diu coluisse, dum novitate rerum & religionum offensos à sacramenti & pactorum oblitis non malus animus, sed avitæ religionis & regiæ majestatis reverentia divulsisset. Quamobrem esse, quod Ordines generales Dei judicium, regis Philippi iram, præsentis ævi damnationem, apud posteritatem infamiam exspectent, quod fœdera, quæ sanguine potius & morte sanciri debuissent, violando, fovendis partibus & earum studijs, novaq; & à Gaudavensi conventione aliena etiam distrahendis provincijs repperissent.
units.tr: Although the General Estates intervened to moderate these matters with remarkable restraint and through embassies of distinguished men, their efforts were received in return with ready hatred. The Hainaulters and their allies replied that the Estates themselves were the first breakers of the treaties, having stirred up discord out of the peace of religion, and that the remedies they sought for civil evils had only sufficed to increase them. As for themselves, they testified that they had revered the Ghent treaty and cultivated peace for so long, and that it was not ill will but reverence for ancestral religion and royal majesty that had torn away from their oath and pacts those who were offended by the novelty of affairs and religions. Therefore, they said, the General Estates should expect God's judgment, King Philip's wrath, condemnation by the present age, and infamy with posterity, because by violating treaties which ought rather to have been confirmed with blood and death, by fostering the factions and their zeal, and by devising new arrangements foreign to the Ghent agreement, they had even sought to tear the provinces apart.

units.la: Ad quæ Ordines generales: Nihil magis unquam sibi curæ fuisse, quam ut fœdus Gandavense sartum inviolatumque caverent, cuius ea prima & potissima lex esset, ut indivisas provincias præstaret mutuaque ad auxilia præter patrij juris quod violatum erat, restitutionem exterminandæ peregrinæ genti obligaret. Cujus fœderis religione ne exsolvi quidem adhuc vellent, parati datam conventioni fidem non ore tenus sed facto adstruere. Sed religionis discordiâ, cujus Austriacus autor fuisset, impulsos Artesios primos societatem exuisse, quod scire eos crederent quos conscientiæ testimonium redargueret. Se vero non inani gratiæ ex Hispaniâ petitæ, non Escovedi malis artibus aliquid daturos, laturosque ut provincias sanctissimo Gandavensi fœsi foedere colligatas paucorum levitas ac defectio dissolvat. Ideo cum cIↄ. Iↄ. Hollandis Zelandisque eadem conventione depactos ne religio civilis vitae vinculum & conciliandis dissensionibus efficax, seminandae discordiae reperta diceretur.
