Infestari Geldriam, vastari Cliviam & ad Rhenum agros, neque aliud metuendum esse, quam ut, velut secundo amne ferox & nulli rei abstinens Philippi exercitus descendat, majore impetu, sicut exeuntia in mare flumina solent, Frisiorum agros & extrema littorum petiturus. Atqui auxilia nulla aut non nisi imbecilla si id eveniat, ad manum esse, neque subministrari a superioribus provincijs posse, quas aut arma, aut bello perniciosior potentum discordia fatigaret. Depugnari scilicet in ipsis Brabantiae visceribus & jam eo infoelicitatis perventum ut vicinos suos, quos socios habuisset, hostes timeat. Novo foedere, ubi vetera cessarent, parandas vires esse. Haec Ultrajectinorum Legati.
units.tr: Therefore plans must be hastened so that they turn out well, lest, through the carelessness of those deliberating or through untimely partisan zeal, the savagery of the enemy, proud and prevailing, take heart. Gelderland was being harassed, Cleves laid waste, and the fields along the Rhine; nothing was to be feared more than that Philip's army, fierce and abstaining from nothing, would come down like a river carried by its current, with greater force, as rivers flowing into the sea are wont to do, seeking the fields of the Frisians and the outer shores. Yet no auxiliaries were at hand, or only feeble ones if that happened, nor could they be supplied from the upper provinces, which were worn down by arms or by the discord of the powerful, more ruinous than war. Fighting was going on in the very heart of Brabant, and misfortune had reached such a point that they feared as enemies those neighbours whom they had had as allies. New strength must be prepared by a new covenant, since the old had ceased. So spoke the envoys of the Utrechters.

units.la: Igitur provincialium quin; qui in partibus libertatis censebantur, post aliquot dies acerbis altercationibus insumtos, hunc in modum rescriptere:
units.tr: Therefore the provincials, who were reckoned among the party of liberty, after some days spent in bitter disputes, replied in this manner:

units.la: QUandoquidem nos Delegati cum plena potestate statuendi definiendique repraesentantes agrorum oppidorumque Frisiae Ordines, de mandato RENNEBERGIJ Praefecti convocati sumus & ejusdem nomine propositum sit, ut Delegatos ad diem 1 x. Kal. Decembr. proximum Vtrajectum mitteremus, consultandi cum Legatis Geldriae, Zutphaniae, Hollandiae, Zelandiae, Vltrajecti, Frisiae, Transisulaniae, Groningae, Omlandiae, Drentiae, Tubantum & Lingae super articulis arctioris foederis, ea de re conscriptis & in acta redactis. Et ne propterea delegavimus D. Barthium Idsaerda & Douwonem Sixma cum plenis mandatis agrariorum oppidanorumque, per quos foedus illud signatum est, ea tamen conditione addita, ut ab Ordinibus Frisiae firmaretur approbaretur que. Ita nos infra scripti, pro qualitate nostra, considerantes quam necessarium foedus sit, & quam expediat illud ipsum ex actis precedentibus ad finem perduci, delegavimus & delegamus Barthium Idsaerda, & Gellium Sibaeum Consulem Leovardiensium Vltrajectum eundi, condescendendique cum socijs in Foedus x. Kal. Feb. perscriptum & post publicatum. Hac tamen cautione interposita, ut Legati curam gerent, ne provincia in causa tributi supra caeteras & plus quam aequum est, gravetur, tam ratione quantitatis quam aliter. Hoc etiam cavebunt, ne provincia tributum in foedere expressum ante pendere cogatur, quam vicini nostri in idem foedus adsciti sint. A foedere vero signato cum socijs consultabunt & definient, ut Legati Antverpiam ad conventum Ordinum generalium cum istiusmodi mandatis mittantur, prout de communi consilio conducere censebunt.
units.tr: Since we, the delegates with full power to decide and define, representing the Estates of the fields and towns of Friesland, have been summoned by order of Rennenberg the Governor, and in his name it has been proposed that we send delegates to Utrecht on the 10th of the Kalends of December next, to consult with the envoys of Gelderland, Zutphen, Holland, Zeeland, Utrecht, Friesland, Overijssel, Groningen, Ommelanden, Drenthe, the Tubantes and Lingen on the articles of a closer covenant, written on that matter and entered in the record; and since we did not for that reason send D. Barthius of Idsaerd and Douwo Sixma, with full mandates of the country and towns, by whom that covenant was signed, on the added condition that it be confirmed and approved by the Estates of Friesland: therefore we, the undersigned, in our capacity, considering how necessary the covenant is and how expedient it is that it be brought to an end from the preceding acts, have delegated and do delegate Barthius of Idsaerd and Gellius Sibaeus, consul of Leeuwarden, to go to Utrecht and there to agree with the allies to the covenant drawn up on the 10th of the Kalends of February and published afterwards. Yet this caution is interposed: the envoys shall take care that the province not be burdened in the matter of tribute beyond the other provinces and more than is fair, both in amount and otherwise. They shall also take care that the province not be forced to pay the tribute stated in the covenant before our neighbours have been admitted to the same covenant. But after the covenant has been signed with the allies, they shall consult and decide that envoys be sent to Antwerp to the assembly of the General Estates, with such mandates as they judge expedient by common counsel.

units.la: Actum Leovardiae 1 v. Eid. Mart. Iulius Bottnia pro Franequerensibus, Meinardus Wigerius & Ioannes Aysma pro Leovardiensibus, B. Loo, Doco a Martna, Renicus a Camminga, S. Galama R. M. praetor Baerderanus, Lafius Iongema, Diorraeus Annij pro Snecanis, Douwo Sixma, T. Aylva, Sixtus Bottnia R. M. Praetor pro Wimbritserijs, Carolus Roorda, Popko Roorda, Vitus Camminga, Justus Ockingha, B. Idsaerda, Scipio Meckmans, Sixtus Sceltama pro Dongrijs occioccidentalibus, Justus Herama, Tiallinghus Wikelius, Jorritius Hania, Auco Edonius pro me & fratre Oenso Edonio, Otto Herama R. M. praetor Rauerderhemus, Doco Aysma, Otto Sualue ; Sibrandus Camminga R. M. praetor pro territorio Leovardiensi, Epo Douma Hallemius, Oeno Grovensteinius, Pibo Vitus Abbema, Joannes de Verwou, Orichius Doyem cum praetore Galama pro Baerderanis ; Joannes Petri Sannes, R. M. praetor pro Stellinguerfijs occidentalibus, Hyeronimus Winterius pro se & ijsdem. E. Herama, Regnerus Idsius cohortis ductor pro Geesterlandis, Johannes Hottingha, Wibrandus Roorda & Arnoldus Annij Pastor in Jesium pro Ferverderanis.
units.tr: Done at Leeuwarden, 5 Ides of March. Julius Bottnia for Franeker; Meinardus Wigerius and Johannes Aysma for Leeuwarden; B. Loo, Doco a Martna, Renicus a Camminga, S. Galama, praetor of Baarderadeel; Lafius Iongema, Diorraeus Annij for Sneek; Douwo Sixma, T. Aylva, Sixtus Bottnia, praetor, for Wymbritseradeel; Carolus Roorda, Popko Roorda, Vitus Camminga, Justus Ockingha, B. Idsaerda, Scipio Meckmans, Sixtus Sceltama for the western Dongeradeel; Justus Herama, Tiallinghus Wikelius, Jorritius Hania, Auco Edonius for me and my brother Oenso Edonius; Otto Herama, praetor of Rauwerderhem; Doco Aysma, Otto Sualue; Sibrandus Camminga, praetor, for the territory of Leeuwarden; Epo Douma Hallemius, Oeno Grovensteinius, Pibo Vitus Abbema, Johannes de Verwou, Orichius Doyem with praetor Galama for Baarderadeel; Johannes Petri Sannes, praetor, for western Stellingwerf; Hieronymus Winterius for himself and the same; E. Herama; Regnerus Idsius, commander of a cohort, for the Geest lands; Johannes Hottingha, Wibrandus Roorda and Arnoldus Annij, minister at Jelsum, for Ferwerderadeel.

units.la: Caeterum postero die, qui III. Eid. Mart. erat, praepollentibus infirmando priori decreto partis adversae suffragijs rescriptum hoc modo.
units.tr: Moreover, on the following day, which was 3 Ides of March, the opposing party, with the votes of the stronger men to overturn the earlier decree, sent back this reply in the following manner:

units.la: ORdines Frisiae de voluntate RENNEBERGIJ Praesidis provinciae Leovardiae solemniter congregati, audita propositione per Reverendos Nobiles & eruditos viros Antonium Galama Vicedecanum Ultrajectinum ac Praepositum Northusanum & Florentium Thinnium Juris consultum, Ordinum Ultrajectinae Dioecesis Advocatum, ex fiduciarijs litteris facta, quo ijdem Frisiae Ordines Ultrajectinum foedus approbarent recipierentque. Decernunt ex singulari in legatos propensione & affectu, quod grates imprimis legatis agant, pro suscepta molestia, Declarantes interea, se Gandavensi foederi & secutae unioni obligatos, quibus abunde hostis repelli & conservari ex praescripto foederis possit novi Foederis auxilio non egere paratí, quod huc usque experimento ostendissent, Gandavensem conventionem omnibus viribus etiam cum vita atque anima tutari. Rogare ut Ordines istarum provinciarum quae arctiore foedere se obligassent, id responsum humaniter interpretentur confidantque pacificationem & secutam Vnionem ratam facturos culturoq; amicitiam atq; societatem cum vicinis provincijs, tui rei fidem publica relatione facere Legati possent.
units.tr: The Estates of Friesland, solemnly assembled at the will of Rennenberg, governor of the province of Leeuwarden, having heard the proposal made through the reverend noble and learned men Antonius Galama, vice-dean of Utrecht and provost of Northuizen, and Florentius Thinnius, jurist, advocate of the Estates of the diocese of Utrecht, made by letters of trust, that the same Estates of Friesland approve and receive the Utrecht covenant, decide, out of a singular goodwill and affection towards the envoys, that they first give thanks to the envoys for the trouble they have taken; declaring meanwhile that they are bound to the Ghent covenant and the union that followed it, by which the enemy can be sufficiently repelled and the country preserved, according to the terms of that covenant, and that they are ready not to need the help of a new covenant, as they have shown by experience until now, and that they will defend the Ghent agreement with all their strength, even with life and soul. They ask that the Estates of those provinces which have bound themselves by a closer covenant interpret this answer humanely, and trust that they will make the pacification and the union that followed valid, and that the envoys can give assurance of this by public report, and cultivate friendship and fellowship with the neighbouring provinces.

units.la: Haec III. Eid. Mart. in acta relata, ac nomine Ordinum manu Henrici Heffelij Praesulis Doccomiensium, Livij Wijtsma, Ottonis Vincentij, Hectoris Henrici Elinxma, Sixti Emingha, Upkonis Tallumij signata
units.tr: These things were entered in the acts on 3 Ides of March, and signed in the name of the Estates by the hand of Henricus Heffelius, prelate of the Doccum people, Livius Wijtsma, Otto Vincentius, Hector Henricus Elinxma, Sixtus Emingha and Upko Tallumius.

units.la: Qui mox libello supplice ad Lalainium misso, & decreti sui copiam & voluntatem exposuere, haud dubie apud benignum istius consilij interpretem, qui omne scribendi novi foederis studium, quod jam ante professus erat, manifesta ejus invidiae & indecora levitate mutaverat. Libellum, ut eorum nomina, qui in partibus fuere, recenseam I Bouricius, Nicolaus Laudensis in Hemelum Abbas Stauriae, Gerardus Iacobi Abbas Clare-campensium, Paulus Costerius Fosverdiensium; Thomas Groningensis Floridi campi, Riquinius Groningensis Gerricon nis coenobij, Henricus Kessel Doccomiensium, Rudolphus Pauli Faber Pastor Tzumarumanus, Gellius Ilstanus Commendator in Hospitali, Hubertus Scoeffius Commendator in Nes, Ioannes Bistemius Prior in Thabor, Ioannes Antonius Prior Novi Coenobij, Melchior Germanici Ordinis apud Slotenses Commendator, Wibrandus Schenichanius prior Cruciferorum apud Snecenses. Iarichus Bottnia, Hector Albada, Oeno Wijtsma, Iacobus Hornius, Oedsius Arnoldius, Elco Heringha, Ioannes Roorda, Isbrandus Slotius Prior in Aengium, Herco Ianconius, Syriacus
units.tr: These men soon sent a supplicating petition to Lalaing, setting out the copy of their decree and their intention, no doubt to that favourable interpreter of his council, who had changed his whole zeal for writing a new covenant, which he had already professed earlier, by plain envy and shameful fickleness. I shall recount the names of those who were on the side of the party in that petition: Bouricius; Nicolaus of Laudens, abbot of Hemelum at Stavoren; Gerardus Iacobi, abbot of the Clare-campers; Paulus Costerius of Fosverden; Thomas of Groningen of the Floridus field; Riquinius of Groningen, of the monastery of Gerricon; Henricus Kessel of Doccum; Rudolphus Pauli Faber, minister at Tzummarum; Gellius Ilstanus, commendator of the Hospital; Hubertus Scoeffius, commendator at Nes; Johannes Bistemius, prior at Thabor; Johannes Antonius, prior of the New Monastery; Melchior, commendator of the German Order among the Sloten people; Wibrandus Schenichanius, prior of the Crosiers at Sneek; Iarichus Bottnia; Hector Albada; Oeno Wijtsma; Jacobus Hornius; Oedsius Arnoldius; Elco Heringha; Johannes Roorda; Isbrandus Slotius, prior at Aengwirden; Herco Ianconius; Syriacus.

units.la: Margin notes (right, small italic): "Frisij fa-dus Vltraiectinum ratificare ... pudiant."
units.tr: Margin note: "The Frisians ... ashamed to ratify the Utrecht covenant ..."

units.la: Adeo ut mihi istorum temporum conditionem expendenti falsò ex-istumasse non videantur, Frisiorum plerosque à foedere Ultrajectino alienos, magis in Artesiae sociorumque consilia tanquam vetera & usu recepta, quam in novas vicinarum gentium societates inclinasse. Quamobrem à foederis Ultrajectini amantibus libellus quoque supplex formatus ac Rennebergio exhibitus, quo & memoriam signati per Legatos foederis innovabant serioque obtestabantur, se nihil in ista actione, praeterquam de praefecti consilio, egisse. Interim rem arbitrio Ordinum relictam, per absentiam Praefecti in suspenso mansisse, recusantibus Ordinibus tantae molis negotium sine consultore & arbitro subire. Igitur datis ad foederatos Ordines Ultrajectum litteris in adventum Praefecti distulisse, non sine spe aut fiducia hoc ipsum comitium isti negotio serviturum. Praesertim cum scripto & ore tenus conficiendi foederis desiderium praefectus non dissimulaverit; Atqui experimento se deprehendere, non socordia tantum in promovendo Ultrajectino foedere, sed morâ & pervicacia peccari, nonnullosque ex agrarijs, procul comitij lege privatis damnatisque coitionibus animum praefecti & consilia invertisse. Igitur non potuisse se deesse suis officijs, quin Praefectum de imminentibus periculis hoc belli incendio monerent; Neque enim hostem ignavum, neque inopem virorum aut Ducis esse, qui si in Frisiam aut vicina irruat, provinciam auxilia non ex Brabantiâ aut superioribus provincijs, sed vicinis habituram. Didicisse Lalainium expugnandis Camporum aut Daventriae civitatibus occupatum, quam paucis auxilijs se & socios praejuverint & quam Geldriam furoribus hostium permiserint, sua damna & incommoda è tarditate auxiliorum expertam. Adeo verum esse, patriae iniquos deprehendi, qui isti foederi adversi sint, quod reprobare illos tantummodo sciret, quibus volupè futurum sit, libertatis & omnium rerum ruinâ se pascere. Non ignorare praefectum, quibus autoribus stet publicae salutis mora & quam importunitatem professi sint, qui Harlingauum quoque conventum nuper habitum factiosis consilijs disturbaverint. Igitur se rogare Lalainium, ut prioris consilij & decreti tenax, plus conscientiae suae quam aliorum importunitati aut gratiae tribuendo, foedus Ultrajectinum probet, ne apud socios levitatis vitio Frisij traducantur & ne revocare ea videantur, quae ipsi etiam praefecto in adeundo foedere Harlingano comitio placuissent. Haec in acta relata ac ab Epaeo Douma Hallemio, Docone Martna, Epone Herama, MeiMeinardo Wigerio, Douwone Sixma, Ioanne Aysma, Joanne Martna cIↄ. Iↄ. pro Corniumanis, Wilcone Holdingha, Broërio Hesselio, Haione Cam-lxxii. mingha, Wibrando Roorda, Sixto Scheltama, Ioanne Bonga, Ja-richo Hottingha, Oenæo Grovensteinio, Justo Ockingha, Martino Schonbergio, Edzardo Glinsio, Frederico Fervovio, Orichio Doiemo, Ottone Sualue, A. Hercama, Tiallengo Wikelio, Pierio Auconio, Hieronymo Winterio, Lasio Iongama, Barthio Idsaerda, Iulio Botnia, Gellio Sibæo, Diorræo Annio, Bennerto Roorda, Renico Camminga, Sibrando Camminga, Vito Camminga, Docone Aysma, Arnoldo Annij pastore Iesłumano, S. Galama, Sixto Botnia, Vlpio Aylua, Foppio Grovensteinio, Tiallengo Sixma, Ioanne Fervovio, Iusto Herema, Ottone Herama, D. Roorda, Iulio Aysma, I. Sannes, Aucone Edonio, Iacobo Tiebbæo & Tetardo Tetardio signata.
units.tr: So that, when I weigh the circumstances of those times, they do not seem to have been wrongly judged: most of the Frisians were opposed to the Utrecht covenant and leaned more toward the plans of Artois and its allies, as old and customary arrangements, than toward the new alliances with neighbouring peoples. For this reason, a humble petition was drawn up by the friends of the Utrecht covenant and presented to Rennenberg. In it they renewed their memory of the covenant sealed through the envoys, and earnestly protested that in this business they had done nothing except by the Governor's counsel. Meanwhile the matter, left to the judgment of the Estates, had remained in suspense during the Governor's absence, since the Estates refused to undertake so great a business without a counsellor and arbiter. Therefore, by letters sent to the allied Estates at Utrecht, they had put it off until the Governor's arrival, not without hope or confidence that this same assembly would serve that business. Especially since the Governor had not concealed his desire to conclude the covenant, both in writing and by word of mouth. Yet they had discovered by experience that the fault lay not only in sloth in advancing the Utrecht covenant, but in delay and obstinacy; and that some of the landed men, by private meetings condemned outside the law of the assembly, had turned the Governor's mind and plans in another direction. Therefore they could not fail in their duty, but had to warn the Governor of the dangers threatening from this fire of war. For the enemy is neither idle nor short of men or of a leader, and if he should break into Friesland or the neighbouring regions, the province would have help not from Brabant or the upper provinces, but from its neighbours. They had learned that Lalaing, occupied with taking the towns of Campen or Deventer, had paid little heed to how few troops they had helped themselves and their allies with, and had let Gelderland be given over to the fury of the enemy; they had found by experience that the delay of help brought their own losses and disadvantages. So true it is that those who oppose this covenant are found to be enemies of the country, since they knew only those to reject it who would be glad to feed upon the ruin of liberty and of all things. The Governor was not unaware by whose advice the public safety was delayed, and what importunity they had shown, who had recently disturbed the Harlingen assembly with factious plans. Therefore they asked Lalaing to hold firm to his earlier counsel and decree, to give more weight to his own conscience than to the importunity or favour of others, and to approve the Utrecht covenant, lest the Frisians be held up before the allies as fickle, and lest they seem to recall what they themselves had approved, even for the Governor, in entering the Harlingen covenant. These things were recorded in the acts and signed by Epaeus Douma of Hallum, Docon Martna, Epo Herama, Meinard Wigerius, Douwo Sixma, John Aysma, John Martna for the men of Cornjum, 1572, Wilco Holdingha, Broër Hessel, Haio Camminga, Wibrand Roorda, Sixtus Scheltama, John Bonga, Jarich Hottingha, Oenaeus Grovensteinius, Justus Ockinga, Martin Schonberg, Edzard Glinsius, Frederick Fervovius, Orichius Doiemus, Otto Sualue, A. Hercama, Tiallengus Wikelius, Pierius Auconius, Hieronymus Winterius, Lasius Iongama, Barthius Idsaerda, Julius Botnia, Gellius Sibaeus, Diorraeus Annius, Bennert Roorda, Renicus Camminga, Sibrand Camminga, Vitus Camminga, Docon Aysma, Arnold Annius, minister at Jeslum, S. Galama, Sixtus Botnia, Ulpius Aylua, Foppius Grovensteinius, Tiallengus Sixma, John Fervovius, Justus Herema, Otto Herama, D. Roorda, Julius Aysma, I. Sannes, Aucon Edonius, Jacob Tiebbaeus and Tetardus Tetardius.

units.la: V. Cl. Carolus Roorda scribit, utrique libello studio aut incuria Lalainij rescriptum denegatum, monasticamque vitam professos & Roblesij ætate in dignitatibus constitutos & lege exautoratos, isti conventui, tanquam communi & libero interfuisse. Eosdem quoque rebus suis diffisos, libellum supplicem clam conscriptum & per tabernas conquisitorum scripturâ signatum, in comitio non protulisse repudiatâque comitiorum consuetudine & procurationum solemnibus, ex vitioso quoque & corrigendo legibus instrumento, novos Deputatos abrogatis prioribus creasse. In ijs Gerardum Jacobi Antistitem Clarecampensium & Hesselum Emingha Oostergoos, Joannem Roorda & Diricum Fogelsangium Westergoos, Erasmum Douma & Regnerum Idsium Sylvestres fuisse, eorumque postremum, velut dignitatis ex ætate incapacem, favore magis aut gratiâ, quam suo merito & prudentiæ gloriâ evectum. Legationibus quoq; extra provinciam obeundis Commendatorem Snecanum, Erasmum Douma & Diricium Fogelsangium delegasse, comitiumq; reparandis istâ ætate rebus & communi concordiæ institutum, publicâ secessione foedatum. Cæterum illorum autoritate, qui pro foedere Ultrajectino suffragati erant magis validâ, prioribus Ordinum Deputatis dignitates continuatæ factumq; est, ut quod evehendæ parti adversæ repertum credebatur, invidiæ & exitio egregio providentiæ miraculo cederet.
units.tr: The most distinguished Carolus Roorda writes that, through the zeal or carelessness of Lalaing, the rescript on both petitions was refused, and that men who had professed the monastic life, and who in the time of Roblesius had been placed in office and removed by law, took part in that assembly as if it were common and free. These men, distrusting their own cause, did not produce in the assembly the petition written in secret and signed in taverns by searched-out men; and, rejecting the custom of assemblies and the solemn forms of proxies, and also an instrument faulty and in need of correction under the laws, they created new deputies, the former ones being revoked. Among them were Gerard Jacobi, bishop of the men of Klarenkamp, and Hessel Emingha for the Oostergo, John Roorda and Dirk Fogelsang for the Westergo, Erasmus Douma and Regner Idsius for the Sylvestri; and the last of these, as being unfit for office by reason of his age, was advanced by favour and influence rather than by his own merit and the glory of prudence. For embassies also to be undertaken outside the province they had appointed Commander Snecanus, Erasmus Douma and Dirk Fogelsang; and the assembly, instituted to repair affairs in that age and to restore common concord, was disgraced by a public secession. Yet, by the authority of those who had voted for the Utrecht covenant, which was the stronger, the dignities of the former deputies of the Estates were continued; and so it came about that what had been devised to raise up the opposing party turned to their hatred and ruin, a notable miracle of providence.

units.la: Itaque Lalainius haud dubie animi æger & offensionem alens, quod bene destinatis præter spem excidisset Vollenhovam Idib. Mart. profectus est, ubi comitium Trans-Isulanæ gentis ordinaverat.
units.tr: Therefore Lalaing, undoubtedly sick in mind and nursing his resentment that what he had well intended had fallen out contrary to hope, set out for Vollenhove on the Ides of March, where he had called the assembly of the Trans-Isalan people.

units.la: Igitur Vollenhoæ agens, ubi annonæ defectu hostilem exercitum divexari intellexerat, legem de commeatu tulit, vetuitque ne quid frumenti, navi, aut curru hosti subministraretur, & ut omnium mercium professione præmissa, constitutis insuper in quaque civitate, qui lustrandis navibus præessent, Senatorijs viris dolosæ frumenti Rhenum versus aut Isalam subvectiones, amissione mercium, navium, atque currum punirentur.
units.tr: So, while acting at Vollenhove, when he understood that the hostile army was being harassed by a shortage of provisions, he passed a law on supplies. It forbade that any grain, ship or cart be furnished to the enemy; and, a declaration of all goods having been first required, and in addition men of senatorial rank being set in each city to oversee the inspection of ships, fraudulent carriage of grain toward the Rhine or the Yssel was to be punished by the loss of the goods, ships and carts.

units.la: Heymannus scribit Lalainium illo comitio de menstruo 20000. millium tributo legioni præstando propositisse & ut in quodque cerevisiæ vas bini stufferi ex Cortevillij legati, qui id ante rogaverat, consilio penderentur. Dein amovendis generalium collationum oneribus & redimendo quorundam Daniæ mercatorum ære decem millia carolæorum in
units.tr: Heymannus writes that Lalaing proposed at that assembly that 20,000 thousand [florins] be paid monthly as tribute for the legion, and that two stuivers be levied on each vessel of beer, at the advice of the envoy Cortevillius, who had asked for this beforehand. Then, to remove the burdens of the general levies and to redeem the money owed to certain Danish merchants, ten thousand carolus guilders were decreed as a monthly tribute, and three stuivers and a quarter per gold florin were demanded for paying it.

units.la: cIↄ. Io. LXXIX. in menstruum tributum decreta, eique pensitando 3. Stufferi cum quadrante à florenis aureis petiti. Igitur provinciales Paulo Gellio aerarij tribuno ocyus id deferre jussi, ne equitum peditumq; copias in Frisiæ finibus agentes & stipendiorum avidas aeris aut insolentiæ cupido in interiora provinciæ propellat. Id actis commissum ac XVII. Kal. April. manu Baudemontij Graphiarij Curiæ signatum. Cæterum discordi comitio & procerum animis aut à regis dominatione aut suâ libertate alienis, ne tempestiva quidem subsidia debili aerario præstabantur. Cui malo, etiam hoc incommodum accedebat, quod illo publico provincialium dissidio, oppidani quoque cum agrarijs dissentirent, infælicisque comitij concordiam, non tam regia ac religionis odia, quam antiquæ & tum renovatæ æmulationes morarentur. Itaque Lalainio ordinandis provinciæ rebus Leovardiæ adhuc commoranti oppidani libellum istiusmodi exhibuere.
units.tr: Therefore the provincials were ordered to bring this to Paulus Gellius, tribune of the treasury, at once, so that the bands of horse and foot operating within the borders of Friesland, greedy for pay, should not, in their eagerness for money or their insolence, drive into the interior of the province. This was recorded in the acts on the 17th day before the Kalends of April, and signed by the hand of Baudemontius, clerk of the court. But since the assembly was divided and the minds of the nobles were alienated either from the king's domination or from their own liberty, not even timely aid was furnished to the weak treasury. To this evil was added a further disadvantage: amid that public dissension of the provincials, the townsmen too were at odds with the landed men, and the agreement of the unhappy assembly was hindered not so much by royal and religious hatreds as by old rivalries, now renewed. Therefore, while Lalaing was still staying at Leeuwarden arranging the affairs of the province, the townsmen presented to him a petition of this kind.

units.la: ON ignorare te censemus, Præfecte, quantâ agrariorum importunitate exerceamur, quibus & animus & consilium fuit nos & à reip. constituendæ communione arcere & jure suffragiorum privare. Cum hoc velint, ut civitates & oppida partium ac distributuum jus ac conditionem sequantur. Et quanquam, si quid tale à majoribus traditum sit, infirmare nobis propositum non est, ita lubenter assentimur, modo antiquæ consuetudini, tam in exercendæ potestatis, quam sustinendo onerum jure acquiescant. Sed affectibus suis nec modum ponunt & ex lite lites serunt, etsi ita conventum sit ut Deputati quoque, ex oppidanis crearentur, quartamque reip. partem jure conventionis constituerent. Et sic quidem præstructum concordiæ fundamentum credebamus, nosque possessione juris nostri nunquam dimoveri ex formulâ pactionis potuisse. Præsertim cum tributa nostra, quorum immunitate ac exemptione majores nostri fruebantur, subsidio provinciæ & ipsorum quam maximè agrariorum cesserint. Sed istius beneficij memoria languescente, onera, quibus initium apud nos dedere, augent & à commodis reip. nos excludunt, præmissâ denuntiatione non laturos se in collegij publici cætu nostros delegatos considere, aut publicarum litteratum secreta, ex usu antiquæ inscriptionis, ad nos perferri. Itaque factum est, ut nec ad comitium citatissimus, nec Matthiæ Gubernatoris, nec Ordinum generalium, aut Vltrajectinorum litteræ ad nos pervenerint & quidem sinistris eorum artibus inversæ, qui veteres controversias ex novâ & perniciosa æmulatione refricantes paci, qua maximè egemus, impedimentum obtrudunt. Igitur quoniam & comitio interesse & consulere de publicis in commune prohibemur, ne impendia Præfecte & contemptum feramus missionem petimus, ac ut sinas nos in nostra, quando publicis arcemur, sine invidia usurpati juris redire. Obtestamur nihilominus propalam nos jus nostrum vel frementibus agrarijs tutaturos, ne, quæ separari non possunt, emolumenta amittendo, onera & incommoda feramus. Itaque tributorum exceptione nos tuebimur, daturi operam ut oppida nostra tuo auxilio subiuti adversus hostium incursiones, omniumque injuriam tuta atque munita præstemus. Interim neserendis discordijs fovendisque proni & à pacis sollicitudine alieni videamur, parati etiam nunc sumus judicium experiri, modo hoc quod speramus, æquitati nostræ detur, ut quartum reip. membrum habeamur, nihilque omisisse, quod paci & saluti publicæ expedire tua prudentia censebit. Ita pro Franequerensibus Iulius Bottnia, pro Leovardiensibus Meinardus Wigerius, Joannes Aysma, pro Ilstanis & Snecensibus Upco Franciscus & Diorraeus Annius, pro Bolsuerdijs Rinckius Cornelius, pro Staurijs Gerardus Wipkonius, pro Doccomiensibus Cornelius Ludolphi, pro Hindelopijs & Slotanis Wopco Douwonius, pro Worcumanis Gajus Jouconius, pro Harlinganis Cyprianus Ruardus & Cornelius Coninxius signavere.
units.tr: We think you are not unaware, Governor, by how great an importunity of the landed men we are harassed, who have intended and purposed to keep us both from sharing in the constitution of the commonwealth and from the right of voting. While they wish that the cities and towns follow the right and condition of the parts and distributions; and although, if anything of this kind has been handed down by our ancestors, it is not our purpose to weaken it, we gladly agree, provided that they rest content with the ancient custom both in the exercise of authority and in bearing the right of burdens. But they do not set bounds to their passions, and from one quarrel they breed quarrels, even though it was agreed that deputies also should be chosen from the townsmen, and that they should constitute a fourth part of the commonwealth by the right of agreement. And indeed we believed that a foundation of concord had been laid in this way, and that we could never be removed from possession of our right by the terms of the pact. Especially since our taxes, from whose immunity and exemption our ancestors enjoyed, have passed to the support of the province and, above all, of the landed men themselves. But with the memory of that benefit now fading, they increase the burdens which first they imposed upon us, and exclude us from the advantages of the commonwealth, announcing beforehand that they will not allow our delegates to sit in the gathering of the public college, nor that the secrets of public letters be carried to us, as the ancient superscription requires. Thus it has come about that neither the summons to the assembly, nor the letters of Governor Matthias, nor those of the general Estates or of the men of Utrecht have reached us; and indeed these were overturned by the sinister arts of those who, reviving old controversies out of a new and pernicious rivalry, thrust an obstacle against the peace of which we most stand in need. Therefore, since we are forbidden both to attend the assembly and to consult about public matters in common, lest we bear the expense and the contempt, Governor, we ask for dismissal, and that you allow us, since we are shut out of public affairs, to return without envy to the use of our own right in our own affairs. Nevertheless we openly protest that we shall defend our right even though the landed men rage, lest, by losing what cannot be separated, we bear the burdens and disadvantages. And so we shall protect ourselves by the exemption from taxes, and we shall take care that our towns, assisted by your help, be made safe and fortified against the attacks of the enemy and against the injury of all. Meanwhile, lest we seem prone to sowing and fostering discord and alien to care for peace, we are still ready to submit the matter to judgment, provided that what we hope for be granted to our fairness, namely that we be held as a fourth member of the commonwealth; and that nothing has been omitted which your prudence judges to be expedient for peace and the public safety. Thus, for the men of Franeker, Julius Bottnia; for the men of Leeuwarden, Meinard Wigerius and John Aysma; for the men of Ilst and Sneek, Upco Franciscus and Diorraeus Annius; for the men of Bolsward, Rinck Cornelius; for the men of Stavoren, Gerard Wipkonius; for the men of Dokkum, Cornelius Ludolphi; for the men of Hindeloopen and Slotanus, Wopco Douwonius; for the men of Workum, Gaius Jouconius; for the men of Harlingen, Cyprian Ruardus and Cornelius Coninxius signed.

units.la: Hæc xi. Mart. Lalainio exhibita, ac ut in manus agrariorum mox perferrentur cum rescribendi mandato, à Lalainio signata.
units.tr: These were presented to Lalainius on 11 March, and signed by him, together with the order to reply, so that they could soon be delivered into the hands of the agrarians.

units.la: Igitur AGRARIJ rescripsere:
units.tr: Therefore the AGRARIANS replied:

units.la: IVS majoribus nostris quæsitum, Præfecte, pertinaciter tueri in animum induximus, neque ferre, ut præter religiosos, nobiles & agrorum proprietarios jure, societate atque titulo Ordinum gaudeant. Præter hoc volumus, ut oppidani præturis in quibus siti sunt, se subjiciant tributaq; nostrum ad exemplum præstent. Quæ si recusent, obtestamur & vos, aliquid oneris debendi reos nos non esse.
units.tr: We have resolved, Governor, to defend stubbornly the right won by our ancestors, and we will not allow that, apart from the clergy, nobles and owners of estates, others should enjoy the rights, fellowship and title of the Orders. Besides this, we wish the townsmen to submit to the magistracies of the places where they live, and to pay their taxes on our model. If they refuse, we call you to witness that we are not liable for any burden of debt.

units.la: Cæterum Lalainius edixit: Ut oppidanis in istud tempus considendi suffragandique in comitio potestas esset, eorumque suffragia, velut à membro quartam provinciæ partem constituente profecta, rata firmaque essent. Ita lis non direpta, sed suspensa mansit, donec adulta ætate, velut movente bilem Sirio, cum ipso cœli æstu recrudesceret.
units.tr: Meanwhile Lalainius issued an edict that the townsmen should, for the time being, have the power to settle and to vote in the assembly, and that their votes, as coming from a member that makes up a quarter of the province, should be valid and firm. So the dispute was not settled but suspended, until, in the mature season, when the Dog Star stirred up bile, it broke out again with the heat of the sky itself.

units.la: Mox Barthius Idzaerda & Gellius Sibæus Ultrajectum, profecti, salutatisque pro more fœderatarum provinciarum legatis inter Lavicæ & Flevi amnium ostia Frisios sitos Ultrajectino fœderi sociavere.
units.tr: Soon afterwards Barthius of Idzaerda and Gellius Sibaeus went to Utrecht and, having greeted the envoys of the United Provinces according to custom, joined the Frisians who dwell between the mouths of the Lauwers and the Flie to the Union of Utrecht.

units.la: Igitur in consessu ex provincijs delegatorum acta hoc modo ea de re perscripta:
units.tr: Therefore, in the assembly of the deputies of the provinces, the proceedings on this matter were recorded in this way:

units.la: ANNO cIↄ. Iↄ. LXXIX. x. Kal. April. Comparuerunt Ultrajecti in consessu Deputatorum fœderatarum provinciarum, Delegati oppidorum Leovardiæ, Sneca & Franequeræ, cum mandatis quoque præturum & quorundam ex nobilitate Frisicâ, declararuntque se visitatis examinatisque aliis fœderis ex formulâ procurationis xii. Mart. scriptæ, fœdus illud approbare ratumque habere, addita promissione, se sicut reliquos fœderis socios operam daturos, ut in omnibus singulisque rite observetur. Quæ Leovardiensium, Snecensium, Franequerensium, præturum & nobilitatis nomine cauta, ac à Barthio Idsaerda & Gellio Sibæo signata.
units.tr: In the year 1579, 23 March. Delegates of the towns of Leeuwarden, Sneek and Franeker appeared at Utrecht in the assembly of the Deputies of the United Provinces, with mandates also from the magistracies and certain of the Frisian nobility, and declared that, having examined and weighed the other articles of the union, according to the form of the power of attorney written on 12 March, they approve that union and hold it valid, adding the promise that, like the other allies of the union, they will work to ensure that it is duly observed in every particular. This was secured in the name of the Leeuwarden, Sneek and Franeker delegates, of the magistracies and of the nobility, and signed by Barthius of Idzaerda and Gellius Sibaeus.

units.la: Cl. Franckena in diario suo notat iii. Eid. Mart. Frisios in fœdus receptos, solilq; defectionem versus occidentem viii. Kal. April. conspectam, magno metu civiles animos conterruisse.
units.tr: Franckena notes in his diary that on 13 March the Frisians were received into the union, and that on 25 March an eclipse of the sun was seen in the west, which struck civic minds with great fear.

units.la: Reperio in actis publicis Petrum Emskerckium regij sed loco moti Senatus actuarium Francisco Bandimontio successori litem tum movisse, eumque pro obtinendo restitutionis beneficio vehementer & acerbè agentem innocentiæ suæ testimonium rescriptum comitij obtinuisse. Id Henrici Kesselij Doccomiensium Præsulis, Martini Nitsenij & Upconis Talumij manu Idib. Mart. signatum. Ita invidiâ aut ex merito dignitatibus ejectos aliorum importunus favor & suffragatio gatio commendabat, patrociniaque pro animorum statu, aliquando virtuti, nonnunquam improbitati ex studijs partium quaerebantur. Itaque criminationum materies fictis inverisque accusationibus facta, tribunalia Iudicum & Lalainij praecipuè aulam fatigabat, eorum inquietâ malignitate, qui incertis rumoribus multum dando inimicorum injuriam ex magnitudine praecipitis famae aestumabant.
units.tr: I find in the public records that Peter Emskerck, the royal secretary of the Senate who had been removed from his post, then brought a suit against his successor Francis Bandimontius. Pursuing the restoration of his office vigorously and bitterly, he obtained a written testimony of his innocence from the assembly. This was signed on the Ides of March by Henry Kessel, bishop of Doccum, Martin Nitsenius and Upco Talumius. Thus those ejected from their offices, whether through envy or deservedly, were commended by the importunate favour and support of others, and patronage was sought, according to the state of men's minds, sometimes for virtue, sometimes for wickedness, out of partisan zeal. So the matter of accusations was made up of fictitious and true charges, and the courts of the judges, and especially Lalainius's court, were worn out by the restless malice of those who, giving much credit to uncertain rumours, measured the injury to their enemies by the magnitude of headlong fame.

units.la: Hoc vero Pontificij sinisterius interpretabantur, quod provinciae nomine ad Ordines generales scriptae litterae inconsultis Frisiae Ordinibus dicerentur, atrocemque provincialibus, velut tributa non nisi demolitis castellis & amoto regis Senatu detractantibus, injuriam manifesto mendacio inussisse.
units.tr: The Papists interpreted this more unfavourably: that letters written in the name of the province to the General Orders were said to have been sent without consulting the Frisian Orders, and that the provincials, as if refusing taxes unless the castles were demolished and the king's Senate removed, had branded them with an injury by a manifest lie.

units.la: Quare litteris ad Lalainium datis testandi in patriam & socios affectus, excusationem ignorantiae obtenderunt aliosque nomine ac mandato Ordinum male usos enormes calumnias gravandis partibus repperisse.
units.tr: Therefore, by letters given to Lalainius, they professed their feelings toward country and allies, put forward ignorance as their excuse, and claimed that others had misused the name and mandate of the Orders and devised monstrous calumnies to burden their side.

units.la: Quod ad castella regia attineret eius opinionis ac consilij se esse, ut salvâ regiæ majestatis autoritate subverti aut solo æquari non queant, tum demum confusionem & discordias factura si munimentis exuantur. Igitur rogare Lalainium, ut castella regij imperij praesidia integra aut inviolata praestet, aut de ijs ita disponat prout paci & saluti provincialium conducere videbitur.
units.tr: As for the royal castles, they said their opinion and purpose was that they could not be overthrown or levelled to the ground while the authority of the royal majesty remained intact; otherwise, if they were stripped of their fortifications, they would bring about confusion and discord. Therefore they asked Lalainius either to keep the castles, the garrisons of royal rule, whole and unviolated, or to dispose of them as seemed to conduce to the peace and safety of the provincials.

units.la: Hæ Riquinij Groningensis Praesulis Gerriconis coenobij, Nicolai Laudensis Stauriæ Abbatis, Pauli Cofterij Fosverdici, Henrici Kesselij Doccomiensis, Sixti Tiallengij pro Florido Campo, pro Oostergois Herconis Iouconij, Herconis Louwemae, Gellij Ilftani commendatoris in Hospitali, pro Westergois Hotsonis Henrici Æxmerij, Sixti Eminghae, Renici Bardij manu signatae.
units.tr: These were signed by the hands of Riquinius, bishop of Groningen, Gerricus monastery, Nicolaus Laudensis, abbot of Staveren, Paul Cofterius of Fosverdick, Henry Kessel of Doccum, and Sixtus Tiallengius for Florido Campo; for Oostergo, Herconis Iouconius, Herconis Louwema, Gellius, commander of the Hospital at Ilst; for Westergo, Hotsonis, Henry Aexmerius, Sixtus Eminga and Renicus Bardius.

units.la: Buntingius in Chronologiâ suâ notat Cometam obscurum pallidumque mense Octobris à Solis occasu visum, circa hujus anni initium orientalem factum, sparsâque in ortum comâ, ex caelesti motu circumactum caudam versus septentrionem porrexisse oculisque sensim submotum, velut manifestâ tabe sui luminis defecisse. Cujus disparitioni magnam adhuc in res humanas potestatem tribuebant, qui illius, velut diri syderis exortu, superstitione aut metu perculsi sua mala ad conspectum comatae facis, tanquam fatalem causam referebant. Itaque subsecutam aestatem imbrium copiâ messi noxiam, mox autumnum nimio coeli humore, putredine & exinde pestilentiâ gravem curiosi talium etiam defecto syderi imputabant, & quod ruptâ velut omnium rerum fide, etiam in tanto foederum concursu, infoelicibus provincijs desiderata pax exularet. Quae etiam armis silentibus, non levi discordium acerbitate per Frisiam fatiscebat, ita impulsis velut ardentissimo sydere, odijs ut civilis vitae consuetudinem vix paterentur.
units.tr: Bunting in his Chronology notes that a dim and pale comet was seen in October after sunset, and that around the beginning of this year it turned eastward, and with its hair spread toward the east, carried round by the motion of the heavens, it stretched its tail toward the north. Gradually it withdrew from sight, as if it had failed from the plain decay of its light. Those who were struck by superstition or fear, as if at the rising of a dire star, still attributed great power over human affairs to its disappearance, and referred their own misfortunes, as to a fatal cause, to the sight of the hairy torch. Thus the following summer, harmful to the harvest because of the abundance of rains, and then an autumn heavy with the excessive moisture of the sky, rot and from it pestilence, were attributed by the curious even to the failing star. They also blamed it for the fact that, as if all faith had been broken, even in such a gathering of treaties, the longed-for peace was exiled from the unhappy provinces. This, too, with arms silent, was wasting Friesland with no slight bitterness of discord, so that men were stirred, as if by a most burning star, to such hatreds that they could scarcely bear the customs of civil life.

units.la: Itaque regio Senatu suarum partium fiduciâ quasi in comitio praedominaretur, animos erigente, ne foederati quidem ea negligebant, quae praegravandis adversae partis fautoribus reperiebantur.
units.tr: Thus, while the royal Senate, trusting in its party, as if it were dominant in the assembly, raised its spirits, the allies did not neglect those measures which could be found for weighing down the supporters of the opposing side.

units.la: Qui Ultrajectino foedere suspecto, causae defectionem apud Matthiam Gubernatorem Ordinesque generales tum moliebantur, missis Antverpiam Petro Frittema viro nobili & legum doctori & Ioanne Dimero Senatoribus regijs, qui gravissimas accusationes, apud æquissimos, ut rebanrebantur, Pontificijs judices ex occultâ gratiâ elevarent. Quare ex Ordinum generalium consessu, in quo Hesselus Aysma vir eximius Frisiorum nomine tum considebat, Elbertus Leoninus & Liefeltius legum scientiâ clari cum Sillio Ordinum actuario examinandis reis delegati, quorum crimina actis publicis inserta nullâ dissimulatione aut conniventiâ proponebantur.
units.tr: These men, suspicious of the Union of Utrecht, were then plotting the defection of the cause before Matthias the Governor and the General Orders. Peter Frittema, a noble man and doctor of laws, and John Dimerus, both royal Senators, were sent to Antwerp, to bring forward, through secret favour, the gravest accusations before judges who, as they thought, were the most impartial Papists. Therefore, from the assembly of the General Orders, in which Hessel Aysma, an outstanding man, then sat on behalf of the Frisians, Elbert Leoninus and Liefeltius, distinguished in legal learning, were appointed together with Sillius, the actuary of the Orders, to examine the accused. Their crimes, entered in the public records, were set out without any concealment or connivance.

units.la: In istis præcipua erant.
units.tr: Among these the chief were the following.

units.la: I. Quod Senatus à Philippo rege per Frisiam constitutus Gandavensis pacis, vnionis & perpetui editi decretum suppressisset, ejusque copiam Frisij immissis in Basilicam sagittarijs prædicto Senatui extorsissent. II. Quod idem edictum non legitimè aut pro more vulgasset. III. Quod pro captivo Roblesio apud Austriacum intercessisset. IV. Quod in Lalainio Præfecto recipiendo mandatis Ordinum se opposuisset. V. Quod novas copias Remici Dekamæ & Arnoldi Gemenij tuendis partibus sine Decreto Ordinum autorasset. VI. Quod munitionem Oostmahornæ, ne præsidium Ordinum admitteret, suo retinuisset. VII. Quod Ioannem Austriacum hostem declaratumpr Gubernatore habuisset. VIII. Quod Matthiæ Archiducis gubernationem non approbasset. IX. Quod Hispanorum partes fovendo tranquillitatem provinciæ obturbasset. X. Quod Wibio Goutumano aditum cum cohorte ad Leovardiense castellum fecisset. XI. Quod ad Austriacum, Viglum, Lamotium, Bolsuerdienses odiosas & suspicionis plenas litteras dedisset.
units.tr: I. That the Senate, set up in Friesland by King Philip, had suppressed the decree of the Ghent peace, union and perpetual edict, and that the Frisians, by sending archers into the Basilica, had extorted a copy of it from the said Senate. II. That the same edict had not been published lawfully or according to custom. III. That he had interceded with Austria on behalf of the captive Robles. IV. That he had opposed the mandates of the Orders in receiving Lalainius as Governor. V. That he had authorized new troops of Remicus Dekama and Arnold Gemenius for defending their party, without a decree of the Orders. VI. That he had kept the fortress of Oostmahorn in his own hands, so as not to admit a garrison of the Orders. VII. That he had held John of Austria, declared an enemy, as Governor. VIII. That he had not approved the government of Archduke Matthias. IX. That by fostering the Spanish party he had disturbed the tranquillity of the province. X. That he had given Wibius Goutumanus access with a cohort to the castle of Leeuwarden. XI. That he had sent hateful and suspicious letters to Austria, Viglius, Lamotte and the men of Bolsward.

units.la: Ad quæ Senatus Delegati sub juramenti cautione Philippo regi præstitâ responderunt.
units.tr: To these charges the deputies of the Senate, having first given a guarantee under oath to King Philip, replied.

units.la: Gandavense fœdus, quam primum perlatum in Senatum fuisset, Senatui placuisse, tertioque Eld. Januarij acceptum, hybernaque tempestate & ex scribendarum formularum copiâ prolatum, III. Kal. Febr. vulgasse. Quod ad sagittarios in Senatum missos attineret, id se ignoraare, neque aliam locum recitando istius fœderi edicto delegisse, quam quem promulgandis actis publicis consuetudo destinasset. Roblesij vero captivitati & custodiæ non ultro, sed precibus mœstissimæ uxoris exoratos, patrocinium apud Austriacum commodasse, postquam regi Philippo placitum fuisset eum cum imperio in provincias ablegare. De ipso Roblesio nihil vero aliud cognovisse, quam quod in militum odia ex retardatis stipendijs incidisset, neque præterea esset, quod gravioribus eum suspicionibus inligaret. Lalainio vero, recturam provinciæ adepto, ut se opposuerint tantum abfuisse ut stipendia illius copijs ocyus procuraverint & quidem istâ liberalitate, ut proxumas seditioni cohortes exsoluto ære pacaverint. Quod ad conscriptum militem spectaret, id autoritate & de consilio Roblesij factum esse, postquam in potestate Senatus non fuisset, sine regis mandato dilectum copiarum aut missionem instituere. Neque Senatui de Renici Dekamæ cohorte in fide retinendâ constitisse, neque in causâ munitionis Oostmahornæ aliud fecisse, quam quod absente Roblesio, cujus vicarium imperium Senatus gerebat, copias collegerit præsidiumque loco imposuerit. Non diffiteri interim Senatum, quod denuntiationem Ordinum Frisiæ Deputatis, ut ab obsidione istius munitionis desisterent, fieri curaverit, postquam ignorasset Senatus mandatum Ordinum generalium aut Præfecti isti negotio intercIↄ. Io. intervenisse. Præsertim cum Lalainius præsente Indeveldio, Achlenio Senatus præside & quibusdam Deputatis palam Renico Dekamæ in mandatis dedisset, ne munitionem illam præterquam sibi aut mandatorio dederet. Austriacum verò à tempore proclamati edicti pro Gubernatore Philippi non habuisse, neque Matthiæ Archiduci obedientiam negasse, quominus ex illius præscripto ac imperio provincia formaretur. Itaq; non paci, non tranquillitati regionis unquam defuisse, neque occultà cum Joanne Austriaco consilia communicasse, quæ perniciosa provinciæ aut ejus statui fuissent. Denique cum Wibio Goutumano regiam arcem clam occupante nihil rei aut consilij habuisse, qui in castellum inscio Senatu irruisset. Igitur delegasse Senatum Popconem Romboutium & Ioannem Dimerum Senatores, qui de irruptione cognoscerent. Causam istius facti Mareschallo Matthenefsio aut Doconi Martnæ non ignoratam, ipsiusque Wibij confessione detectam, secretis consilijs subtuisse. Postremum Viglij Zuicheni consilio non nisi pro re natà & quod Frisiæ clarissimos natales deberet, usum Senatum fuisse, neque scripsisse ad Lamotium, nisi ut Valonum præsidium, quod Bustamantio Harlinganæ arcis Satrapæ manum injecerat, istius Lamotij, à quo pendebat, intercessione pacaretur. Neque Bolsuerdios aliosque rebellionis in Regem, nisi ante Gandavense fœdus infimulasse, usitato vocabulo, quo descivisse à Philippo stylo temporum arguebantur. Cætera viliora aut sæpè repetita mole magis quam argumento offendebant. Igitur Archiducis Matthiæ & Leonini Liefeltijque delegatorum decreto accusationis acta Frittemæ & Dimero ad rescribendum communicata, ne præceps judicium aut innocentiam illorum gravaret, aut immodestiæ crimi- num parceret. Qui etsi eadem fere eluendis accusationibus proferrent, ita intercessionem pro Roblesio datis ad Austriacum litteris susceptam, elevabant quod in tantà & tam subitâ mutatione rerum, neque quid agerent, neque quid deliberarent, satis expendissent perculsis & velut stupore contectis animis, quod Roblefium provinciæ Præfectum sui confessus principem militaris licentia spreto imperio vinculis indidisset. Quod ad Austriacum attineret, eum regio mandato provincijs Gu- bernatorem datum, reprimendæque Hispanicarum legionum insolentiæ in easdem provincias missum & populi adhuc gratiâ tum florentem præteriri per illa liberandi Præfecti desideria non potuisse, quum Senatus litteris resalutaretur quas ejusdem dignitati adscripserat. Quippe suis vi. Novemb. Anno. cIↄ. Iↄ. lxxvi. datis regias subjunxisse, Philippi mentis interpretes & quibus affectum boni Gubernatoris prætulisset, qui recognosci à Senatu testatione publici officij debuerit. Denique Philippi regis & Austriaci litteras de mandato Concilij Status Bruxellis Leovardiam perlatas non vano judicio novi principis & procerum consensu rationem provincialis imperij tum stetisse. Igitur Roblefium quoque Præfecti loco Concilio Status tum habitum, etsi mutato repente temporum statu, quem prævidere solertia Senatus non po- tuerit. Quæ de præsidio Leovardiæ fovendis partibus inducto obje- cta erant, ita diluebantur, quasi ex usu facta essent, ne Valonum co- hortes ad imperia & jussa præfectorum contumaces & seditionibus pro- xumæ æris inopiâ aut prætextu, Leovardiam urbem Senatus & procerum sedem direptione & insolentiâ vexarent. Eo metu actum Senatum modestius præsidium suæ & civium securitati ordinasse, cum eadem fortuna Bruxellensium ac reliquarum urbium iştâ legionum tempestate fuisset. Itaque restabantur se durante civilium bellorum aut dissensionum incendio nihil fecisse, quod Gandavensi fœderi, Unioni & Reip. adversum exitiosumque fuisset. Igitur neque hoc commeritos esse, ut suspenso judicandi officio, dignitatibus exuantur, quod illi immodestè urgerent, quorum malitiæ approbatam etiam nupero comitio Frisiæ Ordinibus integritatem falsis & ex Invidiâ repertis criminibus oneraret. Rogare interim Archiducem & Concilium Status Regij, ut æquitati patrocinando Senatum & Graphiarium à diu intermissis fori officijs in integrum restituant, neque sinant Senatum absolutâ regij imperij potestate præditum, integritatis suæ amplissima professione fraudari. Libellus quoque Matthiæ Archiduci in Legatum Aysma, velut publicæ causæ privata odia miscentem acerbior oblatus, officium æqui judicis implorabat, & ut innocentiæ Senatus expedito judicio subveniretur.
units.tr: When the Ghent covenant was first brought to the Senate, the Senate approved it. It was received on the third day before the Ides of January, and because of the winter weather and the number of forms to be written out, it was published only on the third day before the Kalends of February. As for the crossbowmen sent to the Senate, he said he did not know about them, and that in reading out the edict of that covenant he had chosen no other place than the one custom had designated for publishing public acts. Roblesius was not freed from captivity and custody of his own accord but was won over by the entreaties of his most grieving wife; the Austrian lent his patronage once it had pleased King Philip to send him away to the provinces with authority. As for Roblesius himself, he had learned nothing more than that he had incurred the soldiers' hatred over delayed pay, and there was nothing further that might bind him with graver suspicions. As for Lalaing, who had obtained the governorship of the province, far from opposing the soldiers, he had hastened to secure their pay, and with such generosity that he had quieted the cohorts nearest the mutiny by paying their wages in full. As for the conscription of soldiers, this had been done on the authority and by the counsel of Roblesius, since, once the Senate had no power, it could not institute levies or discharges of troops without the king's command. The Senate had not hesitated to keep Renicus Dekama's cohort loyal, nor had it done anything in the matter of the fortification of Oostmahorn except, in Roblesius's absence (the Senate exercised his deputed authority), to gather troops and place a garrison in the post. Meanwhile the Senate did not deny that it had arranged for the Deputies of the Frisian Estates to be warned to desist from the siege of that fortification, since the Senate had not known of the mandate of the General Estates or of the Governor's intervention in that business. Especially since Lalaing, in the presence of Indevelt, Achlenius the president of the Senate and certain Deputies, had openly ordered Renicus Dekama that he was not to surrender that fortress to anyone except himself or his deputy. As for the Austrian, from the time the edict was proclaimed he had not regarded himself as governor for Philip, nor had he refused obedience to Archduke Matthias, so that the province might be formed according to his prescription and command. Thus the Senate had never been wanting to peace or to the tranquillity of the region, nor had it secretly communicated with John of Austria any plans that would be harmful to the province or its condition. Finally, the Senate had had no part in the plan or purpose of Wibius Goutumanus, who secretly occupied the royal citadel, since he had burst into the fortress without the Senate's knowledge. Therefore the Senate had appointed the senators Popco Romboutius and John Dimerus to investigate the raid. The cause of this act was not unknown to the marshal Matthenesius or to Doco Martna, and was revealed by Wibius's own confession, and they concealed it through secret counsels. Lastly, the Senate had made use of the counsel of Viglius Zuichemus only as the circumstances required, and because he owed his most distinguished birth to Friesland; and it had written to Lamotius only so that the Walloon garrison, which had laid hands on Bustamante, governor of the Harlingen citadel, might be pacified through the intercession of that Lamotius, on whom it depended. Nor had they accused Bolsuerdius and others of rebellion against the king, except before the Ghent covenant, using the common term by which those who had fallen away from Philip were charged, in the style of the times. The remaining charges were rather tedious, or repeated so often that they offended by their bulk more than by their substance. Therefore, by decree of Archduke Matthias and of the delegates Leoninus and Liefelt, the record of the accusation was communicated to Frittema and Dimerus for reply, lest a hasty judgement burden their innocence or spare the crimes of arrogance. Although they brought forward much the same arguments to wipe away the accusations, they made light of the intercession for Roblesius, sent by letter to the Austrian, on the ground that in so great and so sudden a change of affairs they had not sufficiently weighed what they were doing or deliberating, their minds being struck and as if covered with stupor, since Roblesius, the prefect of the province, had confessed himself to be the prince's man and, scorning authority through military licence, had put him in chains. As for the Austrian, he had been given to the provinces as governor by royal mandate and sent to restrain the insolence of the Spanish legions; and while he still flourished in the favour of the people, his desires for the release of the prefect could not be passed over, since the Senate was greeted in return by the letters it had addressed to his office. Indeed, in its letters dated the sixth day before the Ides of November in the year 1576, it had appended the royal letters, interpreters of Philip's mind, and by which it had prefaced its feeling toward a good governor, which the Senate ought to have acknowledged by a testimony of public duty. Finally, the letters of King Philip and of the Austrian, brought from Brussels to Leeuwarden by mandate of the Council of State, had stood, not by the empty judgement of the new prince and by the consent of the nobles, the reckoning of the provincial government at that time. Therefore Roblesius too had been held by the Council of State in the place of the prefect at that time, even though the state of affairs changed suddenly, a change the Senate's shrewdness could not foresee. The objections raised concerning the garrison introduced at Leeuwarden to foster the party were answered as though they had been done in the ordinary course, lest the Walloon cohorts, insubordinate to the commands and orders of the prefects and close to mutiny through lack of money or on a pretext, should vex the city of Leeuwarden, the seat of the Senate and the nobles, with plunder and insolence. The Senate had, through that fear, arranged the garrison with more moderation for the safety of its own people and of the citizens, since the same fortune had befallen Brussels and the other cities in that storm of the legions. Thus it remained that, while the fire of civil wars and dissensions continued, the Senate had done nothing that was adverse or hurtful to the Ghent covenant, the Union, or the commonwealth. Therefore they had not deserved, by suspending the office of judging, to be stripped of their dignities, as those men unreasonably urged, whose malice burdened with false and invented accusations the integrity of the Senate, which even the recent assembly of the Frisian Estates had approved. Meanwhile they asked the Archduke and the Council of State of the King to restore the Senate and the Graphiarius to the full functions of the court, long interrupted, in defence of equity, and not to allow the Senate, endowed with the full power of royal authority, to be defrauded of the most ample profession of its integrity. A libel also offered to Archduke Matthias against the legate Aysma, which mingled private hatreds with the public cause in a rather bitter way, implored the office of an impartial judge and that the innocence of the Senate be aided by a speedy judgement.

units.la: Cæterum actore legato & vetera repetebantur, & nova gravandis accusationibus non deficiebant prodentibus se magis magisque delegatorum ingenijs, quod acerrima defensione exolescere sensum injuriæ non sinerent Ordinesque Frisiæ suæ liti, tanquam publicæ implicarent. Igitur delegatis Frittema & Dimero Antverpiæ hærentibus; multa ad huc onerandæ criminum famæ adferebantur, Matthiæque Gubernatoris animum fœcundis argumentis instruebant. Qui novorum Legatorum è Frisiâ adventu cognito, in quibus Gellius Ilstanus commendator Nessanus, & annalium scriptor, Erasmus Douma & Diricius Fogelsangius erant, rescripto ad libellum supplicem Prid. Non. April. à delegatis Senatus exhibitum dato, explorandas legatorum voluntates decernebat quo provinciæ in veterem Senatum propensionem aut odium cognosceret. Cæterum Ilstanus cæterique legati, id à mandatis suis alienum regerebant, publicæque causæ destinatos, privatæ cum Senatu actionis invidiem respuere. Ita res in suspenso, non cessantibus interea altercationibus, mansit, donec invalescente Ultrajectino fœdere, in majora odia erumperet.
units.tr: Besides this, the old charges were repeated by the legate, and new ones did not fail to burden the accusations, the delegates revealing themselves more and more in their cleverness, since by their most fierce defence they did not allow the sense of injury to fade and entangled the Frisian Estates in their suit as though it were a public matter. Therefore, while the delegates Frittema and Dimerus remained at Antwerp, many more things were brought forward to load the reputation of the accused with crimes, and supplied the mind of Governor Matthias with fertile arguments. He, learning of the arrival of the new legates from Friesland, among whom were Gellius Ilstanus, commander of Nes and writer of annals, Erasmus Douma and Dirk Fogelsang, by a rescript dated the fourth day before the Nones of April, given to the supplicating libel presented by the delegates of the Senate, decreed that the wills of the legates be examined, so that he might learn whether the province inclined toward or hated the old Senate. But Ilstanus and the other legates replied that this was foreign to their instructions, that they had been appointed for a public cause, and that they repudiated the odium of a private action against the Senate. So the matter remained in suspense, with the quarrels meanwhile not ceasing, until, as the Union of Utrecht grew strong, it broke out into greater hatreds.

units.la: Mox Cunerus Leovardiensium Episcopus privatæ apud Bergumanos custodiæ mancipatus, per apparitores jussu novi Senatus Wigerum Mockanam, & Boccatium Douwonem spiculatoribus publicis stipatos more captivi Leovardiam pertractus est, quod secretam cum Gasparo Roblesio conjurationem inijsse suspiciosis indicijs diceretur. Cæterum eodem die à Senatu dimissus, & in Bergumanos veterem secessum expendendis suarum rerum rationibus, tanquam honestam custodiam amotus est. Arnoldus Gemenius & Vibius Crusius diuturniore quoque custodiâ liberati.
units.tr: Soon afterwards Cunerus, bishop of Leeuwarden, who had been placed in private custody among the Bergumers, was brought to Leeuwarden by the officers, by order of the new Senate, with Wiger Mockana and Boccatius Douwo escorted by public executioners, in the manner of a captive, because he was said to have entered a secret conspiracy with Gaspar Roblesius, as suspicious indications suggested. However, on the same day he was dismissed by the Senate and withdrew to his former retreat among the Bergumers, to weigh his affairs, having been removed as into honourable custody. Arnold Gemenius and Vibius Crusius were also released after a longer custody.

units.la: Heymannus notat viii. Eid. April. phasma quoddam specie hemicycli apparuisse, aliudque à pluvio arcu, velut soli opposito & depressiore, verticale cœli punctum tenuisse. Quæ phænomea, ut solent, ex naturæ causis, aut fulgore roridarum nubium sæpe orta, prodigiorum ostentui imbecillibus ingenijs æquabantur.
units.tr: Heymannus notes that on the eighth day before the Ides of April a certain phantasm appeared in the form of a half-circle, and a point different from the rainbow, as if opposite the sun and lower, held the vertical point of the sky. These phenomena, as usual, arising from natural causes, or often from the flash of dewy clouds, were by weak minds equated with portents and omens.

units.la: LXXIX. Mox Lalainius Vollenhovâ in Frisiam regressus mense Aprili assumptis in comitatum Versteverano & Rhala Senatoribus aggeres marinos, qui à Feenhusâ ad Lavicæ ostium Frisico littori prætexuntur, ocyus lustrari fecit, quo hybernis tempestatibus aut continuo æstu continentem lambente arrosi aut disjecti novæ molis aggestione sustinendis fluctibus firmarentur. Legatis vero, quos cum mandatis è Frisiâ Antverpiam missos memoravi, à Matthia Gubernatore haud levia & a tempore conditione aliena proponebantur. Ista erant.
units.tr: LXXIX. Soon afterwards Lalainius returned from Vollenhove to Friesland in April. Taking with him as companions the senators of Versteveen and Rhala, he had the sea dykes inspected without delay. These run along the Frisian coast from Feenhusa to the mouth of the Lauwers. In winter storms, or under constant tides, the dykes had been eaten away by the sea, which licked at the mainland, or broken apart, so they needed new embankments to withstand the waves.

units.la: I. Ut provinciæ aut earum Legati pro observando aut deserendo Gandavensi fœdere sententias exponant. II. Ut provinciæ defectioni proximæ ad antiqui fœderis societatem reducantur, eoque innovato firmatoque, de rebus pace bellove necessariis in commune consultetur. III. Ut provinciæ ex jure istius fœderis pendendis intendendisque pro re natâ publicis collationibus, salva nihilominus uniuscuiusq; provinciæ immunitate, se obligent. IV. Ut tollendis de religione controversiis certa & syncera pax & conventio scribatur. V. Ut provinciæ ocyus Delegatos autoritate & prudentiâ spectabiles patriæ fidos ad conventum Ordinum generalium mittant. VI. Ut provinciæ pacem faciendo, eam ad præscriptum Ordinum generalium firment. VII. Ut militari disciplinæ, juris & æqui observantiæ, in promptu stipendia tributaque habeantur, Matthiæque Archiduci, Ordinibus & Præfectis provinciarum sua autoritas constet. VIII. Ut durante pacis actione, de belli ordine, de formando exercitu, liberandâque ab Hispanorum obsidione Trajectensium ad Mosam civitate cogitent.
units.tr: The envoys whom I mentioned as sent from Friesland to Antwerp were presented with proposals from Governor Matthias that were not light and were ill-suited to the times. They were these: (I) that the provinces, or their envoys, should state their opinions on whether to observe or abandon the Ghent covenant; (II) that the provinces nearest to defection should be brought back into the alliance of the old covenant, and that, once this was renewed and confirmed, they should deliberate together on matters of peace and war; (III) that the provinces should bind themselves, according to the right of that covenant, to pay and levy public contributions as circumstances required, though each province's immunity should nonetheless remain intact; (IV) that a certain and sincere peace and agreement should be drawn up to settle the controversies over religion; (V) that the provinces should send without delay delegates distinguished by authority and prudence and loyal to the country to the assembly of the General Estates; (VI) that in making peace the provinces should confirm it according to the terms laid down by the General Estates; (VII) that money and taxes should be kept ready for military discipline and the observance of law and justice, and that the authority of Archduke Matthias, of the Estates and of the provincial governors should be secure; (VIII) that, while the peace negotiations went on, they should consider the conduct of the war, the forming of an army, and the liberation of the city of Utrecht, which the Spaniards had besieged, from the Meuse.

units.la: Quibus, Matthiæ Gubernatoris & Ordinum nomine ab Elberto Leonino legum peritiâ & eloquentiæ artibus claro nonnulla addebantur. Convenisse scilicet se, non instituendis novorum Principum inaugurationibus, quæ lætiora majorum ætati fortuna obtulisset, cæterum quærendis malorum remedijs, in quæ Hispanorum, hostiumque vis aut insolentia infœlices provincias perduxisset. Deliberari pro conjugum atque liberorum vitâ atque sanguine, pro declinandâ durissimâ servitute, & omnium rerum ruinâ quam discrepantium in conventibus suffragiorum diversitas propè intuentibus minaretur. Sed isti subveniri posse, si quisque quam in patriam affectus esse debet, tam de onere belli ferundo, & simul subjuvandis socijs cogitet, quos in ultimo discrimine constitutos infœlix miseratio spectaret. Hac solâ viâ ad pacem perveniri posse, quam utilem & bonam habere, non nisi superatis hostibus aut nisi eorum vires æquaveris posses. Fine belli pacem æstumari, quam honestam obtinere Ordines nequirent, præterquam socia Trajecti ad Mosam urbe, hostium castris cinctâ, libertati restitutâ. Atque ut id fiat & rerum & gloriæ gentis interesse, quæ non siverit Albani ac Requesentij ætate tabescere ærarium gerendis armis efficax.
units.tr: To these, in the name of Governor Matthias and the Estates, Elbert Leoninus, distinguished for his knowledge of law and his skill in eloquence, added some further remarks. They had met, he said, not to institute the inaugurations of new princes, which a happier fortune had offered to the age of our ancestors, but to seek remedies for the evils into which the power and insolence of the Spaniards and of the enemy had led the unhappy provinces. They must deliberate concerning the lives and blood of their wives and children, concerning how to avoid the harshest slavery, and concerning the ruin of all things, which the differing votes in the assemblies, which those looking on nearly foresaw, threatened. But this could be remedied, if each man thought as much about bearing the burden of war, and at the same time about aiding his allies, who stood in the utmost danger and whom unhappy pity looked upon, as he ought to think about his country. Peace could be reached by this path alone, and it could be useful and good only if the enemies were overcome, or if you could match their strength. Peace should be valued by its end, and the Estates could not obtain an honourable peace unless the city of Utrecht on the Meuse, surrounded by enemy camps, were restored to freedom. That this should happen was in the interest both of their affairs and of the glory of the nation, which, in the time of Alba and Requesens, had not allowed the treasury to waste away, being effective in waging war.

units.la: Postquam verò illius incuriâ & inopiâ laboratum, res infœlicius cessisse, quas seorsim Belgicæ & trans Rhenum Frisiorum gentes olim magnâ cum laude suis cum hostibus gessissent. Igitur opprobrio & infamiæ fore, conjunctis tanto numero & nexu provincijs non vires, sed consilia defuisse, sociosque pro salute publicâ, prò conjugum ac liberorum incolumitate pugnantes, denique ipsam remp. satiscentem occasui proxumam opportunis & ad manum auxilijs non sublevasse. Caeterum salubriter & pro aegerrimi provinciarum corporis statu praescripta imbecillior natura respuebat, cum essent, qui affirmanda numerosissimi exercitus stipendijs tributa, velut aspera & modum excedentia, à suis quique provincijs averterent. Ita cum singulas desiderati tributi fastidium aut aversatio occuparet, universae subsidijs destituebantur.
units.tr: But after this, when they had been labouring under his carelessness and lack of resources, affairs had turned out more unhappily, though the peoples of Belgium and of the Frisians beyond the Rhine had once waged their own wars against their enemies with great renown. Therefore it would be a source of disgrace and infamy that, though the provinces were joined in so great a number and so close a bond, it was not their strength but their counsels that had failed; that they had not relieved their allies, who fought for public safety and for the safety of their wives and children, and had not, with timely and ready help, rescued the commonwealth itself, now sinking toward its fall. Moreover, the weaker nature rejected the prescriptions that were salutary and suited to the very sick state of the provincial body, since there were some who, to support the pay of the very numerous army, turned their provinces away from the taxes as harsh and excessive. Thus, while a loathing or aversion for each proposed tax seized them individually, all were left without aid.

units.la: Erant quoque qui novum tributi genus declinando; vetera & sub Albano decimae centesimaeque nomine reperta commendarent, debilique & velut moriente aerario extrema ope subveniendum. Alij vero, etsi potentia & opibus validi, ex erogandi aeris causa indemnes praestari cautione à socijs volebant, ijs quoque minus ad sociorum pericula affectis, quos Mosa aut Rheno hostilibus castris presso, extra discrimen positos vana securitatis humanae opinio faciebat. Sed occulta fati vis, quae ad secessiones & arma trahebat, quasi causam aut praetextum quaerens, ut consilij, ita provincialium concordiam morabatur, postquam ita constitutum videretur, ut Hannoniâ & superioris Belgicae tractu à caeteris avulso, inferiores quoque provincias, quae ad Oceanum vergunt, Ultrajectinum foedus combinaret. Ita evenit ut magnum illud & regi etiam Philippo formidabile Belgicae corpus dissolveretur, belloque in tot annos exituro infausta initia perdundis rebus solers fortuna praestrueret. Igitur Bolsuerdiâ, Doccomio, Harlingâ aliisque oppidis à foedere adhuc Ultrajectino exclusis foederati Ordines Ultrajecto litteras ad eadem civitates misère, quibus ad novi foederis communionem speciosis rationibus sollicitabant. Imprimis vero commonebant, ne provinciali concordiae ex se validae adversarentur & ne Frisij occasionum segnes & sua commoda negligendo soli palantes & mutuis societatibus destituti, intestinis dissensionibus diffluerent. Caeterum omnem illum foederis eventum partium adhuc aemulatio tardabat, non cessante Senatu regio tum praesulum & earum partium intercessione, gravem illum & regiae dominationi mancipem spiritum invalescenti foederis potentiae objicere. Quibus & hoc accedebat, quod Lalainius litteris suis vi. April. datis, foederis Ultrajectini receptionem segniter frigidèque habuisset, neminemque se isti retinendo impulsurum fidem fecisset. Igitur inter regij Senatus & provinciae legatos Antverpiae commorantes, novae partium acerbitates recrudescebant, urgente Hesselo Aysma legato, ut acta exercitae Senatoriae examinationis ad Deputatos Frisiae perferrentur, ipsique Lalainio provinciae praefecto communicata cognitione solemnis judicij determinarentur. Hoc vero rescripto Matthiae Gubernatoris cautum est, ut intra bimestre, post exhibita Deputatis Frisiae & ejusdem provinciae Praefecto acerbae litis instrumenta, negotium definiretur, omnique dilatione ac morâ cessante finem haberet.
units.tr: There were also some who, avoiding a new kind of tax, recommended the old ones, which had been devised under Alba under the name of tithe and hundredth penny, and said that the feeble treasury, as if dying, must be helped with a final effort. Others, though strong in power and wealth, wanted to be secured by their allies with a guarantee against loss from the spending of money; these men were also less affected by the dangers of their allies, whom the empty confidence of human security made to seem out of danger, though the Meuse or the Rhine was pressed by hostile camps. But a hidden force of fate, which drew them towards secession and arms, as if seeking a cause or pretext, delayed the agreement of the provinces just as it delayed their deliberation. It seemed decided that, with Hainault and the district of Upper Belgium cut off from the rest, the lower provinces, which slope toward the Ocean, should form the Union of Utrecht. So it happened that that great body of Belgium, which was formidable even to King Philip, was dissolved, and a fortune that was clever at ruin prepared unlucky beginnings for a war that was to last for so many years. Therefore the confederated Estates sent letters from Utrecht to the towns of Bolsward, Dokkum, Harlingen and others, which were still excluded from the Union of Utrecht, and urged them with plausible reasons to join the new covenant.
