Above all they warned them not to oppose the provincial agreement, which was strong in itself, and not to let the Frisians, slack in seizing opportunities and neglecting their own advantages, wander alone and without mutual alliances and dissolve in internal dissensions. But the rivalry of the parties still delayed the whole outcome of the covenant, since the royal Senate, with the intervention of the prelates and of those parties, did not cease to set against the strengthening power of the covenant that grave spirit, a spirit that is subject to royal dominion. To these difficulties this was also added: Lalainius, in his letter dated 6 April, had received the acceptance of the Union of Utrecht sluggishly and coldly, and had given no assurance that he would urge anyone to hold to it. Therefore, while the envoys of the royal Senate and of the province were staying at Antwerp, the bitter disputes between the parties broke out again, Hessel Aysma, the envoy, urging that the records of the examination conducted by the Senate be delivered to the Deputies of Friesland, and that, once the findings had been shared with Lalainius himself, the governor of the province, the dispute be settled by a formal judgment. But by a rescript of Governor Matthias it was provided that, within two months after the documents of the bitter lawsuit had been presented to the Deputies of Friesland and to the governor of that province, the matter should be decided, and that, with all delay and hindrance ceasing, it should come to an end.

units.la: Caeterum fortuna, ut solet, serendis discordijs insolens potentum consilia corruperat. Igitur foedus à defectoribus viii. Eid. April. i-ctum. Eo cautum ut religio Catholicâ Romana haberetur, regi ejusque praesidi obsequium esset; Hispani peregrinique Belgio ex formula Gandavensis foederis excedant, id nisi rex ratum praestaret, à foedere recedendi liberum foret. Quod ad D. Eligij montem haud procul à Regiaco cIↄ. Iↄ. giaco in Attrebatibus scriptum Ordinibusque provinciarum, etsi aliud simulantibus, communicatum, velut tristissimi casus obnuntiatione prona paci ingenia affecit. Itaque responderunt se illorum studia in retinendâ majorum religione, ac praestando regi obsequio probare, caeterum hoc velle, ne speciosis Hispanorum deceptionibus nimium fidant, circumspectique & prudentes priorum temporum exempla pro recentibus expendant. Notam scilicet Ferdinandi Albani immanissimi Ducum perfidiam fuisse, atque Hyeronimum Rodam illius artis magistrum dissimulasse, quae perjurij nomine olim traducta, speciem prudentiae & virtutis illam apud gentem induisset. Adhaec Norcarmij acta non aliunde quam ab illius disciplinae professione petita, quae licentiam fraudi faceret crederetque posse Principes augendae dominationi obligatos utilia honestis anteferre. Denique Escovedi ingenium doli prudens nihil aliud principi suo suasisse, quam ut provinciarum vires secessionibus debilitaret, potentiamque Ordinum concordiâ validam mutuâ dissensione attereret. Igitur se Deum rogare ut sanam & introspiciendis Hispanorum artibus sagacem mentem ijs donet, quo perviderent quantum inter illorum consilia & curas libertatis interfit & quam expediat in commune consuli, quod divisum, fragile & infirmum factura discessio esset. Se quidem Legatos Coloniam petente Caesare missuros, hortarique ut idem faciant, si forte diu desideratae pacis felicitatem divina benignitas promittat.
units.tr: But fortune, as usual, which is apt to sow discord, had upset the plans of the powerful. Therefore the defectors concluded a covenant on 6 April. In it it was provided that the Roman Catholic religion should be kept, that obedience should be rendered to the king and his governor, and that the Spaniards and foreigners should leave Belgium according to the terms of the Ghent covenant; and that if the king did not ratify this, it would be free to withdraw from the covenant. When this was written at Mount Saint Eligius, not far from Regiacum in Artois, and was communicated to the Estates of the provinces, though they pretended otherwise, it made their minds, inclined to peace, feel as if the announcement of a most sorrowful event had reached them. So they replied that they approved of the zeal of those men in maintaining the religion of their ancestors and in rendering obedience to the king; but they wished this: that they should not trust too much to the specious deceptions of the Spaniards, and that, being cautious and prudent, they should weigh the examples of earlier times as though they were recent. For the treachery of Ferdinand Alva, the most savage of dukes, was notorious, and Jerónimo de Roda, a master of that art, had concealed his intent; this art, once branded with the name of perjury, had put on among that people the appearance of prudence and virtue. Besides, the acts of Noircarmes were drawn from nothing but the profession of that discipline, which made licence a tool of fraud, and which believed that princes, bound to extend their dominion, could prefer useful things to honourable ones. Finally, the cunning mind of Escobedo had advised his prince to nothing else than to weaken the strength of the provinces by secessions, and to grind down the power of the Estates, strong through their concord, by mutual dissension. Therefore they prayed God to give them a sound mind, one sharp enough to see through the arts of the Spaniards, so that they might perceive how great is the difference between the counsels and cares of those men and the cause of liberty, and how expedient it is to consult in common, since a division would make a thing divided, fragile and weak. They themselves would send envoys, since the Emperor was seeking them at Cologne, and they urged the others to do the same, if perhaps the divine goodness should promise the happiness of a peace long desired.

units.la: Thuanus scribit, Ordines generales nummum aeneum Egmondani Hornijque recisa truncis orae vultusque exprimentem refricanda veterum memoriae tum cudisse, tutiusque bellum simulata pace honestâ & ad continuanda arma efficaci inscriptione suasisse. Quod isti fini factum prudentiores quique interpretabantur, quo antiquae crudelitatis & perfidiae exempla in memoriam revocando praesentis aevi ingenia à superstitioso regiae fidei cultu atque veneratione deterrerent. Indignatura haud dubie, si expenderint, Belgici sanguinis Principes & regi ex societatis Burgundicae jure fidissimos in exorabili regis saevitiâ formidata hostibus & tot vulnerum notis interstincta corpora detestandis carnificum ministerijs prostravisse. Econtra Farnesius alimenta provinciarum dissensionibus subministrabat, regisque Philippi animum pacis cupidissimum ostentans, quo eas foederibus exsolvendo regis obsequio ligaret, civilibus morbis, velut optuma discordantis Belgicae remedia, tristem & non profuturam medicinam praescripsit. Ista erat ut solius Catholicae Romanae religionis exercitia essent, indictoque reformatae repudio aut silentio, Philippi imperia paternis assimularentur. Quippe ea provincialium juramento & ejus religione firmata, tum divinis humanisque legibus subnixa subverti non posse, certissima solidae pacis fundamenta, quae substerni lubricis rebus & ruinam minantibus nulla cunctatione deberent. Ordinum esse de statu & voluntate provinciarum ocyus referre, quo rex agat, quod é re sua videatur. Atqui Ordines sua in regem & pacem studia laudabili responso repetebant: Sic Augusto mense elapso, advocatis Caesaris, Galliae & Angliae regnorum legatis cum Joanne Austriaco colloquia inisse, in medio cursu rerum Philippi interventu subversa. Tum Philippum coeptam cum Austriaco actionem
units.tr: Thuanus writes that the States General struck a bronze coin bearing the portraits of Egmont and Horn, their heads severed from their trunks, to refresh the memory of the old wrongs; and that by this inscription, under the pretence of honourable peace, they urged war more safely and to keep up the arms. Those who were more prudent interpreted this as done for this end: by recalling examples of past cruelty and treachery, they would turn the minds of the present age away from the superstitious cult and veneration of the royal faith. Undoubtedly, if they weighed the matter, the princes of Belgian blood, who were most loyal to the king by the law of the Burgundian alliance, would be indignant that their bodies, feared by enemies and marked with so many wounds, had been struck down by the king's implacable savagery and by the abhorrent work of executioners. On the other side, Farnesius was feeding the provinces' dissensions. Professing the king Philip's great desire for peace, he prescribed, as a sad and useless medicine for the diseases of a divided Belgium, civil strife, by which he might bind the provinces, once their treaties were dissolved, to the king's obedience. The plan was that only the exercises of the Roman Catholic religion should exist, the reformed religion being forbidden or passed over in silence, so that Philip's rule would resemble that of his father. Indeed, the provinces held that these arrangements, confirmed by the provincials' oath and their religion, and supported by divine and human laws, could not be overturned; they were the surest foundations of a lasting peace, which ought to be laid without any delay on slippery affairs threatening ruin. It was for the Estates to report quickly on the condition and will of the provinces, so that the king might act as seemed to his advantage. The Estates, however, answered in a praiseworthy reply, repeating their zeal for the king and for peace. Thus, last August, after calling in the envoys of the Emperor and of the kingdoms of France and England, they had entered into talks with John of Austria, but in the middle of the business the affair had been overturned by Philip's intervention. Then Philip reported the begun action with Austria to the Emperor

units.la: {a} Farnesius alimenta dissensionibus Belgarum substernit. nem Cæsari detulisse, quanquam augustum imperatoris judicium ipsi Ordines non defugerent Suartsenburgio Cæsaris Legato ad Farnesium non semel misso, quo de regis sui mente testaretur. Sed dilationibus, aut sinistris artibus usum Farnesium pacis actionem traxisse, cui inanem affectum, ut & rex Philippus, præferret. Quippe Philippum repudiatâ & ruptâ Gandavensi conventione, cujus servandæ desiderio provinciæ tum tenebantur, alienatis interea animis offerre, & quidem ita, ut conditionum iniquitas vim atque efficaciam istius fœderis tollat. Neque enim Caroli Cæsaris imperium neque memoriam gratam esse apud eos præsertim, qui edicta fœdissimi rigoris sub illius dominatione promulgata non ignorarent. Sed dolosis consilijs serenæ pacis actionem involvi, cui submittere modo sincera sit, se Ordines parati etiamnum essent, sed ita ut Cæsaris Legato potestas fiat ocyus aliquid agendi statuendique quod ex usu futurum sit.
units.tr: {a} Farnesius feeds the dissensions of the Belgians. Although the Estates did not refuse the Emperor's august judgment, they had more than once sent Suartsenburg, the Emperor's envoy, to Farnesius, to make known the mind of their king. But Farnesius, by delays and sinister arts, had dragged out the peace negotiation, showing an empty intention, as King Philip did too. Indeed, Philip, having repudiated and broken the Ghent Pacification, whose observance the provinces were then bound to keep, was meanwhile alienating minds and offering terms of such iniquity that they would destroy the force and effect of that treaty. For neither the rule of the Emperor Charles nor his memory was welcome among them, especially among those who were not ignorant of the most shameful edicts of harsh severity issued under his dominion. But the peace negotiation was being involved in deceitful counsels; the Estates were still ready to submit to it, if it were sincere, but on condition that the Emperor's envoy be given the power to act and decide quickly on what would be to the advantage.

units.la: Mox de conventu mittendisque Coloniam legatis consultatum, quo actione pacis maturata induciæ saltem sistendis armis scriberentur ipseque Farnesius, qui ad Trajectum Mosæ castra posuerat, agris vicisq; depopulatis, sociæ civitatis obsidio decederet. Unde Ordinum nomine Philippus Crojus Dux Arschotanus, Joannes Lindanus D. Geertrudis, Fredericus Hyperius Marolius abbas, Concilij Status Senator, Buccho Ayta D. Bavonis Præpositus, Caspar Schetus, Adolphus Metkerckius Equites & Consiliarij Ordinum. Adrianus Mylius LL. Doctor & in Curiâ Hollandiæ Senator, Bernardus Baro Merodius, Adolphus Goeranus, & Aggæus Albada Delegati, profectioneque vergente Aprili institutâ ad iv. Non. Maï. Coloniam advenere: Ubi Rudolphus Cæsar, pacis auspex, festinando negotio legatos suos præmiserat. In ijs Jacobus Trevirensium, Gebhardus Coloniensium Præsules, Romani imperij Electores, Julius Wirceburgensium Episcopus, Warnerus Gymnichus pro Juliacensium & Clivæ Duce, ac Otto Henricus Suartsenburgius fuere, Joanne Baptista Castaneta Rossanensium Præsule à Gregorio xiii. ejus nominis Pontifice Romano Coloniam præmisso. Philippo vero Regi Carolus Arragonius Castrenantius pro Legato erat, qui post Maximilianum Longevallium, Joannem Fonckium, Christophorum Assonvilium & Urbanum Scouwenburgium ab epistolis in consilium adscitos, regiæ Philippi majestatis secreta mandata attulerat. Igitur conventu instituto, salutatisque Imperij & Cæsaris legatis, & de actorum suorum formulâ utrinque edoctis, Matthiæ & Ordinum cæterique mandatarijs Aggæum Albadam juris-consultissimum, Senatorio patre apud Frisios editum, in Germaniâ tum agentem interpretandis actis sententijsque delegere, & qui eruditæ vocis, qua pollebat, facundia titulo Oratoris in relationibus procerum præesset.
units.tr: Soon afterwards they discussed a conference and the sending of envoys to Cologne, so that, with the peace business hastened, a truce would at least be drawn up to halt the arms, and Farnesius himself, who had pitched his camp at Maastricht on the Meuse, would withdraw from the siege of the allied city after the fields and villages had been laid waste. Accordingly, on behalf of the Estates were chosen Philip Croy, Duke of Arschot; John Linden, lord of Sainte-Gertrude; Frederick Hyperius Marolius, abbot and senator of the Council of State; Buccho Ayta, provost of St Bavo; Caspar Schetus and Adolphus Metkerck, knights and councillors of the Estates; Adrian Mylius, Doctor of Laws and senator in the Court of Holland; and Bernard Baron Merode, Adolphus Goeranus and Aggaeus Albada as delegates. Setting out towards the end of April, they arrived at Cologne on 28 April. There Rudolf the Emperor, the herald of peace, had sent his envoys ahead to hasten the business. Among them were James, archbishop of Trier, and Gebhard, archbishop of Cologne, electors of the Roman Empire; Julius, bishop of Würzburg; Warner Gymnich, for the Duke of Jülich and Cleves; and Otto Henry Suartsenburg. John Baptist Castaneta, bishop of Rossano, had been sent ahead to Cologne by Pope Gregory XIII. For King Philip, Charles of Aragon, Lord of Chastenaye, served as envoy; after Maximilian Longueval, John Fonck, Christopher Assonville and Urban Schouwenburg, who had been taken into the council as secretaries, he had brought the secret instructions of His Royal Majesty Philip. Therefore, when the conference was set up, the envoys of the Empire and of the Emperor were greeted, and each side had been informed of the form of the other's proceedings, Matthias and the Estates and the other envoys chose Aggaeus Albada, a most learned jurist, born to a senatorial father among the Frisians, who was then active in Germany, to interpret the acts and opinions, and to preside over the reports of the nobles with the eloquence of learned speech in which he excelled, with the title of orator.

units.la: Albada scribit se Frisiorum nomine & benevolentiâ, Legatis etiam ad tractandam pacem dictis adjectum fuisse, honestàque tenuitatis suæ excusatione Dei gloriam, reip. utilitatem suis in actionibus Deputatis Ordinum commendasse. Et quamquam eas ipsas in gravissimis negotijs fœlices & secundas Deus voluisset, ita id prosperi in hac actione in his Belgicæ miserijs polliceri sibi non posse, quod eas expiandæ criminum moli providentiæ æquitasBelgicis terris intulisset. Se autem sperare divinæ cleclementiæ remedium quæ sola reddendæ paci par atque auxiliaris esse possit. Se interim etsi otio ac quieti dare brevissimum ævi maluisset, non defuturum interim officio, daturumque operam, ut de singulis, quæ Frisiam spectarent suis ex litteris cognoscant. Litteræ iv. Maii datæ.
units.tr: Albada writes that he had been added to the envoys appointed to negotiate peace on behalf and by the goodwill of the Frisians, and that, with the honourable excuse of his humble station, he had commended to the deputies of the Estates in their actions the glory of God and the good of the commonwealth. And although God had willed that these very things be happy and successful in most serious affairs, he could not promise himself such prosperity in this business, in these miseries of Belgium, because the providence and justice of God had brought these very things upon the Belgian lands to atone for the mass of their crimes. He himself, however, hoped for the remedy of divine clemency, which alone could be equal and helpful in restoring peace. Meanwhile, although he would have preferred to give the very brief span of his life to leisure and quiet, he would not fail in his duty in the meantime, and would take care that his friends learn from his letters about each matter that concerns Friesland. Letters dated 4 May.

units.la: Quæ omnia quanquam conciliandis animis, actisque instituta viderentur, Philippo Croio Arschotano legationis principe pro sanciendâ pace verba faciente, ita suspectam paci fidem faciebat, quod Castrenantius Philippi legatus armistitium aut inducias detrectaret, ipseque Farnesius regij ad Trajectum exercitus imperator à bene coepta obsidione, & felicibus militiæ rudimentis abstinere gravaretur. Cui diffidentiæ malo & hoc accedebat, quod fama aut suspicio icti xvi. Kal. Iun. inter Farnesium & Artesios fœderis coloniam emanaret, Gulielmusque Aurantius datis ad Arschotanum litteris, consilia Farnesij ciendis civitatum provinciarumque defectionibus valida non dissimulato indicio detexisset. Itaque quam maximè legatos Ordinum offendebat, quod Farnesius etsi jure mandati destitutus pacis quoque negotio se interponeret, Regisque legato Castrenantio Philippi mandatis alligato veniam aut licentiam trahendæ actionis & negandi armistitij fecisset. Econtra Castrenantio Philippi mandatorio displicebat, quod in Matthiæ Ordinumque mandatis Joannis Austriaci, etsi fato functi, tum ipsius quoque Regis ingenium paci adversum traduceretur, eademque mandata omni comperendinatione amotâ sex septimanarum breve & finiendæ actioni incommodum tempus præfinirent. Præter hoc indignabatur Castrenantius Farnesium amplissimâ gerendarum per Philippi ditiones rerum potestate instructum male usurpatæ autoritatis insimulari criminantibus Ordinum legatis, reliquaque Belgicæ provincias cum Farnesio fœdus non depactas, tacitæ in Philippum rebellionis & occulti criminis redargui. Quæ singula ut animos confidentium procerum, ita negotium pacis distrahebant. Ad quam quoque perveniri non posse illi ominabantur, qui exemplis temporum eruditi præstrui inducias redimendo bello & permulcendæ animorum immodestiæ volebant. Reperio in actis provinciæ Legatis Coloniam ituris, præter mandata quæ scriptores evulgavere, Matthiam Gubernatorem & Ordines cavisse, ut nisi conventui intra condictum tempus finem rex imponeret, jure principis excidere, populoque Belgico libero & ab externi imperij cultu soluto ad quorumvis Principum fœdera atque societates aditus pateret. Quæ duriora & haud dubiè ab animo regiæ iniquitatis conscio profecta pacis tamen actioni non serviebant.
units.tr: Although all these things seemed to be arranged to win minds and to advance the business, the word of Philip Croy, Duke of Arschot, leader of the embassy, speaking for the sanctioning of peace, was made suspect by this: the envoy of Philip, Castrenantius, rejected an armistice or truce; and Farnesius himself, the commander of the royal army at Maastricht, was reluctant to abstain from the well-begun siege and the favourable first fruits of war. To this evil of distrust was added the rumour or suspicion that a league had been made, on 16 May, between Farnesius and the Artois, and William of Orange, having sent letters to Arschot, had revealed without concealment, with solid evidence, Farnesius's plans to stir up the defections of cities and provinces. Thus the envoys of the Estates were chiefly offended that Farnesius, though lacking the authority of a mandate, interposed himself in the peace business as well, and had obtained from the king's envoy Castrenantius, bound by Philip's instructions, permission or licence to prolong the negotiation and to refuse the armistice. On the other side, Castrenantius, bound by Philip's mandate, was displeased that in the mandates of Matthias and the Estates the disposition of John of Austria, though dead, and of the king himself, was represented as hostile to peace; and that the same mandates, with every delay removed, fixed a brief time of six weeks, inconvenient for finishing the business. Besides this, Castrenantius was indignant that Farnesius, endowed with the fullest power to carry out the king's affairs in his dominions, was accused by the envoys of the Estates of misusing his authority, and that the remaining Belgian provinces, which had not made a treaty with Farnesius, were charged with a tacit rebellion against Philip and a hidden crime. These points, as they divided the minds of the leading men, so they divided the business of peace. Those who, taught by the examples of their times, wished for a truce to buy off war and to soothe the immoderate passions of minds, predicted that peace could not be reached either. I find in the records of the province that the envoys about to go to Cologne, besides the mandates which the writers have published, had provided, Matthias the Governor and the Estates, that unless the king set an end to the conference within the agreed time, the prince would forfeit his right, and that for the free Belgian people, released from the rule of a foreign empire, access would be open to the alliances and leagues of whatever princes. These harsher terms, undoubtedly issued by a mind conscious of royal injustice, did not serve the peace negotiation.

units.la: Hæc etiam volebant.
units.tr: They also wanted these things.

units.la: I. Ut omnium anteactorum venia esset, Rexque Philippus sacta Matthiae & Ordinum ratihabendo, æquo cum Brabantiâ jure reliquas provincias haberet. II. Ut Hispani, Itali, Burgundiones, Germani, Galli, Angli, Scoti in Belgio militantes intra sex Septimanas proxumas provincijs excederent, Farnesiusque oppida à tempore occupata Namurcorum civitatis, cum omni commeatu bellico restituat, eaque præsidio ex inquilinis & Ordinum partes secutis de consensu Ordinum firmet. III. Ut ydem inquilini, præter juramentum regi dicendum, patriæ quoquoque & provincijs fidem praestarent, conventioneque Coloniensi comprehenfis morem gerant. iv. Vt captivi nullo ære aut lytro, nisi qui id depacti sunt, dimitterentur, Comesque Buranus contra privilegia & universitatis & Brabantiæ Albano regnante Lovanio abductus, in Belgium revocaretur. v. Vt singulis in sua per provincias etiam per Burgundiam, Luxemburgum, Hollandiam, atque Zelandiam bona restituerentur, provincialibusque utrinq; in Belgium redire, regi & patriæ fide datâ jus esset. vi. Vt Gandavensis conventio rata firmaque haberetur, statusq; religionis tam reformatæ quam Augustanæ confessionis, prout esset, ita per provincias foret. vii. Vt Matthiae Archiduci Præfectura Belgij continuaretur, ejusq; morte aut excessu rex Philippus non nisi sui sanguinis Principem & in Belgio constitueret, & qui in acta Matthiæ Gubernatoris juraret. viii. Vt Præfecti provinciarum, oppidorum, arcium, cohortium, ÿ quoque qui in concilium Status aut rationum cooptantur, inquilini forent, ÿque in acta fœderis, jura & immunitates Belgicarum provinciarum jurando, contra facientes sub pœnâ perjurij deferrent. ix. Vt Rex Ordinibus pecuniam in bellum per eos erogatam decies centena aureorum coronatorum millia restitueret, Ordinumque syngraphas ex causâ defectionis Austriacae & violato sacramento liberet. x. Vt Angliæ regina & Andium Dux loc ipso fœdere comprehenderentur, istiique confirmando, ratihabitio Pontificis Romani, Cæsaris, Christianissimi Galliarum regis, Elisabethæ Anglicæ, Principum & Electorum Imperij, Ducisq; Juliacensium peteretur. xi. Vt Fœdus ipsum publicâ juris-jurandi religione firmatum intra Bimestre aut citius Philippus rex signaret.
units.tr: I. That there be a pardon for all past acts, and that King Philip, by ratifying the deeds of Matthias and the Estates, hold the remaining provinces on the same terms as Brabant. II. That the Spaniards, Italians, Burgundians, Germans, French, English and Scots serving in Belgium leave the provinces within the next six weeks, and that Farnesius restore the towns occupied since the time of the Namur citizens' seizure, with all military supplies, and secure them with a garrison of residents and of those who followed the Estates' side, by the consent of the Estates. III. That the same residents, besides the oath to be sworn to the king, also pledge their faith to the fatherland and the provinces, and obey what is comprehended in the Cologne agreement. IV. That prisoners be released without any ransom or payment, unless they were bound by agreement; and that Count Buren, carried off to Louvain under Alva's rule, against the privileges of the university and of Brabant, be returned to Belgium. V. That everyone be restored to his goods in each province, and also in Burgundy, Luxembourg, Holland and Zeeland, and that provincials be allowed to return to Belgium on both sides, with faith given to the king and the fatherland. VI. That the Pacification of Ghent be held ratified and firm, and that the state of religion, both reformed and Augsburg Confession, be as it is in each province. VII. That the governorship of Belgium be continued for Archduke Matthias, and that, on his death or departure, King Philip appoint in Belgium none but a prince of his own blood, who shall swear to the acts of Governor Matthias. VIII. That the governors of provinces, towns, citadels and cohorts, and also those who are co-opted into the Council of State or the accounts, be residents, and that they swear to the acts of the treaty, the rights and immunities of the Belgian provinces, and denounce those acting against them under penalty of perjury. IX. That the king repay to the Estates the money spent by them on the war, ten hundred thousand gold crowns, and release the Estates' bonds, on account of the defection from Austria and the violated oath. X. That the Queen of England and the Duke of Anjou be included in this same treaty, and that for its confirmation the ratification of the Roman Pontiff, the Emperor, the Most Christian King of France, Elizabeth of England, the princes and electors of the Empire, and the Duke of Jülich be sought. XI. That the treaty itself, confirmed by the public sanction of an oath, be signed by King Philip within two months, or sooner.

units.la: Quæ xvi. Kal. Iun. perscripta, & à Trevirensi Cancellario legatorum Cæsaris Oratore exagitata præfractæ atque asperæ iniquitatis insimulabantur.
units.tr: These terms, drawn up on 17 May, were attacked by the Chancellor of Trier, the envoy of the imperial legates, who charged them with being headstrong, harsh and unjust.

units.la: Itaque scripto Legatis Imperij xxi. Maii. exhibito hunc in modum differebant.
units.tr: Accordingly, on 21 May, a written statement was presented to the imperial legates, which argued as follows.

units.la: VT multis postulatis & jus causæ nostræ & vos arbitros gravaremus; animus nunquam fuit. Ita enim censemus non longe quærendam esse diuturm & infelicis belli causam, quam aut è religione aut ex autoritate Regis enata dissensio dedit. Ac divino cultui tam regem quam populum adstringi scimus, neque humanæ potestatis aut legis aut commodi esse, eam vi aut armis imperare. Itaque Gandavenfi & post Bruxellensi conventione religionis Edicta suspensa aut rescissa mansere, tacitâ interpretatione, ut quisque ex præscripto conscientiæ Deum coleret. Nam id deprehendimus, Legati, animos cogi non posse vitio mortalis ingenij tristi imperio contumaces. Ita fit, ut ipsa quoque religio, interceptis fidei incrementis, damnum sentiat rerumque exitus probent nihil profici per eos qui regis nomine ac celsissimo imperio abusi suis magis affectibus quam voluntati regiæ indulgent. Quos frenare, quanquam consilium nobis fuerit, rege ipso Hispaniæ suâ clauso & qui salutari sine manifesto discrimine adeuntium non posset, aut velit, ita saepenumero remedia nostris morbis invenimus, ceterum à regis medicinâ & ingenio aliena. Tantum autem abest, ut aut impius miles aut districtus ensis donum fidei adferat, quod à cælesti Spiritu profectum, premi violentiâ aut servitute non potest. Itaque petimus, ut Religionis libertata atque pace à nobis præscriptâ & multi gentibus terrarum usurpata frui sinatis, quæ & Dro consiliare populum & simul regi posset. Quod vero ad autoritatem Regis attinet, tam ex conventionum jure, ex patrum formula deferimus à nullo consilio minus, quam à reverentia regis alieni. Atque ijs terminis Regis autoritatem, nostrum obsequium atque sacramentum circumscribi postulamus parati ad ista quoque animos & consilia formare, quæ vobis imperatoriæ majestatis Legatis & juxta nobis æqua aut honesta videbuntur.
units.tr: "Although we have burdened you, the arbiters, with many demands, and with the right of our cause, it was never our intention. For we judge that the cause of this long and unhappy war is not to be sought far off: it was given by the dissension arising from religion or from the authority of the King. We know that both king and people are bound to divine worship, and that it is neither in the interest of human power, law or advantage to enforce it by force or arms. Thus, by the Ghent and afterwards the Brussels agreement, the edicts on religion remained suspended or rescinded, by tacit interpretation, so that each might worship God according to the rule of conscience. For we have found, legates, that minds cannot be compelled, being by the fault of mortal nature obstinate against a harsh rule. So it happens that religion itself, with the growth of faith cut off, suffers loss, and the outcome of events proves that nothing is achieved through those who, abusing the name of the king and his most high power, indulge their own passions rather than the king's will. We intended to restrain these men, though the king of Spain himself was shut away and could not, or would not, approach them without manifest danger. So we have often found remedies for our ills, but remedies alien to the king's medicine and disposition. So far is it from being the case that either an impious soldier or a drawn sword brings the gift of faith, which, proceeding from the heavenly Spirit, cannot be pressed down by violence or servitude. Therefore we ask that you allow us to enjoy the liberty of religion and the peace prescribed by us and used by many nations of the earth, which could both counsel the people and at the same time serve the king. As for the authority of the King, we defer to it, by the law of agreements and the formula of the fathers, from no counsel less than from reverence for the king, who is not alien to us. And we ask that the King's authority, our obedience and our oath be circumscribed by these limits, and we are prepared to shape our minds and plans also to those things which seem fair or honourable to you, the legates of the imperial majesty, and to us."

units.la: Itaque ista nec Cæsari, aut Regi, nec Castrenantio approbare se posse obtestabatur, quod ea mandatorum suorum & futuræ pacis ratio esset, ut superstrui antiquis fœderum conventionibus deberet. In quibus quoque si quid ruptum infirmatumque licentia temporum aut error fecisset, id emendare sui officij esse, quo inter Regem subditosque dissociatæ res ex priorum actorum fide atque efficacia coalescant. Quod ad reliqua postulata attinerent, ea tanquam duriora & paci adversa emollienda se censere, cui sanciundæ hoc imprimis expediret, ut acta Gandavensis & Bruxellensis fœderum rata per Ordines haberentur, quo Philippi legatum asperitate conditionum offensum paciscendas ad inducias commoveant.
units.tr: He protested that they could approve neither these terms nor the Emperor's, the King's or Champagny's, because these were the basis of his commands and of the future peace, which ought to be built upon the old covenants. If anything in those covenants had been broken or weakened by the license of the times or by error, it was his duty to amend it, so that matters divided between King and subjects might cohere again through the good faith and effectiveness of the earlier acts. As for the remaining demands, they thought them harder and adverse to peace, and to be softened. For ratifying a peace, it was especially expedient that the acts of the Ghent and Brussels covenants be held valid by the Estates, so that they might move Philip's legate, offended by the harshness of the conditions, to negotiate a truce.

units.la: Itaque conditiones in spem obtinendi armistitij & liberandæ Trajectensium ad Mosam civitatis nonnihil lenitæ, addito ut à parte Ordinum Gandavense fœdus & Bruxellensis unio valerent, Comesij; Buranus ex Hispaniâ dimissus intra trimestre spatium Antverpiæ sisteretur.
units.tr: So the conditions were somewhat softened, in hope of obtaining an armistice and freeing the city of Utrecht on the Maas. It was added that, on the part of the Estates, the Ghent covenant and the Brussels union should stand, and that the counts, with Buren released from Spain, should be presented at Antwerp within three months.

units.la: Mox colloquium examinandis conditionibus institutum, quo Ordines actorum nomine, quæ rata caverant, convocationes Ordinum, fœdera & societates demoliendarum arcium aut tributorum decreta, tum edicta regio titulo vulgata, denique collationes beneficiorum dignitatumque tanquam justas atque legitimas comprehendi interpretabantur. Neque privilegia alia intelligi, quam quæ singulis provincijs indulta fuissent, neque aliam religionem, quam Gandavense fœdus haberet, aut quas admitti ex decreto Ordinum, pacis publicæ & Philippi regis interesset. Post Matthiæ Archiducis diploma Cæsaris Legatis exhibitum, maturandis rebus quæ legatorum tarditate expugnando Trajecto, & Alexandri Farnesij belli imperium capessentis gloriæ ac famæ trahebantur. Igitur socia Trajectensium civitate in ultimo discrimine constitutâ, quam Melchior Suartsenbergius vir nobilis & militiæ impiger cum imperio & simul præsidio tenebat, Farnesio insuper divellendis clam provincijs occupato, de signando Ultrajectino fœdere cogitatum, quod arrecta ad Colonienses fœdus multorum spes studio certæ pacis distulerat.
units.tr: Soon a colloquy was set up to examine the conditions. The Estates, in the name of the acts, interpreted as just and lawful whatever they had secured as valid: the summoning of the Estates, leagues and associations, decrees for demolishing citadels or imposing taxes, edicts published under the royal title, and finally grants of benefices and dignities. Nor were privileges to be understood as anything other than those granted to individual provinces, nor any religion other than that which the Ghent covenant held, or which the decree of the Estates admitted, as far as public peace and King Philip's interest required. After the diploma of Archduke Matthias had been presented to the imperial legates, matters were to be hastened, since the legates' delay was turning them to the glory and fame of storming Utrecht and of Alexander Farnese, who had taken up the command of the war. So, with the allied city of Utrecht placed in the greatest danger, which Melchior Suartsenberg, a noble and war-active man, held with command and garrison at once, and with Farnese secretly occupying the provinces to be torn apart, it was considered to sign the Utrecht covenant. The hopes of many, raised towards the Cologne covenant, had delayed this for the sake of a sure peace.

units.la: Postquam verò & isti diffisum est, Farnesioque ipso belli magis quam pacis incentore, Gulielmus Aurantius Antverpiam reversus, Ultrajectino fœderi subscripsit illudque ipsum, velut Belgicarum provinciarum incolumitati repertum, neque Matthiæ Gubernatoris autoritati adversum, secretis quoque ab eodem provincijs commendavit. Erant namque, qui Matthiam Archiducem ex formulâ Gandavensis pacis receptum lædi novo ex fœdere clamitarent, serendisque malis in populum rumoribus sagaces, suo ex ingenio cæteris quoque malitiem affingerent. Inde serius signatum fœdus ab Aurantio interpretabantur, etsi essent in prudentioribus, qui non ignorarent omne novi fœderis consilium ab eo præfectum esse, eumque secessione sociali impulsum & simul irritatum, ad Ultrajectini fœderis sanctionem, tanquam publicæ infirmitatis remedium, confugisse. Itaque de Belgicis Frisiorum-que trans Rhenum provinciis, quas Sequanæ fontes & Amisij amnis ostia terminabant, firma pace conciliandis desperatio tum incesit, creditumque fuit, parte nationum Philippi artibus & secretis inlicijs avulsâ, solam spem incolumitatis Ultrajectino in foedere relictam. Quippe discretis provincijs & ærarium contabuerat & exercituum fides solvebatur, qui in omnem insolentiam vitio quietis & ignaviæ proni, magis imperia Farnesij novi & egregij Ducis, quam dissidentium Ordinum sequebantur.
units.tr: But when this too was distrusted, and Farnese himself was more an instigator of war than of peace, William of Orange returned to Antwerp, subscribed to the Utrecht covenant, and commended it to the provinces, secretly as well, as a discovery for the safety of the Belgic provinces, not opposed to the authority of Governor Matthias. For there were those who cried out that Archduke Matthias, received according to the form of the Ghent peace, was injured by the new covenant; and, being sharp at sowing evils among the people, they attributed malice to others from their own nature. Hence they interpreted the covenant as signed later by Orange. Yet some of the more prudent, who did not ignore that every plan of the new covenant had been devised by him, and that he had been driven and at the same time provoked by the secession of the allies, had fled to the sanctioning of the Utrecht covenant as a remedy for public weakness. Thus despair then arose of concluding a firm peace concerning the Belgic provinces and the Frisian provinces beyond the Rhine, which were bounded by the sources of the Seine and the mouth of the Ems. It was believed that, with part of the nations drawn away by Philip's arts and secret enticements, the only hope of safety was left in the Utrecht covenant. Indeed, with the provinces divided, the treasury had wasted away and the fidelity of the armies was dissolving. These, prone to every insolence through the vice of idleness and quiet, followed the commands of Farnese, a new and excellent leader, more than those of the dissenting Estates.

units.la: Reperio in actis Hesselum Aysma provinciæ Legatum Antverpiæ hærentem de 12000. millibus Carolaeorum Frisiorum nomine communi ærario inferendis acerbe conventum, arrestoque mox pressum, pro liberandâ legati fide, ut indemnem præstarent, acribus litteris suos provinciales sollicitasse.
units.tr: I find in the records that Hessel Aysma, legate of the province, staying at Antwerp, was harshly summoned concerning 12,000 thousand Carolus guilders of Frisian money to be paid into the common treasury. Soon he was arrested and pressed, and, to secure his release and guarantee his indemnity, he urged his provincials sharply by letter.

units.la: Quare firmando per Frisiam Ultrajectino foederi, reparandisque provinciæ, quas odia partium attriverant, rebus Senatus juris dicundi suprema potestate tum valens petente Lalainio comitium Leovardiæ ad xiii. Kal. Jun. indixit, crudisque & in diversa scissis provincialium animis in vii. Kal. proferri fecit. Tanta cum difficultate approbandi Ultrajectini foederis mandata impetrabantur, quæ traditione majorum interveniente populi suffragio firmata, vim comitij exequebantur. Neque enim foedera inire aut rescindere, tributum ordinare, bellum aut pacem facere, præterquam populi tum erat, qui mandatarios creando jus nihilominus suffragij & supremæ majestatis retinebat. Inde relationes ad populum dubijs in rebus introductæ, quas certamina dominationis & profusâ boni moris libertate succrescens licentia præclaris cum moribus secutis temporibus abolevere. Quare componendis per Frisiam dissensionibus, urgente Lalainio, qui ab exitu Martij mensis animum foederi magis addictum ostenderat, die condicto comitium Leovardiæ instítutum, in quo Lalainij litteræ Winsumo è Translavicanis iii. Kal. Junij datæ, plenius de ejus voluntate & in foedus propensione discordem populum docebant.
units.tr: Therefore, to confirm the Utrecht covenant throughout Friesland and to repair the province, which hatred of the parties had worn down, the Senate, then powerful with the supreme authority of judicial power, at Lalaing's request appointed an assembly at Leeuwarden for 20 May. It was put off to 26 May, because the minds of the people were raw and split into different parties. Mandates for approving the Utrecht covenant were obtained with such difficulty that, by the handing down of tradition and the intervention of the people's vote, they were confirmed and carried out the power of the assembly. For to enter into or rescind covenants, to impose taxes, to make war or peace, was then within the power of no one but the people, who, by appointing deputies, nonetheless retained the right of vote and supreme majesty. Hence reports to the people were introduced in doubtful matters, a custom which, as struggles for dominance and a license growing from the lavish liberty of good custom increased, later times abolished along with its fine customs. Therefore, to settle the disputes throughout Friesland, at Lalaing's urging (he had from the end of March shown his mind more inclined to the covenant), an assembly was held at Leeuwarden on the appointed day. In it, Lalaing's letters, dated at Winsum among the Translavicani on 30 May, taught the discordant people more fully about his will and his inclination towards the covenant.

units.la: ADVENERE apud vos Ultrajecto provinciarum foederata- rum Legati, quo mandata sua exponant.
units.tr: Legates of the United Provinces have arrived among you at Utrecht to set out their instructions.

units.la: Quæ cum pacì, concordiæ atque saluti vestræ destinata sint, moneo ac hortor, ut ad mandata eorum arrecti ac prudentes decreta formetis. Ne trahendo publica, aut per incuriam negligendo, quod securitatis aut fiduciæ vitium est, eorum auxilijs destituamini, qui contermini nobis & effectum rebus angustiis erga nos professi, adhuc de suâ in vos salutemque vestram propensione abunde testantur. Itaque vestrum erit & veteris in vos studij memoriam evolvere & præsens beneficium amplecti, de cujus fructu, plenius vos docturi erunt. Quo facto mihi dubium non est, quin animis atque consilijs vestris insinuatura se sit sollicita vetustatis cura, quæ concordia res parvas crescere, magnas ac prosperas dissensione dilabi monuisset. Quare concordiam unicum rerum vinculum & robur vobis commendo & ut ante oculos patriam, conjuges, liberos habeatis. Quibus quam maximè prospicietis, si quod absens & gerendis pro patriâ vestrâ rebus intentus peto, ne quæ mora aut lis decretis vestris interveniat.
units.tr: Since these instructions are aimed at your peace, concord and well-being, I advise and urge you to consider their instructions attentively and to frame wise decrees. Do not delay public business, nor neglect it through carelessness, which is a fault of over-confidence or complacency, and so be left without the help of those who are your neighbours, who have professed by deeds their goodwill towards us in our difficulties, and who still bear abundant witness to their inclination towards you and your safety. It will therefore be your task both to recall their past zeal for you and to embrace the present kindness, the fruit of which the envoys will explain to you more fully. Once this is done, I have no doubt that the anxious care of antiquity will steal into your minds and counsels, teaching that concord makes small things grow, while great and prosperous things collapse through discord. I therefore commend concord to you as the one bond and strength of affairs, and bid you keep before your eyes your country, your wives and your children. You will provide for these most of all if, as I ask while absent and occupied with business for your country, no delay or dispute stands in the way of your decrees.

units.la: Creditum fuit Georgium Lalainiu Gulielmi Aurantij, cui multum tribuebat, consilijs & post exemplo evictum minuendis in quas inciderat, suspicionibus aut studium promovendo foederi praetulisse.
units.tr: It was believed that Georges de Lalaing, who had been much relied upon by William of Orange in counsels, and who was later overcome by the suspicions into which he had fallen, had preferred to promote the cause of the league.

units.la: Itaque à bimestri spatio evoluto sociandae foederi Groningae in Transllavicanos profectus, ubi odia & partes regiae tum maxime gliscebant, Visfleti ad Lavicam comitium gentis indixerat, Groninganisque per litteras adesse iussis de foedere Ultrajectino proposuerat. Qui illegitimo coetu ac loco se convocari regerentes contumaciam veterem ex nuperâ dissensione profitebantur, Aurantijque compositionem, etsi in speciem approbatam, acrioribus in Omlandos odijs obtegebant. Adeo peculiare hominibus est injuriae minus quam beneficij oblivisci, partiumq; inimicitias publicis officijs obruere. Itaque petierant, ut Lalainius urbem habendis comitijs longâ temporum aetate destinatam, justo cum comitatu intraret sponsioneque publicae pacis securitatisque acceptâ comitio interesset. Sed Lalainius, urbi partium validae & quod nullo aut minimo praesidio tenderetur, diffisus, binas peditum collortes Frisiâ evocavit, quas Bartholdus Entenius vir bello acer, veteri in urbem odio & nuperi carceris reminiscentiâ Lopperfemum, Dammonam, Farmsemumque duxit. Quae res Groninganos valde exasperavit agrariaeque nobilitati, velut arma repetenti odium dedit.
units.tr: So, after two months had passed, he set out to join the league at Groningen, in the Translavican district, where hatreds and factions were then at their height. He had called a meeting of the district's people at Visvliet on the Lauwers, and had proposed the Utrecht league to the people of Groningen, who had been ordered to attend by letter. They replied that they were being summoned to an illegitimate assembly and place, and they confessed their old obstinacy arising from the recent dispute. They concealed their approval of the Orange settlement, though it seemed approved, behind sharper hatreds against the men of the Ommelands. So peculiar is it to men to forget an injury less readily than a kindness, and to bury private enmities beneath public duties. They had therefore asked that Lalaing enter the city, which had long been fixed for the assembly, with a proper escort, and that he attend the meeting once a pledge of public peace and safety had been received. But Lalaing, distrusting a city full of partisans of the other side, and because it was held with little or no garrison, summoned two companies of infantry from Friesland. Bartholdus Entenius, a man fierce in war, led them to Loppersum, Dommen and Farmsum, moved by his old hatred of the city and his memory of recent imprisonment. This action greatly exasperated the Groningers and gave the landed nobility a cause for hatred, as if they were taking up arms again.

units.la: Quare Pompeius Ufkenius vir elegantis judicij & qui in partibus libertatis diu fuerat, ad Groninganos ablegatus, honestaque nequicquam excusatione usus, quod de voluntate Regis Ordinumque id fieri affirmaret, civiles & Magistratuum animos, quibus sedandis mittebantur, illo responso irritavit. Quippe addiderat rerum omnium & infoelicijs patriae discrimen id postulare, postquam exploratum esset, omnem per oram foederi insidias struī, clandestinaque hostium consilia praesidio armorum amovenda.
units.tr: Therefore Pompeius Ufkens, a man of refined judgement who had long been on the side of liberty, was sent to the Groningers. Though he used an honourable excuse, saying that this was done by the will of the King and the States, his answer only stirred up the feelings of the citizens and magistrates, whom he had been sent to calm. For he added that the danger to all affairs and to the unhappy fatherland required it, since it was known that plots were being laid against the league throughout the region, and that the secret plans of the enemy had to be removed by the protection of arms.

units.la: Mox Dammonam versus, quam Fivela amnis modico alveo interluit, tres cohortes per Lalainium ductae, impediendis Groningensium commeatibus, qui Delphzylaeo portu, quem Amasus flumen facit, recepti Fivelae navigabili amne Groningam subvehebantur. Ibi agens, parandis militi stipendijs & ne populationibus agros infestaret, colligendo collationum tributo per Omlandiae pagos quaestores constituit, Ordinumque generalium indictiones egestate aeris & ut publicam imperij auctoritatem sanciret, ratas esse jussit. Tum Hovetmannis fidei suspectis juris dicundi potestatem abrogavit, eorumque edicta, praeterquam suâ manu signata, vicinum per agrum recipi vetuit. Decem quoque peditum signa, ductore Entenio in Selverdicum coenobium immitti fecit, populatisque agris & omni suburbano pecore abacto Winsumum communivit. Ipse Eusumanâ in arce validissimâ ordinandis porro rebus desedit, Dammonamque prohibendis Groninganorum eruptionibus vallo fossaque circumduci imperavit. Caeterum cingendae aut oppugnandae urbi impar latissimo moenium ambitu operumque firmitate validae, nihil grande ac magnum gessit, nisi quod Groninganos castra rudia & nulla lege circumscripta infestantes retro ageret, rusticamque praefecturae veteris ad Amasi ripam ac Dullarti sinum procurrentis plebem in sua redire irrogatâ grandi mulctâ compelleret. A cujus fugâ, unâ cohorte praesidio relicta, Groningani erectis vexillis fortis effusi haud procul Selverdico coenobio aciem instruxere, collatisque cum Lalainio signis suo magis metu, quam vi hostium in urbem compulsi sunt. Desiderati ex ijs praeter saucios, haud pauci & duae quoque virgines, quae ad numerum quingentarum custodiendis tormentis destinatae muliebri planctu ac ejulatu res Groninganorum ordinesque turbabant. Igitur de dedenda civitate ab illa levi clade consultatum, missis in castra Lalainij Jacobo Hildebrando, Gulielmo Ubbena, & centurione civico Vinckeburgio, qui aequis conditionibus urbem se tradituros nuntiabant. Quibus impetrandis Regnerus Asselvinius, Loesius Harius, & Regnerus Cantius foederatorum Ordinum Legati opportune intervenere, Groninganique fide data & accepta partibus Ordinum generalium & Matthiae Gubernatoris se permisere. Conditiones hae erant.
units.tr: Soon afterwards three companies, led by Lalaing, marched towards Dommen, which the river Fivel washes with a shallow channel. Their aim was to block the supplies of the Groningers, who, received at the Delfzijl harbour, which the river Ems forms, were being carried up to Groningen by the navigable Fivel. There, busy with providing pay for the soldiers, and so that he would not harass the fields with plundering, he appointed treasurers to collect the tax on contributions through the parishes of the Ommelands, and ordered that the levies of the General States, made necessary by the lack of money and to confirm the public authority of the state, be held valid. Then he took the power of administering justice from the captains whose loyalty was suspect, and forbade their edicts to be received in the neighbouring countryside unless marked with his own hand. He also sent ten companies of infantry under Entenius into the Selwerd convent, and, having plundered the fields and driven off all the cattle of the suburbs, fortified Winsum. He himself settled at Ewsum, in a very strong castle, to order affairs further, and commanded that Dommen be surrounded by a rampart and ditch to prevent sallies by the Groningers. Yet, being unequal to encircling or attacking the city, which had very wide walls and strong works, he accomplished nothing great or important, except that he drove back the Groningers who were harassing him with a rough camp not bound by any rule, and compelled the country people of the old prefecture, who ran out to the bank of the Ems and the Dollard bay, to return to their homes under a heavy fine. After their flight, leaving one company as a garrison, the Groningers, with banners raised, poured out boldly and drew up their battle line not far from the Selwerd convent. When the standards were joined with Lalaing's, they were driven back into the city more by their own fear than by the force of the enemy. Among those missing, apart from the wounded, were not a few, and two of the women who were assigned to guard the artillery, about five hundred in number, disturbed the Groningers' affairs and their ranks with their weeping and wailing. Therefore they deliberated on surrendering the city after that slight defeat, and sent to Lalaing's camp Jacob Hildebrand, Willem Ubbens and the civic captain Vinckeburgh, who announced that they would surrender the city on fair terms. To obtain these, the envoys of the United Provinces, Regnerus Asselvinius, Loes Harius and Regnerus Cantius, intervened at the right moment. The Groningers, having given and received a pledge of faith, surrendered themselves to the party of the General States and to the governor Matthias. The terms were these.

units.la: Ut Groningani Matthiae Archiducis, Concilij Status & Ordinum generalium decretis parerent, praestandisq; pactis, dum inter eos Ordinesq; conventum foret, obsides darent. Militem suo sacramento ac aere autoratum misum facerent, eoque facto Lalainius copias abduceret, munitiones solo aequaret. Captivis utrinq; Lalainius & oppidani veniam facerent, pecusque abactum oppidanis restitueretur. Oppidani de ceteris cum Lalainio amice transfigerent, id si fieri non posset, lege ageretur. Matthiae Archiducis edicta rata essent, vis utrinque cessaret. Lalainius Groningianos in fidem ac tutelam reciperet, ij pactis conventis, sub poena detentionis bonorum, starent. Id si non facerent, a vicinis etiam per arma ad praestandum compellerentur.
units.tr: That the Groningers should obey the decrees of the Archduke Matthias, the Council of State and the General States, and, while agreements were being negotiated between them and the States, should give hostages, and that they should dismiss the soldiers sworn and paid by them; once this was done, Lalaing would withdraw his forces and level the fortifications to the ground. Lalaing and the townspeople should pardon each other for prisoners taken on both sides, and the cattle driven off should be restored to the townspeople. The townspeople should settle the rest with Lalaing amicably, and if this could not be done, the matter should be decided by law. The edicts of the Archduke Matthias should be held valid, and violence should cease on both sides. Lalaing should receive the Groningers into his protection and guardianship, and they, once the agreements were concluded, should abide by them under penalty of the forfeiture of their goods. If they did not do so, they should be compelled to comply by force of arms by their neighbours as well.

units.la: Ea Winsumi in Traslavicanis VIII. Eid. Ian. acta.
units.tr: These things were done at Winsum in the Translavican district, on the eighth day before the Ides of January.

units.la: Quare Bolsuerdij perspecto Lalainium, qui istius rei diu consilium traxerat, in partes novi foederis propendere, adulta nocte Senatum haberi consultarique super adeundo foedere fecerunt, quo Ordinum foederatorum desiderijs ac Lalainij litteris satisfacerent. Caeterum dissidentibus ex religione animis & civitate ultro discordi, parum prosectum, urgentibus nonnullis Concilium juratum, velut tuendae adversus Senatum plebi a majoribus institutum in partem publicae deliberationis adhiberi. Quod cum aegre pontificij quique a reliquo Senatu obtinerent, Rinckius Cornelius Senatus Praeses, clavibus scriniorum & sigillo urbis projecto discessionem se facturum in Senatu pronuntiavit, foedusq; Ultrajectinum suae conscientiae, sacramento Senatus, paci Gandavensi, tum saluti publicae adversum detestatus est. Sed validiore illorum suffragio, qui pro Ultrajectino foedere, tanquam praesidio libertatis certabant, Ordinum foederatorum Lalainijque litteris benigniter responsum, potestate Jacobo Simonio Consuli facta, qui mandato senatus foederi subscriberet. Igitur Bolsuerdia in fidem recepta Rinckius Cornelius claves portarum, sigilla, caeteraque Senatus & imperij munimenta Hesselo Livio collegae tradidit, depositaque cum Douwone Epaeo consulatus dignitate Curia excessit. Unde civium murmura, mox inconditae voces erumpebant, interque omnem licentiam & immodestos discursantis populi mores constituta civitas spectabatur. Qui, minus grato Magistratus imperio, ne in seditionem erumperent, mandato supremi per Frisiam Senatus novi civicis cohortibus a Magistratu centuriocIↄ. Iↄ. nes creati, qui postulante necessitate populari immodestiæ subvenirent. LXXIX. In ijs Joachimus Jacobæus, Suffridus Petræus, PetrusVibenius, Valerius Petræus omnes amantes fœderis fuere. Quo facto cives Pontificij prostitutâ oris libertate, cædes exsiliraque comminati, majore licentiâ egere, moreque furentum per urbem acti majoris periculi metum Magistratui injecere. Quare supremo Senatu, cui Lalainius Winsumi in Omlandiâ agens, omnem curandarum rerum potestatem concesserat, in consilium adhibito, Sibrandus Richæus vir acer & eloquens fisci provincialis procurator Bolsuerdiam missus, Ubi collato cum Magistratus actuario secreto sermone in oppidanam Curiam mox concessit, populumque signo per præconem dato pro Curia frequentem adesse jussit.
units.tr: Therefore, when Bolsward saw that Lalaing, who had long deliberated on this matter, was inclined to the side of the new league, they made the Senate meet and take counsel in the middle of the night on joining the league, so that they might satisfy the wishes of the United Provinces and Lalaing's letters. However, since minds were divided over religion and the city was itself discordant, little progress was made, until some pressed that the sworn Council, which the forefathers had established as a protection for the people against the Senate, should be admitted to a share in public deliberation. When the Papists and the rest of the Senate resisted this with difficulty, Cornelius Rinckius, president of the Senate, threw down the keys of the chests and the city seal, declared in the Senate that he would secede, and protested that the Utrecht league was contrary to his conscience, to his oath as a senator, to the Peace of Ghent, and to the public safety. But by the greater vote of those who fought for the Utrecht league as a bulwark of liberty, a favourable reply was made to the letters of the United Provinces and of Lalaing, and power was given to Jacob Simonius, the consul, to sign the league on the Senate's mandate. So Bolsward was received into the allegiance, and Cornelius Rinckius handed the keys of the gates, the seals and the other insignia of the Senate and of government to his colleague Hessel Livius. Having laid down the dignity of consul with Douwe Epeus, he left the council chamber. Thereupon the murmurs of the citizens, and soon disorderly shouts, broke out, and the city was seen amid all licence and the unbridled behaviour of a running populace. The new civic companies were created by the magistracy, on the mandate of the Supreme Senate for Friesland, to put down popular disorder, since the need demanded it, as the magistracy's rule was not welcome to the people and they did not wish to break out into sedition. LXXIX. Among them were Joachim Jacobaeus, Suffridus Petreus, Petrus Vibenius and Valerius Petreus, all lovers of the league. Thereupon the Papist citizens, having let loose their freedom of speech, threatened slaughter and exile, and acted with greater licence, and, driving through the city like madmen, instilled in the magistracy a fear of greater danger. Therefore the Supreme Senate, which had given Lalaing, then acting at Winsum in the Ommelands, full power to manage affairs, was consulted, and Sibrandus Richaeus, a keen and eloquent man, procurator of the provincial treasury, was sent to Bolsward. After a private conversation with the secretary of the magistracy, he soon went into the town hall, and ordered the people to attend the hall in large numbers at a signal given by the herald.

units.la: Tum Magistratuum nomina, quos Senatus supremus pacandæ urbi, & mutandis in melius rebus nuncupaverat, in publico recitata, adactiqueque ad sacramentum Hesselus Aysma, Franciscus Jacobæus, Petrus Vibenius, Joannes Romckenius, Theodorus Occonius, Joannes Harmannus Consules, Nicolaus Joannis, Jarichus Hero Senatores.
units.tr: Then the names of the magistrates whom the supreme Senate had appointed to pacify the city and set its affairs right were read out publicly. Hesselus Aysma, Franciscus Jacobaeus, Petrus Vibenius, Joannes Romckenius, Theodorus Occonius and Joannes Harmannus were sworn in as consuls, and Nicolaus Joannis and Jarichus Hero as senators.

units.la: Igitur xv. Kal. Iul. Magistratus dicundo juri tribunali præsedit, concilioque jurato ritè & ex usu temporum constituto, centuriones cohortium sacramento obligavit, urbisque præsidium disponi jussit. Dein minuendæ Pontificiorum licentiæ, qui solennes amburbiorum ritus adhuc exercebant, ad supremum Senatum scripsit, convocatisque in ædem Prædicatorum fidei consortibus Ruardum Acronium hominem Frisicæ gentis Alcmariæ in minoribus Frisijs tum agentem, docendis sacris delegit.
units.tr: Accordingly, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of July, the magistrate presided over the tribunal for administering justice. Having constituted the council under oath, duly and according to the custom of the times, he bound the centurions of the cohorts by oath and ordered the city's garrison to be arranged. Then, to curb the licence of the Papists, who still performed the solemn amburbial rites, he wrote to the supreme Senate. Having summoned the fellow-believers to the church of the Preachers, he chose Ruardus Acronius, a man of Frisian stock then serving at Alkmaar in Minor Friesland, to teach the sacred doctrine.

units.la: Annotatum invenio i v. Non. Iun. portæ amplissimæ validissimæq; quam Leovardiæ urbi in occidentem D. Matri illorum temporum religio dedicaverat, fundamenta jacta fuisse, Adiumq; Lambertum, Meinardum Wigerium & Gellium Sibæum, consularî imperio antoratos, curationem novi operis collegarum decreto accepisse.
units.tr: I find it noted that on the fourth day before the Nones of June the foundations were laid of a very large and strong gate, on the western side of Leeuwarden, which the religion of those times had dedicated to the Blessed Mother. Adius Lambertus, Meinardus Wigerius and Gellius Sibaeus, invested with consular authority, received the charge of the new work by decree of their colleagues.

units.la: Igitur durante Comitio, quod Leovardiæ indictum, Cl. Franckena in ephemeride istius anni prorogatum in Kal. Junias notat, urgentibus Regnero Assuinio, Loefio Hario, & Regnero Cantio Ordinum Foederatorum legatis colloquium pro Ultrajectino fœdere repetitum. Quod etsi ijs maximè reprobaretur, qui regiæ dominationis etiam senescentem potentiam venerabantur, ita erant & in patriæ partibus, qui sinistrâ fœderis suspicione gravarentur, curiosique, ut hominum ingenia solent, & ad futura solliciti omne ex Ultrajectinâ societate nasciturum discrimen expenderent.
units.tr: Meanwhile, while the assembly was in session at Leeuwarden (Franckena, in his yearbook for that year, notes that it was prorogued to the Kalends of June), the envoys of the Confederated Provinces, Regnerus Assuinius, Loefius Harius and Regnerus Cantius, pressed for the negotiations over the Utrecht treaty to be resumed. Although this was most strongly rejected by those who still revered the waning power of royal rule, there were also in the country those who were troubled by a sinister suspicion of the alliance. Anxious and curious, as men's minds usually are, and fearful of the future, they weighed every danger that might arise from the Utrecht association.

units.la: Quippe præter tributi & generalium indictionum onus, à quo ferundo alieni erant, & quod grave ac molestum provinciæ fore occulto animorum præsagio ominabantur, ita maxime metuebant, ne juris antiqui possessione isto ex fœdere exuerentur, clarissimæque Frisiorum genti & tantorum temporum libertati novâ aliquid conventione decederet. Quæ quanquam eorum justa sollicitudo renovaret, qui antiquas Principum gentiumq; cum Frisijs pactiones in animos & memoriam revocabant, ita præcipuè nuperâ superioris Belgicæ, quam Gandavense fœdus socieverat, secessione, tanquam crudo adhuc vulnere offendebantur.
units.tr: For apart from the burden of taxes and general levies, which they could not bear, and which they foresaw, by a hidden presentiment, would be a grave and troublesome thing for the province, they feared above all that by this treaty they would lose possession of their ancient right, and that something new would be yielded in the agreement to the most illustrious Frisian nation and to the liberty of such great times. Although their anxiety renewed the memory of the old pacts between princes and peoples and the Frisians, they were offended especially by the recent secession of the Upper Netherlands, which the Ghent treaty had united, as if by a wound still raw.

units.la: Nihil scilicet tam sanctum atque firmum esse, quin temerare sociales dissensio sensu audeat, cum fides aut ex questu, aut ex potentiae augendae studio, aut humani ingenii imbecillitate rupta religionem foederum auferret. Coivisse Gan- davi cum Belgicae ac Burgundiae provinciis, quas à suis terris, atque finibus morum divisitas, legum atque libertatis gloria secrevisset, quo Philippi & suorum injurijs, qui imperium suum armis magis quam pace tueri maluerat, communis nationum tenerdia occurreret. Atqui clarissimi & solemniter illi foederis infamia dissolutam societatem, ut ante ex religione odia, ita bella atque sanguinem spirare, levitate illorum qui veterum & praesentium fastidio, ac libertatis sensu excusso probrosa servitia ejutate Hispanorum dominationis adiissent. Sed eam rerum humanarum fragilitatem & inconstantiam esse, ut eodem tempore eius subsistere fortuna, aut mortale consilium nolit, nova dissidia haud dubie novo ex foedere seminaturum, nisi expulsa gentibus sola foederum tutrix fides redeat, & in patriarum legum amplexu firmetur nutantis reip. imbecillitas. Matthiae quoque provinciarum Gubernatoris jus atque auctoritas constet, facturà sui periculum si provincias & oppida illius imperio subducat nova & nisi ex aequitate sancitatur, non duratura societas.
units.tr: Nothing, of course, is so holy and firm that dissension among allies does not dare to violate it, when faith, broken either by greed, or by a desire to increase power, or by human weakness, takes away the sanctity of treaties. Consider how the provinces of Belgium and Burgundy came together at Ghent, having been divided from their lands and borders by custom, and separated by the glory of their laws and liberty, so that the common resolve of the nations might meet the wrongs of Philip and his men, who had preferred to defend his dominion by arms rather than by peace. Yet that most famous and solemn treaty, once dissolved, breathes forth, as it did before from religious hatreds, now wars and blood, through the fickleness of those who, from weariness of the past and the present and with the sense of liberty cast off, had shamefully embraced servitude under the Spanish rule. But such is the fragility and inconstancy of human affairs that neither fortune nor mortal counsel wishes any one thing to endure. Without doubt, new discord will be sown by a new treaty, unless, the peoples being expelled, faith, the sole guardian of treaties, returns, and the weakness of the tottering commonwealth is strengthened by an embrace of the native laws. Let the right and authority of Governor Matthias also stand; for if he withdraws provinces and towns from his rule, and this is not sanctioned by equity, the society, which is itself at risk, will not last.

units.la: Itaque Legati foederatarum provinciarum, sanandis Frisiorum criminationibus, fide datâ conceptisque verbis caverant: Ne in Vltrajectinum foedus recepti ex eodem foedere ad ferendas indictionum generalium leges tenerentur, & ut tributa communi provinciarum decreto ordinanda, aequalia socijs forent. Ius quoque Frisicae genti petuliare integrum inviolatumque maneret, Matthiaeque Gubernatori, etiam ex hoc ipso foedere, confirmata autoritas esset.
units.tr: Therefore the envoys of the confederated provinces, to heal the accusations of the Frisians, took care by a pledge given and in set words that: those received into the Utrecht treaty should not be bound by that same treaty to bear the laws of general levies; that taxes ordered by common decree of the provinces should be equal for the allies. The right peculiar to the Frisian nation should also remain whole and inviolate, and the authority of Governor Matthias should be confirmed by this very treaty.

units.la: Quae per Regnerum Assuinium, Loefium Harium & Regnerum Cantium Kal. Jun. signata, animos Frisiorum recipiendo foederi perpulere.
units.tr: These terms, sealed by Regnerus Assuinius, Loefius Harius and Regnerus Cantius on the Kalends of June, moved the minds of the Frisians to accept the treaty.

units.la: Itaque postero die, qui IV. Non. erat, ab oppidanis in aede praedicatorum solemniter & pro more congregatis foedus confirmatum; ac à Julio Bottnia Oldermanno, Georgio Henrico Consule pro Franequerensibus, Henrico Jarichio & Joanne Joannis nomine Adij Lambertij qui absens erat & ilti rei mandatum acceperat pro Leovardiensibus, Nicolao Horatio, Petro Livio pro Snecanis, Jacobo Suffridaeo & Francisco Jacobaeo pro Bolsuerdijs, Bonnone Petraeo & Jeltzone Galama pro Ilstanis, Regnero Olpherdio pro Stauriis, Gulielmo Sippio pro Slotanis, Joanne Boëtio & Douwone Abbaeo pro Worcumanis signatum.
units.tr: Accordingly, on the following day, which was the fourth before the Nones, the treaty was solemnly confirmed by the townsmen, gathered in the church of the Preachers as custom required. It was signed by Julius Bottnia, oldermann; Georgius Henricus, consul, for the Franekerers; Henricus Jarichius and Joannes Joannis, for the Leeuwarders, Joannes acting on the commission of Adius Lambertus, who was absent; Nicolaus Horatius and Petrus Livius for the Sneekers; Jacobus Suffridaeus and Franciscus Jacobaeus for the Bolswarders; Bonno Petraeus and Jeltzo Galama for the Ilsters; Regnerus Olpherdius for the Stavernese; Gulielmus Sippius for the Slotaners; and Joannes Boetius and Douwo Abbaeus for the Workumers.

units.la: Igitur signato per oppidanos Ultrajectino foedere, Westergoi palam discordes pro recipiendo aut repudiando eodem foedere consultavere. Erant namque qui Matthiae Gubernatoris sententiae totum negotium deferrent, foedusque Ultrajectinum, modo à Gandavensi & Bruxellensi Unione tum religionis concordiâ non dissentiret, amplectendum pronuntiarent.
units.tr: With the Utrecht treaty thus signed by the townsmen, the Westergoers openly disagreed about whether to accept or reject it. For some referred the whole matter to the judgement of Governor Matthias, and declared that the Utrecht treaty should be embraced, provided it did not differ from the Ghent and Brussels Union or from the concord of religion.

units.la: Itaque obtestabantur nisi de eo caveretur, foedus se non probaturos, habituosque rationem mandatorum suorum, quae violari non possent. Ita Sixtus Bottnia & Joannes Suffridaeus pro Wimbritterijs, pro Wonseranis Janco Ofingha, Jarichius Gulielmius presbyter, Reinicus Suffridaeus Baerdius, pro Hemelumolpherdijs Hinno Jarichius & Reinicus Hissius rescripsere.
units.tr: They insisted that, unless provision were made on this point, they would not approve the treaty, and that they would keep to the terms of their instructions, which could not be violated. Thus Sixtus Bottnia and Joannes Suffridaeus, for the Wymbritseradeel men; Jancus Ofinga, for the Wonseradeel men; and Jarichius Gulielmius, the elder, Reinicus Suffridaeus Baerdius, for the Hemelumer men, Hinnus Jarichius and Reinicus Hissius, replied in writing.

units.la: Hoc etiam additum a posteritatibus, ut, si foedus adeundum foret, præcIↄ. Iↄ. præturæ suæ& districtui, in causa tributi, ex inundatione terrarum suarum & secutâ egestate parceretur, & ut è pecorum pastu aut seminatis agris nată indictione omissâ, tributum quoque floreni aureï non intenderetur.
units.tr: The Westergoers also added this condition: that if the treaty had to be accepted, their district should be spared the tax on account of the flooding of their lands and the want that followed, and that, when a general levy was imposed on the pasturing of livestock or on sown fields, the tax of a gold florin should be omitted as well.

units.la: Contra purâ fœderis aditione pro Menaldumæis Foppo Grovensteinius & Scelto Siricius, pro Baerderanis Serapius Galama & Orichius Doiemus, Poppo Burmania & Oeno Regnerius pro Hennardijs, Hobbo Baerdius pro H. Waltingha aut Frederico Offenhusano Franequerensij tuebantur, opponentibus se Hesselo Hania, Tito Regnero Baerderanis, & inter Hennardios Sixto Popma Iure-consulto & Gerlaco Rispenio, è Barranis Cornelio Gabinio, qui conditiones fœderis, tanquam à Gandavensi pace & cæteris pactorum formulis differentes repudiando, decreto nuperi comitij, quod fœdus abrogasse dictitabant, immodestiâ sermonum patrocinabantur.
units.tr: On the other side, for unconditional acceptance of the treaty, Poppo Grovensteinius and Sjelte Siricius for the Menaldumadeel men; Serapius Galama and Orichius Doiemus for the Baarderadeel men; Poppo Burmania and Oeno Regnerius for the Hennaarders; and Hobbo Baerdius for H. Waltinga, or Frederick Offenhuis, of Franeker, defended it. Opposing them were Hessel Hania and Tito Regnerus of Baarderadeel, and among the Hennaarders Sixtus Popma, jurist, and Gerlach Rispenius; and from Barradeel Cornelius Gabinius. They rejected the terms of the treaty as differing from the Ghent peace and the other forms of agreement, and with immoderate speech they defended the decree of the recent assembly, which they kept saying had abrogated the treaty.

units.la: Itaque Serapius Galama Baerderanus prætor contumaci adversariorum importunitate excandescens, id vero alienum & manifestæ falsitatis ajebat, fœdusque Ultrajectinum à patriæ amantibus approbatum, non nisi paucorum, qui secretos contra leges conventus habuissent, præpeditum asserebat.
units.tr: Therefore Serapius Galama, praetor of Baarderadeel, flaring up at the stubborn importunity of his opponents, declared that this was indeed a foreign and manifestly false claim. He asserted that the Utrecht treaty, approved by lovers of the fatherland, was being hindered only by a few men who had held secret meetings contrary to the laws.

units.la: Hæc in acta relata & Non. Jun. legatis Ultrajectinis exhibita. Tantam in animis acerbitatem aut sollicitudinem Ultrajectini fœderis disceptatio injecerat. Cui malo quorundam suspicio aut cura fomentum aliquod subministrabat, cum essent qui fidem facerent, provincias Ultrajectino fœdere & simul ære ex alieno creditoribus nexas Frisiæ provinciam ex jure societatis gravaturas.
units.tr: These matters were entered in the minutes and presented on the Nones of June to the Utrecht envoys. So great was the bitterness and anxiety which the dispute over the Utrecht treaty had stirred in men's minds. To this evil the suspicion or care of some supplied fuel, since there were those who gave assurance that the provinces bound to the Utrecht treaty, and at the same time bound by money debts to creditors, would burden the province of Friesland by right of the alliance.

units.la: Quamobrem à Legatis cautum. Ne æs alienum oneri eorum aut damno, qui in præsens fœdus adijssent, cederet, & ut omni debito liberando quod jam ante natum esset, fides antiquæ obligationis interveniret. Igitur Ordines Frisiæ spectatâ Legatorum integritate, & ne comitium quod in octiduum prolatum criminabantur, majore provinciæ impendio traheretur, ijs qui in parte adhuc adversâ erant, colloquium atque arbitros componendæ dissensioni obtulere, sub hac obtestatione, ut oblatam æquitatem respuenti culpa retardatæ aut ruptæ pacis imputaretur, suaeque innocentiæ testimonium tam fœderatarum provinciarum quam Trans-lavicanæ, qui comparuerant, gentis legati acciperent. Id prid. Non. Jun. factum ac à Docone Martna, Douwone Sixma, Jancone Osingha, Barthio Idzaerda pro fœderatis provincialibus signatum.
units.tr: Wherefore the envoys took precautions that the debt should not fall as a burden or loss on those who had now joined the treaty, and that for the discharge of every debt which already existed, the faith of the old obligation should hold good. Therefore the Estates of Friesland, trusting the integrity of the envoys, and so that the assembly, which they were accused of having put off for eight days, should not be prolonged at greater expense to the province, offered to those who were still in the opposing party a conference and arbiters for settling the dispute. They did so under this condition: that whoever refused the fairness offered would be blamed for the delay or breaking of the peace, and that they would receive a testimony of their innocence from the envoys both of the confederated provinces and of the Trans-Lauwers people who had appeared. This was done on the day before the Nones of June and signed by Docco Martna, Douwo Sixma, Jancus Osinga and Bartho Idzerda for the confederated provincials.

units.la: Igitur fœdere icto & à Frisijs, ut ante dixi, per Barthium Idzaerdam & Gellium Sibæum Ultrajecti signato, mense Junio modus tributi per provincias constitutus, conventumque ut Geldri quovis mense 40000. Hollandi 83000. Zelandi 17000. Frisij 24000. Ultrajectini 12000. Transisulani & Lingenses 23000. Groningenses 6000. Omlandi 12000. Drentini 6000. Carolæorum penderent, ærisque corrogati subsidium gerendo bello serviret.
units.tr: Therefore, the treaty having been concluded, and signed at Utrecht by the Frisians (as I said before) through Barthius Idzaerda and Gellius Sibaeus, a method of paying the tax was set out for the provinces in June, and they agreed to pay each month: Gelderland 40,000, Holland 83,000, Zeeland 17,000, Friesland 24,000, Utrecht 12,000, Overijssel and Lingen 23,000, Groningen 6,000, Ommelanden 12,000, Drenthe 6,000 Carolus-guilders, and that the money raised should serve as support for carrying on the war.
