units.la: Reperio in actis istius conventus Sibrandum Hiddium Geesterlandiæ nomine in comitio tum agentem, collatam legitimo more à Sylvestribus Deputati dignitatem Barthio Idzaerdæ asseruisse, ejusque rei fidem ab actuario Ordinum Isbrandio perscriptam vim mandati habuisse. Lit-
units.tr: I find in the records of that assembly that Sibrandus Hiddius, then speaking in the assembly on behalf of Geesterland, asserted that the office of deputy, conferred by the Sylvestrines in the lawful manner, had been given to Barthius Idzaerda, and that the record of this matter, written down by Isbrandius, the clerk of the States, had the force of a mandate.

units.la: Historiarum Lib. V.
units.tr: Book V of the Histories.

units.la: Litteras quoque ab Ordinibus generalibus in Frisios Antverpiâ missas, quibus de subsidiario ære ocyus mittendo solvendæ Trajectensium lxxix. obsidioni cæterisque necessarijs hortabantur.
units.tr: They also sent letters from the General States at Antwerp to the Frisians, urging them to send the subsidy money more quickly, to pay for the siege of the men of Utrecht (79) and for other necessities.

units.la: Quippe præter publicarum collationum pecuniam, centesimæ quoque æs sustinendis belli oneribus poscere coactos, solutum ignaviâ & ex stipendiorum morâ exercitus disciplinam comperisse. Neque aliud superesse, quam ut Trajecto subsidiario ad Mosam per vim expugnato reliquas quoque civitates hostium armis exponat magnis rebus adversa salubris consilij cunctatio. Se verò Deum, conscientiam generis humani & provincialium fidem pro suâ innocentiâ obtestari, quæ ex indignatione instantis periculi dissimulare non posset secundarum rerum impedimenta aliis autoribus stare. Atque hoc inde esse, quod sui confessus autoritas provincialis imperij prætenso majestatis jure arceatur, quod non velit, istis à suo consessu prospici, in quibus festinato opus sit, & quibus mederi relationum tarditas non posset. Itaque sisti se ad triste mentis patriæ spectaculum, postquam illius ostentatio movere illorum sanguinem atque animos non posset, qui res suas atque corpora amovendis externis servitijs consecrare salutî publicæ justa devotione debuissent. Interim sperare se meliora & ex magnitudine præsentis mali emendata consilia, quo subvenire eminenti reip. possit necessarij subsidiaryque æris maturitas.
units.tr: For, they wrote, besides the money from the public collections, they had been forced to demand a hundredth penny to bear the burdens of war, and they had discovered that the army's discipline was loosened by idleness and by the delay in pay. Nothing else remained except that, with Utrecht stormed by force on the Maas side, the hesitation of a healthy plan, which was adverse to great matters, should also expose the remaining cities to the enemy's arms. They called on God, the conscience of mankind and the faith of the provincials to witness their innocence. Indignation at the impending danger, they said, would not let them keep silent: other men were standing in the way of the success of affairs. This was because the authority of their own assembly was being kept back by a pretended right of sovereignty, since it did not wish that provision be made by those people for matters that needed haste and that the slowness of reports could not remedy. Therefore they presented themselves at the sad spectacle of the mind of the fatherland, since its display could not move the blood and spirits of those men who ought to have devoted their goods and bodies, with due devotion, to the public safety by driving off foreign servitude. Meanwhile they hoped for better things and for counsels improved by the greatness of the present evil, by which the timely supply of the necessary subsidy money might come to the aid of the threatened commonwealth.

units.la: Mox decreto Ordinum prid. Non. Ianuar. perscripto & per Arnoldum Hardervicenum, Douwonem Nyenhusium & Ludovicum Foxium actuarios publicos ad Præsules cæterosque adversæ partis perlato responsum est.
units.tr: Soon afterwards, a reply was delivered to the prelates and the others of the opposing party, by the public notaries Arnoldus Hardervicenus, Douwo Nyenhusius and Ludovicus Foxius. It had been written in a decree of the States dated the day before the Nones of January.

units.la: Id moris apud majores suos in comitijs obtinuisse, ut suffragiorum ratio haberetur, quæ quo plura eo validiora fuissent.
units.tr: It had been the custom among their ancestors in the assemblies, they said, that account be taken of the votes, and the more of these there were, the more valid they were.

units.la: Et quoniam in causâ Ultrajectini fœderis, (ad quod constringi nemo jure posset) & ut nulli constringerentur Lalainius voluisset, ita conscientiæ suæ ductum secutos statuisse, quæ plures decrevissent. Quare obtestationem Ordinum tanquam inefficacem & cum patrijs legibus pugnantem se habere, quæ comitiorum & suffragij jure oppidanos prohibuissent, neque prætores admitterent, quibus ex actis fas non esset, sicuti neq; privatis, solemni comitio interesse. Itaque id responsum de quo actuarij referebant, Ordinibus minus gratum & acceptum firmandis partibus animos accendit.
units.tr: And since, in the matter of the Utrecht covenant, to which no one could lawfully be bound, and since Lalaing had wished that no one be bound, they had decided to follow what the majority had determined, guided by their conscience. Therefore they held the States' entreaty to be ineffective and at odds with the native laws, which had forbidden townsmen to take part in the assembly and the right of voting; nor would the magistrates admit those to whom, by the records, it was not lawful, nor private persons either, to attend the solemn assembly. So that reply, which the notaries reported, was less welcome to the States and kindled the minds of the parties to strengthen their side.

units.la: Unde postero à Westergois decretum.
units.tr: Whereupon, the following day, a decree from the Westergo district.

units.la: Ut rationum magistri dignitate atque munere suo cederent, Ordinumque Deputati provinciæ rationibus præessent. Pecunias quoque publicas rationariorum incuriâ segnius in erarium perlatas, inferri in idem ærarium ocyus curarent, eaque potestate Iancø Osingha & Orichius Doyenius fungerentur. Ut eorum mandatis signandis Foppo Grovensteinus & Goslicius Hiddama vacarent, ijsdemque Deputatis fas esset in gravioribus causis binos ternosve è Westergois in consilium adhibere, decernereque quod ex usu sit. Et quoniam foederatorum Ordinum legati fidem fecissent, se de mensurâ 24. millium tributo, quod Frisijs impositum erat, pactâ ac transigere non posse, Deputatis ijsdem jus atque potestas facta esset delegandi Ultrajectum, qui cum Carolo Rodrda Legato Ultrajectini agente consilia communicarent, deque justo & æquali cum Societ tributo pacificantur, eiusque remissione socijs indulta, idem beneficij Frisijs obveniret. Lucæ Iargao provinciæ actuario Antistitium Ordinii addito Eo Isbrandius in dignitate succederet. Id actis insertum, & Foppij Grovensteinij, Sixti Bottniæ, Oeronis Rinsij & H. Bardij manu signatum.
units.tr: That the masters of accounts should give way in dignity and office, and that the deputies of the States should preside over the accounts of the province. They should also see to it that the public money, which had been carried into the treasury more slowly through the carelessness of the accountants, be brought into the same treasury more quickly; and Jancho Osingha and Orichius Doyenius were to exercise this power. Foppo Grovensteinus and Goslicius Hiddama were to be occupied in sealing their mandates. And it was to be lawful for the same deputies, in the more serious cases, to take two or three from Westergo as counsellors and to decide what is expedient. And since the envoys of the confederated States had made it plain that they could not agree or settle on the matter of the 24,000 tax which had been imposed on the Frisians, the same deputies were given the right and power to send delegates to Utrecht, who would confer with Carolus Rodrda, acting as envoy of Utrecht, and make peace about a just and equal tax with the associates; and, when that tax had been remitted to the associates, the same benefit would fall to the Frisians. To Lucas Iargao, actuary of the province, the office of the Antistitium of the Order was added, and Eo Isbrandius was to succeed him in that dignity. This was entered in the records and signed by the hand of Foppius Grovensteinius, Sixtus Bottnia, Oeron Rinsius and H. Bardius.

units.la: Quo Westergoënsium decreto à foederatis Oostergoïs & majore Sylvestrium parte, quæ cum oppidanis foederi Ultrajectino se obligaverat, approbato, ijdem Oostergoï Scipionem Meckmannum & Renicum Cammingham cognomento Majorem Deputatos creavere, eorumque mandatis scribendis Doconem Martnam & Tetardum Aylvam delegavere. Hæc à Joanne Martna Corniumano & Broerio Hesselio perscripta. Neque Sylvestibus pax quoque & quies tum erat.
units.tr: With this decree of Westergo approved by the confederated Oostergoi and by the greater part of the Sylvestri, who had bound themselves with the townsmen by the Utrecht covenant, the same Oostergoi created as deputies Scipio Meckmannus and Renicontus Cammingham, surnamed Major, and they appointed Doco Martna and Tetardus Aylva to write their mandates. These were written out by Joannes Martna of Cornum and Broerius Hesselius. Nor, at that time, did peace and quiet prevail among the Sylvestri either.

units.la: Quippe Deputatis cum rationum magistro per eos, qui Præsulum Ordini favebant, extra comitij locum constitutis Barthius Idsaerda, Joannes Sannius, Sibrandus, Hiddius, Auco Edonius & Feico Tatmannus de mandato sociorum se opposuere, rescissâque electione & damnatis actis obtestatione usi, publicarum rationum curam Deputatis permisere. Ea Non. Jun. facta.
units.tr: For when the deputies, together with the master of accounts, were set up outside the place of the assembly by those who favoured the Order of the prelates, Barthius Idsaerda, Joannes Sannius, Sibrandus Hiddius, Auco Edonius and Feico Tatmannus opposed them on the mandate of their associates. They rescinded the election, condemned the acts, made use of a protest, and left the care of the public accounts to the deputies. This was done on the Nones of June.

units.la: Quæ dum Leovardiæ in comitio turbido & exitiali provincialium discordia scisso fiunt, per Hesselum Aysmam legatum apud Antverpios adhuc agentem libellus supplex Deputatorum Frisiæ nomine MATTHIÆ Gubernatori hunc in modum oblatus.
units.tr: While these things were happening at Leeuwarden in an assembly thrown into turmoil and split by the destructive discord of the provincials, a humble petition from the deputies of Friesland was presented in this way to Governor Matthias, through Hesselus Aysma, the envoy who was still staying at Antwerp.

units.la: ANNVS & ultra est, Serenissime GUBERNATOR, quo hosti per Frisiam addictos vinculis dari, ac dignitate moveri & loco imperasti. Hac tamen cautione addita, ut finito hoc ipso quo exagitamur bello, jure cum ijs ageretur. Quo mandato fretus LALAINIUS Frisiæ præfectus Episcopum & Senatum esse ab Ordinarijs officijs justè, eâque de re ad te rettulit. Et quamquam istius facti atque decreti ratio firma & immutata esse debeat, tamen loco moti restitutionis in integrum beneficium implorauere, ac ut eos, etiam machinationum hostilium convictos, tribunalibus atque dignitatibus redderes. Quod cum à tuo decreto alienum esset, sanxisti, ut causæ actorumque cognitio LALAINIO ac Deputatis Frisiæ permitteretur. In quam proficisci perferendis actis nostræ occupationes, quibus hic detinemur, & impedita itinera non sinunt. Igitur petimus, ut mandato tuo, quod scripsisti, robur addas, Episcopumque ac Senatum durante hoc bello, judicio prohibeas. Fisci quoque apud Frisios procuratori potestatem facias ex actis ceterisque in quæ inquiri faciet, adversum eosdem agendi, aut proferri sinas diem cognitionis, quo LALAINIUS belli & pacis rebus expeditis, vacare judicio & committi mandatis possit.
units.tr: It is a year and more, most Serene Governor, since those who were devoted to the enemy throughout Friesland were ordered to be put in chains, and to be removed from their dignity and place. This was added, however, on condition that, once this very war by which we are harassed had ended, the case should be pursued lawfully against them. Relying on this mandate, Lalaing, prefect of Friesland, reported to you that the bishop and the senate had been justly removed from their ordinary offices, and about this matter he has referred to you. And although the reasoning of that act and decree ought to be firm and unchanged, nevertheless they implored the benefit of restitution to the former state, even for the prelates removed from their place, and that you would restore to the tribunals and dignities even those who had been convicted of hostile plots. Since this was foreign to your decree, you ruled that the inquiry into the case and the acts should be entrusted to Lalaing and the deputies of Friesland. Our occupations, by which we are detained here, and obstructed journeys, do not allow us to set out for that place to carry the acts. Therefore we ask that you add strength to the mandate which you have written, and that you forbid the bishop and the senate from judging while this war lasts. Also, that you give the procurator of the treasury among the Frisians power to act against the same men on the basis of the acts and of the other matters into which he shall cause inquiry to be made, or else that you allow the day of the hearing to be postponed, so that Lalaing, once the affairs of war and peace are settled, may be free for the judicial business and may be entrusted with the mandates.

units.la: Quare rescripto Matthiæ cognitionis dies in bimestre prolatus ejusque rescripti denuntiatio Wilhelmo Mennenio apparitore, Ioanni Smeicro procuratori exautorati Senatus facta.
units.tr: Therefore, by a rescript of Matthias, the day of the hearing was postponed for two months, and the announcement of this rescript was made to Wilhelmus Mennenius, the usher, and to Joannes Smeicus, procurator of the deposed senate.

units.la: Tum lite fæderis nondum sopitâ Feico Tatmannus Utingeranorum Prætor pro Barthio Idsaerda, in Deputatum à Sylvestribus communi suffragio electo, testimonium dixit, manuque Ecoris Isbrandij scriptum, frenandæ adversariorum importunitati referri in acta fecit. In quæ illorum quoque nomina, qui convellendo Ultrajectino fœderi suffragia ac consiconsilia commodaverant, relata, instruendaq; posteritati quo illorum cl.To. temporum motus & factiosas coitiones cognoscat, archivi provinciae Lxxiij. inserta hoc Ordine recitabantur.
units.tr: Then, the dispute over the covenant not yet having subsided, Feico Tatmannus, praetor of the Utingeri, gave testimony on behalf of Barthius Idsaerda, who had been elected by common vote of the Sylvestri as deputy, and he had a document written by the hand of Ecor Isbrandius, in order to restrain the importunity of the opponents, entered into the records. Into these were also entered the names of those who had lent their votes and counsels to overturn the Utrecht covenant, and, so that posterity might learn the commotions and factious gatherings of those times, they were read out in this order, inserted into the archive of the province, Lxxiij.

units.la: In quibus è territorio Leovardiensi Hesselus Emingha, Hesselus Feitsma & Renicus Tetardius, èFerverderano Nicolaus Lovius, Laurentius Buwo presbyter, è Dongrijs occidentalibus Nicolaus Cleffenius, ex orientalibus Elco Mockama, Wigerus Gabinius, pro pagis quibusdam Columani territorij Edo Alma, pro Octopagicis Livius Ielgersma, pro Dantumanis Oeno Wijtsma praetor & Tiepco Goslingha, pro Tietzerkijs Oedsius Arnoldus, pro Smallengijs Erco Arnoldius, pro Raverdijs Ado Heringha & Otto Bottesius, pro Idardijs Biuco Edsardius fuere. Inter Westergoos Titus Regnerius, Hesselus Hania, Hanso Roorda, Tiepco Gerbranda, D. Sixtus Popma LL. Doctor, Gerlacus Rispenius & Cornelius Gabinius nominati. In Sylvestrium numero Kempo Hajonius Opsterlandus, Heyno Abelius ex Stellinguerfijs orientalibus, Ulpianus Godofredus Scoterlandus, Gellius Broerius Haskeranus, Euco Tetardius Lemsterius, Foppius Douma & Ansko Meinius Donieverstallenses periscripti. Caeterum Opsterlandis, Stellinguerfijs occiduis, Scoterlandis, Utingeranis, Geesterlandis caeterisque multitudine suffragiorum primis & foederi unitis illorum, quos recensui, partibus boni in comitio exitus non fuere.
units.tr: Among them, from the territory of Leeuwarden, were listed Hesselus Emingha, Hesselus Feitsma and Renicus Tetardius; from Ferwerderadiel, Nicolaus Lovius, Laurentius Buwo, presbyter; from the western Dongeradeel, Nicolaus Cleffenius; from the eastern, Elco Mockama and Wigerus Gabinius; for certain villages of the Columani territory, Edo Alma; for the Octopagici, Livius Ielgersma; for the Dantumadeel, Oeno Wijtsma, praetor, and Tiepco Goslingha; for the Tietjerksteradeel, Oedsius Arnoldus; for the Smallingerland, Ercus Arnoldius; for the Raverdijs, Ado Heringha and Otto Bottesius; for the Idaarderadeel, Biuco Edsardius. Among the Westergoi were named Titus Regnerius, Hesselus Hania, Hanso Roorda, Tiepco Gerbranda, Sixtus Popma, Doctor of Laws, Gerlacus Rispenius and Cornelius Gabinius. In the number of the Sylvestri were listed in writing Kempo Hajonius of Opsterland, Heyno Abelius from the eastern Stellingwerf, Ulpianus Godofredus of Schoterland, Gellius Broerius of Haskerland, Euco Tetardius of Lemsterland, Foppius Douma and Ansko Meinius of Donjewerstal. Moreover, for the Opsterlanders, the western Stellingwerfers, the Schoterlanders, the Utingeri, the Geesterlanders, and the other most numerous and confederated parties of the Sylvestri, whom I have recounted, there was no good outcome in the assembly.

units.la: Quippe praeter procurationes quas plena agendi potestate firmatas, oppidani exceptis Hindelopijs ad signandum foedus attulerant, etiam ex Oostergoïs Octopagici, Tietzerkij, Collumani, Smallengij, Dongrij plerique è Westergois Winbritserij, Hemelumolphardij, Baerderani, Menaldumaei & Franekerensis territorij, è Sylvestribus Opsterlandi, Stellinguerfij, Utingerani, Lemsterij & Geesterlandi mandata praeferebant, reliquosque & in ijs presbyteros eosque dubios & vacillantes, aut immodestia partium suspectos, concordibus suffragijs superabant. Quibus & hoc accedebat, quod semiplenis mandatis instructi velut accisa agendi potestate priorum causam praejuvarent, metuque majoris periculi in illa conversione rerum coorto, silentium profiterentur. In eorum numero ex Idardijs, Roordahutani, Frensij, Idardij, Warregai, Leovardiensis territorij, Dantumani, Oostergoi, Barrani, Hennardij, Womseran i, Westergoi; Donieverstallenses & Haskerij Sylvestres censebantur.
units.tr: For besides the proxies, which the townsmen, with the exception of Hindeloopen, had brought to sign the covenant, confirmed with full power of acting, there were also mandates presented from the Oostergoi: the Octopagici, Tietjerksteradeel, Columani, Smallingerland, Dongeradeel for the most part; from the Westergoi: Wymbritseradeel, Hemelumer Oldephaert, Baarderadeel, Menaldumadeel and the territory of Franeker; from the Sylvestri: Opsterland, Stellingwerf, Utingeradeel, Lemsterland and Geesterland. And they outvoted the rest, including the presbyters, with unanimous votes, even those who were doubtful and wavering, or suspected of immoderate partisanship. To these was added the fact that, being furnished with half-full mandates, they supported the former side as if their power of acting had been clipped, and, out of fear of a greater danger arising from that change of affairs, they professed silence. Among their number were counted, from Idaarderadeel: Roordahuizen, Franeker-Frenschwerd, Idaarderadeel, Warga, Leeuwarden territory, Dantumadeel, Oostergo, Barradeel, Hennaarderadeel, Wonseradeel, Westergo; and the Donjewerstal and Haskerland Sylvestri.

units.la: Igitur foedere per Frisiam cum Geldris, Hollandis caeterisque provincijs per plerosque percussò, caeteri qui specie tuendae apud Gandavum ictae pacis firmandis Philippi partibus utebantur, retro citroque cum Farnesio secreta communicabant, multique etiam ex ipso Ordinum generalium consessu, aut qui militaribus dignitatibus pollebant odio, ut creditum fuit, Ultrajectini foederis a libertatis patrocinio alienabantur.
units.tr: So, with the covenant struck through Friesland by most of Gelderland, Holland and the other provinces, the rest, who under the pretext of defending the peace made at Ghent were serving Philip's cause, secretly communicated with Farnese back and forth. Many even from the very assembly of the General States, or those who held military rank, were, as was believed, being estranged from the defence of liberty by hatred of the Union of Utrecht.

units.la: Insertum actis invenio, Carolum Gauraeum Equestri Ordinis virum, praeclaris legationibus ad Andinum nuper functum, clandestinam a partibus Ordinum defectionem tum parasse, datisque ad primatem litteris & in vetere quod Philippo regi praestitisset sacramento & foederati exercitus seditione sibi placuisse.
units.tr: I find it recorded in the minutes that Charles Gauraeus, a man of the equestrian order who had lately discharged distinguished embassies to Andinum, was then preparing a secret defection from the side of the States. He had written to the primate, and had pleased himself by breaking, through a sedition in the allied army, the oath he had once sworn to King Philip.

units.la: Unde Antverpiae & simul Coloniae, ubi pacis negotium tardius procedebat, asserende regiae partis arcana consilia fabricata, quae quo majore cIↄ. Iↄ. majore vehementia incalescebant, majore quoque impetu acta promiscue vulgabantur.
units.tr: Hence, at Antwerp and at the same time at Cologne, where the peace negotiation was proceeding more slowly, secret plans in support of the royal party were fabricated. The more heated these grew, the more hastily they were spread about indiscriminately.

units.la: Reperio in litteris Gelliae Aylvae nobilis foeminae, erat ea Gemmae Burmanniae uxor, ad Renicum Cammingha Coloniâ datis, eum de instantibus periculis monuisse, & ut dignitate regijs per Frisiam officiarijs abrogatâ novi & nuper creati in possessione suorum munerum ocyus locarentur. Quippe esse Coloniae, qui de restituendo vetere Senatu cogitent, & qui expugnato ad Mosam Trajecto irruptionem Frisiae comminentur. Gellium quoque Tetardium opificio vitriarium Coloniae tum in exilio agentem, eadem patri suo per litteras approbasse fratrique ut evitando, quod Frisiae immineret, periculo Coloniam festinaret, consilium dedisse.
units.tr: I find in letters from Gellia Aylva, a noblewoman, the wife of Gemma Burmannia, written to Renicus Cammingha at Cologne, that she had warned him of impending dangers, and that, the royal offices in Friesland having been revoked, the new and recently appointed men should be quickly placed in possession of their posts. For there were men at Cologne who were thinking of restoring the old Senate, and who threatened an invasion of Friesland once Maastricht on the Maas had been taken. She also reports that Gellius Tetardius, a glassmaker then living in exile at Cologne, had approved the same by letter to her father, and had advised his brother to hurry to Cologne to avoid the danger that threatened Friesland.

units.la: Aysma scribit foedus Ultrajectinum prid. Eid. Iun. Antverpiae cum religionis Edicto publicatum tacitâ offensione nonnullorum animos perculisse, eosque novi foederis odio & recitatione correptos Senatu abstinuisse. Quae faciendis secessionibus reperta Ordinum societatem ultro ex impulso aerario debilem, tanquam natis in perniciem exemplis, infirmabant. Itaque eveniebat ut sessis Trajectensium rebus auxilia non suppeditarentur, equestresque copiae ex inopia stipendiorum ignavia contabescerent. Ipse etiam Castrenantius, notante Albada, tardius postulatis Ordinum responderet, actaque etiam Kalend. Iun. perscripta in spem expugnandi Trajecti serius traderentur. Ijs cavebat. Ut omnium anteactorum venia restitutoque patrio jure peregrinae legiones exautorarentur. Inquilini civitatum atque castellorum praesidijs praesent omnique exercitu dimisso, cessante armorum usu, intermissa aut bello impedita commercia reflorescerent. Vectigalia & indictiones gravandis provincialibus institutae tollerentur, & ut quique uti possedissent utrobivis locorum, ita res ac bona sua possiderent. Functionibus ac dignitatibus, exceptis perduellibus, caeteri restituerentur ijque ex inquilinis essent. Captivis venia fieret, Buranus Belgio redderetur, Hollandiam, Zelandiam & Ultrajectum, vicario imperio tenerct. Acta Matthiae & Ordinum, quamvis legitimae potestatis & juris defectu laborarent, rata essent proque legitimis haberentur, exceptis quae juris regij fuissent. Magistratus lege & recepto more crearentur. Catholica Romana religio sola haberetur, caeteris ab eâ alienis jus intra quadriennium proxumum fieret provincijs excedendi, bonorum administrationem quibus velint demandandi. Obedientia regiae majestati, tanquam naturali & legitimo principi ex formulâ Carolinae conventionis & Philippi regis praestaretur. Regij sanguinis princeps & regendae Belgicae par in provincias mitteretur. Ei civitates, oppida, fortalitia unâ & cum regis patrimonio & cum omni commeatu Ordinum traderentur. Gandavense foedus integrum foret, caetera pacta, conventa, foedera, sponsiones initae essent. Regina Angliae & Andinus Coloniensi foedere comprehenderentur. Pontifex caeteriq; principes ad hanc conventionem delegati sartam rectam praestarent. Idem sub religione jurisjurandi rex faceret, ejus acta archivis publicis inserarentur. Ab Ordinum parte idem fieret.
units.tr: Aysma writes that the Union of Utrecht, published at Antwerp on the day before the Ides of June together with the edict on religion, struck the minds of some with a silent offence, and that they, seized by hatred of the new covenant and by its recitation, kept away from the Senate. These things, devised to bring about secessions, weakened the society of the States, which was already feeble through the drained treasury, as though examples had been born for their ruin. Thus it came about that aid was not supplied to the besieged affairs of Utrecht, and the cavalry wasted away through lack of pay and idleness. Even Castrenantius himself, as Albada remarks, replied more slowly to the demands of the States, and the acts drawn up even on the Kalends of June were handed down too late for the hope of taking Utrecht. Against these things he provided: that, with all past offences pardoned and the ancestral right restored, foreign legions should be discharged; that the residents of cities and fortresses should hold the garrisons, with the whole army dismissed and the use of arms ceasing, interrupted or hindered commerce should flourish again; that tolls and levies instituted to burden the provincials should be abolished, and that each should hold his goods and property in whichever place he had held them before. Apart from traitors, the rest should be restored to their functions and dignities, and they should be residents. Pardon should be granted to prisoners; Buren should be returned to Belgium; Holland, Zealand and Utrecht he would hold under vicarious rule. The acts of Matthias and of the States, though they laboured under a lack of lawful power and right, should be valid and regarded as lawful, except those which were matters of royal right. Magistrates should be created by law and accepted custom. The Roman Catholic religion alone should be held; to others alien to it, the right should be given, within the next four years, to leave the provinces and to commit the administration of their goods to whomever they wish. Obedience should be rendered to his royal majesty, as to a natural and lawful prince, according to the formula of the Carolingian convention and of King Philip. A prince of royal blood, equal to governing the Netherlands, should be sent into the provinces. Cities, towns and fortresses should be handed over to him, together with the king's patrimony and with every supply from the States. The Ghent covenant should remain entire, and the other pacts, agreements, covenants and undertakings made should stand. The Queen of England and Anjou should be included in the Cologne covenant. The Pope and the other princes delegated to this convention should guarantee it as sound and right. The king should do the same under the sanction of an oath, and his acts should be placed in the public archives. On the part of the States the same should be done.

units.la: Ad quae eorum Legati responderunt. Certam pacis spem jam pridem dem se concepisse, sed eam novorum postulatorum, quae Castrenantius fecisset, iniquitate convelli. Neque enim eam Gandavensi aut Brabantis...
units.tr: To these demands their legates replied. They said they had long since conceived a sure hope of peace, but that it was being shaken by the unfairness of the new demands which Castrenantius had made.

units.la: xellensi pactis convenire, neque alia esse, quam quae Ordinum, si de ijs referant, animos, velut talium impatientes, exacerbare queant. Aequiora scilicet Bredano conventu, Aurantio ac socijs oblatos, quae illi respuissent, qui soli bellum tum sustinebant. Igitur petere ut Caesaris legati regium Philippi melius instruant, faciantque quam ocyus, ut molliora & ad pacem factura proponi curet. De Aurantio additum; Nam id mandatarij Caesaris quaesiverant, ejus speciale mandatum cum id commune includeret, Colonienssi actioni non requisivisse, facturos ut id habeant si viderint certiora ad pacem judicia se ostendere. Mox de inducijs sanciendis nullo item exitu collocutum volentibus Caesaris mandatarijs, ut Castrenantij postulata, velut aequitati innixa legati Ordinum approbarent, eoque armistitium aut inducias, velut emollito rege paciscierentur.
units.tr: Nor did these agree with the agreements of Ghent or Brussels, nor were they anything other than what could only exasperate the minds of the States, should the envoys report them, since the States were impatient of such things. Evidently the terms offered at the Breda congress, and to Orange and his associates, were fairer, and those who alone were then sustaining the war had rejected them. Therefore they asked that Caesar's legates better instruct the royal officials of Philip, and see to it that milder proposals, likely to further peace, be put forward as quickly as possible. About Orange it was added: Caesar's commissioners had asked for his special mandate, since that matter involved the common cause, and had not sought it for the Cologne proceedings; they would make sure they had it if they saw that it showed more certain judgments toward peace. Soon, concerning the sanctioning of truces, likewise no result was reached in discussion. The commissioners of Caesar, wishing the demands of Castrenantius, as resting on fairness, to be approved by the legates of the States, would then agree to an armistice or truces, as though the king had been softened.

units.la: Albada Frisiorum legatus & orator scribit, Ordinum Legatos obtinendis inducijs, etiam inclinante Junio, aequissima quaeque regijs imperatorijsque mandatarijs obtulisse, iniquitateque adversariorum ad desperationem pacis actos plus regiae tamen venerationi, obtinendo armistitio quam suis mandatis dedisse. Hoc namque scribente Albada, metuebant, ne jus suum pertinacius aut immodestius tutando impedimentum pacis actioni injicerent, ipsumque Romanum imperium, tanquam Austriae domui & Philippo magis aequum acerrima libertatis defensione in odium foederati populi convitaretur.
units.tr: Albada, envoy and spokesman of the Frisians, writes that the legates of the States, in obtaining truces, even as June was waning, offered all the fairest terms to the royal and imperial commissioners. Though driven to despair of peace by the unfairness of their opponents, they gave more to royal dignity in obtaining the armistice than to their own instructions. For, as Albada writes, they feared that by defending their right more stubbornly or immodestly they might put an obstacle in the way of the peace negotiation, and that the Roman empire itself might be reviled, as more favourable to the house of Austria and to Philip, by the fiercest defence of liberty, into hatred of the confederated people.

units.la: Econtra hoc legatos clam urebat, quod Castrenantius paternum Philippi affectum speciosa praedicatione offerret, servatoque postulatorum rigore & ne ab ijs recederetur cavendo, alienum a pace animum ostenderet.
units.tr: On the other hand, this secretly stung the legates: that Castrenantius offered Philip's paternal affection with specious praise, and, while keeping the rigour of the demands and guarding against any departure from them, showed a mind alien to peace.

units.la: Itaque stabiliendae aequitati conditionum, quas jam ante obtulerant, hunc in modum scribebant.
units.tr: Therefore, to establish the fairness of the conditions they had already offered, they wrote in this manner.

units.la: LEGES ad quas provocavimus, Mandatarij Caesaris, tum pacta & conventiones nostrae sunt & semper fuere. Quas antiquare aut imminuere, nec regi aut Principi olim fas fuit, neque etiamnum licet. Vt de Tributis noni dicamus, in quibus edicendis, ut modum retinere coactus Rex est, ita in ejus potestate nunquam fuit sine Ordinum consensu ea intendere. Atqui nec dignitates, nec beneficia non nisi sub conditionibus conferebat, quas multum aberat, ut Prorex aut Praefectus, Senatus aut Legionum Tribuni violarent. Quare ubi illorum fidelitate & imperio, omne quod pro jure nostro stabat, oppressum aut infirmatum est, divino atque humano jure impulsi arma cepimus, sub quibus corporum nostrorum, rerum atque juris tutela haberetur. Nam alias obsequium Regi tanquam legitimo principi nunquam detrectavimus, neque ut faciamus animum induximus, caeterum volumus, ut imperio suo, quod legibus nostris atque conventionibus inligatum est, populum suum regat. Vnum vero est, quod deberi Regi gratia potest ut religionis libertatem ex usu temporum indulgeat, cum aliam a pontificia profitentibus nihil concedi velit, quam ut mitiore paenâ corrigantur, aut patriâ suâ ac possessionibus ejecti, desertis propinquis & omni amicorum ac rerum solatio de-
units.tr: The laws to which we have appealed, commissioners of Caesar, together with the pacts and agreements, are and always have been ours. It was never lawful for a king or prince in former times to abolish or diminish them, nor is it lawful even now. To speak of the tax of the ninth penny: in ordaining it, the king is bound to keep moderation, and it was never in his power to extend it without the consent of the States. Indeed he did not confer offices or benefits except under conditions, which a viceroy or prefect, a senate or tribunes of the legions were far from violating. Wherefore, when by their faithlessness and command everything that stood for our right was oppressed or weakened, impelled by divine and human law we took up arms, under which the protection of our bodies, goods and right might be maintained. For otherwise we have never refused obedience to the king as a lawful prince, nor have we resolved to do so; rather we want him to rule his people with the authority that is bound by our laws and agreements. There is indeed one thing which the king can grant as a matter of grace, namely to indulge religious liberty according to the custom of the times; yet since those professing a religion other than the papist are to be granted nothing except to be corrected with a milder penalty, or, expelled from their homeland and possessions, deprived of kin and of all the comfort of friends and goods,

units.la: {cont}destituti, exilia tollerent. Qua cum dura & plane inhumana sint, ita bre- vibus de jure nostro impræsentiarum testamur, cui tuendo Deo coram & terrarum orbis gentibus abunde pares sumus. Quo ipso etsi regem reuereri & cole- re obligamur, ita non ignoramus, quid principem inter & vasallos intercedat. Nos de singulis quæ rex Philippus proposuit ad provincias & de religionis po- stulato imprimis referemus, quo si pertinaciter stare rex velit, infructuosa omnis Romani imperij ad pacem intercessio erit. Quod ad inducias attinet, parati sumus eas sancire & quidem hac lege, ut in spem futuræ pacis liber u- trinque commeatus sit & ut sepositâ omni lite atque vi mutua provincialium societas habeatur. Hæc xiii. Kalend. Iul. scripta.
units.tr: to bear exile. Since these things are harsh and plainly inhuman, we briefly testify to our right at present, in defending which we are amply equal before God and the nations of the world. By this very fact, though we are bound to revere and honour the king, we are not unaware of what lies between a prince and his vassals. We will report on each of the things King Philip has proposed to the provinces, and especially on the demand concerning religion; if the king is willing to stand stubbornly on this, all intercession of the Roman empire toward peace will be fruitless. As for truces, we are prepared to sanction them, and indeed on this condition: that there be free passage on both sides in hope of future peace, and that, all dispute and mutual violence set aside, there be a fellowship between the provincials. Written on the 13th day before the Kalends of July.

units.la: Cui petitioni etsi ultro Castrenantius adversaretur, ita tum offendi se durioribus Ordinum mandatis asserebat, specioso obtentui, quo ur- bem, vigiliis & cæde fessam Farnesius vir gloriæ imprimis appetens, rudimentis militaris imperij adjiceret. Quippe addebat suæ potestatis non esse de obsessa urbe pacisci, Alexandro Farnesio cum exercitu & imperio res Philippi gerente. Itaque inter cavillationes relationesque fœcialium tractâ actione, Alexander Farnesius collectis quas po- terat copijs urbem oppugnare constituit, quo toleratas trimestribus castris difficultates egregio victoriæ exitu & cum incremento principis famæ leniret.
units.tr: Although Castrenantius opposed this request, he declared that he had been so offended by the harsher orders of the States that he could not agree to it. Under the specious pretext that Farnesius, a man keen above all for glory, wished to add to the beginnings of his military rule a city already worn down by sieges and slaughter, he insisted that it was not within his power to negotiate over a besieged city, since Alexander Farnesius was conducting Philip's affairs with the army and command. So, with cavils and reports carried back and forth by the heralds, the business was dragged out. Alexander Farnesius then gathered whatever troops he could and resolved to storm the city, so that the hardships endured through a three-month camp might be eased by a splendid victory and an increase in the prince's reputation.

units.la: Cæterum novies cum jactura suorum repulsus, dum obsessi somnolenti & exangues reficiendis somno viribus student, decimo infultu suæ eam potestatis fecit. Ad quam expugnandam extenuatum præsidium, à Farnesij parte, nox & recentes copiæ juvârunt. Igitur urbe capta in promiscuam cædem itum, donec tandem inanis clementiæ exem- plum editurus Farnesius abstineri cædibus jussit. Suartsenburgius præsidij ductor, qui res præclarè & in exemplum gesserat, cum plerisque suorum occubuit.
units.tr: Yet he was repulsed nine times with the loss of his own men. While the besieged, drowsy and exhausted, strove to restore their strength with sleep, he made a tenth assault and brought the city under his power. To capture it, the weakened garrison was overcome by the night and by fresh troops on Farnesius' side. Once the city was taken, there was a general slaughter, until at last Farnesius, about to give an example of empty clemency, ordered the killing to stop. Suartsenburgius, the leader of the garrison, who had conducted himself nobly and admirably, fell with most of his men.

units.la: Tradunt historiæ occupatâ ab Hispanis urbe, mulierum puerorumq; ejulatus per spacium mill. pass. auditos, fugientemque inermium turbam aut Mosæ amni immersam, aut gladijs hostium expositam, velut civitatis funeri, communibus exequijs interfuisse. Ita Trajectum ad Mosam in finibus Eburonum Brabantiæq, situm à trium mensium obsidione expugnatum, promissorum auxiliorum ac Coloniensis (de qua dixi) pacis infœlices cruentosque fructus accepit.
units.tr: Histories relate that when the city was occupied by the Spaniards, the wailing of women and children could be heard for a mile around, and the fleeing crowd of unarmed people either drowned in the Meuse or was exposed to the enemy's swords, as if taking part in the funeral of the city, with its common obsequies. Thus Maastricht, on the Meuse in the territory of the Eburones and Brabant, taken after a three-month siege, received the unhappy and bloody fruits of promised aid and of the Cologne peace (which I have mentioned).

units.la: Aggæus Albada in litteris ad Deputatos Frisiæ xiii. Kalend. Iul. Coloniâ datis, scribit præcipuum dissensionis argumentum in Romanæ religionis exercitio tum stetisse, illudque velut grave & cum armis natum ab infœlicibus provincijs beneficium præcipuè pacis amovisse. Quæ per ipsam quoque Frisiam lubrica adhuc & exilis, ex Ultrajectini fœ- deris amore aut odio animos ac consilia sejungebat.
units.tr: Aggaeus Albada, in a letter to the deputies of Friesland dated at Cologne on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of July, writes that the chief cause of dissension at that time lay in the exercise of the Roman religion, and that this, like a grievous thing born of arms, had above all removed the benefit of peace from the unhappy provinces. Even in Friesland itself, which was still unsteady and fragile, this divided minds and plans, according to love or hatred for the Union of Utrecht.

units.la: Itaque ab Albada Legato viro patriæ amantissimo multa sanandis dissensionibus suadebantur, quas domesticâ pace ac civili concordiâ com- poni removendis quam maximè instantibus interesset.
units.tr: Therefore Albada, the legate, a man most devoted to his country, urged many measures for healing the dissensions, which it was of great importance to settle by domestic peace and civil concord, by removing the most pressing causes.

units.la: LITTERAE erant.
units.tr: There were letters.

units.la: CVM
units.tr: WHEN

units.la: Historiarum Lib. V.
units.tr: Book V of the History

units.la: CUM dolore discordias vestras intellexi, propterea quod occasionem & causam dare poterunt totius patriæ nostræ ruinæ. Nec tamen arbitror ex vobis quenquam esse, qui Hispanos in patriam nostram reducere cupiat, vel qui arma unus in alterum propter religionem suscipere cogitet. In eâ enim re vos omnes prudentiores esse judico. Considerare ergo vos velim discordias vestras non alio servire posse, quam ut occultis vestris hostibus, qui ab Hispanorum partibus stant, viam præparetis, qua facilius vos invadant & opprimant. Hoc ut scribem necessitas me cogit, qui sciam exercitum jam contra vos destinatum esse, & nisi Deus consilium eorum ac propositum impediverit ac perturbaverit, non diu erit quin intra limites vestros hostium vestrorum exercitum habituri sitis. Quamobrem amanter vos rogo, ut mutuam concordiam & amorem inter vos foveatis & colatis. Hac unâ re hostibus vestris superiores esse poteritis, ab Vnione reliquarum & maximè vicinarum provinciarum ne vos separetis. Plura per litteras scribere non audeo, sed ut istud scribam & petam magnæ me causæ movent. Bene valete viri optimi & patriæ amantissimi. Coloniæ 19. Iun. 1579.
units.tr: I have learned with sorrow of your dissensions, because they may give occasion and cause for the ruin of our whole fatherland. Yet I do not think there is anyone among you who wishes to bring the Spaniards back into our country, or who intends to take up arms against another for the sake of religion. For I judge that you are all wiser than that in this matter. I would have you consider, then, that your dissensions can serve no other purpose than to prepare the way for your hidden enemies, who stand on the Spanish side, so that they may attack and crush you more easily. I am compelled by necessity to write this, since I know that an army has already been sent against you, and unless God frustrates and disrupts their plan and purpose, it will not be long before you have your enemies' army within your borders. Therefore I earnestly beg you to foster and cherish mutual concord and love among yourselves. By this one thing you will be able to prevail over your enemies, and you must not separate yourselves from the union of the other and especially the neighbouring provinces. I dare not write more at length, but I am moved by great reasons to write this and to ask it. Farewell, most excellent men and most loving of your country. Cologne, 19 June 1579.

units.la: Similes litteræ ad virum nobilem Renicum Camminga, qui in Deputatis tum erat, ab eodem legato datæ.
units.tr: Similar letters, written by the same envoy, were sent to the noble man Renicus Camminga, who was then among the Deputies.

units.la: Itaque soluto quem mense Iunio habitum memoravi, apud Frisios conventu, Regnerus Asseyinius, Loefius Harius & Regnerus Cantius Ultrajectum regressi, præsidente Joanne Nassovio Geldriæ Gubernatore, de singulis per Frisiam actis relationem instituerunt. Ista erat: Rennebergium reliquamque Frisiam, & in eâ Bolsuerdios, Staurios, Worcumios, Ilstanos Westergoos, & ex Oostergois plurimos Ultrajectinum fœdus approbasse proque menstruo 24000. tributo solvendo fidem interposuisse. Hac tamen cautione addita, ut, si quota tributi plures per provincias remitteretur, idem Frisiis beneficium esset quæ in acta decretorum fœderis Ultrajecti xiv. Kalend. Iul. relata.
units.tr: So, when the assembly held among the Frisians in June, which I have mentioned, was dismissed, Regnerus Asseyinius, Loefius Harius and Regnerus Cantius returned to Utrecht, with John of Nassau, Governor of Gelderland, presiding, and they gave an account of what had been done throughout Friesland. It was this: Rennenberg and the rest of Friesland, including the Bolsward, Stavoren, Workum and Ilst districts of the Westergo, and many of the Oostergo, had approved the Union of Utrecht and had pledged to pay 24,000 as a monthly tax. With this caution added, however, that if a share of the tax were remitted in some provinces, the same favour should apply to the Frisians, as recorded in the decrees of the Treaty of Utrecht, 18 June.

units.la: Reperio in actis, Matthiam Gubernatorem de præstandis quoque Ordinum generalium ærario tributis Frisios pendendis militum stipendijs tum monuisse, ac ut, quod ante ad v 1. Iun. factum esset, quam ocyus legatos Antverpiam mitterent, plenis mandatis & agendi potestate instructos. Fœderatos quoq; Ordinum Ultrajecti commorantes subsidia poposcisse, ac ut Frisij tributum ex fœdere promissum defendendis provincijs & seorsim fœderatis præstarent. Adeo superioris Belgicæ defectio & Coloniensis pacis infida spes novarum rerum desideria cum fastidio veterum accenderat.
units.tr: I find in the records that Governor Matthias then also warned the Frisians, who were to pay the taxes for the soldiers' wages and also for the treasury of the States General, that they should send envoys to Antwerp as quickly as possible, furnished with full mandates and powers to act, as had been done before by 1 June. The allied members of the Union staying at Utrecht also demanded subsidies, and urged the Frisians to pay the tax promised under the treaty, both for the defence of the provinces and separately for the allies. So far the revolt of the Walloon provinces and the faithless hope of the Peace of Cologne had kindled in people a desire for change, with disgust for the old order.

units.la: Mox Georgius Lalainius (nam ita indigitatum tum reperio) acceptis ex pacto Groningensium obsidibus castra Groningâ movit, obsidesque Campos in oppidum Isalis amnis sicum oppidum ablegatos haberi in custodia fecit. Tum incerto an urbem armis victam sed fidei dubiam intraret, diversa consilia se obtulere, cum essent, qui censerent ejus præsentiæ turbidam & partium fœcundam civitatem egere, omniaque præsentis præfecti imperio dispecta fœlicius processura. Alijs placebat non committendum esse infidæ civitati provinciæ rectorem, & quem eo loco providentia rerum posuisset, ut in ejus securitate omnium salus, in periculo discrimen constitueretur. Sed fiduciæ ex ipsa quæ
units.tr: Soon afterwards Georgius Lalainius (for that is what he is found to have been called then), having received hostages from Groningen under the agreement, moved his camp from Groningen and had the hostages, who had been sent off to Kampen, a town on the river Isala, kept in custody. Then, unsure whether to enter the city, which was conquered by arms but doubtful in its loyalty, various plans presented themselves. Some thought that a city turbulent and fertile in factions needed his presence, and that everything would go more happily under the command of the prefect on the spot. Others were pleased that the governor of the province should not be committed to a faithless city, and that the position in which providence had placed him should not be one where the safety of all depended on his security and the danger of ruin on his peril. But, trusting in the very hostages who would prevail...

units.la: {a} Lalainius accepti obsidibus Groningani intras. cIↄ. Iↄ. LXXIX. quæ prævalerent certus urbem intravit, verso in prosperum omen ingenio, quod memoratum annalibus diem suo ingressui fortuna reservasset. Erant namque qui vetustorum curiosi recordabantur, Mariam Caroli Cæsaris sororem eodem, qui Joanni Baptistæ sacer est, die Groningam advenisse, Florentiumque & Maximilianum Buranos tum Joannem Lignæum Arenbergium Caroli ac Philippi præfectos civium festivitate exceptos illum diem, tanquam principum inaugurationibus, solemnem insignivisse. Igitur arrectæ ad magna indoli haud difficulter persuasum, id secundis rebus & ad lætiora indicium esse, quæ extrema adversitate pensare fortuna laborabat.
units.tr: {a} Lalainius enters Groningen after receiving hostages. 1579. Lalainius, certain of his strength, entered the city, turning the omen to a favourable one, since, as the annals record, fortune had reserved that day for his entry. For there were some who, curious about the past, recalled that Mary, sister of Emperor Charles, arrived at Groningen on the same day that is sacred to John the Baptist, and that Florentius and Maximilian of Büren, and John Ligne of Arenberg, prefects of Charles and Philip, were received by the citizens with festivities, and that they made that day, as at the inaugurations of princes, a solemn one. Therefore, the minds of the people, raised to great hopes, were not hard to persuade that this was a sign of good fortune and of happier things, which fortune, labouring under extreme adversity, was trying to balance.

units.la: Quare Groningæ Magistratu constituto & ad fidem adacto, tum religionis pace per edictum promulgatâ, reformatæ exercitijs D. Walburgis ædem & Prædicatorum fanum assignavit, Ordinatisque pro temporum statu apud Groningam rebus signa per Drentiam movit. Jam enim quatuor legionis suæ cohortes Drentinorum finibus ejectas acceperat, illumque populum, velut paludibus & ingenio soli fisum, omnem insolentiam reprimendis Ordinum partibus exercuisse. Igitur legione haud procul Slochtero, vicus in Fredonaldijs est, per fossam ducendis palustribus aquis facilem transmissâ, novâ quoque Oenonis Grovensteinij nobilis Frisij cohorte tum tribus tormentis campestribus quæ Leovardiâ adduci curaverat, validior, medios Drentiæ per agros exercitum duxit, versusque Coverdiam, olim Vacciforum in Historiâ Wilhelmi Hedæ nominatam, quam Entius Satrapa cum imperio tenebat, iter intendit. Quo in fugam abrepto & omni vicino municipio in fidem accepto, muniendi, quod ibi erat, castelli mandatum Computtio dedit, Oldenzelamque & Linganos imperata facere jussit. Sed contumaciâ satraparum & Linganæ plebis Pontificijs sacris ferventius imbutæ nihil actum, dissimulante Lalainio minus ad famam, magis molestiæ fore, si per inculta & fœda paludum uligine loci fractum itinere & molestijs militem neglectâ magnarum rerum occasione duxisset. Quæ res subsecutæ defectionis suspicionem in Lalainio auxit. Igitur Coputtius talium solers castellum, quod vetustate aut ruinâ collapsum cernebatur, multiplici muro latissimisque fossis præcinxit, Coverdiamque erecto ex arte opere communiri fecit. Quo necdum confecto triste mox incendium illuxit, tertiamque ædificiorum partem fortuito igne absumpsit. Itaque firmata Coverdia Lalainio magnam apud fœderatos Ordines gratiam conciliavit. Quorum propterea decreto factum est, ut militare ejus imperium augeretur, quatuorque cohortes sexcentorum equitum conscribendi potestatem acciperet. Igitur litteris ad Frisiæ Ordines 1 x. Kal. Iul. datis de eo monuere, & ut fertilem virorum proviciam ac vicinos agros equestribus delectibus permitterent. Lalainius quoque una cum Frisiæ & Omlandiæ Delegatis, isti negotio tanquam imprimis necessario ocyus vacaret, fidosque & fœderi socios militaribus dignitatibus præficeret. Hic etiam addebant, ut præter lanceariorum alam, sclopetariorum quoque cohors inter cæteras legeretur, & ut æs, autorandis copijs destinatum, in promptu esset. Unde Ailco Onsta, Reinsuoldius, Afingha, Entenius & Dodo Larius ex Translavicanâ ac Drentinâ nobilitate ducendis cohortihortibus delecti, quæ ex agrario populo ex perturbatione temporum inquieto & ad bellum facili nullâ difficultate conducebantur.
units.tr: Accordingly, when a magistracy had been set up at Groningen and brought to loyalty, and freedom of religion had been proclaimed by edict, he assigned the church of St Walburga and the chapel of the Preachers to the reformed worship. Having arranged matters at Groningen according to the state of the times, he moved his standards through Drenthe. For he had already learned that four cohorts of his legion had been driven out of the territory of the Drentians, and that this people, relying on their marshes and the nature of their soil, had practised every insolence in repressing the cause of the States. So, with the legion having crossed easily, by means of a ditch that drained the marshy waters, near Slochteren, a village in the Fredonalds, and having been strengthened by a new cohort under Oeno of Grovestins, a noble Frisian, and by three field guns that he had arranged to be brought from Leeuwarden, he led the army through the middle fields of Drenthe, and set his course towards Coevorden, once called Vaccia in the History of Wilhelm Heda, which the satrap Entius held with authority. Its garrison fled, and every neighbouring town came under his allegiance; he gave Coputtius orders to fortify the castle that was there, and commanded Oldenzaal and the Lingen district to obey his commands. But because of the obstinacy of the satraps and of the people of Lingen, who were more fervently steeped in Papist rites, nothing was achieved, Lalainius being unwilling to conceal that, as far as reputation went, it would bring more trouble than gain if he led his soldiers by a broken route through uncultivated and foul places, damp with the marsh, neglecting a great opportunity. These events, following upon one another, increased suspicion of defection against Lalainius. Therefore Coputtius, clever in such matters, surrounded the castle, which was seen to have collapsed through age or ruin, with a multiple wall and very wide ditches, and had Coevorden fortified with a work raised according to the rules of the art. Before this was finished, a grievous fire broke out, and consumed a third part of the buildings by chance. Thus, with Coevorden secured, Lalainius won great favour with the allied States. Accordingly, by a decree of those States it was resolved that his military command should be enlarged, and that he should receive power to enlist four cohorts of six hundred horse. Therefore, by letters given to the Frisian States on 22 June, they gave notice of this, and asked them to allow the fertile men of the province and the neighbouring lands to be levied for cavalry. Lalainius also, together with the Deputies of Friesland and Ommelanden, was to devote himself more quickly to this business as especially necessary, and to set over the military ranks men faithful and allied to the union. They added also that, besides the lancers' wing, a cohort of musketeers should be chosen among the others, and that the money intended for paying the troops should be ready at hand. Hence Ailco Onsta, Reinsoldius, Afingha, Entenius and Dodo Larius were chosen from the nobility of Overijssel and Drenthe to lead the cohorts, which were drawn without any difficulty from the agrarian people, restless in the disturbance of the times and easily moved to war.

units.la: Mox Lalainius litteris Deputatorum quas Renicus Cammingha, Ianco Osingha, Douwo Sixma, Scipio Meckma & Gellius Sybæus collegarum nomine signaverant per Orichium Doihemum collegij legatum in Frisiam & Leovardiam Translavicanis evocatus, ducendis illorum ingeniijs qui novam fœderis Ultrajectini sanctionem seditiosis per Frisiam consilijs obtendebant. Igitur Leovardiæ hærens, ubi Hesselus Aysma legatus Antverpiâ cum literis & mandatis Ordinum generalium advenerat, de habendo populi inter Flevum & Lavicam comitio deliberavit, copiasque equestres ex inquilinis collectas armari ocyus fecit. Hesseli vero Aysma mandata hæc erant: Ut 12. millia Carolæorum liberandis Trajectensibus decreta ocyssimè exigeret, decemque & octo aureorum millia menstruum tributum communis Belgicæ provincijs impetraret.
units.tr: Soon afterwards Lalainius, having been summoned to Friesland and Leeuwarden from the Overijssel side by letters of the Deputies, which Renicus Camminga, Jancko Osinga, Douwe Sixma, Scipio Meckema and Gellius Sybæus had signed in the name of their colleagues, through Orichius Doihemus, the envoy of the college, to lead on those minds who were using a new ratification of the Treaty of Utrecht as a pretext for seditious plans throughout Friesland. Therefore, staying at Leeuwarden, where Hessel Aysma had arrived from Antwerp with letters and mandates of the General States, he deliberated about holding an assembly of the people between the Vlie and the Lauwers, and had the cavalry collected from the tenants armed without delay. Now Hessel Aysma's mandates were these: that he should exact without delay the twelve thousand Carolus guilders decreed for relieving the people of Utrecht, and obtain from the provinces of the common Netherlands a monthly tax of eighteen thousand gold pieces.

units.la: Sed Frisij exsolutum æs ac ad Ultrajectinos transmissum solvendæ Trajectensium obsidioni fidem faciebant, cum honestâ obtestatione miserrimæ urbis casum suæ moræ non imputandum. De reliquo tributo, quod in mensem poscebatur, respondebant, se necdum statuisse, magnitudine onerum fructos & enerves, qui decimestri spatio octoginta millia aureorum socio ærario intulissent. Esse sibi provinciam angustis finibus clausam, quam præter rapinas & inruptiones hostium, militum centurionumq; stipendia & avarities exhausisset. Nihilominus testandæ in socios fidei conventum propediem habituros facturosq; quod suarum virium sit. Id iv. Kal. Iul. perscriptum.
units.tr: But the Frisians declared that the money had been paid and sent to the men of Utrecht, to provide for the raising of the siege of the Utrecht people, and with an honourable protest they stated that the disaster of that most wretched city should not be laid to their delay. As for the rest of the tax, which was demanded for the month, they replied that they had not yet decided, being exhausted and drained by the greatness of their burdens, which had contributed eighty thousand gold pieces to the common treasury within a fifteen-month period. They said that their province was enclosed within narrow limits, and had been exhausted, apart from the plunderings and raids of the enemy, by the pay of soldiers and captains and by avarice. Nevertheless, they would soon hold an assembly to attest their fidelity to the allies, and would do whatever was within their power. This was written on 28 June.

units.la: Cui rei grave quoque impedimentum injiciebat, quod fœderati Ordines datis Ultrajecto vi. Non. Iul. litteris menstrui 24000 carolæorum tributi Frisios commonerent, Pontificiorumque per provinciam importunitas indicendo populi comitio & colligendis subsidijs obesset. Quæ Senatus regij, qui Leovardiæ adhuc secretiore vita & simul custodia procul foro & judicijs agebat, clandestinis consilijs interversa fœdere Ultrajectino nexos acerbioribus odijs accendebant. Itaque plebe turbidâ, & Magistratu urbis actionibus Senatus inritato, Philippi Senatus ante solis occasum excedere urbe & simul provinciâ jussus, missis actuarijs publicis, qui decreta perferrent.
units.tr: To this matter a serious obstacle was also thrown in: the United Provinces, by letters given at Utrecht on 2 July, reminded the Frisians of the monthly tribute of 24,000 carolus guilders. The Papists' importunity throughout the province also hindered the calling of a popular assembly and the collection of subsidies. The senators of the king, who were still living in secret at Leeuwarden, away from the forum and the courts and under guard, inflamed with bitter hatred the men bound by the Union of Utrecht, having disrupted matters by secret plans. Therefore, with the populace in turmoil and the city magistrate irritated by the senate's actions, Philip's senate was ordered to leave the city and the province before sunset, and public clerks were sent to deliver the decrees.

units.la: Sunt qui tradunt obnuntiationem titulo proscriptionis factam, Senatuique regio tam urbe à Magistratu, quam provinciâ de mandato Collegij interdictum. Mox in cives immodestiâ partium & expulsi Senatus commiseratione exacerbatos idem statutum, Vibiusque Crusius, Wibrandus Goutumanus, Pompeius Gabinius, & Suffridus Petræus urbe ac municipio ejecti. Addunt Scriptores Valonem quoque hominem importunum & stipendia sub Gasparo Roblesio meritum, eadem pœnâ multatum, reliquosque Pontificios metu sui ac terrore exempli evictos ex adversis temporum inquieta ingenia & immodestiam morum repressisse. Quare altius per urbem passim silentium, Pontificisque dolore & simul ira ex proscripto Senatu jam ante accensi promendis in publicum seditiosis vocibus abstinere. Quippe Magistratus in secreta coitionum & domesticos cœtus accuratè inquirebat, dispositisque per ordicIↄ. Iↄ. ordinaria loca vigilibus spiculatore, tanquam exploratore utebatur.
units.tr: Some writers report that the notice was given under the title of proscription, and that by mandate of the college the king's senate was forbidden, by the city magistrate, to enter the city and, by the province, to enter its territory. Soon afterwards the same decree was passed against citizens inflamed by their immoderate partisanship and pity for the expelled senate: Vibius Crusius, Wibrandus Goutumanus, Pompeius Gabinius and Suffridus Petraeus were thrown out of the city and its jurisdiction. The writers add that Valon too, a troublesome man who had served under Gaspar de Robles, was punished with the same penalty, and that the other Papists, cowed by fear of him and terror of the example, restrained their restless spirits and unruly manners in the adverse conditions of the time. Hence silence spread everywhere through the city, and the Papists, already kindled with grief and anger over the proscribed senate, refrained from uttering seditious words in public. Indeed the magistrate inquired closely into secret gatherings and private meetings, posted watchmen at the usual places, and used a spy as an informer.

units.la: Ferunt per noctes quas sublustres Cancrinus dies & æstivi solis fulgor faciebat, conventus adversarum partium quoque observatos, ne tenebrarum aut noctium arcanâ opacitate prona turbandæ civitati consilia tegerentur.
units.tr: They report that during the nights made bright by the twilight of the summer days and the glow of the midsummer sun, the meetings of the opposing party were also watched, lest plans to disturb the city be hidden in the secret darkness of the night.

units.la: Creditum fuit Senatorias domos extrusis habitatoribus desertas mærore & exinde indignatione plurimos affecisse & quod præter istarum ædium solitudinem eidem ruinæ regij Senatus actuarios & ex apparitoribus quosdam mutatio temporum involuisset. Itaq; amoto Philippi Senatu, regiæ per provinciam factionis & simul imperij post præfectum principe, servor quoque turbulentorum civium per urbem elanguit, novusque Senatus, quem Ordinum autoritas, antiquato Burgundico ritu, dicundo juri præfecerat, in tutissimâ judiciorum possessione collocatus est. Igitur civili concordiâ Leovardiæ & alibi per provinciam aucta Georgius Lalainius post Groningam Coverdiamque in fidem receptas, magnarum porro rerum spes atque desideria agitabat, quo secundo fortunæ vento provectus incrementa gloriæ ex ulteriore consiliorum successu acciperet. Sed tardâ tributi collatione tenue ærarium, quod in bello primum est, bene destinata subvertebat, ejusque inopiâ gerendæ res omissæ cursum majoris famæ & anteactæ prosperitatis fœlicem impetum morabantur.
units.tr: It was believed that the senators' houses, emptied of their occupants, affected many with grief and then indignation, and that, besides the desolation of those houses, some of the king's senate's clerks and attendants had been caught up in the same ruin through the change of times. Therefore, with Philip's senate removed, the royal faction throughout the province, and at the same time the imperial authority once the prince was set aside, the ferment of the turbulent citizens also subsided throughout the city. The new senate, which the authority of the Estates had set over dispensing justice, restoring the old Burgundian custom, was placed in the most secure possession of the courts. Accordingly, with civic harmony increased at Leeuwarden and elsewhere in the province, George Lalaing, after Groningen and Coevorden had been received into allegiance, went on nursing great hopes and desires, and, carried forward by this favourable wind of fortune, he hoped to gain increased glory from further success in his plans. But the slow collection of the tribute was undermining the meagre treasury, which is the first thing in war, and for lack of money well-planned enterprises were abandoned; this shortage held back the happy course of greater renown and past prosperity.

units.la: Itaque Ultrajectum profectus, ubi & Joannes Nassovius Geldriæ rector tractandis fœderis negotijs advenerat, de redigendo in Ordinem ærario consultatum, multoque sermone in consessu repetito conventio tributi inita. Eâ cautum fuit:
units.tr: Accordingly he went to Utrecht, where John of Nassau, governor of Gelderland, had also arrived to handle the affairs of the union. The question of bringing money into the treasury of the Estates was considered, and after much discussion, repeated in the assembly, an agreement on the tribute was reached. By it, provision was made:

units.la: Ut provinciæ fœdere comprehensæ, die constituto tributi quotam ad ærarium perferrent, negligentesque aut contumaces creditum æs cum usuris præstarent. Isti rei personarum, rerum & actionum obligatio interveniret, ex eaque contumacium personas ac bona disinendi alienandique citra juris actionem jus socijs foret. Damnum, quod ex detensione aut venditione bonorum nasciturum esset, contumaci provinciæ aut quæ in morâ foret cederet, neque ante audiretur, quam consignatum æs cum usuris præstitisset. Quæstiones ex divenditis intra fœderatas provincias bonis natæ, præfectorum arbitrijs definirentur, conjumacibus, aut negligentibus nullum juris aut fori beneficium esset. Menstruum tributum ad centena nonaginta bina aureorum millia supportaretur, eique Geldri quadraginta, Hollandi octoginta, Zelandi viginti, Frisij viginti quatuor, Vltrajectim duodecim, Omlandi sedecim millia ex pacto præscripti fœderis penderent. Præfecti provinciarum conventionem ratam facerent, contumaces pendendum ad tributum cogerent. Fœderati de singulis ad suas quaque provincias referrent, intraque tres septimanas, aut mensem proxumum de mandato caverent.
units.tr: That the provinces included in the union should, on a fixed day, bring their quota of tribute to the treasury, and that those who were negligent or obstinate should pay the money owed with interest. An obligation of persons, goods and actions should attach to this, and from it the partners should have the right, without legal process, to seize and alienate the persons and goods of the obstinate. Any loss arising from the detention or sale of goods would fall on the obstinate province or the one in default, and it would not be heard until it had paid the deposited money with interest. Disputes arising from sales of goods within the united provinces would be settled by the decision of the governors; the obstinate or negligent would have no benefit of law or court. The monthly tribute would be raised to 192,000 gold pieces, and of this Gelderland should pay 40,000, Holland 80,000, Zeeland 20,000, Friesland 24,000, Utrecht 12,000 and Overijssel 16,000, as prescribed by the agreed treaty. The governors of the provinces would ratify the agreement and compel the obstinate to pay the tribute. The Union would refer each matter to its own provinces, and within three weeks, or the following month, they would give a mandate.

units.la: Hæc in acta relata, & Ioannis Nassovij Georgij Lalainij, A. Boinenbroeckij, Gerardi Lonij pro Geldris, pro Hollandis Botzelarij, P. Busij, Wilhelmi Stopij, A Madij, Regneri Cantij, Theodori Ioannis Lonckij, Francisci Maelsonij, pro Zelandis Iacobi Valckij, Pro Frisijs Caroli Roordæ, Ioannis Aysmæ, pro Ultrajectinis Gerardi Knopij, Regneri Assevinij, Ioannis Dreunij, Florentij Thinnij, pro Omlandis E. Iargaei manu III. Eid. Iul. signata. Re-
units.tr: These matters were recorded in the acts and signed by John of Nassau, George Lalaing, A. Boinenbroeck, Gerard Lon for Gelderland, Bootzelaer, P. Busius, William Stop, A. Madius, Reiner Cant, Theodore John Lonck and Francis Maelson for Holland, Jacob Valck for Zeeland, Charles Roorda and John Aysma for Friesland, Gerard Knop, Reiner Assevin, John Dreun and Florentius Thin for Utrecht, and E. Iargaeus for Ommelanden, in his own hand, on 13 July. Re-

units.la: LXXIX. Ferunt per noctes quas sublustres Cancrinus dies & æstivi solis fulgor faciebat...
units.tr: LXXIX. They report that through the nights, which were dimly lit by the days of Cancer and the glow of the summer sun...

units.la: Reperio in actis provinciae Carolum Roordam & Ioannem Aysmam, Delegatos difficultatem apud Lalainium signandae conventioni movisse, Lalainiumque ut proxumo Frisiorum comitio ratam praestaret, scripto obligasse. Quippe metuebant, ne ex illa tributi conventione majestatis postularentur, eamque sine speciali mandato populi, aut cautione Praefecti approbatam ex invidia facti comitium populi rescinderet. Igitur vulgato per Alexandrum Farnesium Artesiam Hannoniamque Philippi partibus assertas pro vocando Francisco Alençonio Andium Duce consultatum, arrectis in spem conventionis multorum animis, quod Audinus speciosis cum mandatis Henricum Guserium Bonivetum legatum in provincias misisset.
units.tr: I find in the records of the province that Charles Roorda and John Aysma, the delegates, raised difficulties with Lalaing about signing the convention, and that Lalaing bound himself in writing to ratify it at the next Frisian assembly. For they feared they might be prosecuted for treason on account of that tax agreement, and that the popular assembly, disapproving of the act because it had been approved without a special mandate from the people or a guarantee from the governor, might rescind it out of resentment. Therefore, when it had been spread abroad through Alexander Farnese that Artois and Hainaut had been won over to Philip's side, and that Francis of Alençon, Duke of Anjou, was being consulted about being summoned, many minds were raised in hope of an agreement, because Anjou had sent Henry Guser de Bonivet to the provinces as envoy with specious mandates.

units.la: Quorum non ignarum, qui Coloniae tractandae paci adhuc subsistebant, Ordinum mandatarij intercessionem ad pacem legatos Caesaris oravere, ne ut omni mora commodissimi temporis abrupta actioni exitum maturarent. Offerri scilicet ab Andino honesta & profutura auxilia referebant, quae tanto magis valitura essent, si communicatos cum Elisabetha Anglorum regina amores foelici matrimonio expleverit. Esse namque eo loco secreti affectus indicium, ut spem conjugalis tori promittat, arcanisque jam ante internuntijs commissem hominum famae se commiserit. Itaque fieri posse, ut Andini fortunam & simul vires posthabere regio Philippi juri incipiat, cujus exercitus in onnem insolentiam effusus exacerbet magis animos ultro ex Philippi & Praefectorum imperio a veteri dominatione alienos. Quibus post addebant, infirmari priorum foederum sanctiones & damnatis Ordinum actis de ijs ipsis ab omni dignitate removendis cogitari, ac ut regius satelles, & aulae minister res ac honores gerat, quae stante principum imperio ipsi Ordines aut eorum beneficiarij jure legitimae potestatis usurpassent. Itaq; pro eo tuendo non ante laborasse, quam Praefectorum licentia omnem regendi modum transmigrasset, & cum ipso legum excidio liberrimam gentem tributariae onere multasset. Cum novis judicijs constitutis vilissimi & imperitissimi quique ad publica officia aere aut gratia protrusi venalem remp. fecere, Ordinesque provinciarum, cum ad legum auxilia non possent, ad justa arma provocavere.
units.tr: The imperial envoys, who were still at Cologne negotiating peace, were not unaware of this. The deputies of the Estates begged them to intervene for peace, lest by delay they cut off the most favourable moment and hasten the outcome of the affair. They reported that Anjou offered honourable and advantageous aid, which would be all the more effective if he should crown the affection he shared with Elizabeth, queen of the English, with a happy marriage. For there was already a sign of secret feeling in that quarter, such that he promised hope of a marriage bed, and he had earlier entrusted himself, through secret go-betweens, to the talk of men. So it might come about that Anjou's fortune and at the same time his forces began to be preferred to the royal right of Philip, whose army, poured out into every insolence, exasperated minds all the more, already estranged from the old domination by the commands of Philip and the governors. After these things they added that the sanctions of the earlier treaties were weakened, and that the acts of the Estates had been condemned, with plans to remove from all dignity those very men, so that the king's henchman and court minister should carry out the affairs and honours which the Estates themselves, or their beneficiaries, had usurped by lawful power while the prince's rule stood. Therefore they had laboured for its defence only after the governors' licence had overstepped every rule of government, and with the very destruction of the laws had burdened the freest nation with the burden of tribute. With new courts set up, the vilest and most inexperienced men, thrust into public offices by money or favour, made the commonwealth venal; and the provincial Estates, since they could get no help from the laws, appealed to just arms.

units.la: Sed Philippi regis jus alibi examinandum esse, qui hoc scire debuisset, imperia, etsi summo majestatis jure subnixa, serviendo exerceri omnemque principatum regundo populo datum, principes quosque honestis imperandi rationibus obligasse. Igitur moderatione aliqua pacem cogitanti opus esse, ac ut opinionem quaesiti juris leniat, qui injuriae excepit. Caeterum acerrimo religionis Romanae argumento regem ac legatos stare, quod mitigari exemplo Germaniae deberet, quae privata exercitia secus sentientibus indulsisset. Non esse conscientijs denuo imperandum, neq; resuscitanda Philippi edicta tanto sanguine foedata.
units.tr: But the king's right, they said, was to be examined elsewhere, and he ought to have known this: commands, although supported by the highest right of majesty, are exercised by serving, and every prince given rule over a people has been bound to honourable methods of commanding. Therefore some moderation is needed by anyone who thinks of peace, and to soften the impression of the right sought, he who has received the injury must yield. Moreover, the king and his envoys stand firm on the strongest argument of the Roman religion, which ought to be softened by the example of Germany, which had granted private exercises to those who thought otherwise. Men's consciences must not be commanded again, nor Philip's edicts, stained with so much blood, be revived.

units.la: Albada in litteris prid. Eid. Jul. in Frisiam datis, scribit regium mandatarium de una religione articulum pertinacius confirmasse, quo Philippus Romanae religionis cura & ejus tuendae sollicitudine gratior provinciales Pontificios a reformatis caeterisque ex instituto Farnesij & Hannoniae Artesiaeque gentium divelleret. Idem addit Caesaris quoq; mandatarios de Philippici Legati pertinacia testatos, eumque in mitigando religionis articulo inexorabilem & praefractum omnem Colonien-sis & simul domesticae pacis spem praecidisse. Neque enim Pontificios in armis adversus regem perseveraturos, neque laturos Hollandis, sociosque ut suae religionis exercitio exuantur. Ita fieri non posse, ut in concordiam coalescat antiqua & a Philippo refricata animorum civilium dissensio. Quare ab Ordinum mandatariis legatis Caesaris objectum, quod plus regij mandatarij aut Philippi gratiae, quam suis arbitrijs & intercessorum aequitati dedisset.
units.tr: Albada, in letters given the day before the Ides of July and sent into Friesland, writes that the king's envoy had more stubbornly insisted on the article concerning one religion, by which Philip, more concerned with the cause and defence of the Roman religion, would tear the Papist provincials away from the reformed and others, according to the plan of Farnese and the peoples of Hainaut and Artois. The same writer adds that the imperial envoys too testified to the obstinacy of Philip's legate, and that he, inexorable and unbending in softening the article on religion, cut off all hope of peace both at Cologne and at home. For the Papists would not persist in arms against the king, nor would they bear that the Hollanders and their allies be stripped of the exercise of their religion. Thus it could not happen that the ancient dissension of civic minds, reopened by Philip, would coalesce into concord. Therefore the imperial envoys objected to the Estates' envoys that the king's envoy had given more to Philip's favour, or to his own wishes, than to their own judgments and the fairness of the mediators.

units.la: Albada notat se Comiti Suartsenbergio Legato Caesareo soluto istius die conventu, id in os exprobrasse, eundemque Suartsenbergium fiducia loquentis pudefactum leniora mandata obtulisse.
units.tr: Albada notes that when the meeting broke up that day, he reproached Count Suartsenberg, the imperial legate, to his face, and Suartsenberg, abashed by the boldness of his words, then offered milder instructions.

units.la: Itaque per Ordinum Legatos postulatum, ut sibi de singulis ad provincias referendi mandatarij Caesaris potestatem facerent & ut interea temporis arma ad bimestre differantur.
