Cujus boni certum Albadam tum praeconcepisse in ejus litteris ad Ordines Frisiae xii. Kal. Augusti scripti reperio. Hoc vero cavebat, ne Frisij delinimento militaris otij segnitiem induerent, armisque cessantibus civilem & domestici foederis concordiam luxarent. Quam Upsterani curante Hepcone Fockenio praetore Ultrajectino foederi sociati, reliquique ex Sylvestribus etsi ex Coloniensi foedere ancipites, in molliora consilia perducti. Cui rei prosperandae etiam hoc faciebat, quod Carolus Roorda & Joannes Aysma foederatorum Delegati in Frisiam Ultrajecto advenissent, foederisque sanctionem & simul commoda incertis temporum nata dubijs ingenijs commendarent. Eorum mandata erant, ut pro Julio atque Augusto mensibus residuum Tributi, quod 25000. aureorum aequabat, Frisios poscerent, pecuniamque autorandis equestribus turmis decretam pro quota tributi mille & ducentos carolaeos impetrarent.
units.tr: So the legates of the Estates demanded that the imperial commissioners be given power to refer each matter back to the provinces, and that arms be deferred for two months in the meantime. I find that Albada had clearly anticipated this outcome in his letter to the Estates of Friesland, written on the twelfth day before the Kalends of August. But he took care that the Frisians, lulled by the idleness of peace, should not grow slack and, with arms laid aside, loosen the civil and domestic concord of the covenant. Through the efforts of Hepco Fockenius, praetor of Utrecht, the men of Upsterland were joined to the Union of Utrecht, and the rest of the Sylvestrians, though wavering over the Cologne covenant, were brought to softer counsels. This also helped the cause: Carolus Roorda and Joannes Aysma, delegates of the United Provinces, had come to Friesland from Utrecht to commend the sanction of the covenant and its advantages to minds uncertain of the times and troubled by doubts. Their instructions were to demand from the Frisians the remaining tribute for the months of July and August, which amounted to 25,000 gold pieces, and to obtain the sum decreed for equipping cavalry troops, 1,200 carolus coins as their quota of the tribute.

units.la: Quare Lalainius etsi Ultrajecti haereret, litteris ix. Kal. Aug. perscriptis comitium ad viii. Eid. Aug. haberi fecit, Ordinesque plenis cum mandatis, quod res moram non ferret, adesse frequentes jussit.
units.tr: Therefore Lalaing, although he was staying at Utrecht, by a letter written on the ninth day before the Kalends of August had the assembly convened for the eighth day before the Ides of August, and he ordered the Estates to attend in full numbers with full powers, since the business would not bear delay.

units.la: Caeterum omnem comitij progressum caenobiorum Praesules morabantur, suaeque immodestiae, ut ante observantiam Gandavensis foederis, ita tum reprobatam religionis pacem obtendebant, itaque Clarecampius Antistes in coetu commotior primas istius ordinis & coenobij opibus etiam ex plebeio genere magnos spiritus gerens religionis pacem impugnabat, sociosque sui consilij Hiddingium Gerricomij Praesulis legatum atq; ipsum Docomiensium praeferebat. Unde Leovardiensis territorij mandatarij remissioribus ab Ultrajectino foedere, & simul tributo animis e Ferverdijs, Dongrijs orientalibus, Dantumanis, Octopagicis quosdam concitavere, tributique molestiam pecori gravari florem aurei exactione agrarium populum indignabantur. In ijs Menno Scheltema, Nicolaus Laurentius e Ferverdijs, e Dongrijs Wigerus Gabinius, e Collumanis Edo Alma & I. Riddersma, e Dantumanis Martinius Bootsma & Upco Buma, ex Octopagicis Haio Gerbranda fuere. Econtra e Ferverdijs Epo Douma, Igo Goslingha, Wibrandus Ailva, Poppo Feitsma, Tiesso Boetius pro Feddino Albada & Arnoldio Annio presbytero Jesumano, e Dongrijs occidentalibus Vibius Scettema, Siuckius Humalda, e Collumanis, Scipio Meckama, Mar-
units.tr: Meanwhile the abbots of the monasteries were holding up the whole progress of the assembly, and they put forward as a pretext the peace of religion, which they now rejected just as they had earlier rejected observance of the Ghent covenant, out of their own arrogance. Thus Clarecamp, the abbot, more agitated in the assembly, the first of his order and, through the wealth of his monastery, bearing great pride even though of plebeian birth, attacked the peace of religion, and he put forward as allies of his plan Hiddingius, legate of the abbot of Gerricomium, and the abbot of Dockum himself. Hence the deputies of the Leeuwarden district, who were more lax toward the Union of Utrecht, and at the same time some men from Ferwerd, East Dongeradeel, Dantumadiel and Achtkarspelen were stirred up by the tribute, and the country folk were indignant that the tax burden fell heavily on their cattle and that the gold florin was being exacted from their fields. Among them were Menno Scheltema, Nicolaus Laurentius from Ferwerd, Wigerus Gabinius from East Dongeradeel, Edo Alma and I. Riddersma from Kollumerland, Martinus Bootsma and Upco Buma from Dantumadiel, and Haio Gerbranda from Achtkarspelen. On the other side, from Ferwerd, Epo Douma, Igo Goslingha, Wibrandus Ailva, Poppo Feitsma and Tiesso Boetius stood for Feddinus Albada and Arnoldus Annius, presbyter of Jesum; from West Dongeradeel, Vibius Scettema and Siuckius Humalda; from Kollumerland, Scipio Meckama, Mar-

units.la: Martinus Schonenburgius pendendum tributum è jure Ultrajectini fœderis recipiebant, reliquíque Ooftergoï, in quibus Tietzerckij, Idarđij & Raverdij erant, scriptis obtestationibus adversabantur. Erant namque qui ostenderent accidi tributum ex egentiâ rerum non posse, ultimæque legi, quæ exceptionem non pateretur petentibus socijs se obligasse. Trahendum scilicet collato ære bellum esse, cui pendendo se ultro offerebant, qui alijs etiam mandatis distracti privatas facultates & earum impendia saluti publicæ offerebant. Neq; minoribus contractionibus Westergoï exercebantur, donec autoritate Lalainij & interventu Senatus languelcerent. Creditum fuit, Lalainium quod isti rei Ultrajecti se interposuisset, vehementius intercessisse, tributumque tanquam salubre sui imperij subsidium durioribus ingenijs imperasse.
units.tr: Martinus Schonenburgius and his party held that the tribute must be paid by the right of the Union of Utrecht, while the rest of Oostergo, among whom were the men of Tietzerck, Idaard and Raverd, opposed it with written protests. Some argued that the tax could not be paid because goods were scarce, and that the last law, which admitted no exception, had bound them to their allies only on the condition of the petition. Clearly the war had to be carried on with pooled money, and those who were distracted by other duties offered their private means and their expenses to the public safety, of their own accord, to pay for it. Westergo was troubled by smaller disputes too, until they subsided through the authority of Lalaing and the mediation of the Senate. It was believed that Lalaing, because he had interposed himself in this matter at Utrecht, opposed it more vehemently and imposed the tribute on the harsher minds as a wholesome support for his rule.

units.la: F. Nicolaus tradit post longas altercationes, quadraginta octo aureorum millia stipendijs militum & promovendo fœderi decreta libellumque supplicem ad Aurantium principem recuperandis cænobij Mariengardensis reditibus, quos à Matthia Gubernatore clam Canonici obtinuerant, per Hesselum Aÿsma remissum.
units.tr: Friar Nicolaus reports that after long disputes, forty-eight thousand gold pieces were decreed for the soldiers' pay and for promoting the covenant, together with a suppliant petition to Prince Orange to recover the revenues of the Mariengarde monastery, which the canons had secretly obtained from Governor Matthias, the petition being sent through Hessel Aysma.

units.la: Scribit Heymannus inclinante Julio horrendam tempestatem emersisse, præterque virum Dresumi in Dantumanis fulmine percussum, pecora quoque circa Oostmahornam littus pascentia cœlesti igne icta.
units.tr: Heymann writes that in late July a dreadful storm broke out; besides a man of Dresum struck by lightning in Dantumadiel, cattle grazing on the shore near Oostmahorn were also struck by fire from heaven.

units.la: Tum præsidente Adio Lambertio consule in Leovardiæ civitatis jus, quod cudendæ monetæ habuerat, publicè inquisitum, istique rei testimonium à senioribus civium in Senatu dictum. At Doccomij inter Magistratum ac primores oppidi de Ultrajectino fœdere disceptatum, à quo post reliquos urbium Magistratus in fœdus adscitos, Doccomiensium Senatum Pontificiorum immodestia abstraxerat. Cui malo fomentum addebat, quod Cornelius Lutenius Consul, ad comitium provinciæ missus, mandato Senatus signandum fœdus dissuaderet, populique consilio vanis & fallacibus sermonibus effugia captaret. Igitur primores civitatis, præterito Magistratu non dissimulando quæ agerentur, Ultrajectinum in fœdus recepti, additâ obtestatione. Ut quod contra dictum aut factum à Senatu esset, id paci publicæ & commodo civitatis adversum haberetur. Id prid. Non. Augusti in actum relatum ac à Tacone Ailva, Suffrido Vrielsma, Henrico Bra Medico, Joanne Marsemio, Herone Sixti, Tiepcone Vibio, Sibrando Ripkenio, Tiebbone Jelgerio, Henrico Joannis, Georgio Francisci, Andræa Edonio, Sixto Joannis, Francisco Francisci, Bernardo Luneburgio, Romberto Ofkenio, & Wibrando Hermanno signatum. Quod in comitium provinciæ, quod tum habebatur, perlatum, oppidanorum, qui cum agrarijs dissidebant partes, ex concordiâ recepti fœderis firmavit.
units.tr: Then, with Adio Lambertius presiding as consul, the right the city of Leeuwarden had held to mint coin was publicly investigated, and testimony on the matter was given in the Senate by the elders of the citizens. At Dokkum, however, the Union of Utrecht was debated among the magistrates and leading men of the town. The Senate there, drawn away by the arrogance of the Papists, had held back from the covenant, after the other city magistracies had been admitted to it. Adding fuel to this evil, Cornelius Lutenius, consul, sent to the provincial assembly, urged against sealing the covenant by order of the Senate, and with empty and deceptive speeches sought escapes for the people's counsel. Therefore the leading men of the city, passing over the magistracy and not concealing what was being done, were received into the Union of Utrecht with an added oath: whatever was said or done against it by the Senate should be held adverse to public peace and the welfare of the city. This was enacted on the day before the Nones of August and signed by Tacco Aylva, Suffridus Vriesma, Henricus Bra the physician, Joannes Marsemius, Heron Sixti, Tiepco Vibius, Sibrandus Ripkenius, Tiebbo Jelgerius, Henricus Joannis, Georgius Francisci, Andreas Edonius, Sixtus Joannis, Franciscus Francisci, Bernardus Luneburgius, Romberdus Ofkenius and Wibrandus Hermanni. This was carried to the provincial assembly then being held, and by the agreed terms of the covenant it confirmed the townsmen who differed with the country folk.

units.la: Igitur post longas in conventu Ordinum disceptationes, quæ ex menstruo tributo fiebant, decretum, ut negotium arbitris ex supremo Senatu Joanni Versteverano & Fecconi Rhalæ permitteretur, ijque cum Lalainio præfecto controversiam tributi definirent. Cautione tamen addita, ne quid juri oppidanis in causâ suffragij quæsito illo judicio decederet. Ita pro Leovardiensibus M. Wigerius, Joannes Aÿsma, pro Bolsuerdijs Petrus Vibius & Jacobus Jacobæus, pro Franequerensibus Julius Bottnia Oldermannus & Regnerus Francisci, pro Snecanis Ni-
units.tr: Therefore after long debates in the assembly of the Estates, which arose over the monthly tribute, it was decreed that the matter be entrusted to arbiters from the Supreme Council, Joannes Versteveren and Feccon Rhala, who with Lalaing the prefect should settle the dispute over the tribute. A caveat was added, however, that nothing of the townspeople's right to a vote in the matter, sought in that judgment, should be lost. So for Leeuwarden, M. Wigerius and Joannes Aysma; for Bolsward, Petrus Vibius and Jacobus Jacobaeus; for Franeker, Julius Bottnia, alderman, and Regnerus Francisci; for Sneek, Ni-

units.la: cIↄ. Iↄ. LXXIX. colaus Aitsonius, Olpherdus Francisci, pro Harlingijs Gerbrandus Gosfius, cum Vibio Joannis, pro Doccomiensibus, Jacobus Gabinius, pro Worcumijs Hiddo Jarichius & Epco Meius, pro Staurijs Jacobus Edsius & Albertus Florentius, pro Ilstanis Bonno Petræus, pro Slotanis, Simon Potterus iv. Eid. Aug. subscriptores.
units.tr: 1579. Nicolaus Aitsonius and Olpherdus Francisci; for Harlingen, Gerbrandus Gosfius, with Vibius Joannis; for Dokkum, Jacobus Gabinius; for Workum, Hiddo Jarichius and Epco Meius; for Stavoren, Jacobus Edsius and Albertus Florentius; for Hindeloopen, Bonno Petraeus; for Slotanis, Simon Potterus. They signed as subscribers on the fourth day before the Ides of August.

units.la: Quo die à Feicone Tatmanno Utingeranorum Prætore fœdus Ultrajectinum approbatum reperio, Pontificiosque serendis per provinciam discordijs & seditionibus occupatos, agros passim infestis grassatoribus implevisse. Quare frænandæ prædonum insolentiæ remedia petita, volentibus, agrarijs ut agris ac villis prædo amoveretur, Lalainiusque procurandæ paci publicæ recepto ritu præsidia cohortium per cænobia disponeret. Neque enim loca illa, ut ajebant, tot flagitijs & tantâ impietate profanata eximenda molestijs esse, & habendos melius provinciales, qui fœdere nexi, liberos, conjuges, bona atq; corpora saluti publicæ obligavissent. Passim scilicet cædibus & rapinis provinciam sterni, non alijs autoribus, quam qui signa & sacramenta mentientes, aut Pontificum sacris innexi certissimum confusionis instrumentum populares discordias seminarent. Ab ijs intra urbem comitiorum turbas insolentiam & rapinas per agros excerceri fierique ut speratæ libertatis incrementa tardius adolescant. Mitti clam per provincias, qui regis & Hispanorum res gerant, Farnesiumque inter arma libertati minacia, exploratorum quoque ope invalescere. Neque enim alio fine Joannem Roordam ex imperio Coloniâ in Frisiam & Translavicanos missum, quam ut à fœderè Ordinum plurimos deterrendo regis gratiam & affectum ducendis popularibus animis offerret. Eosque distrahendo concordiam & simul vires fœderatæ gentis dissolveret. Igitur libellus supplex Lalainio & Delegatis fœderatorum Ordinum, qui ad conventum viii. Eid. Aug. indictum advenerant, hunc in modum oblatus.
units.tr: On that same day I find that the Union of Utrecht was approved by Feicon Tatmannus, praetor of the Utingerani. The Papists, busy sowing discord and sedition throughout the province, had filled the fields everywhere with hostile marauders. Therefore remedies were sought to restrain the insolence of these robbers: the country folk wanted the robbers removed from their fields and farms, and Lalaing, in the accustomed manner for securing public peace, set garrisons of cohorts through the monasteries. For those places, they said, profaned by so many crimes and such impiety, should not be exempt from these burdens, and the provincials, who by covenant had bound their children, wives, goods and persons to public safety, were better trusted. Clearly the province was being strewn with slaughter and plunder everywhere, and the authors were none other than those who, feigning signs and sacraments or bound to the rites of the Pontiffs, sowed the most certain instrument of confusion, popular discord. From them came the tumults of the assemblies within the city, insolence and robbery through the countryside, and so the growth of the hoped-for liberty matures more slowly. Men were being sent secretly through the provinces to carry on the king's and the Spaniards' business, and Farnese, a threat to liberty in arms, grew stronger also through spies. For Joannes Roorda was sent from the imperial city of Cologne into Friesland and the regions beyond the Lauwers, for no other purpose than to deter most of the Estates from the Union, to offer the king's favour and goodwill to lead popular minds, and by dividing them to dissolve the concord and at the same time the strength of the united nation. Therefore a suppliant petition was presented in this manner to Lalaing and to the delegates of the united Estates who had come to the assembly summoned for the eighth day before the Ides of August.

units.la: INTELLEXIMUS, PRAEFECTE & Delegati ORDINUM, nonnullos ex Oostergois, ac Westergois Ordinum nomen mentitos, scriptum quoddam evulgasse, actis fœderum & religionis paci tum mandatis MATTHIAE Gubernatoris, AURANTIJ Principis & Concilij STATUS Ordinumq; generalium adversum. Quod approbare cum patriæ leges & nostra fœdera vetent, ita palam tanquam vitio natam, rescindimus. Præterquam cujus quod invalidis procurationibus aut suffragio publico infirmatis eorum immodestia stet, ita in illorum potestate non fuit priorum temporum fœdera & conventiones, acta & mandata Ordinum subvertere. Igitur cum solâ Romanâ religione stare divinum cultum & exercitia fidei velint, societatis antiquæ vim ac reverentiam tollunt, fœderumque solemnium ruptores clandestinis conspirationibus se tuentur. In quorum numero & illi sunt, qui Joannis Roordæ arcano colloquio instructi pacis nomine bellum velant, hostilium consiliorum interpretes. Qui serendo falsa & à verò alienâ fœdus Ultrajectinum ex gravitate tributi respuunt. Quasi certè sub antiquo PHILIPPI & insolentium Præfectorum imperio, inter honoraria & donativa non sudaverit populi ærarium, cujus exhausti angustia ultimam in egestatem florentissimam olim provinciam protrusisset. Nunc Præter ista mala, dissensiones ac turbas seri & hoc agi ut Hispania per Frisiam dominationis vestigia extent Frisijque sijque vicinis nationibus jure fœderum connexi, repudiatâ Ordinum societate, regijs rectoribus se permittant. Cui malo quo occurri possit, petimus Præfecte, ut turbida & fovendis seditionibus exercita ingenia comitio prohibens suspectosque maleficij & violatæ pacis adscitis in consilium arbitris corrigas. Hoc etiam addimus, ut æquali cum socijs tributo haberi nos facias omnisque inter agrarios oppidanosque dissensio tuo & arbitrorum interventu cesset.
units.tr: We have understood, Prefect and Delegates of the Estates, that some men from Oostergo and Westergo, falsely using the name of the Estates, have published a certain writing against the acts of the covenants and of religious peace, against the mandates of Governor Matthias, Prince Orange, the Council of State and the general Estates. Since the laws of the country and our covenants forbid us to approve it, we openly rescind it as born of a defect. Besides, their presumption rests on invalid proxies or on votes weakened by public suffrage, and it was not within their power to overturn the covenants and agreements, acts and mandates of the Estates of earlier times. Therefore, since they wish divine worship and the exercise of faith to stand only with the Roman religion, they destroy the force and reverence of the ancient alliance, and as breakers of solemn covenants they shelter themselves behind secret conspiracies. Among their number are also those who, having been instructed in a secret conference with Joannes Roorda, veil war under the name of peace; they are interpreters of hostile designs. They sow falsehoods, alien to the truth, and reject the Union of Utrecht on account of the burden of the tribute. As if, indeed, under the old rule of Philip and his insolent prefects, the people's treasury had not sweated over honoraria and gifts, whose exhausted poverty had thrust the once flourishing province into final want. Now, besides these evils, dissensions and disturbances are being sown, and the aim is that traces of Spanish dominion should remain through Friesland, and that the Frisians, bound by the law of covenants to neighbouring nations, should repudiate the society of the Estates and entrust themselves to royal governors. To meet this evil, we ask, Prefect, that you restrain minds turbulent and practised in fostering sedition, bar from the assembly those suspected of mischief and of violating the peace, and correct them with arbiters taken into counsel. We add this too: that you have us held to tribute equal with our allies, and that all dissension between the country folk and the townsfolk cease through your intervention and that of the arbiters.

units.la: Id ııı. Eid. Aug. perscriptum.
units.tr: Written on the third day before the Ides of August.

units.la: Notant Scriptores, in Geesterlandiæ finibus quatuor mangonés ex eodem agro & Donieverstallensi coëmendis equis, profectos ab Ordinum equitatu spoliatos, unumque glande transverberatum natale solum suo sanguine imbuisse. Igitur Ioanne Rorda Iureconsulto, qui Farnefij negotia in Frisijs clam gesserat, Groningam profecto, in ejus consilia à Senatu quoque Groningano inquisitum deprehensoque Farnesij arcana illo tanquam internuncio turbandis provincijs gesta, de ejus custodia deliberatum. In quam per publicos urbis spiculatores pertractus gravissimas de se suspiciones auxit, quasi omnem pacis publicæ rationem per ipsam quoque Frisiam secretis colloquijs conturbavisset. Unde à Frisiæ Ordinibus literæ Groningam datæ, quibus petebant, ut ad habendum rei examen legatus provinciæ admitteretur, audiendisque arcanis Roordæ hostiumque consilijs interesset. Quo impetrato legatus Groningam missus, ipseque Roorda civici tumultus & seditionis crimine gravatus arctiore custodiâ obseptus est. Qui Groningâ Leovardiam dein in arcem Stauriæ amotus, Woerdano & post Rammekensi in Zelandiâ carcere infaustæ legationis præmio multatus est. Sed Leovardiæ populi comitium, quod in x. Kal. Sept. protractum.
units.tr: The writers note that in the territory of Geesterland four horse-dealers, who had set out from the same district to buy horses at Donieverstal, were robbed by the cavalry of the States, and one of them, struck by a sling-stone, stained his native soil with his blood. Then Johannes Rorda, a jurist who had secretly carried on Farnese's business in Friesland, went to Groningen. The Groningen Senate also began an inquiry into his plans, and when it discovered that he had acted as Farnese's secret go-between to disturb the provinces, it deliberated about his custody. Brought in by the city's public officers, he increased the very grave suspicions against him, since it was thought that by secret conferences he had also disturbed the public peace in Friesland itself. Hence the Estates of Friesland sent a letter to Groningen asking that a deputy of the province be admitted to hold the examination of the matter and to be present for the hearing of Rorda's secrets and the plans of the enemy. This was granted, and the deputy was sent to Groningen. Rorda himself, charged with the crime of civil tumult and sedition, was kept under closer guard. From Groningen he was then moved to the castle at Leeuwarden in Stavoren, and afterwards to the prison at Woerden and then at Rammekens in Zeeland, and he paid for his unhappy embassy with these penalties. But at Leeuwarden the assembly of the people, which had been put off to 23 August, ...

units.la: Cl. Franckena notat turbulentis dissensionibus fervescebat, volente Præsulum Ordine, ne à pacis Gandavensis conventione recederetur, & ne onera tributi Ultrajectino ex fœdere præstarentur. Quæ res, cum sefcessionem procerum spectaret, ab agrarijs, oppidanis Biltanisq; inter quos disceptatum erat, tota lis arbitrio Lalainij & Supremi Senatus permissum. In eo namq; suprema difficultas versebatur, ut tributum quod in bimestre ad 48000 aureorum depacta provincia erat, æquis inter agrarios oppidanosq; portionibus divideretur, ijque ipsi certâ quantitate tributi pro ratione oppidorum tenerentur. Itaque à Præfecto Senatuq, decretum: Ut oppidani nonam, Biltani 2 5. tributi provincialis partem penderent, ijque durante bello, salvo partium jure, confessem & suffragia in comitijs haberent. Agrorum quoque tributum ex floreno aureo peteretur, colligereturque ocyus, ejusque onus proprietarij coloni sustinerent. Pecuniam quoque, sed sub deductione coloni in promptu præstarent, oppidanique modum colligendi per oppida tributi rite perscriptum in comitio exhiberent, quo à præfecto Senatuque statuatur, quod ex usu sit. Id in acta relatum, ac xviiiKalend. Sept. signatum.
units.tr: Cl. Franckena notes that the quarrels were growing hot, since the Order of the Prelates wished that no departure be made from the Pacification of Ghent, and that the tribute owed under the Union of Utrecht be paid. Since this matter touched the secession of the nobles, the whole dispute, in which the country people and the townsmen and the Bildts were involved, was left to the decision of Lalaing and the Supreme Council. The chief difficulty lay in this: the tribute which the province had agreed to pay for two months, amounting to 48,000 gold pieces, had to be divided between the country people and the townsmen in equal shares, and each group was to be held to a fixed amount of tribute according to the number of towns. So the Governor and the Senate decreed that the townsmen should pay one-ninth and the Bildts two-fifths of the provincial tribute, and that these should, while the war lasted and without prejudice to the rights of the parties, keep their seats and votes in the assemblies. The land tax was also to be demanded at the rate of one gold florin and collected more quickly, and the landowners and the tenant farmers were to bear its burden. They were also to pay the money promptly, with the tenant's share deducted, and the townsmen were to present in the assembly the duly written method of collecting the tribute in the towns, so that the Governor and the Senate might decide what was expedient. This was entered in the records and signed on 15 August.

units.la: Mox inter oppidanos portio tributi definita ac à Delegatis Senatus Ioanne Versteverano, Feccone Rhala, Gisberto Aernsma & Sibrando Richaeo pronuntiatum, ut solvendo millium quadringentorum sexaginta sex & 13. stufferorum tributo, Leovardij mille quingentos, octoginta sex Caro-
units.tr: Soon afterwards the share of the tribute for the townsmen was fixed and announced by the delegates of the Senate, Johannes Versteveen, Feccio Rhala, Gijsbert Aernsma and Sibrandus Richaeus: that, in paying the tribute of 466,130 stuivers, Leeuwarden should pay 1,586 Carolus guilders,

units.la: Oppidani nonam tributi Frisiæ partem exsolvere jussi.
units.tr: The townsmen were ordered to pay one-ninth of the tribute of Friesland.

units.la: cIↄ. Iↄ. Carolæos, Bolsuerdij octingentos, quinquaginta Snecani, & Franekerenses sexcentos, Harlingani & Doccomienses quingentos, Worcumij trecentos & viginti, Staurij ducentos viginti quinque, Ilstani centum & triginta, Slotenses nonaginta, Hindelopij sexaginta carolæos 13. stuferos bimestri tributo præstarent. Hæc actis inserta ac Francisci Bandimontij Graphiarij manu signata.
units.tr: 1500 Carolus guilders, Bolsward 850, Sneek 850, Franeker 600, Harlingen and Dokkum 500, Workum 320, Stavoren 225, Ilst 130, Sloten 90, and Hindeloopen 60 Carolus guilders and 13 stuivers, were to pay for the two-month tribute. These things were entered in the records and signed by the hand of the clerk Franciscus Bandimontius.

units.la: Cæterum ne hæc quidem præstandis bello subsidijs scripta transactio duravit. Erant quippe ex oppidanis & præsertim minoribus, qui rata commercia, exhaustos præsidiorum insolentiâ cives, quererentur mare; alibi turbidum & littori infestum inopem populum fecisse. Econtra Leovardiam pingui ac fertili solo sitam, commercio & opibus, sicut reliqua majora oppida, florentem, præstandis tributis parem esse, quæ conferre ij in ærarium non possent, quos non animus juvandi socios sed facultas destitueret. Itaque mitigatâ sententiâ per supremi Senatus arbitros latâ inter ipsos oppidanos rejecta in novos arbitros Meinardum Wigerium, Jacobum Jacobæum, Jacobum Idzium, Econem Isbrandium controversiâ conventum: ut à Leovardijs mille septingenti septuaginta quinque, à Bolsuerdijs octingenti triginta, à Franequerensibus septingenti octoginta quatuor, à Snecanis quingenti viginti quatuor, ab Harlingijs quadringenti quinquaginta, à Doccomiensibus quadrigenti, à Worcumijs ducenti viginti quatuor, à Staurijs centum & viginti quinque, ab Ilstanis centum, à Slotensibus sexaginta, 13. stuff. ab Hindelopijs quinquaginta in bimestre tributum penderentur. Ita xiv. Kal. Sept. in comitio pronuntiatum.
units.tr: But even this agreement, written about paying the war subsidies, did not last. For some of the townsmen, especially of the smaller towns, complained that the sea, which had kept their trade going, had been made turbulent and hostile to the shore, and that their citizens were drained by the insolence of the garrisons and the people were left poor. On the other hand, they said that Leeuwarden, set in rich and fertile soil and flourishing in trade and wealth, like the other larger towns, was able to pay the tributes, while those who could not pay into the treasury were not lacking in will to help their allies but in means. So the decision was softened by the arbiters of the Supreme Senate, and then, the award being rejected among the townsmen themselves, new arbiters, Meinard Wiger, Jacob Jacobs, Jacob Idzes and Eco Isbrand, were agreed upon to settle the dispute: that for two months Leeuwarden should pay 1,775, Bolsward 830, Franeker 784, Sneek 524, Harlingen 450, Dokkum 400, Workum 224, Stavoren 125, Ilst 100, Sloten 60, and Hindeloopen 50 stuivers in tribute. This was announced in the assembly on 18 August.

units.la: Igitur æquato inter oppidanos tributo cujus egentiam in tantâ mole ac fœlicitate rerum suarum Lalainius non dissimulabat in agrarios qui Præsulum factiones tuebantur acerrimè invectus laudatâq; civitatum in patriam & libertatem fide proditionis & Hispanicarum partium turbulentissimos agrariorum insimulavit. Qui cum mandatis suis se stare modestâ excusatione testarentur, deque tributis cæterisque, quæ majestatis jure populum obligarent, relationes ad suos instituendas obicerent, acrius Lalainij animum pupugere, ut solet illâ ætate moderandis affectibus infirmum. Itaque (inquit) hoc inaudio, si illi, qui vestrarum partium sunt, cum Hispanis faciant, ex ijsdem & vos esse, quorum tamen consilia propediem detecturus sum. Unde proponi quædam redigique in acta fecit, quo de singulis interea suos docerent, ac ad xxv. Aug. comitio se sisterent: Acta hæc erant.
units.tr: Therefore, with the tribute now equalised among the townsmen, Lalaing, who did not hide the poverty of the people amid the great burden and good fortune of their own affairs, inveighed most bitterly against the country people, who defended the factions of the prelates. He praised the cities for their loyalty to the fatherland and liberty, and accused the country people, who were most turbulent, of treachery and of siding with Spain. When they declared with modest excuse that they stood by their instructions, and objected that they must report to their own people about the tributes and the other matters which bind the people by the right of sovereignty, Lalaing's spirit was stung more sharply, as is usual in an age that is weak at controlling its passions. "Therefore," he said, "I hear that if those who belong to your party make an alliance with the Spaniards, you too are of the same kind, and I shall soon uncover your plans." Hence he had certain things proposed and entered in the records, so that they might instruct their people about each point in the meantime, and present themselves at the assembly on 25 August. These were the records.

units.la: Quandoquidem provinciæ quædam contra datam fidem & jus fœderum, desertâ Ordinum generalium societate, cum Hispanis patriæ hostibus se conjunxerunt, necessarium & utile duxi hoc ipso conventu quædam perscribere, sub illâ cautione, ut quique in suo distrietu, signo campanæ dato & denuntiatione ad populum factâ, advocatis insuper prætoribus & eorum actuarijs postulata mea exhibeant, populumque suffragij jure pollentem ad decernendum compellant. Hoc etiam mando, ut ad diem Lunæ proxumum denuo ad comitium redeant, & quidem illi, qui patriæ amantissimi reprimendis hostibus fortunas, vitam atque sanguinem impendere libertati constituunt. Quod ut faciant, plenâ agendi consulendique potestate instructos esse volo, quo declarent an in generalium OrdiOrdinum societate perseverare, an defectorum exemplo in Hispanorum hostium que partes transfire in animum induxerint. Praeter haec pendendis tributis, comparandis commeatibus caeterisque rebus tres stuferos in singulas cerevisiae tonnas praestari cupio, & ut de modo è conquirendi tributi pacificè consultent. Reliquos privata foedera cum Hispanis agitantes & mandata isti rei adferentes notari, eorumque nomina actis perscribi volo, quo à me statuatur, quod ex republica sit. Id xix. Aug. in acta relatum.
units.tr: Since certain provinces, against their pledged faith and the right of the treaties, have deserted the society of the General Estates and joined themselves with the Spanish enemies of the fatherland, I have judged it necessary and useful to lay down certain things in this very assembly, with this caution: that each person in his own district, once the bell has been sounded and a proclamation made to the people, and with the magistrates and their secretaries also summoned, shall present my demands and compel the people, who have the right of voting, to decide. I also order that they return to the assembly again on the next Monday, and indeed those who, most loving of the fatherland, resolve to risk their fortunes, life and blood for liberty in restraining the enemies. In order that they do so, I wish them to be furnished with full power to act and to deliberate, so that they may declare whether they have resolved to persevere in the society of the General Estates, or, following the example of the deserters, to pass over to the side of the Spanish enemies. Besides these things, I wish three stuivers to be paid on each tun of beer for paying the tributes, procuring provisions and other necessities, and that they consult peaceably about the method of collecting the tribute. I want those who are negotiating private treaties with the Spaniards and bringing commissions for that business to be noted, and their names to be written into the records, so that I may decide what is good for the commonwealth. Entered in the records on 19 August.

units.la: Tum Deputatique in annum ex Oostergois Scipio Meckama, Renicus Cammingha, è Westergois Ianco Osingha, Orichius Doihemus, è Sylvestribus Barthius Idsaerda & Auco Edonius, ex oppidanis Gellius Sibæus & Douwo Sixma creati. Eorum mandata erant:
units.tr: Then the deputies for the year were chosen: from the Oostergo, Scipio Meckama, Reinier Cammingha; from the Westergo, Jancko Osinga, Orichius Doihema; from the Sylvestrian district, Barthius Idsaerda and Auco Edonius; and from the townsmen, Gellius Sibaeus and Douwe Sixma. Their instructions were these:

units.la: Ut cum Lalainio Rennebergio Regis Hispaniae hereditarij domini & archigubernatoris nomine Romani imperij per Frisiam omne adversus jura, privilegia, statuta, consuetudines tam agrorum quam oppidorum ullo modo introductum, rescindi facerent, eademque jura ac privilegia adversum quosvis provinciae adferent. Gandavense foedus inter Ordines generales & Aurantium Principem cum Hollandis ac Zelandis ictum, deniq; Vniónem generalem & religionis pacem, cum Vltrajectino foedere integrum curarent, & quidem ex veteri formula ne quid detrimenti. Regium censum, tuendae olim provinciae regi indultum defendendae Frisiae applicarent, cænobiorumque vacantium reditus, deducto ære alieno, ijsdem usibus impenderent. Omne publicum aggeres, vias, aquarum ductus catarractas caeterasque illasa praestarent. Inquirendi in officiales, agendique quod ex usu foret jus esset. Pensio annua, quibus extra urbem domicilium esset quadringentorum, reliquis trecentorum assignaretur. Salarium non nisi volentibus partibus daretur. Deputatis extra provinciam ire fas non esset, quoscunque vellent ad Archiducem Matthiam, Aurantium, generales Ordines & foederatos Vltrajectinos stabiliendo juri publico ablegare illorum potestatis foret. Legati impendio iii. Carol. & 10. stuff. in diem haberentur. Deputatis comitium indicendi jus esset. Ijdem, potestate rationum magistris nupero comitio abrogata rationibus praeessent. Exauctoratos ob rem damnosè gestam ad rationes cogerent, easque in ordinem & aerarium referrent. Morbo aut gravi causâ, quo minus conventui interesse possint, impeditis substituendi ad illum actum quempiam jus esset. Deputati mandata quotannis in comitio deponerent, deque ære expenso sub actuarij manu commentarium facerent, eumque comitio exhiberent. Tabella quinquaginta carolæorum summam excedens, omnium Deputatorum manu ac scriptura signaretur. Nemo à conventu, nisi morbo aut aliâ ex causâ præpeditus, & sub pœnâ duorum aureorum Philippicorum abesset. Mandata Deputatorum Ordines rata, sub indemnitatis & ratihabitionis clausulâ præstarent.
units.tr: That they should cause all that has been introduced anywhere in Friesland against the rights, privileges, statutes and customs, both of the country people and of the towns, to be rescinded by Lalaing Rennenberg, in the name of the King of Spain, hereditary lord and archgovernor of the Roman Empire, and that they should bring these same rights and privileges against any who oppose the province. That they should see to it that the Ghent treaty concluded between the General Estates and William Prince of Orange with Holland and Zeeland, and finally the General Union and the religious peace, be kept intact together with the Utrecht treaty, and indeed according to the old formula, lest any harm come of it. That they should apply the royal tax, once granted to the province for its defence, to the defence of Friesland, and devote the revenues of the vacant monasteries, after the debt has been deducted, to the same uses. That they should provide for all public dykes, roads, water channels, sluices, and other such things. That they should have the right to inquire into the officials and to act as is expedient. That the annual pension should be assigned, four hundred to those whose residence is outside the city, and three hundred to the rest. That a salary should not be given except to those willing to take it. That the deputies may not go outside the province, but whomever they wish to send to Archduke Matthias, Orange, the General Estates and the Utrecht allies, to establish public law, it is within their power to dispatch. That the envoys should be kept at the expense of three Carolus guilders and ten stuivers a day. That the deputies should have the right of calling an assembly. That the same deputies, with the power of the accountants abolished at the recent assembly, should preside over the accounts. That they should compel those dismissed for having managed badly to render their accounts, and should bring them back into order and into the treasury. That if anyone is prevented from attending the meeting by illness or some serious cause, he has the right to substitute someone for that business. That the deputies should lay down their instructions every year in the assembly, and make a record of the money spent under the hand of the clerk, and present it to the assembly. That a table exceeding the sum of fifty Carolus guilders be signed by the hand and writing of all the deputies. That no one be absent from the meeting unless hindered by illness or another cause, and under penalty of two Philippine gold pieces. That the Estates should ratify the instructions of the deputies, under the clause of indemnity and ratification.

units.la: Hoc à Docone Martna, Julio Bottnia, Epone Douma Hallemio, Livio Beiemo, Foppio Grovensteinio, F. Tatmanno, T. Wikelio, & Meinardo Wigerio iii. Kal. Sept signata.
units.tr: Signed here by Docon Martna, Julius Bottnia, Epo Douma Hallemius, Livius Beiemus, Foppius Grovensteinius, F. Tatmannus, T. Wikelius and Meinardus Wigerius, on the third day before the Kalends of September.

units.la: Quo tempore Ultrajectino quoque & foederato consessui novae leges scripta. Istae erant. ●
units.tr: At that time new rules were also drawn up for the assembly of Utrecht and the confederated states. They were these.

units.la: Ut certus numerus Delegatorum esset ac è Geldris, Hollandis Frisijs, Vltrajectinis terni, è Zelandis, Antverpiensibus, Gandavensibus & Iprensibus bini
units.tr: That there should be a fixed number of delegates: three each from Gelderland, Holland, Friesland and Utrecht, and two each from Zeeland, Antwerp, Ghent and Ypres.

units.la: Fff bini legerentur, Ii provincias, civitates earundem are atque sumptibus mu-nirent, plenâq; potestate definiendi causas fœderis acceptâ, conflandi ad 50000. tributi etiam sine mandato suo arbitratu jus haberent. Præfectos provinciarum unum aut plures, qui absentium nomine in consessu consideant, constituendi jus foret. Provincijs unum quoque mense & qui cum reliquis consulant, ex delegatis suis revocare liberum esset. Qui in consessu delegabuntur procurationum formulis, aut fiduciarijs litteris rité instructi publicæ provinciarum saluti sacramentum dicent, omniaque sine dissimulatione aut conniventiâ, odio aut gratiâ se fa-cturos, neque evulgaturos consilia promittent. Iuramenti formula actis publicis insereretur, additoque mense & quovis die à dicentibus signaretur. Conventus singulis diebus haberetur, isque à Kal. April. ad priduanum Octobris diem à septimâ matutinâ in undecimum à Kal. Octobris in Kal. April. ab octavâ matutinâ in duodecimam esset. Pomeridianæ consultationes à tertiâ in quintam desinerent. Si graves causæ poscerent, convocandi Delegatos Præsidi jus esset. Dies Dominicus divino cultui dictus conventum non admitteret, Mercuriique aut Veneris diebus pomeridianus nunquam, nisi exigente necessitate, haberent. Præses collegij, muneri par & molestiæ in xiv. dies crearetur. Ejus officij foret singula proponere, sententias perrogare, eoque facto ex formulâ scripti fœderis statuere, denique in Senatu verba facientibus prompte respondere, facere>que Præsidis sit. Qui aliquid in consessu proposuissent, dum quid statutum esset, eo excederent. In extraordinarijs conventibus si vocati non compareant, nulla eorum ratio, præsidi cum cæteris definiendi, quod ex re, potestas sit. Nulli in conventu, quicquam proponere, præterquam præsidi aut assessoribus fas foret. Reliqui quod proponi velint, scripto Præsidi exhiberent, qui pro re natâ copiam dicendi faciet. Præses suffragia ex ordine colligeret, ea non nisi rogati ferrent, interrumpendi facultas, nulli præterquam sub pœnâ silentij esset. In suffragijs ferendis unum tantum provinciæ nomine suffragium foret. Decreta collegij in acta referri Præses curaret, eaque majoris momenti visitanda collegis exhiberet. Præsidi præterquam æquivalentibus sententijs, nullum & nisi requisitum suffragium esset. Illi ordinatè ac benè res gerenti præmium statueretur. Nemo à conventu non nisi de consensu collegij abesset, legationes, judicia, examinationes partium, non detrectaret, id faciens in posterum consessu abstineret. Vacationes & officia Collegij distribuerentur. Speciale mandatum rem pecuniariam distributuri acciperent. Ij æraria, stipendia militum, reliquasque pecuniæ erogationes curarent, rationes seorsim contra quæstores, reliquosque publici æris acceptores conficerent. Isti negotio unus è Geldris, Hollandis & Ultraiectinis præesset. Commeatus & annonæ cura uni itidem è Geldris, Hollandis ac Frisijs demandaretur. Militares res, ut recensiones copiarum præsidia tribunorum officia, stratagemata, explorationes munitionesque locorum è Geldris, Hollandis, Zelandis, Antverpiensibus & Gandensibus tractarent. Reliquis juris dicundi & politeiæ, tam sæcularis, quam ecclesiasticæ administratio, pacis publicæ, concordiæ, libellorum supplicum, rescriptorum cura committeretur, idque uni è Zelandis, Frisijs, Ultrajectinis, Antverpiensibus & Iprensibus incumberet. Præses ista observari operam navaret, rataque singula faceret, dum provinciæ secus statuissent. Hæc actis inserta, ac xiv. Kal. Sept. manu actuarij signata.
units.tr: Two each should be elected. These delegates should fortify the provinces and their cities at their own expense. Having received full power to decide matters of the covenant, they should have the right to raise up to 50,000 in tribute, even without a mandate, at their own discretion. Each province should have the right to appoint one or more governors who sit in the assembly in the names of absent members. Each province might freely recall one of its delegates each month and send another to consult with the rest. Those chosen for the assembly, duly furnished with forms of procuration or letters of trust, shall take an oath for the public safety of the provinces and promise that they will act in everything without dissimulation or connivance, whether from hatred or favour, and will not divulge the deliberations. The form of the oath shall be inserted in the public records, and each speaker shall sign it, with the month and day added. The assembly shall meet every day, from the Kalends of April until the day before the Ides of October, from seven in the morning until eleven; from the Kalends of October until the Kalends of April, from eight in the morning until noon. Afternoon deliberations shall run from three until five. If grave matters demanded it, the President shall have the right to summon the delegates. Sunday, set aside for divine worship, admits no assembly, and on Wednesday or Friday afternoons they shall never meet unless necessity requires it. A president of the college, equal to the office and its burden, shall be chosen for fourteen days. His duty shall be to put each item forward, to take the votes in turn, and, having done so, to decide according to the formula of the written covenant; finally, to answer promptly those who speak in the Senate, and to do whatever else belongs to the President. Those who have proposed something shall not leave the assembly until a decision has been reached. In extraordinary meetings, if those summoned do not appear, the President, together with the others, has the power to decide as the matter requires, without regard to their absence. No one in the assembly may propose anything except the President or the assessors. Others who wish something to be proposed shall hand it to the President in writing, and he will give them an opportunity to speak as occasion arises. The President shall collect the votes in order, and these shall be given only when asked; no one may interrupt, on pain of silence. In giving votes, each province has only one vote. The President shall see that the decisions of the college are entered in the records, and shall show the more important ones to his colleagues for inspection. The President has no vote except in the case of equal opinions, and even then only if one is required. A reward shall be set for him who conducts affairs in an orderly and good manner. No one may be absent from the assembly without the consent of the college, nor refuse embassies, judicial duties or the examination of parties; whoever does so shall be kept from the assembly in future. The duties and offices of the college shall be distributed. Those who distribute money shall receive a special mandate for it. They shall oversee the treasuries, the soldiers' pay and the other disbursements of money, and shall draw up accounts separately against the quaestors and the other receivers of public money. One from Gelderland, Holland and Utrecht shall preside over this business. The care of supplies and provisions shall likewise be entrusted to one from Gelderland, Holland and Friesland. Military affairs, namely the musters of troops, garrisons, the duties of tribunes, stratagems, reconnaissance and the fortifications of places, shall be handled by those from Gelderland, Holland, Zeeland, Antwerp and Ghent. The rest, namely the administration of justice and of civil government, both secular and ecclesiastical, and the care of public peace, concord, petitions and rescripts, shall be committed to one from Zeeland, Friesland, Utrecht, Antwerp and Ypres. The President shall take care that these rules are observed and shall make each one valid, unless the provinces decide otherwise. These were inserted in the records and signed by the clerk's hand on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of September.

units.la: Reperio in actis provinciæ Sigismundo Curtspacchio Baroni Trachenbergio & Multio, à civico præsidio manus Ultrajecti injectas, habitumbitumque proterviter & sex dierum custodiâ, velut hostilis consilij suspectum æratissimâ custodiâ detentum intercessione Hohenloi & Hardecis Comitum ægrè liberatum. Eundem quoque Curtspacchium enormis injuriæ indignatione offensum missionem Ordines ac stipendia postulasse, editoque publico defensionis suæ scripto & sub signaturâ annuli in Frisiam misso, suæ innocentiæ testimonium isti genti commendavisse.
units.tr: I find in the records of the province that Sigismund Curtspacchius, Baron of Trachenberg, and Multius were seized by the civic guard at Utrecht, and that their demeanour was insolently scrutinised; they were held for six days in the strictest custody, as suspected of hostile designs, and were barely freed through the intercession of the Counts Hohenlohe and Hardeck. Curtspacchius, offended by indignation at this outrageous injury, also demanded his discharge and pay from the Estates. Having published a public written defence and sent it into Friesland under his signet ring, he commended to that people the testimony of his innocence.

units.la: Creditum fuit eum cum Martino Schenckio, commune quoddam secretum habuisse, clarissimoque proderum, qui Ultrajecti tum habebatur conventu, dubiæ fidei indicium secreta prodentibus fecisse. Addit Curtspacchius se à Joanne Nassovio quod in castris hostium visus esset, commonitum aut insimulatum immodestam accusatorum falsitatem egregio & constanti veriloquio diluisse.
units.tr: It was believed that he had a certain shared secret with Martin Schenck, and that at the most illustrious assembly then held at Utrecht he gave a sign of doubtful loyalty to those who betrayed secrets. Curtspacchius adds that, because he had been seen in the enemy camp, John of Nassau warned him or accused him, and that he refuted the shameless falsehood of his accusers with an excellent and steadfast truthful statement.

units.la: Mox à Frisiæ Ordinibus super modis corrogandi menstrui tributi in comitio actum decretumque hujusmodi perscriptum.
units.tr: Next, the Frisian Estates drew up and decreed the following in the assembly concerning the manner of collecting the monthly tax.

units.la: I. Ex quaque prætura atque oppido publicâ autoritate delegabuntur, qui locaria immobilium bonorum commentario perscribant. II. Coloni agrorum & ædium tam secularer, quam ecclesiastici nullo locario, proprium fundum colentes, aut domos inhabitantes, locaria ad exemplum vicini fundi, aut domus secundum æstimationem delegatorum persolvent. III. Iis intendendi remittendique tributum ex æquitate potestas esset. IV. Coloni proximo Septembri ex quovis aureo quinquagesimum sextum nummum pendent, eumque in locarij rationibus proprietario agri, aut fundi in solutum dabant. V. Omnes vectigales, coloni aut inquilini pro locario agrorum aut ædium, familiaque & mobilibus, mediam quinquagesimi sexti nummi partem præstabunt. VI. Proprietarij agrorum atque ædium tam quinquagesimo cuiusque aurei nummo, salvâ tamen onerum soli ratione, quam medio præstando tenebuntur. VII. Cænobia pro bonitate soli & magnitudine ædium æstimationi Delegatorum subjacebunt. VIII. In Biltanis idem valeret. IX. Mercaturam tam in pagis quam oppidis frumenti, caseï, butyri, pannorum & similium mercimoniorum exercentes pro æstimatione bonorum gravabuntur. X. Isti tributo pro qualitate suâ honorabiles personæ parebunt. XI. Legi huic nulla conventio aut pactum derogabit. XII. Locaria agrorum ædiumque dolosè professi pænâ quadrupli bono fisci corrigentur. XIII. Colonis ædium aut agrorum, si proprietarij in prædictis locarijs deduci à colonis tributi summam nolint; jus deductionis salvum erit, ÿisq; beneficium si velint, retinendæ conductionis, etiam invito domino, in quinquennium prorogabitur. XIV. Præveniendis quæstorum ærarij fraudibus, aut similibus suspicionibus, quæstores cujuscunque aris, etiam non petentibus provincialibus, apocham suâ manu scribent, expensasque in quaque urbe aut prætura in indicem rationum referent. XV. Quæstor Generalis nullas pecunias publicas, sine mandato & tabellis tum agrariorum quam oppidanorum Deputatorum ex ærario assignabit, earumque proximo quovis comitio, si moneatur, rationes reddet. XVI. Qui modus corrogandi æris, in proximum mensem valebit, dum Ordinum decreto addendum aliquid aut detrahendum ratio tributi exiget. XVII. Atque hæc singula sub obtestatione salvi juris erga regium censum, Biltanos & vacantium cænobiorum reditus usurpandos, rata erunt. Quare LALAINIUS Leovardiæ curandis rebus adhuc agens, illam ordinandi tributi sanctionem tanquam optimam & utilissimam approbavit, suaque manu III. Kal. Sept. signari fecit.
units.tr: I. From each praetorship and town, delegates shall be chosen by public authority, who shall record the rents of immovable goods in a register. II. Tenants of fields and houses, whether secular or ecclesiastical, who farm their own land or inhabit houses without paying rent, shall pay rent on the model of the neighbouring field or house, according to the valuation of the delegates. III. They shall have the power, in equity, to extend or remit the tax. IV. Tenants shall pay, next September, one fifty-sixth of a coin from each gold piece, and shall enter it in the rent accounts and hand it to the owner of the field or farm in payment. V. All tax-payers, whether tenants or lodgers, shall pay half of one fifty-sixth of a coin for the rent of fields or houses, their households and movables. VI. Owners of fields and houses shall be bound to pay half of one fiftieth of each gold coin, saving however the rate of charges on the land. VII. Monasteries shall be subject to the valuation of the delegates according to the quality of the soil and the size of the buildings. VIII. The same shall hold in the Bilt. IX. Those who trade in grain, cheese, butter, cloth and similar wares, in villages as well as towns, shall be burdened according to the valuation of their goods. X. These shall pay the tax according to their rank as respectable persons. XI. No agreement or pact shall derogate from this law. XII. Those who falsely declare the rents of fields and houses shall be corrected by a fourfold penalty, to the benefit of the treasury. XIII. If the owners of fields or houses do not wish the sum of the tax to be deducted from the said rents by their tenants, the right of deduction shall remain intact; and for those who wish to keep the lease, even against the owner's will, the benefit shall be extended for five years. XIV. To prevent frauds by the treasurers, or similar suspicions, the treasurers of every treasury shall write receipts in their own hand, even if the provincials do not ask for them, and shall enter the expenses of each city or praetorship in the index of accounts. XV. The Quaestor General shall assign no public money from the treasury without the mandate and tables of the delegates, both rural and urban, and shall render accounts at the next assembly if asked. XVI. This manner of collecting money shall hold good for the next month, while a decree of the Estates requires something to be added or taken away. XVII. All these points, under the reservation of the right regarding the royal census, the revenues of the Bilt and of vacant monasteries to be used, shall be ratified. Therefore Lalainius, who was still at Leeuwarden arranging affairs, approved this sanction for ordering the tax as very good and most useful, and had it signed with his own hand on the third day before the Kalends of September.

units.la: Igitur articulis pacis per legatos Caesaris in provincias & Frisiam mis-sis, Coloniensis actio prolata, provinciarumque decreta, tanquam mali exitus praesagio ob duriores & ad pacem minus profecturas lentis deliberationibus involvebantur.
units.tr: Therefore, when the articles of peace had been sent by Caesar's legates into the provinces and Friesland, the Cologne proposal was put forward, and the decrees of the provinces were entangled in slow deliberations, which presaged an evil outcome, since they were harsher and less likely to advance peace.

units.la: Quibus cum Caesaris Legati Philippo aequiores & festinandis rebus praecipites offenderentur, litteras Antverpiam ad Delegatos Ordinum generalium dedere. Ijs de Caesaris Rudolphi affectu, & singulari in Belgas propensione multa praefati se Coloniam neglectis privatis & simul Imperij rebus contulisse asserebant, non alio fine ac consilio, quam ut in visceribus provinciarum deflagrans bellum bono Christiani orbis cessaret. Caeterum Belgicae legatos & brevissimi temporis actionem voluisse & invalida conficiundae paci mandata attulisse, quae pleniora a provincijs in spem apparentis boni expectabantur. Ab eo tempore nec mandatum plenius allatum, neque litteras ab Ordinibus generalibus Coloniam & ad se datas manifesto indicio, etiam inter arma suspirantem populum desiderio pacis non teneri.
units.tr: When Caesar's legates took offence that the provinces were more favourable to Philip, and too hasty in pressing matters, they sent letters to Antwerp to the delegates of the General Estates. In these letters they asserted that the aforementioned men had gone to Cologne, neglecting private affairs and at the same time those of the Empire, out of the affection of Emperor Rudolf and his singular inclination towards the Belgians, with no other aim or purpose than that the war burning in the heart of the provinces might cease for the good of the Christian world. Moreover, the Belgian legates had wanted a very short negotiation and had brought mandates too weak to conclude peace, whereas fuller ones were expected from the provinces, in hope of an apparent good. From that time no fuller mandate had been brought, nor had any letters been sent from the General Estates to Cologne or to them, a clear sign that the people, even while sighing amid arms, were not held by a desire for peace.

units.la: Quae res, etsi praecidere omne pacis urgendae promovendaeque consilium potuisset, ita mandato Caesaris & Christianâ pietate in Belgicae populum impulsos in bono proposito perseverasse. Et eo quidem rem deductam, ut in aequissimas conditiones Philippi Legatus condescenderit, cui nemo ignoraret praestandam obedientiam, tanquam legitimo Principi esse. Ad religionis vero negotium quod attineret, id mitius quoque hoc ipso conventu, quam Gandavensi Bruxellensique foederibus à Philippi Legato concessum, cujus majestati, praeter priorum foederum pactiones aliquid ultra extorquere, nec aequum esset, nec Belgicae calamitas pateretur. De eâ cogitandum Ordinibus generalibus esse, qui scire deberent socordiâ aut per injuriam trahi tam utile negotium non debere, neque exacerbari illorum patientiam, qui Belgicae curam domesticis rebus quadrimestri spatio antehabuissent. Quae quoniam ulteriores dilationes non ferrent, ita hortari diligenter nomine Caesaris ut voluntates suas & responsa ita formeнт, ut Caesari & Romano imperio grata habeantur, videantque Belgicae populum paci magis quam bello deditum suis commodis non defuisse. Quibus litterae seorsim ad Frisios hunc in modum additae.
units.tr: Although this matter could have cut off every plan for urging and advancing peace, the Belgians, moved by Caesar's commission and Christian piety, nevertheless persisted in their good purpose. The matter was brought so far that Philip's legate came down to very fair conditions, since no one would be ignorant that obedience was owed to him as a lawful prince. As for the question of religion, it was granted in this very congress more mildly than Philip's legate had conceded in the Ghent and Brussels agreements. It was neither fair nor would Belgium's calamity permit extorting anything from his majesty beyond the terms of the earlier agreements. The States-General ought to think about this, since they should know that so useful a business must not be dragged out through sloth or injury, nor should the patience of those be provoked who had put the care of Belgium behind their domestic affairs for four months. Since further delays would not be tolerated, they were diligently urged, in Caesar's name, to frame their wishes and replies so that they would be acceptable to Caesar and the Roman Empire, and so that they might see that the people of Belgium, more devoted to peace than to war, had not neglected their own advantage. Separate letters to the Frisians were added to these in the following manner.

units.la: QVID à nobis in negotio pacis cum Regis Catholici principis vestri mandatario actum sit, haud dubie è legatis vestris Antverpiae commorantibus intellexisse vos arbitramur. Quibuscum solis etsi communicare consilia ac res nostras potuissemus, ita Caesaris mandato obsecuti nihil negligendum duximus quod pacì inserviret. Sed Legatorum vestrorum tarditate aut mandatorum defectu impedimentum illi injectum est, quod facile amovebitur, si vestra autoritate ad promovendum negotium impellantur. Igitur nos hortamur, ut actionis coeptae pondus diligenter & providè expendatis, sciatisque bello hoc, si daret, ad tam opportunam honestamque pacem praecludi aditum posse. Imprimis vero opus est, ut responsum maturetis, & ut vestri legati plenioribus mandatis instruantur. Id si feceritis in tempore, haud dubiè pacem miseris vestris remedium habituri eritis, & quidem tanto certius, si Rege vestro in pacem proclivi, optimi Caesaris intercessione salubre negotium juvetur.
units.tr: What has been done by us in the matter of peace with the agent of your prince, the Catholic King, you no doubt have understood from your legates staying at Antwerp. Although we could have shared our plans and affairs with them alone, we obeyed Caesar's mandate and thought nothing that served peace should be neglected. But through the slowness of your legates or the lack of mandates an obstacle has been thrown in, which will be easily removed if they are urged on by your authority to advance the business. We therefore exhort you to weigh carefully and prudently the weight of the business begun, and to know that by this war, if it were to be waged, access to so opportune and honourable a peace could be closed off. Above all, it is necessary that you hasten your reply and that your legates be furnished with fuller mandates. If you do this in time, you will no doubt have peace as a remedy for your miseries, and all the more surely if, with your king inclined to peace, the business is aided by the intercession of the best of Caesars.

units.la: Hæ Gebhardi Trevirensis Archi-Episcopi, Iulij Wirceburgensium Præsulis, Ottonis Henrici Comitis Schuartsenbergij, Ioannis Schonenburgij Præpositi Trevirensis & Werneri Gemnichij manu atque signaturâ Non. Aug. signatæ.
units.tr: These were signed with the hand and signature of Gebhard, Archbishop of Trier; Julius, Bishop of Würzburg; Count Otto Henry of Schwarzenberg; John Schonenburg, provost of Trier; and Werner Gemnich, on 5 August.

units.la: Albada scribit Ordines generales datis Coloniam litteris de procurandis inducijs tum monuisse, quo manusuefacti otio armorum animi, fastidio belli dulcedine pacis caperentur. De Philippo rege ait, eum haud dubiè inducijs assensurum, si obsequia fidelis populi expenderit, quantisque Carolo Cæsare in filium principatum devolvente officiorum solemnibus egregiâ agnitione ac reverentiâ regiæ imperatoriaque majestatis interfuisset. Contimatam scilicet multis post annis Belgicæ gentis fidem, donec ex imperio immodesti principis & Hispanicarum legionum atroci insolentiâ solveretur. Idem addit duriorem æquo Philippum in causâ inducharum semper fuisse, ægreque sperari posse, ut in melius regiæ menti atque iræ imperet, populusque inducharum voto excidens spem pacis accipiat. Conditiones istæ erant, ut durantibus inducijs partes in locis, civitatibus, munitionibus quas possiderent, se continerent & ut utrinq; liber commeatus, interdictâ tamen consiliorum communicatione haberetur. Itaq; Albada, Frisicæ gentis cujus legatum agebat, sententiam exquisivit copiamque mandati, quo Coloniæ subsistere legati Ordinum jubebantur, in Frisiam III. Eid. Aug. transmisit.
units.tr: Albada writes that the States-General, in letters sent to Cologne, had then advised arranging a truce, so that minds grown tame through idleness from arms might be captured by the sweetness of peace rather than by the weariness of war. About King Philip he says that he would undoubtedly assent to a truce if he weighed the loyalty of the faithful people, and how great was the outstanding acknowledgement and reverence shown in the solemn ceremonies of duty to the royal and imperial majesty when Charles Caesar handed the principate over to his son. Indeed, the loyalty of the Belgian nation had continued unbroken for many years, until it was loosened by the command of an intemperate prince and the savage insolence of the Spanish legions. The same writer adds that Philip had always been harsher than was right in the matter of truces, and that it could hardly be hoped he would govern his royal mind and anger for the better, or that the people, falling from their wish for a truce, would receive hope of peace. The conditions were that, while the truce lasted, each side should keep to the places, cities and fortifications it held, and that free passage should be allowed on both sides, though communication of plans was forbidden. Albada therefore asked the opinion of the Frisians, whose envoy he was, and on 11 August sent to Friesland a copy of the mandate by which the legates of the States were ordered to remain at Cologne.

units.la: Cæterum Cæsaris legatos Hispani favor tum præoccupaverat, erantq; qui desperatione pacis perculsi, exemplo provinciarum quæ defecerant, plus regiæ gratiæ, quam Ordinum fœderi tribuerent. Quæ quoniam Cæsaris, regisque mandatarios non fallebant, ne inducharum quidem beneficium fessis laborantibusque provincijs indulgebant, qui pacis profitebantur. Igitur volebant, ut Ordines à conducendis novis copijs abstinerent, & ne provinciales propioribus fœderum sacramentis ac pactionibus se inligarent. De rege fidem faciebant, eum idem acturum, etsi aperte proderentur, quæ ab inducijs, aut sanciendâ pace discrepantia externa Philippi arma intestinis provinciarum discordijs præjuvanda suaderent. Adeo belli cupido & secretus ardor speciè non quæsitæ pacis tegebatur.
units.tr: Moreover, the favour of the Spanish had already forestalled Caesar's legates, and there were some who, struck by despair of peace and following the example of the provinces that had revolted, gave more weight to royal favour than to the covenant of the States. Since these men did not deceive Caesar's and the king's agents, they did not even grant the benefit of a truce to the weary and suffering provinces that professed peace. They therefore wished the States to refrain from hiring new troops, and the provincials not to bind themselves with closer oaths and agreements of the covenant. They assured them that the king would do the same, even if the foreign arms of Philip were openly, through the internal discords of the provinces, urged to be aided, which the truce or the settlement of peace should discourage. Thus a fierce desire for war and a hidden ardour were concealed under the appearance of a peace not sought.

units.la: Mihi ex actis secretioribus istorum temporum verisimile est, Antonium Perenottum Cardinalem Granvellanum in Hispania tum agentem, Philippo regi alia à pace consilia tum instillasse, magnaque & invidendæ (ut litteræ clam Madrito scriptæ habent) apud Regem gratiæ omnem actionem turbido & serendis discordijs efficaci ingenio corrupisse. Planè quasi fato prævisum esset, ut primus civilium turbarum per Belgicam incentor, molliore senectâ & longo è Belgicâ exilio non mitigaretur, tantisque sanguinis fœditate & invidiâ coopertus, Philippum quoque regem, etsi ultro immanem, majore sævitia instrueret.
units.tr: From the more secret records of those times it seems to me probable that Antoine Perrenot, Cardinal Granvelle, then active in Spain, had instilled into King Philip plans other than peace, and had corrupted every undertaking, by a turbulent and effective talent for sowing discord, to win great and enviable favour with the king (as letters written secretly from Madrid show). It was as if fate had foreseen that the first instigator of civil disturbances in Belgium, not softened by a milder old age or by long exile from Belgium, and covered with the foulness and hatred of so much blood, would also instruct King Philip, already savage, in still greater cruelty.

units.la: Quare Frisij acceptis vergente Augusto à Senatu Groningano litteris, quæ de pace Coloniensi adeundâ & approbandis Philippi articulis habebant, nullâ dissimulatione dolosæ actionis & pacis responderunt: Se Ultrajectino fœderi arctius obligatos sine sociorum decreto & voluntate nihil statuere posse, factuaros alias, quod vicinarum gentium societas atque amicitia postularet. Quin (inquiebant) hoc ipso populi, cui intercIↄ. Iↄ. interfuimus comitio decrevimus; Ne quæ pax cum Hispano fiat & ut LXXIX. omni ope bellum geramus adjuti sociorum auxilijs, qui in fide fœderum perstiterunt. Alias nihil carius sanctiusque nobis erit, quam infidis temporum ætatibus nostra cum vicinis consilia communicare, quo occulti hostium conatus & dolosæ artes vicinarum gentium fide & concordiâ destruantur. Istæ litteræ VI. Kal. Sept. manu Econis Isbrandi Ordinum actuarij signatæ.
units.tr: Therefore the Frisians, having received letters at the end of August from the Senate of Groningen, which concerned approaching the Cologne peace and approving Philip's articles, replied without any dissimulation regarding deceitful dealing and peace: bound more closely to the Union of Utrecht, they could decide nothing without the decree and consent of their allies, and would otherwise act as the alliance and friendship with neighbouring peoples required. Indeed, they said, by this very assembly of the people, in which we took part, we have decreed that no peace be made with the Spaniard, and that we wage war with every effort, aided by the help of allies who have kept faith with the covenants. Otherwise nothing will be dearer and holier to us than to share our plans with our neighbours in these faithless times, so that the secret attempts of enemies and their deceitful arts may be destroyed by the faith and concord of neighbouring peoples. These letters were signed on 27 August by Econ Isbrand, clerk of the States.

units.la: Igitur comitio adhuc in Frisiâ durante legati Ordinum Coloniæ agentes, abruptâ inducianum spe, mandatarijs Cæsaris & Imperij declarare, Castrenantij regij Hispaniæ Legati postulata inritandis magis, quam demulcendis ad pacem provincijs esse, quæ facile spectent, negatis inducijs bellum à Philippo aut ejus Legato decerni. Oriri scilicet venturæ tempestatis signa, regiumque exercitum populandis agris intentum ruinas urbium gentiumque comminari. Quæ ipsæ tamen, quam amore pacis ardeant, Cæsaris Legatos, neque Philippi ignorare, qui haud dubie opinetur plus boni ex civilibus discordijs, quam apertâ pace suo imperio promitti. Ab eo esse, quod dimitti civitatum præsidia postulet, quo inermes & intestinis dissensionibus aut externis furoribus expositos in ipsâ induciarum disceptatione vi aut dolo obtereret. Quod ad mandata attineret, ea vitio non laborare. Quin talia fere esse ut ab Ordinum autoritate ac decreto profecta pacem à legatis iniri aut tractari sine justis relationibus nolint.
units.tr: Therefore, while the assembly was still in session in Friesland, the legates of the States, staying at Cologne and their hope of a truce cut off, declared to Caesar's and the Empire's agents that the demands of Castrenantius, the king's legate from Spain, were more calculated to irritate than to soothe the provinces towards peace, which they could easily foresee; and that, with the truce refused, war would be decreed by Philip or his legate. Plainly the signs of a coming storm were rising, and the royal army, intent on laying waste the fields, threatened the ruin of cities and peoples. Yet Caesar's legates and Philip's were not unaware how ardently the provinces burned with love of peace, since Philip undoubtedly thought more good would come to his rule from civil discords than from open peace. From this it follows that he demands the disbanding of the garrisons of the cities, so that, left defenceless and exposed to internal dissensions or foreign fury, he might crush them by force or fraud in the very discussion of the truce. As for the mandates, they were not at fault in this respect. Indeed they were such that the legates were unwilling to make or negotiate peace without just reports, as proceeding from the authority and decree of the States.

units.la: Reperio in litteris fœderatorum Ordinum Ultrajecto in Frisiam III. Kal. Sept. scriptis Articulos à Cæsaris Legatis typis datos & in publicum evulgatos, à fœderatis Ordinibus publico edicto damnatos, quod à mandatis Legatorum Belgicæ alieni in credulum & vero pacis rudem populum serendis seditionibus spargerentur. Itaque petebant, ut Frisij idem edictum per tribunalia & in publico recitari facerent, Caroloque Roordæ ad Aurantium principem cum collegis ablegato, tres Deputatos Frisiæ jure fœderatæ conventionis sufficerent. His de hostium in Brabantiam irruptionibus litteræ additæ, quæ auxilia & commeatum rogarent, focijq; juris obtestatione sublevanda ad pericula hortarentur.
units.tr: I find in letters of the confederated States, written from Utrecht to Friesland on 30 August, that the articles which Caesar's legates had given to the press and published abroad had been condemned by the confederated States in a public edict, because they were spread, from mandates of legates foreign to Belgium, to sow sedition among a credulous people and one truly unskilled in peace. They therefore asked that the Frisians have the same edict read in the courts and in public, and that they appoint three deputies of Friesland, under the right of the confederated agreement, to be sent with Carolus Roorda to the Prince of Orange and his colleagues. To this were added letters concerning the enemy's incursions into Brabant, which asked for auxiliary troops and supplies, and urged them to meet the dangers, invoking the obligation of the alliance.

units.la: Quare Coloniensi pace suspectâ Ordines generales de revocando, ut dixi, Andino deliberavere. Præterquam enim quod Ordines & Andinum inter antiqua conventio adhuc Andino provincias obligaret, ita eâ cautum erat, ne Ordines cum Philippo pacem à præfinito die facerent, deque externo Principe in auxilium vocando, præterquam Andinò tanquam potiore cogitarent. Hoc modo Andinum ne Coloniense fœdus præcipitaretur, jam ante intercessisse, hoc acerrimè & pertinacissimè urgeutem, ut pactis conventis starētur. Quibus etsi æmulatio, aut fortunæ humana mutantis arbitrium intervenisset, tamen reputandum esse, cum Galliarum regis fratre cum potentissimo principe & regni hærede tractari, & qui irritatus adversa arma pro auxilijs ex offensa principalis eminentiæ daturus sit. Reliquos quoque principes exemplum in Andino habituros, si viderint conventiones solemni religione sancitas levitatis Belgicæ vitio dissolvi. Certè magnos in conducendo exercitu, in commeatibus præstandis ab Andino sumptus factos, quibus nihil gratius ac æquius, quam beneficij memoria & repetitio veteris pacti repen-di di queat. Eo loco, Belgicæ res fortunam scilicet posuisse, ut nec pacem è Philippo rege sperare, nec à Cæsare possit & protectoris egeat, qui regiæ Philippi potentiæ si non par, saltem proxumus sit. Inesse Gallis vetera & cognata ergà Hispanum odia, quæ exercere apertius jure Andinæ societatis possint, Hannoniosque & Artesios foederum ruptores petitis è regno armis infestare. Causæ satis esse cur exui jure ac possessione principatus rex Philippus queat. Præter Albani feritatem & rejectas populi supplicationes, Austriaci defectionem obtendi posse, & ne longè eundum sit, ipso quoque apud Coloniam conventu pacis studia simulari. Quæ si non procedat, deligendum Principem esse, qui inclinantis Belgicæ onus sustineat, fessamque discordijs & ex secessionibus provinciarum periturum libertatem sub imperium Principis redigat. Atqui ab Andino omne labentium rerum fulcimentum peti posse. Hinc obversa hostibus Galliarum latera commeatum hostilibus castris subtractura, illius Belgicæ provincias Philippi armis objectas, quæ positurus facilius erit, si juratos hostes Galliarum populos suum in exitium concitari perspexerit. Conditiones certè magis æquas Cæsarem ac Regem infœlicibus provincijs daturos, quæ incolumitati suæ abundè prospectum credent, si Andino veteri libertatis defensore utantur. Posse reprimi pactorum æquitate principalis ingenij spiritum, ut intra præscriptum maneat, modum agnitura augendæ potentiæ cupido si bello aut pace abstineat, si distribuendi præsidij militaris licentiam remittat, si Ultrajectino fœderi robur atque vim addat, cæteraque faciat, quæ defensoris Belgici imperium patiatur, Ordinum ac reip. majestas prohibeat. Igitur petitum, ut è reliquis fœderatis provincijs Legati Antverpiam cum mandatis mittantur, quibus & exui dominatione Philippus & recipi Andinus ex pactorum formulâ possit. Sed in vanum omniâ per inferiores provincias dulcedine Ultrajectini fœderis recidebant.
units.tr: Therefore, with the Cologne peace under suspicion, the States-General deliberated on recalling, as I have said, Anjou. For apart from the fact that the States and Anjou were still bound by an old agreement, by which the provinces were obligated to Anjou, it was provided that the States should not make peace with Philip after a fixed day, and in summoning a foreign prince for aid they should consider none but Anjou, as the preferred one. In this way, so that the Cologne covenant would not be rushed, he who had already intervened earlier, most fiercely and stubbornly urged that the agreed pacts be kept. Even if rivalry or the judgement of changing human fortune had intervened, it was nevertheless to be considered that they were dealing with the brother of the King of France, a most powerful prince and heir to the kingdom, who, provoked by adversity, would give arms in exchange for help, out of offence to his principal eminence. The other princes too would have Anjou as an example if they saw agreements sanctioned by solemn religion dissolved through the fickleness of Belgium. Certainly Anjou had incurred great expense in hiring the army and providing supplies, for which nothing would be more pleasing and just than to repay him with the memory of the favour and the renewal of the old pact. At this point, Belgium's affairs had evidently placed its fortune in such a state that it could hope for peace neither from King Philip nor from Caesar, and needed a protector who, if not equal to Philip's royal power, was at least the nearest to it. The French have old and kindred hatreds against the Spaniard, which they could exercise more openly by right of the alliance with Anjou, and by arms drawn from the kingdom they could harass Hainaut and Artois, breakers of the covenants.
