units.tr: Wingardius, the leader of a cohort who had been on the right wing, fought bravely and fell, struck down by his own men. Many, weakened by thirst, either from wounds or from blood boiling in the very flight, fell into the enemy's power. Pompeius Ufkenius too was thrown from a hanging carriage, which had been brought to watch the battle, and was killed by the enemy. He was a man most worthy of a better end, who, in his life spent amid cares and troubles for the advancement of the alliance, loving his country, was given up to the will of a proud and bloodthirsty victor, his military and tribunal blood poured out. So great a panic seized the crowd from the flight that they did not even halt at Coevorden. A wooden and beam barrier had been placed across the road, yet they were held back neither by the prayers nor the orders of Cornputus, who stood there. Hence they overran the marshy fields between Coevorden and Bourtange and poured out into the territory of Münster. Cornputus hesitated, uncertain whether to protect Coevorden, a garrison weak and unfortified, against the incursions of the victors. Meanwhile, having vainly sought the help of the fugitives, whom he tried to rouse to courage and glory with fine exhortations, and at last overcome by fear, he hurried with very few of his men by a doubtful route through pathless country into Friesland. By the announcement of this most grievous disaster he struck the hearts of the elders. They, from Hohenlo's letters, had withdrawn from the defeated army partly to Oldenzaal, to which place they had retreated the day after the rout. Then, with their forces hardly restored, they set off for Leeuwarden and conceived an excellent hope of a better and gentler fortune in the future.

units.la: Litterae Hohenloi hujusmodi erant.
units.tr: The letter from Hohenlo was of this kind.

units.la: CELARE vos non possum, ORDINES, quod cum hoste conflixerim. Ac quanquam secunda pugnae initia favore numinis, mea virtute fecerim, hostium equitatu caeso, aut dissipato, ita sola peditum meorum fuga spem victoriae mihi excussit. Ego vero Coverdiam cum fugientibus me recipere in animum induxeram, quo fortunam praelij recollectis copijs repararem. Caeterum Cornputtus, ibi praesidio a me relictus, loco turpiter decessit, ad quod faciendum nulla necessitas sacramenti oblitum adigebat. Quod foedius ne tormentis quidem abducendis tempus impendit, soli fugae ex imbelli pavore quaesitum. Sed mea virtus quae amissa sunt propediem restituet, daturusque sum operam ut majoribus cum auxilijs ad vos veniam. Quippe Scoticae ac Anglorum legiones jam in itinere sunt, fuisetque in manu mea hostem Groningā arcendi, nisi desertā Coverdiā militum fuga sibi dedecus, mihi incommodum peperisset. Et quanquam hostes decem & trium cohortium ope subnixi, de movendis ad Groningam castris vestris cogitare videantur, ita meo officio defuturus non sum, modo hoc agatis, ut ejus quam ocyssime commonear. Arma, res atque vita mea vestrae saluti offeruntur.
units.tr: I cannot conceal from you, my Lords, that I have fought with the enemy. Although the first stages of the battle went well, through the favour of heaven and my own courage, with the enemy cavalry cut down or scattered, the flight of my infantry alone wrested the hope of victory from me. I had indeed resolved to withdraw with the fugitives to Coevorden, so that I could gather my forces again and retrieve the fortune of the field. Meanwhile Cornputtus, whom I had left there as a garrison, shamefully abandoned his post, though no necessity of duty compelled him to do so, and he forgot his oath. What is more disgraceful, he did not even take the time to remove the artillery, but sought safety in flight out of cowardly fear. But my courage will soon restore what has been lost, and I will take care to come to you with greater forces. Indeed, the Scottish and English regiments are already on the march, and it would have been in my power to keep the enemy from Groningen, had the desertion of Coevorden and the flight of the soldiers not brought shame on them and harm on me. And although the enemy, supported by ten and three cohorts, seems to be considering moving his camp toward Groningen, I shall not fail in my duty, provided only that you act so that I am informed of it as quickly as possible. My arms, my property and my life are offered for your safety.

units.la: Cl. Franckenā egregius Hohenloae illo praelio virtutis commendator scribit, Philippum Hohenloum visa peditum suorum fuga, equestres tur-
units.tr: The distinguished Franckena, a notable commender of Hohenlo's valour in that battle, writes that Philip Hohenlo, when he saw his infantry in flight, led his cavalry squadrons, the strength of his army, through the middle of the enemy line,

units.la: turmas, exercitus sui robur, per mediam hostium aciem duxisse, ruptis que eorum ordinibus aut saltem laxatis, salvum & incolumem Oldenzelam in Tubantibus pervenisse. Equites quoque Hohenloi plurimos in illo conflictu desideratos, pedestremque exercitum fuga servatum manifestae cladi non subfuisse. Tum machinae & omnis commeatus hostibus in praedam versus, qui rebus secundis, more mortalium, elati victricia per Drentiam signa solvendo obsidio circumducebat. Quare Hardenbergicae cladis nuntio in castra ad Groningam perlato Enteniana potissimum legio tribuni sui morte & ex retardatis stipendijs turbida castrense officium detrectavit, animisque inquieta, ferox & reliquarum quoque cohortium ingenia seditiosis consilijs tanquam pestilentia infecit. Unde exlex miles & disciplinae immemor nec blandimentis nec auctoritati parebat, quae gregarios inter & calores convicijs exagitata tribunorum quoque centurionumque fidem corruperat.
units.tr: and, having broken or at least loosened their ranks, reached Oldenzaal in Twente safe and sound. He also writes that many of Hohenlo's horsemen were missing from that clash, and that the infantry, saved by flight, did not share in the plain disaster. Then the siege engines and all the supplies fell as booty to the enemy, who, elated by their success, as mortals are, carried their victorious standards through Drenthe, breaking off the siege. Therefore, when news of the disaster at Hardenberg reached the camp at Groningen, the Enkhuizen regiment, above all, roused by the death of its tribune and by the overdue pay, refused the duties of the camp in a mutinous spirit. Restless and fierce in temper, it infected the other cohorts too with its seditious plans, as with a pestilence. Thus the soldiers, lawless and forgetful of discipline, obeyed neither flattery nor authority; among the common men, inflamed and goaded by abuse, they had even corrupted the loyalty of the tribunes and centurions.

units.la: Quare ne in gravius malum militarium animorum fervor erumperet, forisque victor hostis, intra loricam tumultus & sedititio castra infestaret, Gulielmus Ludovicus Nassovius advocato in consilium Sonoio moveri eadem castra etsi invitus fecit, quae incensis tentorijs celerrime rapta, vix sarcinis impedimentisque colligendis tempus reliquerant. Curâ tamen Nassovij, qui opperiendum hostem & conferendam cum victore Schenckio manum suaserat, exercitus Winsumum in Hunesgonios cum omni commeatu & per Omlandiam vicinam ductus, quâ parte Hunesus amnis flexo aut curvato alveo fertilissima terrarum perlabitur. Tum per Longowaldios itinere facto, superato apud Visfletam Lavica flumine pleraque copiae Collumum & Doccomium expeditae, ubi per castrense otium Entenianae legionis saevior seditio ex egestate aeris recruduit. Quippe ab eodem milite pro arbitrio copiarum ductoribus imperatum, qui referre, quae Opslachum destinabantur, signa Doccomium jussi, oppidum velut pignori aut direptioni immodeste insolentibus permittebant. Quamobrem Gulielmus Ludovicus classiario milite revehendis Harlingam tormentis conducto, litteras Doccomio xi. Kalend. Iulij Leovardiam dedit sedandisque emotis mentibus unius mensis stipendium in parato aere poposcit.
units.tr: Therefore, lest the heat of the soldiers' minds break out into a worse evil, and lest the enemy, victorious outside, should assail the camp from within the rampart with tumult and sedition, William Louis of Nassau, having called Sonoy into council, reluctantly had the same camp moved. The tents were set on fire and the camp was hastily struck, leaving scarcely time to gather baggage and wagons. Yet, through the care of Nassau, who had advised waiting for the enemy and joining battle with the victor Schenck, the army was led to Winsum among the Hunsingo people, with all its supplies, and through the neighbouring Omlands, where the river Hunze, its channel bent or curved, flows through the most fertile land. Then, making the march through the Long Woulde region and crossing the river Lauwers at Visvliet, most of the forces were sent to Collum and Dokkum. There, during the camp's idleness, the more savage mutiny of the Enkhuizen regiment broke out again because of the lack of money. For the same soldiers had dictated to the commanders of the troops what they wished; ordered to turn their standards to Dokkum, instead of toward Opslagt as intended, they let the town be given over, as a pledge or to plunder, to the reckless insolence of the mutineers. Therefore William Louis, having hired marines to carry artillery to Harlingen, sent a letter from Dokkum on the 22nd of June to Leeuwarden, and to calm the disturbed minds he demanded a month's pay ready in cash.

units.la: Unde à Deputatis Scipio Meckama vir nobilis & Hesselus Aysina pro legatis ocyus Doccomium missi, numeratoque seditioso militi in mensem stipendio praesidij insolentiam placavere. Mox amovendis quoque in posterum seditionibus militem inter & Legatos Ordinum conventio scripta, quo seditiosissimus quisque otio corruptior repetitis belli officijs ad honesta obsequia & agnitionem decentis imperij rediret.
units.tr: Thereupon Scipio Meckama, a nobleman, and Hesselus Aysma, were sent quickly from the Deputies to Dokkum as envoys. Having paid the seditious soldiers a month's wages, they appeased the insolence of the garrison. Soon afterwards a written agreement was made between the soldiers and the envoys of the States, so that the mutineers, rendered more corrupt by idleness, might return, by renewed military duties, to honourable obedience and acknowledgement of proper authority, and that seditions might be removed in future.

units.la: Eâ cantum fuit.
units.tr: On these terms it was settled.

units.la: Ut unius mensis stipendium post obsidium miles acciperet, eoque evoluto sequente obsidio aliud menstruum stipendium priori superadderetur. Conventione quoque signatâ militi binâ insuper stipendiâ penderentur, singulisque mox septimanis paratum aes tribuno cohortis & juxta militi praestaretur. Centurio ac miles fidem sacramento faceret, Ordinumque imperijs ac mandatis ex articulo, ut vocant, militari parerent. Haec à Ioanne Escheda, Harmanno Olthovio, Iacobo Nettio, Florentio Scagmo, Rudolpho Langio & Bloemio Suetano xiv Kalend. Iul. Doccomij signata.
units.tr: That the soldier should receive one month's pay after the siege, and that when that month had elapsed, another month's pay should be added to the previous one, following the siege. By the same agreement, the soldier should be paid two additional wages, and cash should be given to the cohort's tribune and likewise to the soldier at intervals of every seven weeks. The centurion and the soldier should swear an oath of fidelity, and obey the commands and orders of the States in accordance with what they call the military articles. These were signed at Dokkum by Johannes Eschedius, Hermannus Olthovius, Jacobus Nettius, Florentius Scagmus, Rudolphus Langius and Bloemius Suetanus, on the 18th of June.

units.la: Igitur totâ belli mole in Frisios & Omlandiam vergente, Frisij laftas MDLXXX quasdam secalis quo commeatibus legionum providerent, Amstelodamenses poposcere, & ut illius civitatis Magistratus sociam fidem emendo pro Frisijs frumento interponeret. Quod frigidè à Magistratu habitum, qui Legatos coëmendis necessarijs mitti è Frisiâ volebat, ejusdem regiones proceres haud parum turbavit, qui inter domesticarum seditionum aut hostilium irruptionum metus constituti annonæ caritatem aut penuriam submovendam provinciâ aut infidis castris interpretabantur. Auxilia quoque eosdem Amstelodamenses, ut & minores Frisios petita, ac ut à clade Hardenbergicâ expositam bello provinciam suæ civitatis aut regionis præsidio sublevarent. Sed Magistratus missas à se Suollam & post Oldenzelam auxiliares copias respondebat, extenuatisque præsidij cohortibus binas tantum tuendæ civitati retinuisse. Nihilominus testandæ in socios fidei ad legatos suos Hagam scripsisse, quo afflictis Frisiorum rebus sociale auxilium mitteretur. Idem à minoribus Frisijs Enchusâ responsum. Quare pencитato cohortibus ære militares ex quibusq; signis manipuli Doccomio Opslachum & ad Salinas præmissi, quæ marino littori in Reiderij amnis & Neozilæ ripâ adjectæ præservandis Omlandiæ agris terreo opere tum muniebantur. Quâ munitione perfectâ, ac Doccomiensi seditione compositâ Hermannus Olthovius, Vlietius, Iargæus, Scagenus & Cornelius Veda cohortium præfecti Opslachum pro præsidio expediti, animatâ jam melius Frisiorum gente, quod per Hollandiam cæterasque socias provincias auxilia pararentur. Hoc vero volebant Hollandi, ut auxiliaribus copijs Frisij non campestres ad usus, sed civitatum suarum præsidio uterentur, ne illâ militaris turbæ inopia, interveniente cohortium cæde aut fugâ recuperandorum præsidiorum commoditate Hollandicæ urbes privarenrur.
units.tr: Therefore, with the whole weight of the war turning toward the Frisians and the Omlands, the Frisians demanded that the Amsterdamers supply them with 1,580 lasts of rye, so that they might provision the regiments, and that the magistracy of that city should guarantee by its alliance, by buying grain on behalf of the Frisians. The magistracy received this coolly, since it wished envoys to be sent from Friesland to buy the necessary supplies. This greatly disturbed the nobles of that region, who, caught between fear of domestic sedition and of hostile incursions, explained the high price or scarcity of food as a result of the province's being turned over to the war and to the unfaithful camps. The Amsterdamers likewise asked for auxiliary troops, as did the lesser Frisians, so that they might relieve, with the garrison of their own city or region, the province left exposed to war by the disaster at Hardenberg. But the magistracy replied that it had sent auxiliary forces to Zwolle and afterwards to Oldenzaal, and that, with the garrison cohorts weakened, it had kept only two to defend the city. Nevertheless, it had written to its envoys at The Hague to testify its good faith toward the allies, so that aid might be sent to the Frisians in their distressed situation. The lesser Frisians received the same answer from Engwierum. Hence, with the money for the cohorts paid, soldiers from the various companies were sent forward to Opslagt and to the Salt Marsh, which were added to the sea-shore and the bank of the river Reiderland and the Neuzel, and at that time were being fortified with an earthen work to protect the Omland fields. When this fortification was finished, and the Dokkum sedition quieted, Hermannus Olthovius, Vlietius, Jargaeus, Scagenus and Cornelius Veda, prefects of the cohorts, were sent to Opslagt as a garrison, the Frisian people now being more cheerful, because auxiliaries were being raised through Holland and the other allied provinces. But the Hollanders wanted this: that the Frisians should use the auxiliary forces not for field operations but for the defence of their own cities, lest, with the lack of soldiers in that turmoil, and with the slaughter or flight of cohorts intervening, the Holland towns should be deprived of the opportunity of recovering their garrisons.

units.la: Tum Schenckius victor patentibus campis & cæde hostium constratis unum diem agens, quiete parum per fessos militi datâ Coverdiam properavit, eamque Sonoi avaritiâ aut incuria patrum neglectam tunc incolarum ac præsidij vacuam invenit. Itaque multo partium metu, Hohenloo Oldenzelam cum reliquijs infaustæ cladis amoto, medios per Drentiæ agros Groningam contendit, urbemque soluto obsidio accessui facilem specie triumphantis ingressus est. Quippe Senatus & ex conjuratis primi, quos Lalainius opprimendis jam antè fœderatis habuerat, ei obviam egressi, de victoriâ Hardenbergici prælij gratulabantur, & quod fessis obsessorum rebus ac ad faciendam deditionem pronis victore cum exercitu subvenissent. Tum dies genio vinum inter & epulas delecti, solenniumque veluti festorum hilaritate exacti sunt. Lalainius ipse animi diu anxius & interno tortore pectoris ex defectione æger frontem tum exporrexit, omnemque violati fœderis ac simul fidei pœnitudinem facescere animo jussit. Mox Schenkianum exercitum per omnem Omlandiæ agrum sparsit, Opslachumque & Salinas, quas quinque cohortium præsidio fœderati præoccupaverant, obsidere constituit. Itaque nobilium arces & castella passim à Schenckij exercitu diruta atque direpta, dominorum fugâ vacua cultoribus & omni ornatu jacuere. Quippe auro argentoque tum pretiosâ supellectile in prædam captâ, ferrum & omne æs fusile armorum usui impensum, quæ Lalailainius nullo obstante per Amasi & Reiderij amnis ripas circumserebat.
units.tr: Then Schenck, the victor, with the open fields and the enemy strewn with slaughter, spent a day there. Having given his weary soldiers little rest, he hastened to Coevorden, and found it neglected through the avarice or carelessness of Sonoy, and then empty of its inhabitants and its garrison. Therefore, with great fear among the parties, Hohenlo having withdrawn to Oldenzaal with the remnants of the disastrous defeat, Schenck made his way through the fields of Drenthe to Groningen, and, having broken off the siege, entered the city, which was easy of access, in the appearance of a triumphant man. Indeed, the Senate and the first of the conspirators, whom Lalaing had already held in custody to crush the confederates, came out to meet him, congratulating him on the victory at the battle of Hardenberg, and because he had come with his army to help the besieged, whose situation was exhausted and who were inclined to surrender. Then days were set aside for wine and feasting in honour of the genius of the city, and were spent in the cheerfulness of festivals as it were. Lalaing himself, long anxious in mind and sick from the inner torment of his breast after the defection, now relaxed his brow and ordered the regret for the broken covenant and at the same time for his broken faith to depart from his mind. Soon afterwards he spread Schenck's army throughout the whole Omland region, and resolved to besiege Opslagt and the Salt Marsh, which the confederates had already occupied with garrisons of five cohorts. Thus the castles and fortresses of the nobles, here and there demolished and plundered by Schenck's army, lay open to the cultivators, abandoned by their lords who had fled, and stripped of all their ornaments. For gold and silver, and costly household furniture, had been seized as booty, and iron and all cast bronze used for weapons was carried off, which Lalaing, without any hindrance, was having taken along the banks of the Ems and the Reiderland.

units.la: Quare centuriones, qui Opslachum præsidio tenebant, habito concilio obsidij metu auxilia Frisios petiere, & ut ocyus subvectandis commeatibus oneraria navigia adornarent. Alias fore, ut nullâ sui defensione aut gloriâ instar pecorum mactentur, defectoque commeatu languidi & imbelles promiscuâ morte pereant. Igitur necessarium esse, ut fortissimi quique & perire pro patriâ nati ejus auxilium atque opem sentiant, & ut ad præstandos opportunè commeatus patrum sollicitudo se extendat, habitura viros fortes si fecerit. Hoc ab Harmanno Olthovio, Egberto Bevelandio, Cornelio Weda, Stephano Pensfio, Florentio & Scageno, Sceltone Iargæo signatum.
units.tr: Therefore the centurions who held Opslach with a garrison, having called a council in fear of a siege, sought help from the Frisians and asked them to fit out merchant ships quickly to carry supplies. Otherwise, they said, without any defence or glory they would be slaughtered like cattle, and, with supplies failing, the weak and unwarlike would perish together in a common death. It was therefore necessary that the bravest men, born to die for their country, should feel its help and aid, and that the care of the fathers should extend to supplying provisions in good time, which would win them brave men if they did so. This was signed by Harmann Olthof, Egbert Bevelandt, Cornelis Weda, Stephan Pensfio, Florentius and Scagenus, and Scelto Iargaeus.

units.la: Gulielmus quoque Ludovicus Nassovius Doccomij tum hærens, pro obtinendo tormentario pulvere reliquoque commeatu intercessit, ac ut Bartholomæum Sneburgium virum fortem, comparandis ad obsessos commeatibus delectum, omni necessario præjuvarent. Quo Elberti quoq; Leonini, qui Antverpiâ Daventriam à Concilio Status Belgici amandatus erat, litteræ ad Frisios faciebant, hortantis, ut animos capesserent, Hardenbergicæq; cladi salubres curas reponerent. Neq; enim planè convulsas fœderis vires esse, aut detrimenta cladis sævienti fortunæ imputanda, quæ insp….eratus militum pavor & solâ confusio peperisset. Emendanda esse exercitus vitia & torporem, aut metum virtute aut ejus fiduciâ mutandum, quo omne dedecus ex pavore & fugâ quæsitum resumptæ fortitudinis gloria cooperiat. Se interim apud fœderis socios, apud Hohenloum & suos quoq; Antverpiæ intercessurum, ut stipendia atque auxilia habeantur, & ut Frisiæ vicinarumque gentium discrimini auxiliares Gallorum Scotorumque copiæ subveniant. Hoc tantum petere, ut Frisij mortalium mores & ingenia imitati adversâ ex fortunâ civilem concordiam induant, & ut militum provincialium animos decentibus solatijs erigendo oppida ac castella præsidijs firment. De caetero cogitarent Deum prospera sanctissimo fœderi largiturum, eosq; esse adversarum rerum fines, ut initia secundis præsternant. Sic Leoninus actis pro liberalitate gratijs valere Frisios jussit, interceptâq; in Omlandiam ex Hardenbergico prælio legatione, in Brabantiam recessit. Litteræ viii. Kal. Iul. Daventriâ datæ:
units.tr: Willem Lodewijk of Nassau, who was then staying at Doccum, also intervened to secure gunpowder and the rest of the supplies, and asked that they give every needed help to Bartholomaeus Sneburgius, a brave man chosen to bring supplies to the besieged. At the same time letters from Elbert Leoninus, who had been sent from Antwerp to Deventer by the Council of the Belgian State, went to the Frisians, urging them to take heart and to set aside anxious thoughts about the disaster at Hardenberg, which was a healthy lesson. For the forces of the league were not wholly broken, and the losses of the disaster should not be ascribed to cruel fortune; they were caused by the sudden panic of the soldiers and mere confusion. The faults and sluggishness of the army had to be corrected, and fear had to be replaced by courage or by confidence in it, so that the glory of recovered bravery might cover all the shame gained from panic and flight. Meanwhile he himself would intercede with the allies of the league, with Hohenlo and his own people at Antwerp, so that pay and reinforcements would be provided, and so that Frisian and neighbouring peoples in danger would be helped by auxiliary forces of French and Scots. He asked only this: that the Frisians, imitating the habits and character of mortals, should in adversity put on civic harmony, and that they should encourage the spirits of the provincial soldiers with fitting comfort and strengthen towns and castles with garrisons. As for the rest, they should consider that God would grant prosperity to the most holy league, and that these adversities were the limits of misfortune, so that they might precede beginnings with success. Thus Leoninus, having thanked them for their goodwill, bade the Frisians farewell, and after a letter sent to Ommeland was intercepted from the Hardenberg battle, he withdrew into Brabant. Letters dated Deventer, 24 June.

units.la: Cujus cladis causam, etsi temerarijs Hohenloï consilijs, dubia rerum ut certa habentis, plerique imputarent, ita erant, qui socordiam foederatorum Ordinum criminarentur, quod hostium copijs, transvehendis patêre Rhenum sivissent. Quippe illorum consilio Iselsteinium cum legione è superiore Geldriâ in Transifulaniam evocatum, nudato fluminis margine, qui adiri relicto ad Rhenum præsidio non potuisset. Erant quoque qui crederent, Hohenloum cum imperio & simul mandato pugnasse, quod dubium & obscurum infœlicis prælij eventus fecisset. Prospera scilicet rerum mortales adorare, fericq; in adversis ut eorum culpæ in alios referantur.
units.tr: Although many attributed the cause of this disaster to the rash plans of Hohenlo, who treated doubtful matters as certain, there were others who blamed the sloth of the allied States, because they had let the enemy forces have a passage across the Rhine for their transport. For on their advice Isselstein had been summoned with a legion from Upper Guelders into Overijssel, leaving the river bank bare, which could not be reached since the garrison had been left at the Rhine. There were also those who believed that Hohenlo fought with command and at the same time under orders, and that this uncertainty and obscurity had caused the outcome of the unhappy battle. Surely mortals pray for prosperity, and in adversity they are quick to refer the blame for their faults to others.

units.la: Igitur liberatâ post tres menses & medium Groningâ foederatoque exercitu in Frisios revocato Lalainius, quo quo vellet, copijs suo arbitrio usus Schenckiani exercitus partem Delphzilam duxit quam Fivelæ amni qui in Amasum exit, assitam Bartoldus nuper in justæ munitionis formam mam redegerat. Quippe valli altitudine & mole multo aggere firma-tâ, fossam quoque centum & decem pedum ereẑto operi præduxerat, quod introrsum septingentis & ultra passibus ab Amasi ripâ jactum commoditate amplissimi fluminis parum juvabatur. Quare Lalainius occupato portus ostio, agrisque ad Amasum precurrentibus castra aggeribus circumdedit omnemque, quem petuit, commeatum inferri ijsdem castris jussit. Delphzilam vero præsidio tres cohortes tenebant, quæ etsi mutatis sacramentis, plurimos vetere in Lalainium gratiâ affectos in illâ multitudine numerabant. Sic præsâ levibus castris Delphzilâ per Fivelingios Hunesgoniosque exercitum reduxit, Opslachumq; in ripâ Reiderij annis justo opere erectum, subvertendis præsidij commeatibus properavit. Tredecim cohortes fuisse annalibus proditum est.
units.tr: Therefore, after three and a half months Groningen had been freed, and the league's army had been recalled to the Frisians, Lalainius, using his forces at his own discretion wherever he wished, led part of Schenck's army to Delfzijl, which Bartholdus had recently turned into a properly fortified work on the Fivel river, where it flows into the Ems. For he had strengthened the rampart with great height and bulk and a mass of earth, and had carried a ditch a hundred and ten feet wide in front of the work; but this lay more than seven hundred paces inside from the bank of the Ems, and was little helped by the convenience of so wide a river. Therefore Lalainius, having seized the mouth of the harbour and the fields running down to the Ems, surrounded the camp with earthworks and ordered that all the supplies he sought be brought into the same camp. Three cohorts held the garrison at Delfzijl, and although they had changed their oaths, they counted among that multitude many who were still well disposed to Lalainius from their old friendship. Having thus taken Delfzijl, he led the army back with light baggage through the Fivelingers and Hunsingoers, and hurried to overthrow the supplies of the garrison at Opslach, which had been built with proper work on the bank of the Reiderland river. It is recorded in the annals that there were thirteen cohorts.

units.la: Unde Frisiorum litteris Eschedæ & Rinsuoudij cohortes, quæ in Gerriconis cœnobium diverterant, celerrimo itinere Opslachum ire jussæ, quo obsessi sustinendis opugnationibus impares illarum auxilio juvarentur. Cæterum Rinsuoudij milite cæso aut dissipato, ipso captivo & saucio Escheda cum cohorte pedem retraxit, adaucto magis terrore, quod Schenckius prosperâ fortunâ superbè & crudeliter usus, refectos fomentis ac cibo captivos sedato iracundiæ calore interemisset. Quare obsessorum quoque animi sensim detecere, quorum virtus ex annonæ & commeatuum penuriâ languidior spem liberationis amiserat. Igitur Frisij Didericum Sonoïum, muniendæ Harlingæ intentum, socias naves ut in auxilia procuraret, datis litteris monuere ac ut unam annonâ instructam per æstuaria maris deferri Opslachum ocyus faceret. Is Iohannem Buningam virum fortem præsidium Harlingæ agentem instructissimæ navi præfecit, quæ lecto littore prid. Kal. Iulij medio diei Oostmahornam provecta, ac in anchoris stare jussa tardiori auxilio moram injecerat. Quippe classiarij artium rudes & numero pauci ministeria non implebant, interque otia silente vento dies actus obsessorum angustiam prægravabat. Unde consilium faciendæ deditionis captum, eaque conventum, ut præsidiarij loco salvi & incolumes cum armis & impedimentis exirent, intraque trimestre arma in Regem non ferrent. Quare impulsis per Frisiam rebus, à regiæ factionis multitudine, quæ in provinciarum vicalibus adhuc hærebat, frumenta & commeatus in castra hostium clam subvecti, quorum statíva modo per marini apertique littoris edita, modo fertilium camporum planitiem habebantur. Igitur autorati, qui in criminum ac malorum consiliorum conscios inquirerent, eorumque nomina ad Senatum provinciæ deferrent.
units.tr: Accordingly, the Frisians, by letter, ordered the cohorts of Escheda and Rinsuoudius, which had turned aside into the monastery of Gerriko, to make all speed to Opslach, so that they might help the besieged, who were unequal to sustaining the assaults. But Rinsuoudius's soldiers were either cut down or scattered, and he himself was taken captive and wounded. Escheda withdrew on foot with his cohort, and the terror was increased because Schenck, using his good fortune arrogantly and cruelly, had put to death the captives after they had been restored with warm food and care, once the heat of his anger had cooled. Hence the spirits of the besieged also gradually gave way. Their courage, weakened by the scarcity of food and supplies, had lost hope of relief. So the Frisians, who were busy fortifying Harlingen, wrote to Diederik Sonoy and urged him to procure allied ships to help, and to have one of them, loaded with provisions, carried through the estuaries of the sea to Opslach as quickly as possible. He placed John Bunningh, a brave man who was commanding the garrison at Harlingen, in charge of a well-equipped ship. It left the shore on the day before the Kalends of July and, at midday, sailed to Oostmahorn, where it was ordered to lie at anchor, and so caused delay to the aid that was to come more slowly. Indeed, the sailors, unskilled in their arts and few in number, did not perform their duties, and while the wind lay silent the days passed in idleness, which weighed heavily on the anxious besieged. Hence a plan for surrender was adopted, and it was agreed that the garrison should leave safe and unharmed, with arms and baggage, and should not bear arms against the King for three months. Since affairs in Friesland were thrown into disorder, grain and supplies were secretly carried into the enemy camps by the multitude of the royal faction, which still lingered in the village communities of the province. The enemy's quarters were held sometimes on the sea-coast and open shore, and sometimes on the level plain of the fertile fields. Therefore commissioners were appointed to search out accomplices in crimes and evil designs, and to report their names to the Provincial Senate.

units.la: Mox dilectus per omnem agrum atque municipia habiti, Biltanique viritim coacti armatos recensuere. Reliquis in præturis fortes pavidis immisti difficilius cogebantur, & quod essent qui arma tuendæ patriæ imperata hostium servitijs destinarent. Itaque Lalainius redacto in potestatem Opslacho castra Collumum movit, quem vicum in Oostergoâ amplissimum & modico portu commercijs opportunum circumducere valuo statuerat. Cæterum mutato consilio, quo in inferiora provinciæ pergeret, de oppugnando Doccomio agitavit, quod oppidum Ea amnis lenibus aquis Leovardiâ prolabens, navigabili alveo interluit. Quare Ordinum sollicitudine & curâ omnes copiæ, quas é provincialibus college-rant,
units.tr: Soon levies were held throughout the whole countryside and the towns, and at Bilt men were gathered one by one and mustered under arms. In the remaining districts the brave were mixed with the fearful, and they were more reluctantly called up; and there were some who would hand over to the enemy's service the arms ordered for the defence of the fatherland. Therefore Lalaing, having brought Opslach under his control, moved his camp to Collum, a very large village in Oostergo, suited to trade by its modest harbour, which he had resolved to surround with a rampart. But changing his plan, by which he might proceed into the lower parts of the province, he considered attacking Dokkum, a town which the River Ee, flowing down from Leeuwarden with gentle waters, bathes with its navigable channel. Hence, through the concern and care of the States, all the forces that had been gathered from the provincials were ordered to assemble at that town, so that the labour of fortifying the city, entrusted to the armed garrison, might proceed better and more successfully.

units.la: Rrr rant, istud ad oppidum convenire jussæ, quo permuniendæ urbi destinatus labor armatorum præsidio melius fœliciusque procederet. Sed rara civium manus, agrarij segnes & erigendis operibus invalidi, ægrè suorum imperijs parebant, ipsorumque etiam prætorum contumaciâ curribus atque equis destituebantur. Unde Cuningamus ne moră aut per ignaviam consilium vilesceret, fossores, equos, currus acciri è Dongrijs jussit, prætoresque promovendis novorum operum munimentis tardos acerbissimis litteris perstrinxit. Versari scilicet in summo discrimine provinciam innuebat, postquam ad muros fermè hostis & secundis ferox futuri temporis fortunam suâ ex virtute aut victoriâ æstumaret. Inde capto Opslacho, Collumano agro signa inlata, intra oppidum & in meditullium provinciæ progressura nisi virtute virorum fortium & labore manuum sistantur. Præter militem namque fossores, currus, equos desiderari, ac ut patens oppidum per fœda murorum rudera sustinendo infultivi debile, justo aut pro ratione temporis tumultuario opere firmetur. Quod nisi fiat, oppido & simul provinciæ periculum imminere, cui causam non intermissa militarium tribunorum officia, sed socordia prætorum datura sit. Quas litteras etsi parum efficaces aliorum metus, aliorum contumacia faceret, ita Hohenloï repentino in Frisios adventu invaluere, qui Leovardiâ Doccomium decem cum cohortibus celerrimo itinere provectus, rusticam ac oppidanam plebem emuniendis locorum opportunis adegit.
units.tr: But the scanty band of citizens, sluggish farm labourers, and men too weak for raising earthworks obeyed their orders with difficulty, and even through the obstinacy of their own praetors they were left without carts and horses. Therefore Cuningamus, so that the plan might not be cheapened by delay or idleness, ordered diggers, horses and carts to be summoned from Dongeradeel, and with the most bitter letters he rebuked the praetors who were slow to push forward the fortifications of the new works. He was plainly signalling that the province was in the greatest danger, since the enemy had nearly reached the walls and, fierce with success, would judge the fortune of the future by its own valour or victory. Once Opslach was taken, the standards had been carried into the territory of Collum, and they would advance into the town and into the heart of the province unless they were checked by the courage of brave men and the labour of hands. Besides soldiers, diggers, carts and horses were wanting, and the open town, weak to resist attack through the foul ruins of its walls, must be strengthened by work that is proper, or at least hasty as the time allows. Unless this is done, danger hangs over the town and at the same time over the province, a danger that will be caused not by the neglect of the military tribunes but by the sloth of the praetors. Although these letters would have had little effect, given the fear of some and the obstinacy of others, their force was increased by the sudden arrival of Hohenlo among the Frisians. He hastened from Leeuwarden to Dokkum with ten cohorts by the quickest route, and compelled the rustic and townsfolk plebs to fortify the suitable places.

units.la: Mox copijs Stenuicum ad præsidia expeditis, dispersas cohortes conduci Doccomium præcepit, oppidumque præsidiario ad incursiones milite firmavit. Præter pedestres namque copias, quas Grovensteinius & Feruovius ducebant, Joannes quoq; Escheda cohortis ductor cum reliquis ex Enteniană & Nassovicâ legione oppidum ingressus est, cujus ambitus & suburbana specie castrorum ex magnitudine præsidij visebantur. Tum Oostmahornam Roblefij ætate à Bartoldo Entenio opere circumductam, qua Ea amnis latissimis in æstuaria aquis effunditur, vallo quoque terreo præcinxit, eïque suæ cohortis præsidium imposuit. Dein ut omne littus, quod canales omnium rivorumque demittit, Collumanisque aut Dongricis agris & æstuario obtenditur hostibus inaccessum faceret, lenia quædam castella, amnibus ac mari obiecta rusticæ plebi defendenda commisit, omnemque illum Oostergoæ littoralem tractum armata multitudine obsepsit. Quæ discors & parendi rursum insolens, quod stipendia ad diem non præstarentur, importunius tribunos sollicitabat, ac ut ruptis desertisque signis venale sacramentum inopis domini fastidio exuerent. Quod malum ne contumaciâ provincialium ingravescerët autoritate supremi Senatus apparitores in præturas passim ablegati, qui armatarum cohortium ope bona distraherent. Pecuniam quoque obluctanti populo extortam, aut ex divenditis bonis collectam Paulo Gellio tribuno ærarij penderent, quod illâ tempestate exsangue & impulsum tantæ rerum moli & militaribus impendijs non sufficiebat.
units.tr: Soon afterwards, having sent the troops out to the garrisons, he ordered the scattered cohorts to be brought together at Doccum, and strengthened the town with a garrison of soldiers against raids. Besides the infantry led by Grovensteinius and Feruovius, Joannes Escheda, a cohort commander, also entered the town with the rest of the Entenian and Nassau regiments. Its circuit and suburbs, given the size of the garrison, looked like a camp. Then he surrounded Oostmahorn with an earthen rampart, a place Bartoldus Entenius had walled in the time of Roblef, where the river Ee pours into the broadest estuary waters, and placed a garrison of his cohort there. Next, so that the whole shore, into which all the canals and streams discharge and which lies along the Collumanian and Dongerdian fields and the estuary, might be made inaccessible to the enemy, he entrusted some small forts, exposed to the rivers and the sea, to the country people for defence, and enclosed the whole coastal tract of Oostergo with an armed multitude. This force, unruly and again unused to obedience, because their pay was not handed over on the day, harassed the tribunes more and more, and, with their ranks broken and deserted, tried to cast off, out of disgust at a poor master, the oath they had sold. To keep this evil from growing worse through the defiance of the provincials, officers of the supreme Senate were sent out everywhere into the provinces, to sell goods with the help of armed cohorts. The money extorted from the reluctant people, or collected from the goods sold, they were to pay to Paulus Gellius, treasury tribune, since at that time the treasury was drained, weighed down by such great affairs, and not sufficient for military expenses.

units.la: Quippe publicis sociarum provinciarum indictionibus recipiendis, etsi Ordines annuissent, ita plebs passim refragabatur speciecq; immodesti oneris obsequia & pacem exuebat. Quare nec Matthiæ Gubernatoris hortatu nec Ordinum generalium litteris quid profectum, reputante eodem po-pulo, pulo, liberam gentem, nec absolutis principum imperijs aut dominationi-bus ullo tempore obnoxiam importunis servitijs eximendam. Traduntͮ militum plurimos, sollicitatis perfidè etsi nequicquam tribunis, grege facto ultro à signis descivisse, metuq; periculi, an ob stipendia incertum, debilem exercitum labefactasse. Quare Hohenloiis, datis ad Ordines Frisiæ litteris, obsideri viarum spatia spiculatore petijt, ac ut defectores vinculis datis statuendis exemplis transmitterent.
units.tr: Indeed, although the Orders had agreed to accept the public levies of the allied provinces, the people everywhere objected, and under the pretext of an immoderate burden they cast off obedience and peace. Hence neither the exhortation of Matthias the Governor nor the letters of the General Orders achieved anything, the people reasoning that they were a free nation, never subject to the absolute commands of princes or to domination, and not to be exempted from burdensome services at any time. It is reported that very many soldiers, though the tribunes were treacherously solicited in vain, formed a crowd and voluntarily deserted the standards, and, out of fear of danger or uncertainty about their pay, weakened the army, already feeble. Therefore Hohenlo, having written to the Orders of Friesland, asked that the roads be watched by scouts, and that the deserters be sent over in chains so that examples might be made of them.

units.la: Joanni Fervouio cohortis ductori, qui per Barranum ac Ferverdicum agrum residuum tributi, quod in aureos florenos indictum erat, armatâ manu exegerat bimestre stipendium Kal. Jul. exsolutum. Litterae quoque passim in provinciam ad Quæstores publici indictionum æris missæ, ijsque constitutum, ut in Monasterienses, Dortumanos, vulgares Anglicos & Boechfeldicos pannos decem stuferos exigerent. Cerevisiæ quoque Steenuicanæ, aut Oldemarctanæ, tum apud Drentinos ac per Transssulaniam coctæ, singulas in tonnas sex stuferi, Hollandicæ octo penderentur. Igitur Doccomio oppido, foedâ rusticæ plebis ignaviâ, trecentorum militum ac operariorum industriâ munito, Cuningamus Ordines mercedem laborantibus poposcit, ac ut Hohenloiùm debilitato per excursiones & transfugia præsidio majoribus in Dantumanos cum copijs expedirent. Adeo dubiâ fide ac spe res per Frisiam fluebant, donec Aurantium suscepto præfecturæ imperio regundæ provinciæ à Matthiâ Gubernatore confirmatum constans fama annuntiaret. Quæ ut læta in spem prosperi Frisiorum animos erigebat, ita illi econtra hoc uno consternabantur, quod ejus præsentiam Brabantinæ & Flandricæ adhuc res postularent, gravissimaque belli & rerum moles illo rectore destituta fluctuare per Frisiam cogeretur. Quippe quadraginta peditum cohortes modico cum equitatu irruisse in Flandriam vulgabantur, esseque necessarium, ut Matthiæ Gubernatoris juventâ Aurantij consilijs subnixâ, Frisiorum rebus administrandis legatus decerneretur.
units.tr: To Joannes Fervouius, a cohort commander, who had extracted by armed force a two-month pay from the remaining tax land of Barrum and Ferverdicum, a payment was made on the Kalends of July. Letters were also sent everywhere into the province to the public treasurers of the levies of money, and it was settled that they should exact ten stuivers per piece on the Munster, Dortmund, common English and Boechfeld cloths. Beer brewed at Steenwijk or Oldemarkt, and likewise among the Drenthe people and across the Overijssel region, was to be taxed at six stuivers per tun, and Holland beer at eight. So, with the town of Doccum fortified by the shameful idleness of the country people and the industry of three hundred soldiers and workmen, Cuningamus asked the Orders for wages for the labourers, and that they should send larger forces into Dantumadeel, since the garrison had been weakened by sallies and desertions. Affairs flowed through Friesland with such doubtful faith and hope that a steady rumour announced that Orange, having taken up the command of the prefecture to govern the province, had been confirmed by Matthias the Governor. As this joyful news raised the spirits of the Frisians with hope of success, so on the other hand they were dismayed by this one thing: the affairs of Brabant and Flanders still required his presence, and the heavy weight of war and public business, left without that ruler, would be forced to drift through Friesland. Indeed, it was being reported that forty companies of foot with a small body of cavalry had burst into Flanders, and that it was necessary, with the youth of Matthias the Governor supported by Orange's counsels, to appoint a legate to manage the affairs of the Frisians.

units.la: Quare vicarium Præfecti imperium Bernardo Merodio Rumenio viro provectæ ætatis & prudentiæ non inopi ab Aurantio principe commissum, qui absentiam honestè excusando principalem affectum Frisiorum genti & simul Bernardum Merodium efficacissimis ad solatium litteris commendabat. Is verò vicariâ imperij potestate Aurantij & de consilio Archiducis & Ord. gener. acceptâ itineri se dedit, unaq; cum Barthio Idsaerda Legato, qui in ejus comitatu tum erat, Ultrajecti substitit, deque provinciæ administrandæ rationibus voluntatem Ordinum intellexit. Ibi hærens sarcinas ac impedimenta onerario navigio in Frisiam expediri fecit, exactoque inter publicas deliberationes tridui spatio valere provinciarum Legatos jussit. Mox ipse Harlingam provectus rebus urgentibus Leovardiam properavit, quâ in urbe concursu populi & procerum gratulationibus exceptus, de eorum consilio initia imperij auspicatus est. Ferunt grandiora tormenta bono rerum omini, continuis per urbem fragoribus displosa, armatosque civium manipulos ad gaudia, ut solent, ex novi rectoris adventu excitatos, ejus ac simul publicæ saluti fidem atque auxilia obtulisse. Adeo sepultam secundis fortium virorum virtutem adversæ res accenderant, postquam conjugum atque liberorum perculsæ facies, denique perituræ patriæ imago aut metus oculis cIↄ. Iↄ. LXXX. oculis obversabatur. Sic compositâ civitate patres coacti, advocatis in concilium Hohenloo & simul Merodio, quem asperis imperij rudimentis fortuna exercebat. Quare Didericus Sonoius acciendis in Hollandiam auxilijs confestim missus, & ut solvendo Delphzilae obsidio tum occupando Amaso flumini praesidiarias naves impetraret. Abelo quoq; Franckenae viro doctrinae eximio legationis ad socios onus injunctum, quos Ultrajecto antiquâ concilij sede amotos, Camporum in oppidum ad Isalae fluminis exitum conditio temporum detruserat. Ibi Franckena vir eloquentiae egregius salutatis socijs hoc modo disseruit.
units.tr: Therefore the vicarious command of the prefect was entrusted by Prince Orange to Bernard Merode of Rumen, a man of advanced age and no small prudence, who, honourably excusing the prince's absence, commended his affection to the Frisian people and at the same time commended Bernard Merode himself by most effective letters of consolation. He, having accepted the vicarious power of command from Orange, and with the advice of the Archduke and the General Orders, set out on the journey, and together with Barthius Idsaerda, the legate who was then in his company, halted at Utrecht, and there learned the Orders' wishes concerning how the province was to be administered. Staying there, he had his baggage and equipment sent to Friesland by a freight vessel, and, after a three-day interval spent in public deliberations, ordered the provincial legates to attend. Soon he himself went on to Harlingen, and, as affairs pressed, hastened to Leeuwarden, where he was received in the city with a crowd of people and the congratulations of the nobles, and on their advice began his rule under good auspices. They report that heavy artillery, fired continuously through the city as a good omen, and armed companies of citizens, roused, as usual, to rejoicing by the arrival of the new ruler, offered him their loyalty and help, and at the same time their aid for the public safety. So much had adverse circumstances kindled the courage of brave men, which prosperity had buried, after the faces of wives and children, struck with dismay, and finally the image of the perishing fatherland, or fear, stood before their eyes in the year 1580. With the city thus settled, the elders, calling Hohenlo and Merode to council, were compelled to deal with a man whom fortune was testing in the harsh beginnings of his command. Therefore Didericus Sonoius was sent at once to summon aid from Holland, and to obtain garrison ships to break the siege of Delfzijl and to occupy the river Ems. To Abelus also, a man of distinguished learning from Franeker, was assigned the burden of an embassy to the allies, whom the conditions of the times had driven from Utrecht, the ancient seat of the council, and pushed into the town of Kampen at the mouth of the river Ijssel. There Franeker, a man outstanding in eloquence, having greeted the allies, spoke as follows.

units.la: BELLVM omne in nos Frisios devolutum cernitis Socij.
units.tr: The whole war, Allies, you see, has been turned against us Frisians.

units.la: Quod quoniam sine auxilijs geri nostra ex infirmitate non potest, ita vel maxime necessum est, ut ea ex superiore Belgicâ, imprimis verò à vobis ex jure novissimi foederis habeamus: Quare copias per Drentinos & Omlandiam sparsas nostro sacramento militantes instrui stipendijs in auxilia petimus, ne illorum defectu lubricam fidem ex angustiâ aeris induant. Quin hoc etiam necessarium censemus, ut tormenta & omnem belli commeatum ex publico provinciarum armamentario habeamus, omneque castrense instrumentum communi aere paretur. Et quoniam locorum spatijs à nobis discreti providere nostrae imbecillitati non potestis, existumamus durante apud nos bello confessum vestrum Harlingae & in Frisijs habendum. Quo ita omnes ad casus & momenta rerum circumspecti nostram & simul sequiorem belli fortunam, vestrâ ope ac prudentiâ consilij praejuvetis. Sed aeris potissimum cum inopiâ luctamur, Socij, eoq; deventum est, ut decreto publico pecuniam & commeatum sumendum sub veniâ censeamus. Quae si sortem nostram excedat, quicquid ultrà impensum est, supplendum ex communi aerario aequissimum arbitramur.
units.tr: Since we cannot wage it without help, given our weakness, it is most necessary that we have aid from the upper Netherlands, and above all from you, by right of the newest covenant. We therefore ask that the troops scattered through Drenthe and Omland, serving under our oath, be put on pay as auxiliaries, so that for want of them their wavering loyalty does not fall into the grip of a shortage of money. We also think it necessary that we have artillery and all the munitions of war from the public arsenal of the provinces, and that all camp equipment be procured at common expense. And since you, separated from us by distance, cannot provide for our weakness, we think the assembly should, while the war lasts among us, be held at Harlingen and in Friesland. So, watching every chance and turn of events, you may help our fortune, whether better or worse, by your aid and prudent counsel. But we struggle chiefly with lack of money, Allies, and so it has come to this: we think that money and supplies should be raised by public decree, with your permission. If this exceeds our means, we judge it most fair that whatever is spent beyond that be made up from the common treasury.

units.la: Nam aliter nec interposita fides, nec societas nostra diu integra esse poterit & nisi communicatis consilijs unum in finem patriae commodum conspiremus. Atqui iterum testamur, nos eam sine auxilijs aut deleKuum ope tueri non posse. Quos cum haberi per Nyennortium & Hajonem Manningam conscribendis mille ferentarijs Hohenlous velit, ac ut totidem quingentis aureis autorentur, ita judicium aut assensum vestrum flagitamus & an è rep. ac foedere censeatis nutanti militiae & simul aerario tanto cum onere aut auxilio subveniri.
units.tr: For otherwise neither our pledged faith nor our alliance can long remain whole, unless by sharing counsels we unite for the country's advantage toward one end. Yet again we declare that we cannot defend it without auxiliaries or the help of levies. Hohenlohe wishes these levies to be enrolled through Nyenoort and Hajo Manninga, to raise a thousand light-armed men, and that as many be authorised at five hundred gold pieces each. We therefore ask your judgement or assent, and whether you think, in keeping with the commonwealth and the covenant, that the wavering army and the treasury, at so great a burden, should be relieved with aid.

units.la: Imprimis verò hoc agite, Socij, ut Aurantium ac simul Hollandos auxilia pro nobis petatis, ac ut illi cum Zelandis socijs nostris, intercipiendis hostium ad Delphzilam commeatibus, Amasum flumen praesidiariâ classe ingrediantur. Nam omnia nobis angusta esse ne vos ipsi quidem nescitis, nosque liberando Opslacho omne consilium, omnes vires impendisse. Ita onerarijs navibus ad Oostmabornam positis & milite nostro instructis, aestuaria maris fines ac provinciam nostram pedestribus equestribusq; copijs obsepsimus. Inde fit ut agri nostri ac simul opes atterantur, nostroque in exercitu annonae & commeatuum, demiq; rerum omnium penuria sit. Hosti verò, etsi Omlandiam quoque ac vicina depopuletur, ex Trans-Amasanis, Trans-Iadanisque tum Bremensium ac Monasterienfium tractu alimenta subvehuntur, factura hostibus certum & utile commercium nisi vestra cura ac apud externos intercessio praeveniat. Quare necessarium est, ut litteras ad Trans-Amasanæ Frisiæ, tum Oldenburgensium Comites, denique Bremenses & Monasterienses ocyus mittatis curetisque, ne quid illis ex regionibus hostibus auxilij, nobis incommodi obveniat.
units.tr: Above all, Allies, see to it that you seek auxiliaries for us from Orange and likewise from Holland, and that they, with our Zealand allies, enter the Ems river with a garrison fleet, intercepting the enemy's supplies at Delfzijl. For you yourselves know well that everything is strained for us, and that in freeing Oostwold we have spent all our counsel and all our strength. So, with transport ships placed at Oostmahorn and manned with our soldiers, we have blockaded the sea estuaries and our province with foot and horse. Hence our fields and resources are wasted, and our army lacks food and supplies, indeed everything. The enemy, though he ravages Omland and the neighbouring lands too, is supplied with provisions from across the Ems and the Lauwers, from the tracts of Bremen and Münster. This will become a certain and profitable trade for the enemy unless your care and intercession with foreign powers forestall it. It is therefore necessary that you send letters, and urge them with all speed, to East Frisia beyond the Ems, then to the counts of Oldenburg, and finally to Bremen and Münster, so that no aid from those regions comes to the enemy and no harm comes to us.

units.la: Hæc FRANCKENA:
units.tr: Thus Franckena.

units.la: Ad quae FOEDERATI:
units.tr: To which the Confederates replied:

units.la: PAVCI dies sunt, FRISII, cum Legati nostri in Geldriam, Hollandiam, Zelandiam & Vltrajectinos missi, quo provincijs copias, copijs stipendia assignarent. De reliquis sex cohortibus nullo are, per Drentiam & Omlandos agentibus similiter cogitavimus, daturi operam, stipendia à nobis, aut ab hostilibus agris tributa habituri sint. Quod ad commeatum belli attinet, eum censemus communi provinciarum ære coëmendum, exceptis tormentis machinisque quas quæque provincia suis impensis suæ defensioni paravit. Harlingam vero conventum nostrum Campis transferre, res nostræ hic non ferunt, ordinatis necdum per provincias stipendijs, & Zutphanien-sium Geldriæque agris incursionibus hostium expositis. Adhæc Lubberti Rhemensis tum Germanorum equestribus turmis recensendis dies hos diximus, adeo vario & diviso belli statu, ut de eo commodiore loco quam hoc ipso disponi non possit. Pecunias vero in usuras sumi consultum indicamus, esseque æquissimum, ut nimiâ æris erogatione gravati collatis rationibus sociorum opeleventur. Sed copias plures aut novos ferentarios conscribere, aut conscribi facere id nostræ potestatis non est, ita æquato tributis exercitu ut sine Aurantij aut nostrorum Ordinum decreto novis delectibus gravari ærarium non possit. Id Hohenloo nuper Daventriæ per nos significatum & quod ex Brabantiâ sperata auxilia novo ac ferentario milite non egeant. Interim tam auxiliares copias quam classem premendo Amaso Hollandos sociosque sollicitabimus, dabimusque operam, ne, quod Benthemio Comiti indicatum est, vicinis è locis commeatum hostis, vos detrimenta accipiatis. Hæc VII. Iul. Campis acta.
units.tr: Few days have passed, Frisians, since our envoys were sent to Gelderland, Holland, Zealand and the men of Utrecht, to assign troops to the provinces and pay to the troops. Concerning the remaining six cohorts, operating through Drenthe and Omland without any money, we have likewise considered giving attention, as to whether they will have pay from us or tribute from enemy lands. As for war supplies, we think they should be bought at the common expense of the provinces, except for artillery and engines, which each province has prepared at its own expense for its defence. But our affairs here do not allow us to move our assembly to Harlingen, since pay is not yet arranged through the provinces, and the lands of Zutphen and Gelderland lie open to enemy raids. Besides, we have appointed these days for the review of Lubbert of Rhede and the German cavalry squadrons, in so varied and divided a state of war that it cannot be arranged in a more convenient place than this. As for money, we declare it advisable to borrow at interest, and that it is most fair that you, burdened by excessive outlay, be relieved by the pooled accounts of the allies. But to raise more troops or new light-armed men, or to have them raised, is not in our power. The army, with tributes evened out, cannot be burdened with new levies, and so the treasury cannot bear it, without a decree of Orange or of our Orders. We lately made this known to Hohenlohe at Deventer, and that the auxiliaries hoped for from Brabant do not need new light-armed soldiers. Meanwhile, by pressing both the auxiliary forces and the fleet on the Ems, we will urge Holland and the allies, and we will take care that, as has been announced to Count Bentheim, the enemy get no supplies from nearby places, and that you suffer no harm. Done at Kamp, 7 July.

units.la: Mox Georgij Holsteinij ducentorum & amplius equitum cohors Leovardiam & in suburbanos agros præmissa, actâ ibidem nocte Doccomium perrexit, firmando præsidio ac intendendis militum vigilijs, quorum cohortes quorundam ex Iselsteinia legione fuga & egestas æris extenuaverat. Unde Hohenloüs decreto Ordinum impetrato, autorandis mille ferentarijs præfectos delegit, Egbertumque Stammerum cum mandatis Leovardiam ablegavit. Reliqua, quæ in secreto patrum tractanda decernebat, Ernesto Grovensteinio viro nobili commisit, unicumq; retinendi in officio militis remedium, pecuniam popposcit. Tum Taco Hettingha vir stirpis antiquæ militem per Dantumanos collegit, signumque ex agrariâ plebe erectum sacramento fœderis autoravit. Regneri quoque Idsij pedestris cohors per Sylvestres & Gesterlandiam conducta ad sacramentum adacta, fanoque in Roordahusano à Renico Cammingha censore Frisici exercitus recensita. Dein præsidiariæ naves è minoribus Frisijs Delphzilam missæ, adornataeque per Hollandiam vectoriæ, quæ transportandis in Frisiam auxilijs habiles majore numero subvectantibus quoque commeatibus expectabantur.
units.tr: Soon afterwards George of Holstein's cohort of two hundred and more horse was sent ahead to Leeuwarden and the suburban fields. After passing the night there, it went on to Dokkum, to strengthen the garrison and keep the soldiers on watch, since the flight and want of money had weakened some of the cohorts from the Iselstein legion. Whereupon Hohenlohe, having obtained a decree of the Orders, chose officers to enrol a thousand light-armed men, and sent Egbert Stammer to Leeuwarden with instructions. The remaining matters, which he judged should be handled in the secret council of the fathers, he entrusted to Ernst Grovenstein, a nobleman, and he demanded money as the only remedy for keeping the soldiers in obedience. Then Tako Hettinga, a man of ancient family, gathered soldiers through Dantumadiel, and enrolled under the oath of the covenant a standard raised from the country commons. Regner of Idsega's foot cohort was also brought through the Sylvester district and Gesterland and bound by oath, and it was reviewed in the temple at Roordahuizen by Renicus Camminga, censor of the Frisian army. Then garrison ships were sent from the lesser Frisians to Delfzijl, and transport vessels were fitted out through Holland, which were awaited, being fit to carry aid into Friesland, and in greater numbers to carry supplies too.

units.la: Quarum rerum famâ excitus Schenckius, qui refocillandis copijs Columi adhuc hærebat, adultâ nocte, quam sublustrem æstas faciebat, refectas alimoniâ ac otio cohortes festino itinere Doccomium duxit, militemque victoriâ & secundis rebus elatum oppugnandæ urbi instruxit. Quare agrorum incilibus stramento constratis rivos quosdam fœno, quod resectum æstivus labor collegerat, implevit, scalisque ac omni oppugnationum instrumento exterioribus propugnaculis admoto, acrem in-
units.tr: Roused by the report of these things, Schenck, who was still at Kollum refreshing his troops, led his cohorts, refreshed by food and rest, by a swift march to Dokkum in the dead of night, which the summer made half-bright. He drew up his soldiers, elated by victory and success, to storm the town. There he strewed the ditches of the fields with straw, filled certain channels with hay which summer labour had cut and gathered, and brought up scaling ladders and every siege engine to the outer bulwarks. Then he made a fierce assault on the town.

units.la: insultum & incondito militum clamore subjutum in oppidum fecit. Cæterum terreo vallo continuis imbribus, ut vestigia vix ferret, soluto, infirmi gradus militem fatigabant, cujus lassitudine ingruentem vim propugnantium vigor atque firmitas repellebat. Unde Schenckiani retroacti & glabritie soli præcipites dati, multâ cæde rejecti, in avia locorum profugêre nulloque ordine vagi & palantes Collumum rediere. Multi fugientium vadosis incilibus & imbrium continuâ eluvie lubricis hausti multata & cruore vulnerum fœda corpora victorum iris ac arbitrijs permisere. Ita fortuna more suo recentibus hostium prosperis adversa intermiscebat.
units.tr: ...with a disorderly shout from the soldiers. But the earthen rampart, loosened by continuous rain so that it hardly held a footprint, wearied the soldiers' unsteady steps, and the vigour and firmness of the defenders repulsed the attack by wearing them down. So Schenck's men were driven back, flung headlong by the slipperiness of the ground, beaten off with great slaughter, and fled by pathless ways, scattering without order and wandering back to Kollum. Many of the fugitives were swallowed by the shallow ditches, made slippery by the constant flood of rain, and their bodies, maimed and foul with the blood of their wounds, were left to the pleasure and will of the victors. Thus fortune, in her usual way, mingled adversity with the enemy's recent successes.

units.la: Creditum fuit, equitum turmam, quam Pieckius vir fortis ducebat, è Dongrijs ubi præsidium egerat accitam, pedestre imprimis præsidium præjuviße, eamque fugientes equorum pernicitate assecutam promiscuâ cæde delevisse.
units.tr: It was believed that a troop of horse, which brave Pieck led, summoned from Dongjum where it had been stationed, especially aided the foot garrison, and by the speed of its horses overtook the fugitives and destroyed them in general slaughter.

units.la: Annotatum invenio magnum cælati argenti pondus corrogandis stipendijs Amstelodamensibus à Legato pignori oblatum, ejusque consilium à malitiosis & provinciæ velut derelictæ fidem eluentibus invidiâ fœderis interversum. Igitur Lalainius Doccomio repulsus, quo fati infœlicitatem, & exeâ, ut solet, sui invidiem elevaret, Alexandro Farnesio infaustæ expeditionis seriem perscripsit, Hardenbergicamq; victoriam & secundas ad Opslachum & per Omlandiam res repetendo, prioris fortunæ commendationem novo & gravissimo Doccomianæ cladis vulneri obduxit. Quæ etsi Schenckij temeritate aut fiduciâ obvenisset, quasi tot prosperis usus in potestate fortunam haberet, ita Lalainius omnem cladis causam inclementijs naturæ imputabat; & quod medijs cancri ardoribus, velut eversâ anni temperie, continuo multorum dierum & frigidissimo imbre desuper fuso salubre oppugnationis consilium subvertisset. Sic quod errore aut culpâ Ducis evenerat, rerum naturæ attributum, more, uti assolet, humani ingenij, quod prosperis factorum successibus sua consilia adaptat, adversis providentiam involvit. Quare recollecto Collumi exercitu castris vallum produci jussit, haud ignarus fœderatos victores distributis apud Doccomium præsidijs, Dantumanos per agros excurrere.
units.tr: I find it recorded that a great weight of chased silver was offered in pledge by the Amsterdam legate to collect the pay, and that his plan was overturned by the odium of the covenant, malicious men washing away faith from a province as if it had been abandoned. So Lalaing, repulsed at Dokkum, in order to lighten, as is customary, his unlucky fate and his own unpopularity, wrote to Alexander Farnese an account of the ill-starred expedition. By recalling the Hardenberg victory and the successes at Oostwold and throughout Omland, he covered the credit of his earlier fortune with a new and most grievous wound from the Dokkum disaster. Although this had happened through Schenck's rashness or overconfidence, as if, having enjoyed so many successes, he held fortune in his power, Lalaing imputed the whole cause of the disaster to the harshness of nature. Because in the midst of the summer's heat, as if the temperate season of the year had been overturned, continuous rain of many days and a bitterly cold downpour poured from above, the wholesome plan of the siege was subverted. Thus what had come about through the error or fault of the commander was ascribed to the powers of nature, in the manner of the human mind, which adapts its plans to prosperous outcomes and wraps adversity in providence. Therefore, having gathered the army at Kollum again, he ordered the camp rampart to be extended, not unaware that the Confederate victors, with garrisons distributed at Dokkum, were roaming through the fields of Dantumadiel.

units.la: Tum apud Farnesium de commeatuum penuriâ questus, potiundæ Delphzilæ haud incertam spem fecit, populumq; Groninganum præstandis commeatibus difficilem acerbissimis litteris traduxit. Esse scilicet, qui in urbe annonæ fœcunda serendis in vulgum discordijs periti desiderio fœderis castrensem commeatum impediant, speciosâque libertatis voce & execratione servitij ne civitatem quidem justo regis præsidio haberi velint. Quare frænandos esse civium mores atterendumque armis aut per tributa populum, ne opibus ac commercio ad questum & lubidinem usus damno regiæ autoritatis luxuriet. Mitteret Farnesius auxilia circa Rhenum & per Clivios segni otio corrupta, quo agro Omlandico populationibus ac spolijs exhausto, Groningana quoque civitas impeditis commercijs & accisâ opulentiâ infirmetur. Neque enim aliter retundi posse ferocis & insolentis populi lasciviem, & nisi intromisso in urbem fortiore præsidio vulgus malis opinionibus imbutum intermissæ Inquisitionis æquissimo rigore corrigatur. Renovanda scilicet esse PhiPhilippi edicta morbisque animorum recrudescentibus usurpanda remedia persanandis vitijs opportuna. Adhaec solo eruenda veteris castelli rudera & extruendam de novo arcem esse, ut regiae dominationis ita civilis obsequij munimentum, subsidia quippe tantae moli à tributis haberi posse, aut si fisco, regio privatas opes justa severitas addixerit. Quae à Lalainio foederiter scripta ac à foederatis intercepta, largius infamì perfidiae testimonium improbissimo defectori praebuere.
units.tr: Then, at Farnese's camp, he complained of the shortage of supplies, held out a not uncertain hope of taking Delfzijl, and with the bitterest letters reproached the people of Groningen for being difficult about furnishing provisions. There were, he said, men in the city who, skilled at sowing discord among the common people in a year of abundant harvest, hindered the camp's supplies out of longing for the Union, and who, with the splendid cry of liberty and the abhorrence of slavery, did not want even the city held by the king's just garrison. Therefore the citizens' morals must be curbed and the people worn down by arms or taxes, lest they grow luxurious, using their wealth and commerce for profit and lust, to the loss of royal authority. Farnese should send auxiliaries along the Rhine and through Cleves, corrupted by idle leisure, so that, with the Ommelands land exhausted by raids and plunder, the city of Groningen too might be weakened by hindered commerce and reduced wealth. For otherwise the wantonness of a fierce and insolent people could not be checked; unless a stronger garrison were admitted into the city, the mob, steeped in bad opinions, must be corrected by the most just rigour of the Inquisition, long suspended. Naturally, the edicts of Philip must be renewed and the remedies suited to healing vices applied, since the diseases of the minds were breaking out again. Moreover, the ruins of the old castle must be dug out of the ground and a new citadel built, as a bulwark of royal dominion and civil obedience alike; the funds for so great a work could be had from taxes, or, if just severity should assign private wealth to the treasury. These things, written by Lalaing in a manner bound to the league, and intercepted by the Union, gave the most wicked deserter a larger testimony of infamous perfidy.

units.la: Quare ex clade animi aeger expeditis Collumo trans Lavicam castris omnes vires occupandae Delphzilanae munioni intendit, sollicitatoq; ne quicquam per Oyenbruggium ad deditionem praesidio, arctius obsessos praecinxit. Quippe Fivela amne & omni navigabili alveo obijce aut pontibus strato commeatuum penuria increscebat, & quod occlusis vijs ac itineribus auxiliorum spes atq; fiducia languesceret. Quibus & hoc accedebat, quod Amasus etsi disjunctissimis ripis patentem alveum foederatae classi ostenderet, qua Fivelam excipit, minoribus castellis premeretur obturatiq; portus ac canalium difficultas praesidiarias aegrius naves admitteret. Igitur summa obsessorum angustia Fernovius cum cohorte minoribus navigijs in Amasum provectus, missique à Cornputto, qui nandi peritia flumen transmitterent, obsesisq; auxilia annuntiarent. Caeterum omnes aditus locorum excubiae aut castella obsepserant. Unde Hohenlous, collectis quas poterat copijs, quinquaginta navium classe Doccomio ac Oostmahornā solvens Amasum ingressus est, deliberato, an in terram militem exponeret, an includendo commeatui flumen statione occuparet. Caeterum explorato Epirotas lancearios equites in castra Lalainij advenisse, Schenckiumque cum majore omni exercitu, iter per Omlandiam recta Delphzilam intendere, coepto destitit, & quod ipse nullo commeatu atque annonā instructus subvenire praesidio non posset. Quare levatis, quas in Amaso posuerat, anchoris relegere aestuaria coactus Doccomium revertit, Iselsteiniqe legionis tribunò reliquam in Amaso classem regendam consolandis obsessis commisit. Caeterum extrema annonae penuria pristinum obsessis robur excusserat, & quod auxiliares sociorum naves ex Hollandiā missae, ignavae & imbelles, ne tentato quidem solvendi officij consilio, torpescerent.
units.tr: Therefore, sick at heart from the defeat, he withdrew his army from Collum across the Lauwers and turned all his strength to the siege of the Delfzijl fortification. He also tried to ensure that nothing was done through Oenbrugge toward surrender of the garrison, and he closed in more tightly on the besieged. For the river Fivel and every navigable channel had been blocked or bridged, and the shortage of supplies grew; and since roads and routes were closed, the hope and confidence of relief were weakening. To this was added the fact that Amasus, although its widely separated banks offered an open channel to the Union fleet where the Fivel enters it, was pressed by smaller forts, and the blocking of the harbour and the difficulty of the canals made it harder for the garrison ships to get in. So, in the great distress of the besieged, Fernovius advanced into Amasus with a cohort in smaller vessels, and men were sent from Cornputt who, being good swimmers, would cross the river, reach the besieged and announce help. But guards and forts blocked all the approaches. Whereupon Hohenlo, gathering what troops he could, sailed from Dokkum and Oosthornhaven with fifty ships and entered Amasus, undecided whether to land soldiers or to occupy the river with a station to block the supplies. But learning that the Epirote lancer cavalry had come into Lalaing's camp, and that Schenck, with the whole larger army, was heading straight through Ommeland toward Delfzijl, he gave up the attempt, since he himself was without supplies or provisions and could not bring aid to the garrison. So, weighing the anchors he had set in Amasus, he was forced to sail back out of the estuaries and returned to Dokkum. He left the remaining fleet in Amasus to be commanded by the tribune of Iselstein's legion, to comfort the besieged. But the extreme shortage of food had already stripped the besieged of their former strength, and the auxiliary ships of the allies sent from Holland, lazy and unwarlike, grew sluggish even without attempting to break the siege.

units.la: Igitur Hohenlous desperatā obsidij solutione plebe rustica praesidio Doccomiensibus relictā, expediri copias Opslachum jussit, habitisq; Collumi, quo Schenckius aufugerat, stationibus, annonam militi poposcit. Quae cum aegrius & viarum difficultate quas continui imbres foedaverant, subvehi posset, ad emissarium Collumani deserti navibus petijt, ac ut Ordines ex agrarijs fortissimos quosq; ad numerum octingentorum tuendae orae maritimae armarent. Dein vastandis machinis ac necessarijs rebus octuaginta currus postulavit, raptoque celerius agmine Opslachum obsedit, locumque praesidij metu ac ignaviā suae potestatis fecit. Trecenti Lollio Lilluckema ductore praesidiarij inermes, solo commeatu impetrato exire munitione jussi, fide Hohenloo data, ne intra trimestre signa in Ordines ferrent.
units.tr: Therefore Hohenlo, despairing of lifting the siege, left the rustic population at Dokkum with the garrison and ordered the troops to move out toward Opslagt. Having taken over the posts at Collum, from which Schenck had fled, he demanded provisions for the soldiers. Since these could be carried only slowly and with difficulty over roads the constant rains had ruined, he sought boats from the outlet of the abandoned Collum canal, and ordered that the bravest men from the farming districts, up to eight hundred in number, be armed to guard the seacoast. Then, for the siege machines and necessary equipment, he demanded eighty wagons; and, moving his column more quickly, he laid siege to Opslagt, and through fear and cowardice the place was brought under his power. Three hundred garrison men under Lollio Lilluckema, unarmed, having obtained only leave to take provisions, were ordered out of the fortification, on Hohenlo's pledge that they would not bear arms against the Ordinances within three months.

units.la: Mox Monachozilam levi castrorum opere clausam ijsdem cum copijs in deditionem accepit, quam Sampson Hestenius Germanus cum trecentorum militum cohorte ad Lavicae amnis exitum cum imperio & praesidio cIↄ. Iↄ. LXXXX. sidio tenebat. Conditiones fuere: Ut depositis armis Heftenius cum suis munitione abiret, eumque Hohenloiis, procurata in triduum annona, navi Embdam conduci faceret. Sed Hohenloiis violata, quam hosti depactus erat, fide victos puppi navium alligatos spectantibus Delphzilanis in Amasum demisit, simulatoque an demergi vellet, funibus per flumen tractos inter ludibria ac pavores animandis obsessis habuit. Caeterum animus obsessos jam liquerat, quos fame aut annonae defectu minus fortes ac languidos dimissum e turri nigrius vexillum ostenderat. Unde caduceatores in castra Lalainij & simul intra Delphzilam missi, conventumque ut praesidiarius miles exarmatus albas virgas, velut exorata vitae venia ferens, munitione cederet, ducesque & cohortium praefectos vinculis datos Lalainij victoris clementiae aut severitati traderet. Ipse ad tres menses, quae foede habuerat, Ordinum sacramenta exueret, omnemque belli commeatum Lalainio relinqueret. Itaque exuta veteris obsequij religione centurionibus a proprio milite manus injectae, ne ibi quidem integro pudore, ut desertā turpiter munitione, praefectorum reverentiam retinēret. In eorum numero Asingha, Ioannes & Iacobus Entenij, Nicolaus Burmania, Vogelius Auricanus & Vliegerus Nikerckius fuere, quos Groningam Delphzila cum captivo aere abductos morti aut fugae alijsque belli casibus fortuna reservavit. Quippe carceri mancipatos, saevitiae locum belli lex & disciplina non reliquerat, etsi crederetur Lalainius militum suorum & Heftenij contumeliis irritatus, & ultro ex defectione ferox, effusione captivi sanguinis ultionem recenti ludibrio paravisse. Vogelius Auricanus, unus centurionum in custodia decessit, reliqui lytro aut arte vinculis exsoluti ad signa rediere.
units.tr: Soon after, with the same forces, he accepted into surrender Monnikenzijl, closed by a light field work. It was held by Samson Heftenius, a German, with a cohort of three hundred soldiers, at the mouth of the Lauwers, under his command and garrison. The terms were that Heftenius and his men, laying down their arms, should leave the fortification, and that Hohenlo would have them carried to Emden by ship, with provisions for three days. But Hohenlo broke the faith he had pledged to the enemy. He let the defeated men, tied to the sterns of the ships, be lowered into the Ems while the men of Delfzijl looked on; and, pretending to consider whether he wished them drowned, he kept them dragged on ropes through the river, to the mockery and terror of the besieged. But the spirit had already left the besieged, who, weakened by hunger and lack of supplies, had grown less brave and feeble; a black flag raised from the tower showed that they were giving up. Heralds were therefore sent at once into Lalaing's camp and into Delfzijl, and an agreement was reached that the garrison soldiers, disarmed and carrying white rods as men who have begged for their lives, should yield the fortification, and hand over their leaders and cohort commanders, bound in chains, to the clemency or severity of the victor Lalaing. Hohenlo himself, for three months, would release from the oaths of the Ordinances those whom he had foully kept bound, and leave all the war supplies to Lalaing.
