Therefore, distrustful of the king's actions, we sought the intercession of kings and princes, so that, if it could be arranged through arbiters, we might make peace with the king on equal terms, and we also sent our envoys to Cologne, so that peace might be drawn up with the agreement of the emperor and the electors of the Holy Roman Empire. But that conference had a hidden purpose: to tear province from province and ally from ally, so that by discord he might diminish the strength of the provinces, which was increased by their concord. Then he condemned us by a public edict as guilty of treason, instituted proscriptions, and set a price for whoever would be the assassin who removed Orange. Therefore, with all hope of peace broken, deprived of every remedy for our evils, and imitating the law and instinct of nature, by which we assert and defend the rights of our ancestors, and protect our wives, children, and finally our very posterity from violence and injury by another aid, a means of protecting our laws and ourselves having been found, we make known that we, compelled by the last necessity, by common vote and consent, have deprived the King of Spain of the right of lordship, pre-eminence, jurisdiction and all hereditary right of rule, and we shall not use his name and title as king; and we absolve all magistrates and the people from their oath to him. And since we have met with the Duke of Anjou, supported by the mandates of each province, and have granted to Archduke Matthias the mission he sought, we wish that the seals of the King of Spain be abolished, omitted and handed over to the estates of the provinces, to be used by whichever senate they shall use, whether that of Anjou, that of the province, or that of Orange. We also wish that gold and silver not be stamped with the king's name and insignia, and that the presidents, chancellors, senators, masters of accounts and the other officials, released from the oath which they swore to the king, now take an oath to us under a new formula. In order that all these things may have force and permanence, we commission the President and Chancellor of the Secret Council of Brabant, Guelders and the county of Zutphen, the President and Senate of Flanders, the President and Senate of Holland, the Masters of Accounts of Zeeland, the President and Senate of Friesland, the Praetor of Mechelen, the President and Senate of Utrecht, and others, to see that this our EDICT be published without any delay or dissimulation by the magistrates and officials, in the manner and place customary, since we have judged it fit to be decreed and made known for the good of the commonwealth.

units.la: Magistratibus Officialibus, ut hoc nostrum EDICTUM more locoque solitis publicari, sine ulla mora ac dissimulatione curent, quod ad utilitatem reip. decernendum vulgandumque existimavimus. Datum Hagæ in concessu Ord. Generalium vigesimo sexto mensis Iulij Anno 1581.
units.tr: The magistrates and officials are to see that this our EDICT is published in the customary manner and place, without any delay or concealment, since we have judged it useful to the commonwealth to decree and make it known. Given at The Hague, in the assembly of the General States, on the twenty-sixth day of July, in the year 1581.

units.la: Signatum
units.tr: Signed

units.la: I. DE ASSELIERS.
units.tr: I. DE ASSELIERS.

units.la: Mox IV. Kal. Aug. nova dicundi SACRAMENTI formula ab ijsdem præscripta, quæ amovendæ impositorum diffidentiæ hac jurisjurandi religione firmabatur:
units.tr: Soon after, on 29 July, a new form of oath, prescribed by the same authorities, was introduced; to remove the officials' distrust, it was confirmed by this sanction of an oath:

units.la: IURO me impositerum Regem Hispaniæ, non pro Principe aut Superiore agnituru, quin econtra eundem Hispaniæ Regem deserturum habituruműq; me ipsum pro eo, qui regiâ obedientiâ ad quam publico provinciarum nomine tenebar, solutus sim. Promitto itaq; juroq; me unitis Provincijs Brabantiæ, Geldriæ, Flandriæ, Hollandiæ ac Zelandiæ earumq; socijs ac fœderatis, tum eorundem Provinciali Senatui Magistratibusque ac Ordinibus Generalibus constitutis, fidelem, obsequentem obligatumque fore omneq; auxilium opemque pro viribus meis ipsis præstiturum contra prædictum Regem Hispaniæ ejusque asseclas, reliquosque provinciarum hostes, deniq; facturum ad quæ fidelis subditus unitarum provinciarum tenebitur. ITA ME DEUS ADJUVET. Actum Hagæ 29. Iul. Anno CIↄ. Iↄ. LXXXI.
units.tr: I swear that I will not acknowledge Philip, King of Spain, as prince or superior, but will rather renounce the same King of Spain and hold myself released from the obedience to the king by which I was bound in the name of the provinces. I therefore promise and swear that I will be faithful, obedient and bound to the united provinces of Brabant, Gelderland, Flanders, Holland and Zeeland, their allies and confederates, and likewise to their provincial council, magistrates and the General States now constituted; that I will render them all aid and help with my strength against the said King of Spain, his followers and the other enemies of the provinces; and finally that I will do whatever a faithful subject of the united provinces is bound to do. SO HELP ME GOD. Done at The Hague, 29 July, in the year 1581.

units.la: Quod Edictum etsi pro more promulgaretur, ita per provincias jam ante fœderi inligatas, quam per Frisiam, gratius acceptiusque fuit, quod plerique ex nobilitate regij nominis aut Romanæ sedis veneratione imbuti, nova imperia & religiones tum æqualium, ut in libertate fieri solet, dominationes fastidirent. Cui & hoc incommodi accedebat, quod dubiâ adhuc & ancipiti fortunâ Frisiorum in finibus & per Omlandiam Translavicanosque bellum traheretur, quod à parte Regis morte Renebergij & novi Ducis successione revicturum habiturumque prospera & prioribus adversa ominabantur.
units.tr: Although this edict was promulgated in the customary way, it was more welcome and acceptable in the provinces already bound in confederation than in Friesland. Most of the nobility, steeped in reverence for the royal name or for the Roman see, scorned new rulers and new religions, and domination by their equals, which tends to happen in a free state. There was also this added difficulty: the war in the Frisian territories and in Ommeland and the Trans-Lauwers districts was still being waged with doubtful and uncertain fortune. Our side, after the death of Renneberg and the succession of a new commander, predicted that the war would revive and that the prospects would be favourable for them and adverse for the earlier side.

units.la: Quippe Verdugius conscriptis Coloniensem per Episcopatum & confinia copijs octingentos milites etsi inermes ut Albada scribit, secundo Rheno versus Vesaliam ducebat, auctoratis insuper trecentorum equitum turmis qui Francisco Alençonio Andium Duce (.is Galliâ jam excesserat) deserto perfugarum more nova sacramenta & occasiones bellorum quaerebant. Quibuscum Vesaliae Clivorum subsistens facile sui adventus regiorumque auxiliorum famam vulgavit, quae per Geldriam vicinaque Rheno loca quaquaversum se spargens, novo cum Gubernatore novae quoque fortunae fiduciam neque vanis rumoribus praeferebat.
units.tr: Indeed Verdugo, having levied eight hundred soldiers, though unarmed as Albada writes, through the diocese of Cologne and the neighbouring regions, led them down the Rhine towards Wesel. In addition he had hired squadrons of three hundred cavalry who, having deserted Francis, Duke of Alençon (who had already left France), sought new oaths and opportunities for war in the manner of deserters. Remaining at Wesel in Cleves with these men, he spread word of his arrival and of the royal aid, and this rumour, spreading everywhere through Gelderland and the places near the Rhine, promised, with the new governor, fresh hope of fortune, and it was not based on empty reports.

units.la: Quare Cancellarius Senatusque Geldriae litteris in Frisiam datis nuntiavere.
units.tr: Accordingly the Chancellor and Council of Gelderland sent letters to Friesland announcing this.

units.la: Intelleča Verdugij trans Rhenum expeditione Zutphaniae se comitatu vicinisque locis metuisse. Caeterum certiore veri famâ accepisse eundem VERDUGIUM Grollam prope castra metatum Frisiae comminari, velut in praedam data. Istum in finem exigua stipendia equiti triginta peditì quindecim sestertios assignasse, quo ex rapto auctiora faciat, utilisque agrorum populatione majora ordinarijs emolumenta & juxta gloriam ex direptis hostium finibus accipiat. Monere itaque se Frisios socios ac juxta vicinos, ut in armis quanto ecyus sint finiumque suorum curam & rationem collocatis ibidem praesidijs habeant.
units.tr: They understood that, with Verdugo's expedition across the Rhine, Zutphen and the neighbouring places feared for their territory. However, they had received more reliable news that the same Verdugo had encamped near Grollo, threatening Friesland as if it had been given over to plunder. To this end he had assigned small pay, thirty sestertii to each horseman and fifteen to each foot soldier, so that from the spoil they might grow richer, and gain greater profit from the ravaging of the fields, and, as is the glory of plundering enemy lands, a greater reward. They therefore warn the Frisians, as allies and close neighbours, to be under arms and to take as much care as they can for their borders, and to place garrisons there.

units.la: Quae per Everardum Reidanum Geldriae Graphiarium & Annalium scriptorem Frisijs communicata, populum discriminis & periculi ignarum fidelis officij monuere.
units.tr: These matters were communicated to the Frisians by Everard Reidanus, Gelderland's clerk of the records and annalist, who warned the people, ignorant of the danger and peril, out of loyal duty.

units.la: Similes litterae à provinciali Senatu (qui trans ac cis Mosam à missione Matthiae Austrio factâ & per tardum Andini in Belgicam adventum constitutus erat) ad Deputatos Frisiae datae.
units.tr: Similar letters were sent to the deputies of Friesland by the provincial council (which had been constituted on both sides of the Meuse after the mission of Matthias of Austria and the late arrival of Andinus in Belgium).

units.la: Caeterum Verdugius belli & rerum prudens longo viarum flexu, qui mille & quingentos faciebat, militem circumduxit, peragratisq; Drentiae, qua Westphaliam spectat, finibus Groningam advenit, quem locum ante antecessoris sui vestigia premens sedem novo imperio & simul Philippi bello delegerat. Ubi inter gaudia & spes populi exceptus aegros omnes, nuperoque ex conflictu saucios adivit, educendisque foras & ad Reidam copijs omnia ordinavit.
units.tr: Verdugo, however, being skilled in war and in affairs, led his soldiers around by a long winding route of fifteen hundred miles, passed through the territory of Drenthe, which looks toward Westphalia, and came to Groningen. He had chosen this place, following in the footsteps of his predecessor, as the seat of the new rule and at the same time of the war for Philip. There, received with joy and hope by the people, he visited all the sick and those recently wounded in the fighting, and he arranged everything for bringing them out and for the troops at Reide.

units.la: Wigboldus enim Eusemius Nienortius quatuor peditum cohortes isthuc duxerat, quo locum ad instar promontorij, sinum in Dullartum procurrentem & Embdae urbi Amasoque flumini vicinum occuparet. Quod fugâ regij praesidij nullâ molestiâ effectum est, desiderato tantum ut locum naturâ & ingenio palustris agri munitum novo opere emuniret. Sed fossores milites, arma, pecuniae praeterque ista omnia inter licentiosos & morum solutos disciplina exigebatur, quae neglectâ parendi imperandique lege, & crescentibus etiam nullo socialis imperij respectu flagitijs metum ac formidinem ex adventante Verdugio induerat. Qui decem cohortibus pedestri itinere Reidam perductis disparsis palantibusque Nienortij copijs facile munitionis potitus est; solo Caterio viro nobili & cohortis praefecto fortiter rem gerente glande trajecto. Norritius scribit trecentos milites foederatos sine armis signisque Reidâ excedere jussos, scaphisque vectos & castris jam proximos arma & stipendia petijsse. Quae ipsa ut toti foederato exercitui praestarentur, acri & ad movendos Ordinum animos valido hortatu idem Norritius urge-
units.tr: For Wigbold Eusemius Nienort had led four cohorts of foot to that place, to occupy a spot like a promontory, a bay running out into the Dollard, near the city of Emden and the river Ems. This was done without difficulty, since the royal garrison fled, though it was still wanted to fortify the place, which was protected by nature and by the marshy land, with new works. But diggers, soldiers, arms and money were needed, and besides all this discipline was required among the licentious and loose in morals, which, with the law of obeying and commanding neglected, and with crimes increasing without any respect for the common rule, had brought fear and dread upon them at the approach of Verdugo. He led ten cohorts on foot to Reide, and, with Nienort's scattered and wandering troops, easily took possession of the fortification; only Caterius, a nobleman and commander of a cohort, fought bravely and was struck by a bullet. Norritius writes that three hundred confederate soldiers, ordered to leave Reide without arms or standards, had been carried by boats and, now near the camp, asked for arms and pay. So that these might be furnished to the whole confederate army, Norritius, with a sharp exhortation powerful for stirring the spirits of the States, urged...

units.la: Reidam petit.
units.tr: He makes for Reide.

units.la: Est obtinei. clo. Io. urgebat, quo hostem de Neosilo cogitantem praebito ære majore auxilia, daciâ & vigore corporum adoriatur.
units.tr: ...urged, so that, with greater money offered, they might attack the enemy, who was thinking of Neosilum, with auxiliary troops, daring and vigour of body.

units.la: Ita omnis Omlandia ab Amaso in Lavicam amnem protensa, ejectis foederatis Hispano iterum asserta, retracto jam ante Selverdiâ in Frisiam & circa Collumanos Norritio quem egens aeris & ex hoc solutior exercitus, tum regia Verdugij auxilio rumoribus, ut solent, aucta, movenda ad castra compulerant. Unde per Frisiam metu orto Abelus Franckena Historiae scriptor pro Legato Hagam missus, qui auxilia, qui stipendia tumultuantibus copijs peteret, Principemque Aurantium sociosq; de toto rerum statu edoceret.
units.tr: Thus all Ommeland, stretching from the Ems to the Lauwers river, having been driven from the confederates, was again secured for the Spanish. Norritius had been compelled to withdraw into Friesland, past Selwerd, and near Collum to the camp, for the army was in need of money and was therefore less bound by discipline; and the rumours of Verdugo's royal aid, as usual, had increased their strength. Hence, with fear arising through Friesland, Abel Frankena, a historian, was sent to The Hague as envoy, to ask for aid and pay for the troops in turmoil, and to inform the Prince of Orange and the allies about the whole state of affairs.

units.la: Is copiâ fandi petitâ hunc in modum disseruit:
units.tr: Having asked for permission to speak, he addressed them in this manner:

units.la: RERUM nostrarum conditio, Socij, modo secundis nos efferens, modo deprimens adversis, ut res mortalium ferunt, ea hoc ipso tempore est, ut deterior esse non possit. Castra nostra Selverdiam tertiumque aburbe Groningâ lapidem promota erant, & jam metu civitas tenebatur, ne nostra fierent. Tarditate nostrâ & lenitudine agendi usus hostis auxilia contraxit, & sub Verdugio superato Rheno amne Groningam perductus est. Ibi quae ad bellum pro PHILIPPO gerendum spectabant, novi Ducis rectorisque prudentia ordinavit, captaque à nobis Reidâ, mox potitus hostis est. Igitur copiae nostrae egentiâ stipendiorum effraenes & turbidae trans Lavicam in Frisiae nostrae agros reductae sunt, ulteriorem receptum moliturae, aut vastaturae provinciam nisi sociali fide auxilia & commeatum, ac quod primum disciplinae robur ac firmamentum est, pecuniam & stipendia mittatis.
units.tr: The condition of our affairs, friends, which at one time lifts us up with success and at another depresses us with adversity, as the lot of mortals is, is such at this very time that it cannot be worse. Our camps had been advanced to Selwerd and to a point three miles from the city of Groningen, and already the city was in fear lest it should fall into our hands. Through our slowness and our lax way of acting, the enemy, taking advantage, gathered auxiliary forces, and under Verdugo, having crossed the Rhine, was brought to Groningen. There the new leader and ruler arranged, with prudence, what pertained to waging war for Philip; and after Reide was taken by us, the enemy soon took possession of it. Therefore our troops, unrestrained and in turmoil from lack of pay, have been drawn back across the Lauwers into the fields of our Friesland, about to make a further retreat or to lay waste the province, unless you send, out of common loyalty, aid and supplies, and money and pay, which is the first strength and foundation of discipline.

units.la: RESPONSUM Legato à Principe & Provinciali Senatui fuit.
units.tr: The reply given to the envoy by the Prince and the Provincial Senate.

units.la: Se GULIELMUM NASSOVIUM cum sex cohortibus peditum in FRISIOS missuros, evocaturosque minore Frisiâ SONNOIUM qui conscensis navibus suis cum copijs maiorem in FRISIAM maturet. Quod ad pecuniam attineret, delegaturos quosdam è Senatu suo qui propediem Legatum subsequantur, pecuniamque & commeatum ita postulantibus rebus exercitui subministrent.
units.tr: They said that William Nassau would set out for Friesland with six cohorts of infantry and would summon Sonnoy from Lesser Friesland, who would embark his ships with his troops and hasten to Greater Friesland. As for the money, they would appoint some members of their Senate, who would soon follow the envoy and supply the army with money and provisions, as the needs of the situation demanded.

units.la: Ita Legatus (quod v. Eid. sextilis factum in Ephemeride suâ notat) in Frisiam reversus.
units.tr: So the envoy returned to Friesland, as he notes in his diary for the fifth day before the Ides of August.

units.la: Idem addit Senatum provincialem istâ lege stipendiâ se datiurum promisisse, si Frisij viginti quinque aureorum millia mutuum darent, communique aerario subsidium de suo praestarent. Eundem quoque Senatum Renicum Dekamam Stavoranae nuper arci cum cohorte praefectum arctiori custodiae dedisse, tarditatemque & moram suae in Frisios profectionis non tam suâ culpâ quam defectu aerarij evenisse, quod Hollandico Zelandorumque subsidio sublevatum, majora socijs Frisijs subsidia daturum foret.
units.tr: He adds that the Provincial Senate had promised to provide pay on the condition that the Frisians lend twenty-five thousand gold pieces and contribute support of their own to the common treasury. He also reports that the same Senate had lately placed Renicus Dekama, the commander of the citadel at Stavoren, under closer guard, and that the delay and hold-up in his march against the Frisians had come not so much from his own fault as from a lack of funds. With help from Holland and Zeeland, he said, he would give the allied Frisians greater support.

units.la: Reperio in actis ex eodem quoque Senatu mensis Sextilis initio Frisicae gentis viros Cornelium Coninxium Iurisperitum & Leonem Beiemum virum nobilem in Zelandiam ad Aurantium proceresque istius gentis missos, quo praesidiorum per provincias quasque distribuendorum certum numerum exigerent, stipendiorumque ratione inità ordinarium exexsolvendis militaribus copiis tempus impetrarent. Magistratum quoque Embdanum missis in Frisiam hoc tempore litteris ob Amasum flumen proximosque agros navibus copiisque foederatis infestatos querimoniam attulisse, salvosque gentium fines, salva jura orasse.
units.tr: I find in the records of the same Senate that, at the beginning of August, two men of the Frisian nation, Cornelius Coninxius, a jurist, and Leo Beiema, a nobleman, were sent to Zeeland, to William of Orange and the leaders of that nation. They were to demand a fixed number of garrisons to be distributed throughout the provinces and, having worked out a plan for pay, to obtain a set time for paying the troops in full. The magistrates of Emden, too, had sent letters to Friesland at this time, complaining about the allied ships and troops harassing the River Ems and the neighbouring fields, and begging that the borders of their peoples be kept safe and their rights preserved.

units.la: Igitur regresso in interiora Frisiae Norritio Angli equites quidam non numerato aere populabundi planos per agros se sparsere, Leovardiamque & in suburbana proveêti rusticâ ex plebe caesi vulneratique sunt. Quod agrariae gentis factum, etsi honesto praetextu Frisij velarent, ita Norritius indignissime ferebat, equitem suum non penitatis stipendijs, alimenta vitae quaerentem à sociali armatàque rusticorum manu morte vulnerumq; foeditate multari. Quare litteras ad Delegatos Frisiae dedit, vehementiq; motae mentis ostentatione provinciâ se abiturum ni rustici populi ferociae obviam iretur, comminatus est. Innuebat quippe hoc in Imperatoris Ducisque bellici, qualis ipse foret, arbitrio constitutum esse, partiri copias equitemque castris emissum & annonae stipendijq; egenum rusticorum pagis villisque inducere. Cui rei cum quidam ex Delegatis tacitè contradicerent, qui à mercenario socioq; milite diripi villas, atterique provincialium fortunas nolebant, postero acerbiores dedit. Caeterum revocatâ mente velut, quae evenerant, dissimulans, commeatum castris petijt, Neosilumque emunjri postulavit. Doconi quoque Frisio hostilium actionum rerumque fidissimo exploratori honestam mercedem praestari sollicitavit, quo Praetori Neosilano alijsque prospiceretur, quorum interesset hostium consilia praestandae suorum securitati cognoscere.
units.tr: So when Norris had withdrawn into the interior of Friesland, some English horsemen, unpaid and roaming, scattered across the flat fields; near Leeuwarden and in its suburbs they were attacked by country folk, and some were wounded. Although the Frisians covered this deed with a respectable pretext, Norris took it very badly that his cavalryman, who was seeking food to live on, should be punished with death and foul wounds by an armed body of peasants allied to the cause. So he wrote a letter to the Frisian deputies and, showing great agitation of mind, threatened that he would leave the province unless the fierceness of the country people was checked. He hinted that it lay in the power of the commander-in-chief and the general, whatever he himself might be, to divide the forces, send out cavalry from the camp, and bring them down upon the villages and farms of country folk who lacked both grain and pay. When some of the deputies objected in private to this, since they did not want the villages plundered by hired soldiers, who were allies, and the fortunes of the provincials worn away, he became harsher the next day. Yet, as if setting aside what had happened and recovering his composure, he asked for provisions for the camp and requested that Neosilum be cleared of its soldiers. He also tried to secure an honest reward for the Frisian deacon, a most trustworthy spy on hostile actions and plans, so that the praetor of Neosilum and others, whose interest it was to know the enemy's intentions in order to keep their own people safe, might be provided for.

units.la: Carolus Roorda scribit novam dissensionum materiem Ordinibus Hollandiae cum Senatu provinciali tum subortam magnum firmandae reip. impedimentum attulisse, eoque amoto, prosperum stabilecq; imperium novae libertati foederique gentium portendi. Tum Eckij & Gorae equitum turmas, quae Cunerâ in Stellinguerfios descensurae dicebantur recensendas à Martinio quodam censore exercitus perscripsit, quo vagae huc usque & modo Geldriae, modo Trans-Isulaniae finibus haerentes Frisiorum castris copiisque jungerentur.
units.tr: Carolus Roorda writes that a new source of dissension, arising with the Provincial Senate, had brought a great obstacle to the strengthening of the commonwealth in the eyes of the States of Holland; and that with this removed, a prosperous and stable government was promised to the new liberty and to the alliance of the nations. Then he wrote down, as reviewed by a certain Martinius, the commissioner of the army, the troops of horse from Eck and Gora, which were said to be about to descend from Cuneraga into the Stellingwerf district. They had hitherto been wandering, now stationed in the territory of Gelderland, now in that of Overijssel, and were to be joined to the camps and forces of the Frisians.

units.la: Actis traditum est Verdugium contractis in unum copijs caenobio Adoardico noctem tum egisse, progressumque Northormum Omlandiae pagum, obsidionem Neosilo destinavisse. Quae quanquam de isto loco oppugnando tum temporis dicerentur, qui solus per Omlandiam vincendus Verdugio restabat, tamen majora solitis consilia tum agitabantur. Sive in Verdugium fiducia nova auxilia novas legiones ducentem, sive illorum scelere ac perfidia, qui in Frisia tutissima suorum rerum possessione per aequitatem indulgentiamq; foederati populi fruentes, regiam fidem ac sacramenta exolaturibus patriâ profitebantur.
units.tr: It is recorded in the accounts that Verdugo, having gathered his forces together, spent the night at the monastery of Adoard, and then, advancing to Northorm, a village in Ommeland, planned a siege of Neosilum. Although at that time these things were said about attacking that place, which alone remained for Verdugo to conquer in Ommeland, far greater plans were then being pursued. Either Verdugo, leading new legions with new hopes of aid, was relying on them, or the people who, enjoying the most secure possession of their own affairs in Friesland through the fairness and indulgence of the allied nation, were declaring with their country's consent that they would break the royal faith and oaths, were relying on their treachery and perfidy.

units.la: Quorum pars, quae Groningae agebat, cognito Anglorum equites rusticae plebis, quae arma induerat, virtute caesos dissipatosq; litteras in Frisiam istiusmodi misit. spe solutionis alitus agri messem & anni proventum stipendijs applicaturus sit. Quæ ipsa quoque nisi hoc ipso mittantur, tam de exercitu quam de rep. agi. Cæterum adventu Senatus provincialis nuntiato, qui Leovardiæ jam erat, exorti animorum motus derepente consederunt, erecto ex ipso in lætiora exercitu, quod præter auxiliares copias per Gulielmum Ludovicum Nassovium advectas, pecuniam quoq; adferre padicandis legionibus crederetur.
units.tr: Part of them, who were acting at Groningen, having learned that English horsemen had been defeated and scattered by the bravery of the country people who had taken up arms, sent a letter of this kind into Friesland: that, buoyed by the hope of relief, they would apply the harvest of the field and the year's yield to the pay of the troops. Unless these things were sent immediately, the army and the commonwealth itself would be in danger. However, when the news arrived of the coming of the Provincial Senate, which was already at Leeuwarden, the rising passions of the people suddenly subsided, and the army was raised to a more cheerful mood, because it was believed that, besides the auxiliary forces brought in by William Louis of Nassau, the Senate would also bring money to pay the legions.

units.la: Franckena in Ephemeride notat 26. Sept. omne stipendium exercitui solutum infectaque pestilentiæ vitio castra cum tribunis præfectisq; cohortium plurimos militum abstulisse. Quosdam quoque è Tietierckijs Smallingijsque captivos, qui Hermanni Martenij copiarum censoris militumque ex cohorte Episcopij bona diripuerant, Collumum in castra perductos procurante Ioanne Ratallero loci prætore data Martenio militique damna pensasse. Doconem quoque Martnam virum nobilem jam ante memoratum, morte Livij Beiemi in Senatum provincialem cooptatum, qui acceptis in mutuum à nostrâ gente viginti aureorum millibus de pellendo Frisiorum finibus Verdugio tum cogitabat. Itaque tum annonâ & commeatu ubertim castris, quæ Collumi adhuc erant, inlato, stipendijsq; Anglicæ legioni, quæ maxumè tumultuata erat, persolutis, vigor atq; promptitudo militaribus animis redierent, quos ante desides & ex hoc seditioni proximos egentia æris corruperat.
units.tr: Franckena notes in his diary that on 26 September all the pay was handed over to the army, and that a pestilence infected the camp and carried off many of the tribunes, prefects, and cohort soldiers. Some of the prisoners from Tietjerk and Smallingerland, who had plundered the goods of Hermann Martens, the commissioner of the forces, and of a soldier of Episcopius' cohort, were brought to the camp at Collum, through the agency of John Ratallerus, the praetor of that place, and paid compensation for the losses to Martens and the soldier. Doko Marna, a nobleman already mentioned, who had been co-opted into the Provincial Senate after the death of Livius Beiema, was then planning, having received twenty thousand gold pieces on loan from our nation, to drive Verdugo out of the Frisian territory. And so, with provisions and supplies brought in abundance to the camp that was still at Collum, and with pay given to the English legion, which had been most in uproar, the vigour and readiness of the soldiers' spirits returned; these men had previously been idle, and, since they were close to mutiny because of this, the shortage of money had corrupted them.

units.la: Quorum ignarus Verdugius, qui Norritij exercitum seditione laceratum ex non soluto ære rebatur, Groningâ Adoardiam post castra Nortbormum movit, ductisq; secum viginti & quatuor peditum signis ac quinque equitum turmis additis ut Franckena notat, leve vallum fossamq; castris suis præduxit prælioque se paravit. Neq; minor Norritio virtutis eximio animus erat, quem ultro experiundis arduis asperisque facilem excitasse Frisij subeundum ad certamen odio ac fastidio castrensis otij credebant. Quare ducto per Neosilum exercitu recto itinere tormentis campestribus instructus Northormum contendit, Verdugiumque instructis ad pugnam ordinibus & quidem præmissâ re divinâ parantem insigni alacritate adortus est. Quæ precum solemnitas etsi Anglis ludibrio ac inrisui haberetur, ita plurimum ad fortunam hostium & fœderati exercitus secutam adversitatem valuisse dicebatur.
units.tr: Verdugo, unaware of this, and believing that Norris's army was torn by mutiny because its pay had not been paid, moved from Groningen to Adoard, and after the camp at Northorm, as Franckena notes, he led out his army, with twenty-four infantry standards and five squadrons of cavalry added, and drew a light rampart and ditch before his camp and prepared himself for battle. Nor was Norris's spirit less courageous in valour; the Frisians believed that his eagerness for dangerous and harsh trials had roused him, and that he went readily to the contest, out of hatred and disgust for the idleness of the camp. So, leading his army through Neosilum in a straight line, Norris marched to Northorm with his field artillery in order, and attacked Verdugo, who was preparing for battle with his ranks drawn up, having first held a religious rite, with remarkable zeal. Although this solemnity of prayers was regarded by the English as a joke and a laughing-stock, it was said to have greatly helped the fortune of the enemy and the adversity that followed the allied army.

units.la: Norritium tredecim Anglorum signa, sex Gulielmi Ludovici Nassovij, novem Sonnoi, ex Nienortianæ legionis vexilla sequebantur. Quibuscum in planitiem campumque, qui Northormo ab occasu prætenditur, descendens, signo dato, stipatusque Gulielmo Ludovico Nassovio tanto in hostem Verdugiumque impetu invectus est, ut luxatis hostium ordinibus Verdugij peditem arma, ne oneri forent, projicientem intra Northormum compelleret. Unde victoriæ magna apud Norritium spes erat, quæ, sicut omnia mortalium, instabili fortunæ innixa magnorum sæpe ducum virtutem confudit. Quo tempore lixis calonisbusque qui hostium castra sequebantur, de fugâ quoque cogitatum commentarij prodidere, in quam totus Verdugij exercitus effusus fuisset, nisi Verdugius equestres turmas inclinantibus jam ordinibus immiscuisset. Quæ visâ Anglorum paucitate & raris cuneris, Anglorum in legionem tantâ animi fortitudine procurrerunt ut loco moverent, motamque referre pedem jussam fugæ darent. Quod ne Norritio quidem & Gulielmo Ludovico Nassovio cognitum, quos rem strennuè gerentes medijs confertissimisque hostibus animi vigor & cupido gloriæ intruserat. Qui ubi à tergo versam pugnæ faciem & suorum fugam notavere, aperta ferro via, multisque circum casis periculo subductì sunt.
units.tr: Thirteen English standards followed Norris, six of William Louis of Nassau, nine of Sonnoy, and the banners of the Nienorter legion. With these he descended into the plain and field that stretches west of Northorm, and, giving the signal and attended by William Louis of Nassau, he charged the enemy and Verdugo with such force that, breaking up the enemy ranks, he drove Verdugo's infantry, who were throwing away their arms so they would not be a burden, back into Northorm. From this came great hope of victory for Norris, which, like all things of mortals, rested on unstable fortune and confused the valour of great commanders, often. At that time the commentaries reported that the camp-followers and sutlers who attended the enemy camp were also thinking of flight, into which the whole of Verdugo's army would have been scattered, had Verdugo not thrown his cavalry squadrons into the wavering ranks. Seeing the paucity of the English and their thin wedges, the enemy rushed against the English legion with such courage that they forced it to give ground, and, when it was ordered to retreat, they turned that movement into flight. Neither Norris nor William Louis of Nassau knew this, since the energy of spirit and desire for glory had thrust them, fighting bravely, into the midst of the densest enemy. When they noticed the face of the battle turned behind them and their men in flight, they cut a path through the steel and, after many dangers, withdrew from the enemy.

units.la: Tradunt autores Gulielmum Ludovicum quinque glandibus plumbeis thorace ferreo exceptis, unà sed invalidà in crus prolapsa prælio excessisse, reservatumque fato majoribus rebus primos juventæ annos il- lustri gloriâ honestasse.
units.tr: Authors relate that William Louis, having received five lead balls in his iron breastplate, and one more, though a weak one, that had fallen into his leg, left the battle; and that fate, which had reserved him for greater things, had made the first years of his youth illustrious with glory.

units.la: Franckena notat causam cladis semiplenis copijs & centurionum perfidiæ vulgo tum imputatam, & quod in triginta & ultra peditum signis ne terna quidem millia magno reip. incommodo numerarentur. Alij adversitatem hunc à Norritij equite, qui à pedite Verdugij Northormo procurrente progredi prohibitus fuerat, profectam fuisse tradunt, multaque fœderatis iniqua, viarum angustiam & confertas condensatafq; Norritij turmas, mox confusos ordines, equitumq; fugam concurrisse.
units.tr: Franckena notes that the cause of the disaster was commonly attributed at the time to the half-strength forces and the treachery of the captains, and that among the thirty-odd companies of foot not even three thousand were counted, to the great detriment of the commonwealth. Others report that the reverse arose from the horseman Norritius, who, prevented from advancing when the foot under Verdugius and Northormus rushed forward, was held back; and that many things unfavourable to the confederates coincided: the narrowness of the roads, the crowded and massed squadrons of Norritius, then the disordered ranks and the flight of the horsemen.

units.la: Mihi Cl. Franckenæ fidem secuto ab Anglis à Verdugij equitatu retroactis malum evenisse compertum, impeditaque quo minus officium facerent, tormenta inclinante jam acie Verdugio cessisse. Franckena addit multos milites fœderatos in præcipitem fugam effusos, à lanceario Verdugij, qui insequebatur, equite cæsos, fossisque ac incilibus immersos armorum ponere aut vi prementium perijsse. Quâ clade mediam peditum partem sublatam autores notant, æque præcipuis Rudolphum Scullium, Winandum Ommerium, Carolum Wingardium, Petrum Berensteinium, Matthiam Kærtium, Gerardum Entenium, Cornelium Loënium, ex Anglis Cottonium, Episcopium, Fuillamium, è præfectis equitum Henricum Eckium, Bellevinium & Joannem Nisbetium cecidisse. Nec incruenta Verdugio victoria fuit, quingentis sexcentisve in regio Philippi exercitu desideratis. Pugna Prid. Kal. Octob. facta.
units.tr: I, following the trustworthy Franckena, have found that the misfortune came from the English being driven back by Verdugius' cavalry, and that they were hindered from doing their duty, so that the artillery gave way as Verdugius' line was already advancing. Franckena adds that many confederate soldiers were scattered in headlong flight, cut down by the lancers of Verdugius' cavalry as they pursued, and that those who were plunged into ditches and marshy pools either laid down their arms or perished under the pressure of those behind. By this disaster, the authors note, the middle part of the infantry was destroyed; among the chief men who fell were Rudolph Scullius, Winandus Ommerius, Carolus Wingardius, Petrus Berensteinius, Matthias Kaertius, Gerardus Entenius, Cornelius Loenius, from the English Cotton, Episcopius and Fuillamius, and from the cavalry commanders Henricus Eckius, Bellevinius and Joannes Nisbetius. Nor was the victory bloodless for Verdugius, five or six hundred being missing from King Philip's army. The battle took place on the day before the Kalends of October.

units.la: Tum Verdugius continuatione fortunæ ac rebus circa primæ dignitatis suæ initia prosperis utendum ratus, Neosilum, in quod multi ex acie disparsi palantesque confugerant, obsedit, qui locus trans Lavicam ad rivum ex æstuario proruentem situs quatuor cohortium pedestrium (quibus Steno Maltesius nobilis Danus, Sixtus Sceltema nobilis Frisius, Regnerus Idzius & Schaius præerant) præsidio asservabatur.
units.tr: Then Verdugius, judging that he must make use of the continuing run of fortune and of the favourable beginnings of his high office, laid siege to Neosilum, into which many of the scattered and wandering men from the line had fled. This place, situated beyond the Lavica by a stream flowing out of the estuary, was held under the garrison of four companies of foot, over which Steno Maltesius, a Danish noble, Sixtus Sceltema, a Frisian noble, Regnerus Idzius and Schaius were in command.

units.la: Castra ejus Grypskerckæ & Fissleti ad Lavicam posita, ubi desossis, qui ad emissarium rivi excurrebant, cuniculis, & fluentis alveo onerarijs navigijs obturato, commeatum obsessis intercludere conatus est, quem provincialis Senatus obsidij metuens cum levioribus tormentis Neosilanæ munitioni importaverat. Igitur velut mimum ageret, modo copias suas in formam aciei instruebat, modo velut oppugnationem facturus, obsessis minabatur, non ignavis interea obsessis qui eminus tormentorum ope rem gerentes multos ex Verdugianis sustulere. Dein apertis aquarum claustris, emissarijsque qua æstuaria maris spectant, patefactis vicinos agros & stativa castrorum Verdugij aquis operuere, quas usque ad Emetillam se efferentes vi marinorum æstuum densissimi quoque imbres adaugebant. Unde in castris Verdugij omnia sensim angusta atque difficilia facta ingenio loci sponte depressi nimiâ humiditate aucto & languore insuper militum succrescente, qui ab instituendâ oppugnatione militem molestiæ pertæsum & defectu æris seditiones minantem deterrebat.
units.tr: His camp was pitched at Grypskerck and Fissletum by the Lavica, where, having dug trenches through the dykes that ran down to the outlet of the stream and having blocked the flowing water with heavily laden barges, he tried to cut off supplies from the besieged; the provincial Senate, fearing the siege, had brought lighter artillery into the Neosilan fortification. Thus, as if performing a play, he sometimes drew up his troops in battle formation, sometimes, as if about to make an assault, threatened the besieged; meanwhile the besieged were not idle, and by working their artillery at a distance they cut down many of Verdugius' men. Then, opening the sluices and the outlets that face the estuaries of the sea, they flooded the neighbouring fields and the quarters of Verdugius' camp with water; this water, rising as far as Emetilla under the force of the sea's tides, was swollen further by the heaviest rains. Hence everything in Verdugius' camp gradually became cramped and difficult: the nature of the place, sunk low, was made worse by excessive dampness, and sickness among the soldiers, which grew on top of this, deterred him from beginning the assault; the soldiers, weary of the hardship, and lacking money, threatened mutiny.

units.la: Ita obsidio Neosilana deserta, obsessiq; tergis hostium inuecti, quadraginta trucidatis & viginti quinque militibus captis victores, ovantesque rediere. Ita gravis ad Northormum clades novâ fœlicitate pensata, Verdugiusque repulsæ ignominiâ mærens Groningam recessit: Stenoni Maltefio, qui cum imperio ibi fuerat, resque præclare gesserat, vicarium Merodij munus collocatum, aureaque donaria virtutis ergo militari more concessa.
units.tr: So the siege of Neosilum was abandoned, and the besieged, having attacked the enemy from behind, returned victorious and exultant, after slaying forty and capturing twenty-five soldiers. Thus the grievous disaster at Northormus was offset by a new success, and Verdugius, grieving at the shame of his repulse, withdrew to Groningen. Vicarial command was given to Steno Maltesius, who had held authority there and had performed his duties with distinction, and golden rewards were bestowed on him for his valour in the manner of soldiers.

units.la: Adeo retro citroque modo prosperæ, modo adversæ res illis temporibus fluebant, quæ domi procerum dissensione, foris inopiâ ærarij per avaritiam præfectorum militumque licentiam turbabantur. Unde factum ut à debili infirmoque exercitu fortuna sæpe belli penderet, fœdisque cladibus, etiam connivente Ordinum patientiâ, surgentis reip. primordia insignirentur. Tantum Angliæ ac Germaniæ, tum circumjacentium locorum è quibus auxilia supplementaque legionum habebantur, societatibus dabatur, adnitentibus isto tempore quam maxumè optumatibus sua Philippum in Regem odia fidis aliorum Principum amicitiis velare. Igitur ne fœderato exercitui stipendia desorent, missus Amstelodamum à Senatu Belgico Abelus Franckena, qui subsidia communi ærario ocyus peteret, avertendisq; turbidarum legionum incommodis iter acceleraret. Is acceptis Amstelodami 23. aureorum millibus, quo Senatui Belgico apud Frisios adhuc agenti, allevandis militiæ oneribus traderentur, mox itineri Frisiam versus se dedit, gratissimoq; adventu pecuniam ferendo velut necessariâ corporum refectione militem refocillavit.
units.tr: So, back and forth, fortunes flowed in those times, now favourable, now adverse; at home they were troubled by the dissension of the nobles, abroad by the lack of money in the treasury and by the licence of the captains and soldiers through their greed. Hence it came about that the fortune of war often depended on a weak and feeble army, and the beginnings of the rising commonwealth were marked by shameful disasters, even with the Estates tolerating them. Meanwhile, the nobles at that time were striving as hard as they could to conceal their hatred of Philip as king behind the friendly alliances of England and Germany and of the neighbouring regions from which auxiliaries and reinforcements of legions were obtained. Therefore, lest the pay of the confederate army fail, Abel Franckena was sent to Amsterdam by the Belgian Senate to seek subsidies from the common treasury as quickly as possible, and to speed his journey so as to avert the troubles of the unruly legions. Having received 23,000 gold pieces at Amsterdam, to be handed over to relieve the burdens of the militia while the Belgian Senate was still at work among the Frisians, he then set off for Friesland, and by his most welcome arrival, bringing the money, he refreshed the soldiers as if with necessary food for their bodies.

units.la: Mox vergente eodem Novembri mense, qui ut plurimum occidentibus Vergilijs procellosus noxiusque omni oræ maritimæ esse solet, ve- hemens tempestas coorta, quæ tonitruum fragore, intermistis fulminum ignibus, Floridi campi, quod Bolsuerdiæ vicinum est, cœnobium prodigio & simul damno multavit. Quippe post campanas turri vehementiâ fulminis detonantiumque nubium expulsas, majus quoque altare disjecit, statuasque & imagines tum horti arborem & monialium vestimenta demisso cœlitus igne ambussit. Quod inter prodigia relatum, auctâ simul pestilentiæ, qua plurimi mortales rapiebantur, malignitate, provincialium sollicitudinem metumque vertentium se, quasi retortis sideribus, temporum incendit.
units.tr: Soon, as the same month of November drew toward its end, which as a rule is stormy and hurtful to all the seacoast when the Pleiades set, a violent tempest arose which, with the crash of thunder and intermittent flashes of lightning, struck the monastery of Floridus Field, near Bolsuerdia, with a portent and at the same time with loss. For after the bells had been driven from the tower by the violence of the lightning and the thundering clouds, it also shattered the high altar, and fire sent down from heaven scorched the statues and images, the tree of the garden and the nuns' clothing. This was reckoned among the portents, and the malignity of the plague, by which very many mortals were being carried off, increased at the same time; it inflamed the anxiety and fear of the provincials, who were turning themselves, as if the stars had been turned back, toward the crisis of the times.

units.la: Quare odiosiore sensum Philippi nomine, quod publico per Brabantiam, Geldriam, Flandriam, Hollandiam, reliquasq; provincias edictô jam ante damnatum erat, Senatus Belgicus Leovardiæ adhuc subsistens, post Doccomium, Slotam, Stauriam oppida, reliquaq; maritimæ oræ loca necessario opere ac commeatu emunita, ejurando quoque regio nomini ac simul imperio ordinavit, inligatisque novo libertatis sacramento Magistratibus, Prætoribusque tum pagorum vicorumque magistris, Senatum quoque qui supremâ juris dicundi potestate fungebatur, velut regiæ venerationis dignitatisque retinentem obligare religio- ni fœderis novæque libertatis constituit.
units.tr: Therefore, with the name of Philip rendered more hateful in feeling, since by public edict it had already been condemned throughout Brabant, Gelderland, Flanders, Holland and the other provinces, the Belgian Senate, still sitting at Leeuwarden, after the towns of Dokkum, Sloten and Staveren and the other places on the seacoast had been fortified by necessary work and supplies, also ordered that the royal name be renounced, and, binding the magistrates and praetors, as well as the officers of the villages and hamlets, by a new oath of liberty, it resolved to bind the Senate too, which exercised the supreme power of administering justice, by the sanctity of the covenant and of the new liberty, as though it still held the dignity and reverence of royal majesty.

units.la: cIↄ. Iↄ. LXXXI. Quare congregatis Ordinum Frisiæ Delegatis, citatoq; Senatu Juridico, litteræ Concilij Status ex decreto Ordinum Belgicæ quod mense Augusto perscriptum erat, in publico prælectæ, quibus Rege à Senatu ejurato, novam sacramenti dictionem Senatus Belgicus proponebat. Quod etsi Senatus Judicialis detrectaret, modo actorum copiam modo deliberandi capiendique consilij tempus poscens, ita non obscura sui in regem affectus signa edebat, severiterque & cum rigore quæsitus, quid tergiversationi obtenderet, diem in proximum, qui in Nonas Decembres 1581. incidebat, sententiæ dicendæ animique expromendi solemnitatem extraxit. Itaque tunc, ne judicium, quod tum coeptandum erat, justitio impediretur, præsente Senatu Belgico, Ordinum Frisiæ Deputatis sacramentum dixit, fidemque patriæ & libertati datam publica regij nominis detestatione firmavit. Quâ actione ne durante Fecco Rhala Jurisperitus & Senator, qui consessui erat, damnatione regiæ majestatis imperijque propositâ, repentinâ morte exanimatus est. Quod sive animo, ut creditum fuit, detectione correpto, sive viri consternatione ad tam duram vocem legemque inhorrescentis, factum fuerit in silentio est, hoc saltem de præclaro viro & libertatis patriæ amante traditum est, eum nec à Rege nec à libertate alienum moderatis consilijs egisse.
units.tr: 1581. Therefore the delegates of the Estates of Friesland were gathered together, the judicial Senate was summoned, and the letter of the Council of State, written in August by decree of the Belgian Estates, was read aloud in public; in it, with the king renounced by the Senate, the Belgian Senate proposed a new form of oath. Although the judicial Senate objected to this, now asking for a copy of the acts, now for time to deliberate and take counsel, it showed by these means no obscure signs of its feeling against the king; and when severely and sharply questioned as to what it was using as a pretext for its evasion, it postponed the solemn pronouncement of its judgment and the declaration of its mind until the next day, which fell on the Nones of December 1581. Then, lest the judgment, which was to be begun at that time, be hindered by an impediment, in the presence of the Belgian Senate he took the oath before the Frisian deputies of the Estates and confirmed the faith pledged to the fatherland and to liberty with a public renunciation of the royal name. While this act was in progress, Fecco Rhala, a jurist and senator who was present at the assembly, seized by sudden death, having heard the king's majesty and rule put in danger by the proposed condemnation. Whether this happened from the emotion of fear, as was believed, or from the horror of the man at so harsh a word and law, is left in silence; this at least has been handed down about that distinguished man and lover of his country's liberty, that he acted, being neither alien to the king nor to liberty, with moderate counsels.

units.la: Franckena in Ephemeride notat, non obscuro animorum motu habitam actionem fuisse, Senatumque Juridicum invitum, ut scribit, & sementem sacramento Ordinum Delegatorumque se obligasse. Mox omnis actorum vis ac memoria, quæ CAROLO sub Cæsare, mox PHILIPPO filio invaluerat, infirmata, sigillumque ac nomen regium jussu publico abolitum.
units.tr: Franckena notes in his journal that the action was taken with no obscure stirring of minds, and that the judicial Senate, against its will, as he writes, and in the same way, bound itself by the oath of the Estates and their delegates. Soon the whole force and memory of the acts, which had prevailed under Charles the Emperor and then under his son Philip, was weakened, and the royal seal and name were abolished by public order.

units.la: Ita Natalis LIBERTATI dies ortus, Belgicaq; & Frisiorum gens regijs imperijs exempta, factorum seriem temporaq; libertatis ab illo patrum Senatus-Consulto inchoavit. Quare & adorata quæsitaque ad Gades Herculisque Columnas CAROLI PHILIPPI QUEMajestas Provincijs assignata regiumque imperium in formam REIPUBLICAE redactum velut fatalibus rerum suarum periodis, valido per Provincias fœdere evanuit. D. O. M. Laus & Gloria.
units.tr: Thus the birthday of Liberty dawned, and the Belgian and Frisian nation, freed from royal rule, began the sequence of events and the times of liberty from that senatorial decree of the fathers. Wherefore also the majesty of Charles and Philip, adored and sought as far as Cadiz and the Pillars of Hercules, assigned to the provinces, and the royal rule reduced to the form of a commonwealth, vanished, as it were at the fated turning-points of its affairs, by a strong covenant among the provinces. To God the Best and Greatest, praise and glory.

units.tr: THE END of the Histories of P. Winsemius.
